211-bay-area.name: 2-1-1 Bay Area
211-bay-area.description: 2-1-1 Bay Area, a program of United Way Bay Area, is a free, confidential helpline connecting residents to essential community services 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, in multiple languages.
211-bay-area.what_they_offer:
- Free 24/7 helpline (call or text 2-1-1)
- Referrals to food assistance programs
- Housing and shelter resources
- Legal help connections
- Health care navigation
- Utility assistance referrals
211-bay-area.how_to_get_it:
1. Call or text 2-1-1 from any phone
2. Or search online at 211bayarea.org
3. Speak with trained specialist
4. Describe your needs
5. Receive personalized referrals
6. Follow up on resources provided

czi-community-space.name: CZI Community Space
czi-community-space.description: The Chan Zuckerberg Community Space in downtown Redwood City provides free meeting and event space for nonprofits serving San Mateo County, plus Redwood City and San Mateo County government agencies.
czi-community-space.what_they_offer:
- Free event space (The Grove) for up to 200 people
- Two conference rooms (up to 20 and 12 people)
- Free WiFi, microphones, screens, and videoconferencing tools
- Multiple event layouts (theater, banquet, mix and mingle)
- Weekday day and evening events
- Members can book up to one year in advance
czi-community-space.how_to_get_it:
1. Be a Bay Area nonprofit that serves San Mateo County, or a Redwood City/San Mateo County government agency
2. Contact CZI through the Community Space website about membership
3. Once a member, check room availability on the online calendar
4. Submit a meeting request (up to one year in advance)
5. Follow the Community Space guidelines for your event

dolly-parton-library.name: Dolly Parton Imagination Library
dolly-parton-library.description: Dolly Parton's Imagination Library sends a free, high-quality book every month to registered children from birth to age five, regardless of family income. The Imagination Library of California is expanding county by county with State of California matching funds (42 counties as of March 2026).
dolly-parton-library.what_they_offer:
- Free book mailed monthly
- For children birth to age 5
- High-quality, age-appropriate books
- English or bilingual English/Spanish books
- Build library of up to 60 books
- Delivered directly to your home
dolly-parton-library.how_to_get_it:
1. Visit the Imagination Library of California page
2. Check availability for your address and register (takes under 5 minutes)
3. Enter your child's information and mailing address
4. Register each eligible child separately
5. First book arrives within 8-12 weeks
6. Books continue monthly until age 5

generation-thrive-spaces.name: Generation Thrive
generation-thrive-spaces.description: Generation Thrive, from the Warriors Community Foundation and Kaiser Permanente, provides free meeting and coworking space to registered Bay Area nonprofits at two sites: downtown Oakland (1011 Broadway, in the Oakland Marriott City Center) and San Francisco (1725 3rd St, in Chase Center's Thrive City).
generation-thrive-spaces.what_they_offer:
- Free conference rooms for up to 40 guests
- Single-day coworking reservations (up to 5 people, once a week)
- Free high-speed WiFi and hybrid meeting setup
- Outside food and drinks allowed (no alcohol)
- Non-grantees can book conference rooms once a month (up to 2 days)
- Priority for Warriors Community Foundation and select Kaiser grantees
generation-thrive-spaces.how_to_get_it:
1. Must be a registered Bay Area 501(c)(3) nonprofit
2. Submit a space request on the Generation Thrive website (one request per day of use)
3. Describe your organization and meeting needs
4. A tour may be required for larger or complex events
5. Wait for approval and confirmation
6. Share your guest list before the event; all guests check in on arrival

google-community-space.name: Google Community Space
google-community-space.description: Google Community Space offers free event space in San Francisco to member Bay Area nonprofits and local city and county government departments. It is now located at Hills Plaza (courtyard entrance, Suite 140).
google-community-space.what_they_offer:
- Free event space: Main Room for up to 48 people plus a 12-person workshop room
- Screens, handheld and lapel microphones included
- Free membership for approved organizations
- Google-hosted programming for members (when available)
- One event per business quarter
- No kitchen on site (catering allowed)
google-community-space.how_to_get_it:
1. Must be a registered 501(c)(3) in good standing or a local city/county government department in the 9 Bay Area counties
2. Apply for membership on the Google Community Space website (nonprofits are verified through Benevity)
3. Once accepted, log in to the Member Portal to request a date
4. Book up to 90 days in advance, Monday-Friday 9am-5pm
5. Upload a certificate of insurance (COI) and submit a guest list for each event
6. Schedule space (max once per quarter)

ohana-floor-salesforce.name: Salesforce Ohana Floor
ohana-floor-salesforce.description: Salesforce opens its 61st-floor 'Ohana Floor at Salesforce Tower, with 360-degree Bay Area views, to nonprofits and charitable organizations for fundraisers, receptions, and special events. The space is provided at no charge, but event costs such as catering, security, and A/V are paid by the host.
ohana-floor-salesforce.what_they_offer:
- Event space on the 61st floor at no charge
- Capacity up to 250 guests
- 360-degree views of the Bay Area
- Existing furniture included
- On-site Salesforce event team to help plan
- Available once every 12 months per organization
ohana-floor-salesforce.how_to_get_it:
1. Must be a nonprofit or charitable foundation focused on humanitarian/social causes, public education, or the environment
2. Submit an event request on the Salesforce Tower San Francisco page
3. Events are booked up to six months out; expect a reply in 7-10 business days
4. Events are held on weeknight evenings, based on availability
5. Budget for costs like building security, catering, bar, A/V, and printing (preferred vendors required)
6. Event is confirmed once the booking agreement is signed by both parties
ohana-floor-salesforce.timeframe: Weeknight evenings (5:30-8pm), booked up to 6 months out

season-of-sharing.name: Season of Sharing Fund
season-of-sharing.description: The Season of Sharing Fund provides short-term emergency financial help to Bay Area households facing an unexpected crisis, to keep them housed and prevent homelessness. Help is available in all nine Bay Area counties through local coordinating agencies.
season-of-sharing.what_they_offer:
- Help with rent or mortgage payments
- Move-in costs (first and last month's deposit)
- Utility payment assistance
- Prevents eviction and homelessness
- Short-term, one-time financial support
- Payments made directly to landlord or utility company
season-of-sharing.how_to_get_it:
1. Must live in one of the nine Bay Area counties and be 18 or older
2. Must be facing an emergency or unexpected event that threatens housing stability
3. Find your county's coordinating agency on the Season of Sharing "Get Help" page
4. Contact that agency to apply
5. Funds are paid directly to your landlord or service provider
6. For food help, contact your county food bank

sobrato-conference-space.name: Sobrato Nonprofit Centers Conference Space
sobrato-conference-space.description: Sobrato Philanthropies provides free meeting and conference space to qualified Bay Area nonprofits at its Sobrato Centers for Nonprofits in Redwood Shores (Redwood City), San Jose, and Milpitas.
sobrato-conference-space.what_they_offer:
- Free meeting and conference rooms
- Spaces for 3 to 200 people
- Audio/visual equipment included
- Hospitality and registration areas
- Free on-site parking; food and drinks allowed
- Locations in Redwood Shores, San Jose, and Milpitas
sobrato-conference-space.how_to_get_it:
1. Must be a qualified Bay Area nonprofit
2. Apply through Sobrato website
3. Select preferred location and date
4. Describe meeting or event needs
5. Wait for confirmation
6. Follow facility guidelines

tides-converge.name: Tides Converge
tides-converge.description: Tides Converge is a shared nonprofit campus in the Presidio, home to about 75 nonprofits and social enterprises, offering meeting and event room rentals, coworking, and stable, affordable office leases.
tides-converge.what_they_offer:
- Meeting and event room rentals (fee-based)
- Coworking program (competitive application)
- Affordable office leases
- WiFi, whiteboards, and projector on request with room rentals
- On-site organic cafe; outside catering allowed
- Presidio location with Golden Gate Bridge views
tides-converge.how_to_get_it:
1. Must be a nonprofit or social enterprise (for coworking and leases)
2. For meeting rooms, call 415-561-6300 to check availability and rates
3. Room renters must provide a certificate of insurance
4. For coworking, contact Tides about the application process
5. For office leases, contact the property manager listed on the Tides website
6. Parking in the Presidio is $9/day; a free shuttle runs from downtown

bacn-boutique.name: Bay Area Crisis Nursery - BACN Boutique
bacn-boutique.description: BACN Boutique provides free clothing, shoes, children's furniture, toys, and essential items for families. It is located in the Bay Area Crisis Nursery lobby in Concord and is open to the public.
bacn-boutique.what_they_offer:
- Free clothing and shoes for children and parents
- Children's furniture, books, and toys
- Baby items for expecting parents: clothing, blankets, bottles, strollers, and equipment
- Hygiene products for parents
- Staff can help find items you don't see
- Everything is free
bacn-boutique.how_to_get_it:
1. Visit the Boutique in the Nursery lobby (office hours Mon-Fri 9am-5pm)
2. Open to the public at no cost
3. Browse available items
4. Ask Nursery staff if you need something you don't see
5. Take items home at no cost
6. Call ahead to order food and diapers to pick up at the same visit

bacn-food-pantry-diaper.name: Bay Area Crisis Nursery - Food Pantry & Diaper Bank
bacn-food-pantry-diaper.description: Bay Area Crisis Nursery operates a food pantry and diaper bank providing free non-perishable and fresh food and diapers to families with young children. The Diaper Bank is open to the whole community.
bacn-food-pantry-diaper.what_they_offer:
- Free non-perishable and fresh food
- Free diapers for babies and toddlers
- Order by phone for pickup
- Food pantry open daily for pickups
- Food provided in partnership with the Food Bank of Contra Costa and Solano
- No-cost support for families in need
bacn-food-pantry-diaper.how_to_get_it:
1. Call the Nursery at 925-685-8052
2. Ask to order a food and/or diaper pickup
3. Provide family information
4. Arrange a pickup time
5. Pick up at the Concord location
6. Visit the free BACN Boutique while you're there

sf-diaper-bank.name: San Francisco Diaper Bank
sf-diaper-bank.description: The San Francisco Diaper Bank, a partnership between SFHSA and the nonprofit Help a Mother Out, provides free monthly diapers for children under age two to San Francisco residents who receive Medi-Cal, CalWORKs, or CalFresh. Participating does not reduce your food or cash benefits.
sf-diaper-bank.what_they_offer:
- Free diapers for eligible families
- For children under age two
- Up to two cases per child/month
- Available to CalFresh recipients
- Available to Medi-Cal recipients
- Available to CalWORKs (and Cal-Learn) households
sf-diaper-bank.how_to_get_it:
1. Must be a San Francisco resident enrolled in CalFresh, Medi-Cal, or CalWORKs
2. Child must be under age two
3. Go to an SFHSA Service Center (1440 Harrison St, 170 Otis St, 3120 Mission St, or 1460 Mission St) or a partner family resource center
4. Bring your EBT or BIC card and a valid government-issued ID
5. Someone else can pick up for you with an SFDB Designee Form
6. Pick up your monthly allotment

st-anthonys-clothing.name: St. Anthony's Free Clothing Program
st-anthonys-clothing.description: St. Anthony's runs San Francisco's largest free clothing program, offering new and gently used clothing in a boutique-style store. Anyone with a self-determined need is welcome; all visits are by appointment.
st-anthonys-clothing.what_they_offer:
- Free clothing for adults and families
- Casual wear and warm clothes
- Business attire
- Children's clothing
- Individual Service (adults 18+) and Family Service (families with children under 18)
- No eligibility or income requirements
st-anthonys-clothing.how_to_get_it:
1. First-time guests (or those who haven't shopped in over a year) register in person with Guest Services, 1st floor of 121 Golden Gate Ave
2. Staff may ask for ID; Family Service asks for a document showing custody of children
3. Returning guests book an appointment every 28 days at FreeClothingSF.org (no email or phone booking)
4. Individual Service: Mon-Fri 8:15am-12pm
5. Family Service: Mon, Tue, Thu, Fri 1-4pm and Sat 8:30am-3pm
6. Shop on the 2nd floor at your appointment time

california-grants-portal.name: California Grants Portal
california-grants-portal.description: The California Grants Portal, a project of the California State Library, is a free, searchable one-stop site for grants and loans offered on a competitive or first-come basis by California state agencies, helping nonprofits, tribes, public agencies, and others find funding.
california-grants-portal.what_they_offer:
- Free searchable grant database
- Competitive and first-come state grants and loans
- Filter by category and deadline
- Filter by applicant type
- Application information included
- Email updates for new grants
california-grants-portal.how_to_get_it:
1. Visit grants.ca.gov
2. Subscribe to updates (optional)
3. Search grants by keyword or category
4. Filter by applicant type and deadline
5. Review grant requirements
6. Follow links to apply with the state agency offering the grant

lifemoves-services.name: LifeMoves Opportunity Services Center
lifemoves-services.description: The LifeMoves Opportunity Services Center (OSC) is a low-barrier drop-in center in Palo Alto serving mainly single adults experiencing homelessness, with meals, showers, laundry, and case management. LifeMoves also runs a Palo Alto outreach team out of OSC.
lifemoves-services.what_they_offer:
- Daily breakfast and lunch
- Showers and laundry
- Mailboxes and personal lockers
- Case management and resource navigation
- Connections to shelter and housing
- Palo Alto street outreach team
lifemoves-services.how_to_get_it:
1. Drop in Monday-Friday, 8am-4pm (call to confirm hours)
2. No appointment needed
3. Use meals, showers, laundry, and other services
4. Ask staff about case management
5. For shelter in Santa Clara County, use the county's Coordinated Entry System or dial 2-1-1

haven-family-house.name: Haven Family House (LifeMoves)
haven-family-house.description: Haven Family House is a LifeMoves interim housing facility in Menlo Park providing shelter and comprehensive services for families experiencing homelessness, with dedicated capacity for veteran families.
haven-family-house.what_they_offer:
- Interim shelter for 23 families
- Dedicated veteran family capacity (9 families)
- Supportive services included
- Case management
- Housing placement assistance
- Family-focused environment
haven-family-house.how_to_get_it:
1. Go through San Mateo County's Coordinated Entry System (dial 2-1-1 or text your ZIP code to 898211)
2. Complete intake assessment
3. Demonstrate family homelessness
4. Veteran families may be placed in the 9 units reserved for veterans
5. Accept shelter placement if available
6. Work with case manager on housing plan

friendly-voices-seniors.name: Friendly Voices Phone Buddies for Seniors
friendly-voices-seniors.description: Friendly Voices, now part of the older-adult nonprofit Avenidas, connects isolated seniors age 60+ in the San Francisco Bay Area and beyond with a trained volunteer phone buddy for weekly friendly conversations, reducing loneliness and providing social connection.
friendly-voices-seniors.what_they_offer:
- Weekly volunteer phone calls
- Supportive listening
- Confidential, HIPAA-compliant calls
- Matched 1:1 with the same phone buddy over many months
- Cantonese, Hindi, or Mandarin-speaking volunteers on request
- Free service for seniors 60+
friendly-voices-seniors.how_to_get_it:
1. Visit Friendly Voices website
2. Click "Sign Up an Older Adult" (seniors, family, or caregivers can sign up)
3. Complete the sign-up form
4. Get matched with a screened, trained volunteer buddy
5. Receive weekly phone calls
6. Build ongoing friendship

smc-fixit-clinics.name: Fixit Clinics
smc-fixit-clinics.description: San Mateo County's Fixit Clinics are free community repair events where volunteer coaches help residents fix broken items, reducing waste and saving money on replacements.
smc-fixit-clinics.what_they_offer:
- Free repair assistance
- Electronics repair help
- Appliance troubleshooting
- Computer and device fixes
- Toy and small item repair
- Sewing machine and textile mending
smc-fixit-clinics.how_to_get_it:
1. Check event schedule online
2. Find Fixit Clinic near you
3. Bring broken items to event
4. Work with volunteer coach
5. Learn repair skills
6. Take fixed items home

smc-library-sewing.name: San Mateo County Library Open Sewing Programs
smc-library-sewing.description: Public libraries across San Mateo County offer free open sewing and mending programs, where you can use library sewing machines, repair clothing, and share sewing skills with neighbors. Programs are open to everyone, not just city residents.
smc-library-sewing.what_they_offer:
- Free sewing and mending programs
- Library sewing machines available
- Foster City and Half Moon Bay (Open Sewing)
- Millbrae and Redwood City (Open Sewing; embroidery machine in Redwood City)
- San Mateo (Afternoon Sewing) and South San Francisco (Mending Hour)
- Open to everyone
smc-library-sewing.how_to_get_it:
1. Check the schedule on the County Sustainability Department's Fixit Clinics page
2. Click the program link for your library for current dates
3. Bring items needing repair
4. Attend during program hours
5. Mend and sew alongside neighbors
6. Learn sewing skills

recyclestuff.name: Recyclestuff.org
recyclestuff.description: Recyclestuff.org is a free online search tool for San Mateo County and Santa Clara County residents to find the right place to recycle, donate, or properly dispose of household items. It is run by the San Jose Conservation Corps with the two counties.
recyclestuff.what_they_offer:
- Free online search engine
- Find donation locations
- Find recycling centers
- Household hazardous waste drop-off appointments
- City and county recycling program info
- Help from local recycling experts by phone or email
recyclestuff.how_to_get_it:
1. Visit recyclestuff.org
2. Search for the item you want to get rid of
3. Choose your city or county
4. View nearby options
5. Choose appropriate location
6. Drop off, or schedule a household hazardous waste appointment

acs-discovery-shop-oakland.name: American Cancer Society: Discovery Shop (Oakland)
acs-discovery-shop-oakland.description: The American Cancer Society Discovery Shop in Oakland is a thrift store selling quality secondhand and vintage items, with proceeds supporting cancer research and patient programs.
acs-discovery-shop-oakland.what_they_offer:
- Accept clothing donations
- Accept accessories and housewares
- Accept linens and furniture
- Accept collectibles and vintage items
- Affordable thrift shopping
- Proceeds fund cancer research

2. Donate gently used items
3. Or shop for affordable goods
4. Open Mon-Sat 10am-6pm, Sun 10am-5pm
5. Call (510) 601-0100 for info

ehp-donations.name: Ecumenical Hunger Program Donations
ehp-donations.description: The Ecumenical Hunger Program (EHP) accepts donations of clothing, household items, food, and furniture to support its food and basic-needs services for low-income families in East Palo Alto and surrounding communities.
ehp-donations.what_they_offer:
- Accept clean, gently used clothing and linens (bedding and linens especially needed)
- Accept household items
- Accept food and new items such as toys
- Accept furniture (call first)
- Online form to schedule a donation pick-up
- Supports community food programs
ehp-donations.how_to_get_it:
1. Drop off donations Monday-Thursday, 9am-5pm
2. Make sure clothing and linens are clean and gently used
3. For furniture, call (650) 323-7781 x1100 to see if it can be accepted
4. Or schedule a donation pick-up on the EHP website
5. Donations support local families
6. Hours may change around the holidays; call ahead

family-connections-donations.name: Peninsula Family Connections Donations
family-connections-donations.description: Peninsula Family Connections provides free early childhood education, family support, and mental health services for families with young children, with program sites in East Palo Alto and Redwood City. You can support its work with donations; contact them to ask whether item donations are currently accepted.
family-connections-donations.what_they_offer:
- Online and mailed monetary donations
- Stock gifts and bequests
- Volunteer opportunities (classroom help, tutoring, site upkeep)
- Contact to ask about current item donation needs
- Supports free early learning classes for children birth to 5
- Supports family support and mental health services
family-connections-donations.how_to_get_it:
1. Visit the Family Connections donate page
2. Give online, or mail a check to Peninsula Family Connections, 3460 W. Bayshore Road, Suite 202, Palo Alto, CA 94303
3. For stock gifts or bequests, email info@familyconnections.org or call (669) 237-8911
4. Before bringing any items, call or email to ask what is needed
5. To volunteer, contact them through the Get Involved page

goodwill-sf-sm-marin.name: Goodwill Industries (SF, San Mateo, Marin)
goodwill-sf-sm-marin.description: Goodwill Industries operates thrift stores and donation centers throughout the Bay Area, with proceeds funding job training and employment programs for people facing barriers.
goodwill-sf-sm-marin.what_they_offer:

samaritan-house-donations.description: Samaritan House operates thrift stores throughout San Mateo County, with proceeds supporting their free food, health, and housing programs for low-income residents.

salvation-army-smc.description: The Salvation Army operates thrift stores and accepts donations throughout San Mateo County, with proceeds funding their social services, emergency assistance, and community programs.

ucpa-golden-gate.description: United Cerebral Palsy Association of the Golden Gate accepts donations of household items and vehicles, with proceeds supporting services for people with developmental disabilities.

exploratorium-teacher-free.name: Exploratorium Free Teacher Admission
exploratorium-teacher-free.description: The Exploratorium offers free admission to K-12 teachers, allowing educators to explore exhibits and develop ideas for classroom activities.
exploratorium-teacher-free.what_they_offer:
- Free general admission for K-12 teachers
- Access to all museum exhibits
- Teacher professional development programs
- Free After Dark admission (Thursdays)
- Curriculum resources and ideas
exploratorium-teacher-free.how_to_get_it:
1. Visit the Exploratorium with valid teacher ID
2. Show school-issued ID or pay stub
3. Register at admissions desk
4. Receive free entry to museum
5. Access available year-round

bay-area-writing-project.name: Bay Area Writing Project
bay-area-writing-project.description: The Bay Area Writing Project at UC Berkeley provides professional development programs for teachers, helping educators improve writing instruction and student outcomes.
bay-area-writing-project.what_they_offer:
- Summer Invitational Institute (4-week program)
- Yearlong professional development
- Teacher leadership development
- Writing workshops and coaching
- Classroom-tested strategies
- Community of teacher-writers
bay-area-writing-project.how_to_get_it:
1. Visit BAWP website for program information
2. Apply for Summer Invitational Institute or other programs
3. Describe your teaching context and goals
4. Attend program sessions
5. Join network of teacher-consultants

sf-hsh.name: SF Homelessness and Supportive Housing
sf-hsh.description: San Francisco's Department of Homelessness and Supportive Housing (HSH) coordinates the city's response to homelessness, providing shelter, housing, and supportive services.
sf-hsh.what_they_offer:
- Emergency shelter access
- Navigation centers with services
- Permanent supportive housing
- Rapid rehousing assistance
- Street outreach teams
- Connection to services
sf-hsh.how_to_get_it:
1. Call SF Homeless Outreach Team at 415-734-4233
2. Or call 311 for shelter information
3. Connect with street outreach if unsheltered
4. Complete intake at navigation center
5. Receive housing and service referrals

family-caregiver-alliance.name: Family Caregiver Alliance / Bay Area Caregiver Resource Center
family-caregiver-alliance.description: Family Caregiver Alliance operates the Bay Area Caregiver Resource Center, providing support, education, and services to family caregivers of adults with chronic or disabling conditions.
family-caregiver-alliance.what_they_offer:
- Free caregiver support groups
- Respite care grants
- Individual caregiver coaching
- Educational workshops
- Legal and financial consultations
- Care planning assistance
- Short-term counseling
family-caregiver-alliance.how_to_get_it:
1. Call Family Caregiver Alliance
2. Complete intake assessment
3. Meet with care consultant
4. Develop personalized care plan
5. Access respite grants and services

ihss.name: In-Home Supportive Services (IHSS)
ihss.description: In-Home Supportive Services (IHSS) is California's program that pays family members or others to provide in-home care for aged, blind, or disabled individuals who qualify for Medi-Cal.
ihss.what_they_offer:
- Paid caregiving by family members
- Personal care assistance
- Housekeeping and meal preparation
- Medical accompaniment
- Protective supervision
- Respite for family caregivers
ihss.how_to_get_it:
1. Apply through county social services
2. Must be on Medi-Cal
3. Home assessment conducted
4. Care hours determined by needs
5. Choose caregiver (can be family member)
6. Caregiver receives hourly payment

beyond-emancipation.name: Beyond Emancipation
beyond-emancipation.description: Beyond Emancipation helps current and former foster youth in Alameda County transition to successful adulthood through housing, education, employment, and wellness support.
beyond-emancipation.what_they_offer:
- Housing assistance and placement
- Education support and tutoring
- Employment training and job placement
- Life skills development
- Mental health services
- Financial coaching
- Ongoing case management
beyond-emancipation.how_to_get_it:
1. Contact Beyond Emancipation
2. Must be current or former foster youth ages 16-24
3. Must have connection to Alameda County
4. Complete intake assessment
5. Develop personalized success plan
6. Access comprehensive services

first-place-for-youth.name: First Place for Youth
first-place-for-youth.description: First Place for Youth helps foster youth ages 18-24 build the skills they need to successfully transition to adulthood through housing, education, and employment programs.
first-place-for-youth.what_they_offer:
- Transitional housing placement
- Education coaching and support
- Employment training and placement
- Life skills workshops
- Financial literacy education
- Mental health resources
- Long-term case management
first-place-for-youth.how_to_get_it:
1. Contact First Place for Youth
2. Must be current or former foster youth ages 18-24
3. Complete application and interview
4. Participate in intake assessment
5. Access housing and comprehensive services

chafee-grant.name: Chafee Grant for Foster Youth
chafee-grant.description: The Chafee Grant provides up to $5,000 per year for current and former foster youth to pay for career and technical training or college expenses.
chafee-grant.what_they_offer:
- Up to $5,000 per academic year
- Covers tuition, fees, books, supplies
- Can cover living expenses
- Available through age 26
- For vocational training or college
- Does not have to be repaid
chafee-grant.how_to_get_it:
1. Must be current or former foster youth
2. Must be age 16-26
3. Complete FAFSA or CA Dream Act application
4. Check box for foster youth status
5. Enroll in eligible school or training program
6. Grant automatically considered

sf-casa.name: San Francisco CASA
sf-casa.description: San Francisco Court Appointed Special Advocates (CASA) trains volunteers to advocate for children and youth in the foster care system, ensuring their voices are heard in court.
sf-casa.what_they_offer:
- Trained volunteer advocates for foster youth
- Court advocacy and monitoring
- Educational advocacy
- Connection to services and resources
- Consistent supportive adult relationship
- Voice for child's best interests
sf-casa.how_to_get_it:
1. Foster youth referred by court or social worker
2. CASA volunteer assigned to case
3. Advocate meets regularly with child
4. Advocate reports to court
5. Support continues through case

national-hotline-safety.name: National Safety Hotline
national-hotline-safety.description: The National Safety Hotline provides free, confidential support 24/7 for individuals and families experiencing unsafe situations at home. Trained advocates offer crisis intervention, safety planning, and connections to local resources.
national-hotline-safety.what_they_offer:
- 24/7 phone support (1-800-799-7233)
- Text support (text START to 88788)
- Online chat available
- Safety planning assistance
- Local resource referrals
- Support in 200+ languages
- TTY line for deaf/hard of hearing
national-hotline-safety.how_to_get_it:
1. Call 1-800-799-7233 anytime
2. Or text START to 88788
3. Or chat online at thehotline.org
4. Trained advocates available 24/7
5. Completely confidential
6. No judgment, just support

ywca-silicon-valley.name: YWCA Silicon Valley
ywca-silicon-valley.description: YWCA Silicon Valley provides support services including emergency shelter, transitional housing, counseling, and advocacy for individuals and families in Santa Clara County.
ywca-silicon-valley.what_they_offer:
- Emergency shelter
- Transitional housing
- Counseling services
- Legal advocacy
- Support groups
- Children's programs
- Economic empowerment
- Community education
ywca-silicon-valley.how_to_get_it:
1. Call San Jose: 408-295-4011
2. Or Sunnyvale: 408-749-0793
3. Speak with intake coordinator
4. Complete assessment
5. Access shelter and services
6. Receive ongoing support

headspace-teachers-free.name: Headspace for Educators
headspace-teachers-free.description: Headspace offers free access to K-12 teachers in the US, providing meditation, sleep, and mindfulness exercises to support educator well-being.
headspace-teachers-free.what_they_offer:
- Free Headspace subscription for K-12 teachers
- Guided meditations
- Sleep sounds and exercises
- Stress and anxiety tools
- Focus music and exercises
- Normally $69.99/year value
headspace-teachers-free.how_to_get_it:
1. Visit headspace.com/educators
2. Verify K-12 teacher status through SheerID
3. Create free Headspace account
4. Access full premium content
5. Must be actively employed K-12 educator in US

calvet-college-fee-waiver.name: CalVet College Fee Waiver
calvet-college-fee-waiver.description: The CalVet College Fee Waiver waives enrollment fees and tuition at California public universities (UC, CSU, and Community Colleges) for eligible dependents of disabled or deceased veterans.
calvet-college-fee-waiver.what_they_offer:
- Full waiver of enrollment fees at UC, CSU, and Community Colleges
- Full waiver of state tuition at public universities
- Covers undergraduate and graduate programs
- No limit on number of eligible dependents per veteran
- Renewable each academic year
- Includes children, spouses, and registered domestic partners
calvet-college-fee-waiver.how_to_get_it:
1. Veteran must have service-connected disability rating of 0% or higher
2. Or veteran must have died of service-connected cause
3. Or veteran must have died during active duty
4. Dependent submits application through CalVet
5. Provide DD214, disability rating letter, and proof of relationship
6. Submit fee waiver certification to school financial aid office

act-fee-waivers.name: ACT Fee Waivers
act-fee-waivers.description: The ACT offers fee waivers for students from low-income families, removing financial barriers to college entrance testing.
act-fee-waivers.what_they_offer:
- Two free ACT tests (with or without writing)
- Free access to official ACT Self-Paced Course (Kaplan prep)
- Send scores to up to 20 colleges for free
- Ability to request college application fee waivers
- Waived fees for late registration, standby testing, and test date changes
act-fee-waivers.how_to_get_it:
1. Must be in 11th or 12th grade
2. Must meet income eligibility guidelines
3. Talk to your high school counselor about eligibility
4. Counselor will provide fee waiver form
5. Use fee waiver code when registering for ACT
6. Present fee waiver at test center

ap-exam-fee-reductions.name: AP Exam Fee Reductions
ap-exam-fee-reductions.description: The College Board offers significant fee reductions on AP (Advanced Placement) exams for students with demonstrated financial need.
ap-exam-fee-reductions.what_they_offer:
- $37 College Board fee reduction per AP exam
- Schools forgo $9 rebate, adding to the reduction
- Final cost typically $53-62 per exam (down from $99)
- Some California districts provide additional funding
- Some students pay $0 for exams in participating districts
ap-exam-fee-reductions.how_to_get_it:
1. Must demonstrate financial need (qualify for free/reduced lunch, etc.)
2. Talk to your AP teacher or school counselor
3. School will verify eligibility
4. Fee reduction automatically applied at registration
5. Pay reduced fee by deadline

california-college-promise-grant.name: California College Promise Grant (CCPG)
california-college-promise-grant.description: The California College Promise Grant (formerly BOG Fee Waiver) waives enrollment fees at all 116 California Community Colleges for eligible students.
california-college-promise-grant.what_they_offer:
- Waiver of enrollment fees ($46 per unit)
- Covers entire academic year
- Valid at all California Community Colleges
- May qualify for additional financial aid
- No limit on number of units covered
california-college-promise-grant.how_to_get_it:
1. Complete the FAFSA or California Dream Act Application
2. Apply through CCCApply when enrolling in a community college
3. Qualify based on income, receiving public benefits (CalFresh, TANF, etc.), or other criteria
4. Grant automatically applied to your enrollment fees
5. Renew each academic year

common-app-fee-waiver.name: Common App Fee Waiver
common-app-fee-waiver.description: The Common Application offers fee waivers that eliminate college application fees at over 900 participating colleges for students with financial need.
common-app-fee-waiver.what_they_offer:
- Waived application fees at participating colleges
- Valid at over 900 Common App member schools
- No limit on number of colleges
- Covers the full application fee (typically $50-90)
- Accepted at most selective colleges and universities
common-app-fee-waiver.how_to_get_it:
1. Create a Common App account
2. Complete the Profile section
3. Answer the fee waiver questions in the Profile
4. If eligible, fee waiver automatically applied
5. Can also obtain fee waiver through school counselor
6. Fee waiver travels with you to all Common App colleges

sat-fee-waivers.name: SAT Fee Waivers
sat-fee-waivers.description: The College Board offers SAT fee waivers for low-income 11th and 12th grade students, covering test fees and providing additional benefits.
sat-fee-waivers.what_they_offer:
- Two free SAT tests (with or without Essay)
- Unlimited score reports to colleges
- Waived college application fees at many participating schools
- Free CSS Profile for financial aid applications
- Waived fees for late registration, standby testing, and changes
- Access to Khan Academy Official SAT Practice (free for all)
sat-fee-waivers.how_to_get_it:
1. Must be in 11th or 12th grade
2. Must meet income eligibility guidelines (similar to free/reduced lunch)
3. Request fee waiver from your school counselor
4. Counselor provides fee waiver card/code
5. Use when registering for SAT online
6. Present at test center if requested

cal-grant.name: Cal Grant
cal-grant.description: Cal Grants are free money from the state of California to help eligible students pay for college tuition and fees at California colleges and universities.
cal-grant.what_they_offer:
- Cal Grant A: Covers systemwide tuition at UC and CSU, and part of tuition at private colleges (2025-26 maximums for new students were $14,934 at UC, $6,450 at CSU, and $9,358 at private nonprofit colleges)
- Cal Grant B: Access award for living costs ($1,648, or up to $6,000 for student parents and foster youth), plus tuition help at four-year schools
- Cal Grant C: Help with tuition, books, and supplies for career and technical training
- Amount depends on award type and the kind of school you attend
- Available for up to 4 years of full-time attendance
- No repayment required (not a loan)
cal-grant.how_to_get_it:
1. Complete the FAFSA or California Dream Act Application by the March 2 priority deadline (September 2 for community college students)
2. Make sure a verified Cal Grant GPA is on file (most high schools and colleges submit it for you)
3. Must be a California resident
4. Must attend a Cal Grant eligible California college or career school
5. Must meet income and asset ceilings
6. No separate Cal Grant application is required
cal-grant.timeframe: Annual (apply by March 2; September 2 for community college students)

fafsa-help.name: Free FAFSA Help
fafsa-help.description: Free help completing the FAFSA (Free Application for Federal Student Aid) is available through California Cash for College workshops and other programs.
fafsa-help.what_they_offer:
- Free FAFSA completion workshops and webinars
- Help with California Dream Act Application (CADAA)
- Assistance with financial aid forms and next steps
- Virtual and in-person options available
- Aimed at high school seniors and parents, but open to returning college students and juniors
- Help understanding financial aid awards
fafsa-help.how_to_get_it:
1. Find a Cash for College workshop or webinar near you
2. Bring your StudentAid.gov login (FAFSA filers), Social Security or Alien Registration Number, and tax return
3. Parents/contributors bring their StudentAid.gov login, tax return, bank balances, and untaxed income and asset info
4. Submit the FAFSA or CADAA by the March 2 state priority deadline (September 2 for community college students)
5. Questions: email cashforcollege@csac.ca.gov or call CSAC Student Support
fafsa-help.timeframe: October - March (FAFSA and CA Dream Act open October 1; March 2 priority deadline)

pell-grant.name: Federal Pell Grant
pell-grant.description: The Federal Pell Grant provides free money for college to undergraduate students with financial need. Unlike loans, Pell Grants do not need to be repaid.
pell-grant.what_they_offer:
- Up to $7,395 per year (2026-2027)
- Free money - no repayment required
- Can be used for tuition, fees, books, and living expenses
- Available at most colleges and universities
- Can be combined with other financial aid
pell-grant.how_to_get_it:
1. Complete the FAFSA at studentaid.gov
2. Must demonstrate financial need (based on your Student Aid Index)
3. Must be an undergraduate without a bachelor's degree
4. Part-time students can qualify, but receive a smaller award
5. Must be U.S. citizen or eligible noncitizen
6. Amount depends on financial need, cost of attendance, and enrollment status
7. Lifetime limit of 12 semesters (about 6 years) of Pell funding

head-start-bay-area.name: Head Start / Early Head Start
head-start-bay-area.description: Head Start provides free early childhood education, health, nutrition, and family support services to children from low-income families from birth to age 5.
head-start-bay-area.what_they_offer:
- Free preschool education for children 3-5 years
- Early Head Start for infants and toddlers (0-3)
- Health and developmental screenings
- Nutritious meals and snacks
- Parent engagement and family support services
- Disability services and inclusion support
- Full-day and part-day options available
head-start-bay-area.how_to_get_it:
1. Income must be at or below federal poverty guidelines
2. Or child is in foster care, homeless, or receiving public assistance
3. Contact local Head Start agency to apply
4. Complete application and provide income documentation
5. Children are prioritized based on need

ca-state-preschool.name: California State Preschool Program (CSPP)
ca-state-preschool.description: The California State Preschool Program provides free or low-cost preschool to income-eligible 3 and 4 year olds to prepare them for kindergarten.
ca-state-preschool.what_they_offer:
- Free preschool for eligible children (ages 3-4)
- Part-day and full-day programs available
- Developmentally appropriate curriculum
- Nutritious meals and snacks
- Parent involvement opportunities
- Transition support to kindergarten
ca-state-preschool.how_to_get_it:
1. Must meet income eligibility (based on State Median Income) or other eligibility criteria
2. Child must be 3 or 4 years old
3. Programs run by school districts, colleges, community-action agencies, and nonprofits
4. Contact your local school district or child care resource and referral agency (call 1-800-KIDS-793)
5. Complete application and income verification

adult-school-sf.name: San Francisco City College Adult Education
adult-school-sf.description: City College of San Francisco offers free adult education classes including GED preparation, ESL, citizenship, and career training.
adult-school-sf.what_they_offer:
- Free GED/HiSET and high school diploma preparation
- Free ESL (English as a Second Language) classes
- U.S. Citizenship test preparation
- Basic skills, math, reading, writing, and computer literacy
- Short-term career education certificates (business, culinary, custodial, home health aide, and more)
- Pre-apprenticeship training and programs for adults with disabilities
- Classes for parents, guardians, and foster parents
- Multiple locations throughout San Francisco
adult-school-sf.how_to_get_it:
1. Visit the CCSF Adult Education website or a CCSF center
2. Choose a program (English, high school diploma, citizenship, or job skills)
3. Take placement assessment if required
4. Register for noncredit classes
5. Most adult education classes are free of charge

alameda-adult-school.name: Oakland Adult & Career Education
alameda-adult-school.description: Oakland Adult & Career Education (OACE), part of Oakland Unified School District, provides classes for adults including GED and high school diploma preparation, ESL, and career training.
alameda-adult-school.what_they_offer:
- GED and high school diploma programs
- ESL (English as a Second Language) classes
- Free ESL for OUSD parents through the Family Literacy Program
- Healthcare training (Phlebotomy Technician, Clinical Medical Assistant, EKG Technician, Medical Billing & Coding) in partnership with CALRegional
- Classes at multiple Oakland locations
alameda-adult-school.how_to_get_it:
1. Attend a general student registration session (held before each term; Winter term registration begins in October)
2. Complete registration and assessment at the OACE testing center
3. Enroll in appropriate classes
4. Office hours Monday-Thursday, 9am-4pm; call with questions

smc-adult-education.name: San Mateo Adult & Career Education
smc-adult-education.description: San Mateo Adult & Career Education (SMACE) offers free and low-cost classes for adults including ESL, GED and high school diploma, citizenship, and career training.
smc-adult-education.what_they_offer:
- English (ESL) classes, including ESL citizenship preparation
- Self-paced GED and high school diploma classes
- Career technical education in high-demand fields (such as pharmacy technician), including EDD-approved courses
- Active adult and older adult classes (such as free AI basics workshops for adults 55+)
- Career services and job search tools
smc-adult-education.how_to_get_it:
1. Browse the course catalog on the SMACE website
2. Enroll online or visit the campus at 789 East Poplar Ave
3. Take placement test for ESL if needed
4. Enroll in classes

scusd-adult-education.name: Silicon Valley Adult Education (San Jose)
scusd-adult-education.description: Silicon Valley Adult Education, run by the Metropolitan Education District (MetroED), provides classes for adults in San Jose including ESL, high school diploma, GED/HiSET, and career technical education.
scusd-adult-education.what_they_offer:
- ESL (English) classes
- High school diploma program
- GED and HiSET preparation, plus a regional testing center
- Career and technical education courses
- College and career planning
scusd-adult-education.how_to_get_it:
1. Register online or visit the campus at 760 Hillsdale Avenue
2. Complete registration
3. Take placement assessment if required
4. Enroll in appropriate classes
5. Office hours: Monday-Thursday 8am-8:30pm, Friday 8am-4:30pm

khan-academy.name: Khan Academy
khan-academy.description: Khan Academy provides free online education with video lessons and practice exercises covering math, science, humanities, SAT prep, and more.
khan-academy.what_they_offer:
- Free video lessons on thousands of topics
- Practice exercises with instant feedback
- Personalized learning dashboard
- Test prep (including SAT practice)
- 840+ free courses in K-12 math, science, English language arts, social studies, economics, and computing
- Life skills courses
- Early college-level courses
khan-academy.how_to_get_it:
1. Visit khanacademy.org
2. Create a free account
3. Start learning at your own pace
4. Track progress on personalized dashboard
5. Available on web and mobile apps

free-library-tutoring.name: Free Library Tutoring Programs
free-library-tutoring.description: Bay Area public libraries offer free tutoring and homework help programs for students of all ages, including online tutoring services available with a library card.
free-library-tutoring.what_they_offer:
- Free one-on-one tutoring (in-person and online)
- Homework help in all subjects
- Reading and literacy support
- Math tutoring
- Test prep resources (varies by library)
- Online tutoring through Brainfuse or Tutor.com (varies by library)
free-library-tutoring.how_to_get_it:
1. Get a free library card from your local library
2. Check library website for tutoring programs
3. Many libraries offer Brainfuse HelpNow or similar online tutoring (San Francisco Public Library offers live one-on-one help from Brainfuse)
4. In-person tutoring schedules vary by location
5. Some programs require appointments

trio-upward-bound.name: TRIO Upward Bound
trio-upward-bound.description: TRIO Upward Bound helps high school students from low-income families and first-generation college students prepare for and succeed in higher education.
trio-upward-bound.what_they_offer:
- Academic tutoring and instruction
- College campus visits and exploration
- SAT/ACT preparation
- Financial aid and scholarship guidance
- Summer programs on college campuses
- Mentoring and personal counseling
- Help with college applications
trio-upward-bound.how_to_get_it:
1. Must have completed 8th grade and be ages 13-19
2. Must be low-income or potential first-generation college student
3. Programs are run by colleges and community organizations; availability varies by school
4. Contact local Upward Bound program to apply
5. Application typically includes interview and assessment

eops.name: EOPS/CARE (Extended Opportunity Programs)
eops.description: EOPS provides academic and financial support to low-income community college students, while CARE offers additional support to single parents on public assistance.
eops.what_they_offer:
- Priority registration
- Book vouchers and supplies
- Academic counseling
- Transfer assistance
- Grant aid (in addition to other financial aid)
- CARE program: extra support services for single parents receiving public assistance
- NextUp/Guardian Scholars: support for current and former foster youth
eops.how_to_get_it:
1. Must be enrolled at California Community College
2. Must meet income eligibility requirements
3. Must be educationally disadvantaged
4. Generally must enroll full-time (12 units; some exceptions apply)
5. Apply through college EOPS office
6. CARE: must be single parent receiving CalWORKs/TANF

school-meals-program.name: Free & Reduced School Meals
school-meals-program.description: Under California Universal Meals, public school districts, county offices of education, and charter schools must offer a free breakfast and lunch every school day to any TK-12 student who wants one, regardless of family income.
school-meals-program.what_they_offer:
- Free breakfast and lunch each school day for all TK-12 public school students who request a meal
- No income requirement for these two daily meals
- Nutritious meals meeting federal nutrition standards
- Available during school year
- Some districts offer summer meal programs
school-meals-program.how_to_get_it:
1. Ask for breakfast or lunch at your public or charter school - no application is needed to get the two free daily meals
2. Still complete your school's meal application or Alternative Income Form if asked
3. The form helps your school get funding and can qualify your family for other benefits, like SUN Bucks (Summer EBT)
4. Children in CalFresh, CalWORKs, foster care, or experiencing homelessness are automatically eligible for free meals
5. Private schools set their own policies - check with the school

summer-meals.name: Summer Meals for Kids
summer-meals.description: Free summer meals are available for children and teens 18 and under at schools, parks, libraries, and community sites throughout the Bay Area when school is out.
summer-meals.what_they_offer:
- Free breakfast and/or lunch
- No registration required at most open sites
- No income verification at open sites
- Available at parks, libraries, schools, community centers
- Open to children 18 and under
summer-meals.how_to_get_it:
1. Check the California Department of Education's Summer Meal Service Sites list (updated each summer)
2. Or use the CA Meals for Kids mobile app to find nearby sites
3. Check site days and meal times before you go
4. At most open sites, just show up - no paperwork required
5. Sites operate during summer vacation and other school breaks
summer-meals.timeframe: Summer months (typically June-August; site list updated each year)

ymca.name: YMCA
ymca.description: The YMCA provides community programs and facilities focused on youth development, healthy living, and social responsibility, with financial assistance available to ensure access for all.
ymca.what_they_offer:
- Sliding-scale membership rates
- Fitness facilities and classes
- Youth sports and programs
- Childcare and after-school care
- Swimming lessons and pools
- Community events and activities
ymca.how_to_get_it:
1. Find your local YMCA
2. Inquire about membership options
3. Ask about financial assistance
4. Complete membership application
5. Provide income documentation if needed
6. Receive reduced-rate membership

bacn-emergency-childcare.name: Bay Area Crisis Nursery - Emergency Childcare
bacn-emergency-childcare.description: Bay Area Crisis Nursery provides free emergency childcare for families in crisis, offering a safe, nurturing environment for young children while parents address urgent situations.
bacn-emergency-childcare.what_they_offer:
- FREE emergency childcare
- For children birth to age 6
- Up to 30 days per 6 months
- Maximum 60 days per year
- Safe, nurturing environment
- Helps families during crisis
bacn-emergency-childcare.how_to_get_it:
1. Call Bay Area Crisis Nursery
2. Explain your emergency situation
3. Complete intake process
4. Provide child's information
5. Drop off child during operating hours
6. Access ongoing support as needed

california-state-preschool.name: California State Preschool Program
california-state-preschool.description: The California State Preschool Program provides free or low-cost, high-quality preschool education to income-eligible families, preparing 3- and 4-year-olds for kindergarten success.
california-state-preschool.what_they_offer:
- Free or low-cost part-day and full-day preschool
- For children ages 3-4
- Developmentally, culturally, and linguistically appropriate curriculum
- Kindergarten readiness focus
- Parent education and referrals to health and social services
- Includes meals and snacks
california-state-preschool.how_to_get_it:
1. Check income eligibility requirements
2. Find participating preschool providers (school districts, colleges, and community agencies)
3. Complete application process
4. Provide income documentation
5. Submit required paperwork
6. Enroll child once approved

calworks-child-care.name: CalWORKs Child Care
calworks-child-care.description: CalWORKs Child Care provides free or subsidized childcare for families receiving CalWORKs benefits, helping parents participate in work or training activities through three progressive stages.
calworks-child-care.what_they_offer:
- Free or subsidized child care
- Stage 1: County-administered (current CalWORKs)
- Stage 2: Transitional (leaving CalWORKs)
- Stage 3: Long-term subsidized care
- Supports work and training
- Continuous coverage through stages
calworks-child-care.how_to_get_it:
1. Must be receiving CalWORKs benefits
2. Contact your county welfare office
3. Request child care assistance
4. Choose approved child care provider
5. Complete required paperwork
6. Transition through stages as eligible

childrens-council-sf.name: Children's Council San Francisco
childrens-council-sf.description: Children's Council San Francisco helps income-eligible families access subsidized childcare, providing partial or complete coverage of childcare costs through state-funded programs.
childrens-council-sf.what_they_offer:
- Partial or complete childcare coverage
- For children ages 0-13
- State-funded subsidy programs
- Help finding quality care
- Ongoing support and resources
- Multiple program options
childrens-council-sf.how_to_get_it:
1. Check income eligibility requirements
2. Contact Children's Council
3. Complete subsidy application
4. Provide income documentation
5. Choose approved childcare provider
6. Receive ongoing subsidy support

choices-for-children.name: Choices for Children
choices-for-children.description: Choices for Children provides subsidized childcare services to income-eligible families in Santa Clara County, helping parents work or attend school while their children receive quality care.
choices-for-children.what_they_offer:
- Subsidized child care services
- For income-eligible families
- Multiple childcare options
- Quality care for children
- Supports working parents
- Help with childcare costs
choices-for-children.how_to_get_it:
1. Check income eligibility requirements
2. Contact Choices for Children
3. Complete application process
4. Provide income documentation
5. Choose approved childcare provider
6. Receive subsidy based on funding

head-start.name: Head Start
head-start.description: Head Start is a federally-funded program providing free, comprehensive early childhood education, health, nutrition, and family support services to low-income children and families.
head-start.what_they_offer:
- Free preschool education for children ages 3-5
- Early Head Start for pregnant women, infants, and toddlers
- Comprehensive child development
- Health and nutrition services
- Family support programs
- Special needs support included
head-start.how_to_get_it:
1. Families qualify with income at or below the federal poverty guidelines
2. Families receiving TANF, SSI, or SNAP, children in foster care, and children experiencing homelessness also qualify
3. Find a local Head Start program with the HeadStart.gov Center Locator
4. Contact the program to apply and provide income and family documentation
5. For help finding a program, call 1-866-763-6481

a-greener-source.name: A Greener Source
a-greener-source.description: A Greener Source is an office furniture decommissioning company that keeps unwanted furniture out of landfills by donating it at no cost to registered nonprofits, schools, churches, and charities.
a-greener-source.what_they_offer:
- Free office desks and workstations
- Chairs (office, conference, guest)
- Filing cabinets and storage
- Conference tables
- Cubicle systems and panels
- Other office furnishings as available
- Free curbside delivery within 50 miles of the project site on the removal date
a-greener-source.how_to_get_it:
1. Register your nonprofit organization at agreenersource.com
2. Browse available furniture inventory online
3. Request items through the website (keep requesting if not approved at first)
4. Confirm approval and schedule delivery; have staff or volunteers on site to carry items inside
5. Overstock items at the Hayward warehouse can be picked up by appointment

alameda-county-property-salvage.name: Alameda County Property & Salvage Donations
alameda-county-property-salvage.description: Alameda County's General Services Agency donates surplus office furnishings from its Property & Salvage warehouse to qualified nonprofits that contract with the County to provide community services. Other nonprofits and the public can buy surplus items at low prices.
alameda-county-property-salvage.what_they_offer:
- Free in-kind donations of surplus office furniture for qualified nonprofits
- Low-cost surplus and gently used office furniture for sale ("pennies on the dollar")
- Warehouse shopping Thursdays and Fridays, 9 am-3 pm (closed 12-12:30 pm)
- Availability varies based on county surplus
alameda-county-property-salvage.how_to_get_it:
1. For free donations, your nonprofit must be in contract with Alameda County as a provider of community services
2. Call the Property & Salvage office to request a donation
3. Or visit the warehouse on Thursday or Friday to shop surplus items for sale
4. Arrange pickup of approved or purchased items

building-resources.name: Building Resources
building-resources.description: Building Resources of San Francisco is a nonprofit 501(c)(3) reuse yard that sells low-cost salvaged and donated residential, commercial, and landscaping building materials.
building-resources.what_they_offer:
- Salvaged lumber and wood products
- Doors, windows, and hardware
- Plumbing fixtures
- Kitchen and bathroom cabinets
- Tile and landscaping materials
- Reclaimed and vintage finds (stained glass, light fixtures, and more)
building-resources.how_to_get_it:
1. Visit the Building Resources yard (open 9 am-4:30 pm, 7 days a week)
2. Browse available materials in person or at shop.buildingresources.org
3. Pay low reuse prices
4. Transport materials yourself
5. Donate usable materials 9 am-3 pm

california-federal-surplus-program.name: California Federal Surplus Property Program
california-federal-surplus-program.description: The California Department of General Services' Federal Surplus Personal Property Program (FSPP) obtains federal surplus property for qualifying public agencies and nonprofit organizations ("donees") in California, for a service and handling fee instead of the full cost.
california-federal-surplus-program.what_they_offer:
- Federal surplus personal property for your organization's operations
- Items may include furniture, office equipment, vehicles, electronics, tools, and more (availability varies)
- Service and handling fee instead of purchase price (flat $100 or a percentage of original acquisition cost, e.g. 0-30% for items under $15,000)
california-federal-surplus-program.how_to_get_it:
1. Check the federal eligibility guidelines (public agencies, schools, libraries, museums, nonprofit health providers, providers serving homeless or low-income people, programs for older adults, certain veterans and service organizations, and volunteer fire departments)
2. Submit the donee eligibility application to DGS
3. Once approved, request available federal surplus property
4. Agree to use restrictions and pay the service and handling fee
5. Pick up items directly or arrange your own pickup

city-of-san-jose-surplus.name: City of San José Surplus Property Donation Program
city-of-san-jose-surplus.description: Under City Council Policy 1-20, San José's Director of Public Works can donate surplus city property with an estimated value of $1,500 or less to public agencies, volunteer fire departments, and nonprofit corporations.
city-of-san-jose-surplus.what_they_offer:
- Donated surplus city property valued at $1,500 or less
- Items are posted on the Public Works surplus property page when available
- Availability varies (the list may be empty between donations)
city-of-san-jose-surplus.how_to_get_it:
1. Must be a public or government agency, volunteer fire department, or nonprofit corporation
2. Check the Public Works surplus property page for items available for donation
3. Submit the Donation Request and Disclaimer Form by email to the Public Works contact listed on the page
4. Arrange pickup of approved donations

santa-clara-county-surplus-donations.name: Santa Clara County Surplus Property Donation Program
santa-clara-county-surplus-donations.description: The County of Santa Clara Procurement Department donates County surplus property at no cost to public agencies in the County and private nonprofits working for public benefit in the County.
santa-clara-county-surplus-donations.what_they_offer:
- County surplus goods such as office furniture, seating, and supplies (availability varies)
- Items provided free of charge
- When several organizations request the same items, recipients are chosen by random selection and quantities may be limited
santa-clara-county-surplus-donations.how_to_get_it:
1. Must be a public agency in the County, or a private nonprofit currently working for public benefit in the County
2. Write a letter on agency letterhead, signed by the approving authority, identifying your organization as a nonprofit and describing how the property will be used
3. Mail it to Director of Procurement, Procurement Department, 2310 North First Street, Suite 201, San Jose, CA 95131-1040
4. Wait for notification and arrange pickup of allocated items

santa-clara-county-library-surplus.name: Santa Clara County Library District Surplus Property Donations
santa-clara-county-library-surplus.description: The Santa Clara County Library District's Donation Program gives surplus library property at no cost to local government agencies and private nonprofits working for the public benefit in Santa Clara County.
santa-clara-county-library-surplus.what_they_offer:
- Surplus library property for your organization's business and operational needs (availability varies)
- Items provided at no cost
- When several organizations request the same items, the Library decides (possibly by random selection) and may limit quantities
santa-clara-county-library-surplus.how_to_get_it:
1. Must be a local government agency, or a private nonprofit currently working for the public benefit in Santa Clara County
2. Write a letter on agency letterhead identifying your organization as a nonprofit or public agency, describing how the property will be used, signed by the approving authority
3. Send it to the Procurement Manager, Santa Clara County Library District Services & Support Center, 1370 Dell Avenue, Campbell, CA 95008
4. Questions: SCCLDProcurement@lib.sccgov.org
5. Arrange pickup if your request is approved

sf-virtual-warehouse.name: San Francisco Virtual Warehouse
sf-virtual-warehouse.description: San Francisco's Virtual Warehouse, run by the SF Environment Department on the Rheaply platform, lets nonprofits and schools request free surplus items from City departments.
sf-virtual-warehouse.what_they_offer:
- Surplus City items such as office furniture, supplies, and equipment (availability varies)
- Online platform to view and request available items
- All items free of charge
sf-virtual-warehouse.how_to_get_it:
1. Complete the Virtual Warehouse Non-Profit Sign Up Form (have your EIN, 501(c)(3) or other tax ID document, mission statement, and staff emails ready)
2. SF Environment verifies your organization is a registered 501(c)(3) nonprofit in good standing (or school) and emails next steps within 2-3 weeks
3. Create your Rheaply account to view and request available items
4. Handle all pickup and transportation yourself

scrap-sf.name: SCRAP (Scroungers' Center for Re-usable Art Parts)
scrap-sf.description: SCRAP is a San Francisco creative reuse nonprofit whose Arts & Education Materials Depot offers ever-changing, affordable donated materials for teachers, artists, students, and makers, plus free workshops and giveaways for educators.
scrap-sf.what_they_offer:
- Fabric, yarn, and sewing notions
- Paper, scrapbooking, and school/office supplies
- Art and craft materials, beads, and frames
- Wood, metal, glass, and tile in the Materials Bay
- A free section
- Free monthly teacher workshops (with $25 of free materials) and twice-yearly free teacher giveaways
scrap-sf.how_to_get_it:
1. Visit the SCRAP Depot at 141 Industrial St. (Tuesday-Sunday, 10 am-6 pm)
2. Browse and buy low-cost materials
3. Educators can register for free teacher workshops and giveaways on Eventbrite
4. Donate materials Tuesday-Saturday (appointment needed for more than 2 boxes)

smc-surplus-property.name: San Mateo County Surplus Property Program
smc-surplus-property.description: The San Mateo County Sustainability Department's Surplus Property Program offers retired County furniture, office supplies, electronics, and more at no cost to cities, schools, and certified 501(c) nonprofits located in San Mateo County before items go to public auction.
smc-surplus-property.what_they_offer:
- Office furniture (desks, chairs, tables)
- Office supplies
- Electronics and other equipment
- Occasional "Shopping Days" to pick up items directly during large County moves
- All items free of charge for eligible organizations
smc-surplus-property.how_to_get_it:
1. Must be a city, school, or certified 501(c) nonprofit located in San Mateo County (nonprofits must email a current W-9 to SUST_Surplus@smcgov.org)
2. View listings at govdeals.com/SanMateoCounty, register for a bidder account, and subscribe to the Community Partners Tier
3. Request items for free while they are in the Community Partners Tier (or before an auction ends by emailing the item link)
4. Looking for something not listed? Submit the Reuse Request Form and the County will contact you if it becomes available
5. Your organization handles removal, packing, loading, and transportation

federal-federal-emergency-covid-19-funer.name: FEMA: Covid-19 Funeral Assistance
federal-federal-emergency-covid-19-funer.description: Financial assistance for burial and funeral costs for someone who died of COVID-19. To be eligible, you were not reimbursed for funeral or burial expenses by any organization or agency.
federal-federal-emergency-covid-19-funer.what_they_offer: Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) offers support to people during natural disasters and national emergencies, including housing and funeral assistance.
federal-federal-emergency-covid-19-funer.how_to_get_it:
Eligibility requirements:
- The deceased's death was COVID-19 related
- The deceased died in the U.S.
- The deceased died after May 20th, 2020
- The applicant is a US citizen or an eligible non-citizen

Visit the official website or call for more information.

federal-social-security-retirement-benef.name: Social Security: Retirement Benefits for Children
federal-social-security-retirement-benef.description: Replacement income for underaged children of qualified retirees and families receiving retirement benefits. You only need one application to apply for all disability benefits offered by SSA.
federal-social-security-retirement-benef.what_they_offer: Administers Social Security, as well as disability insurance, and other benefits.
federal-social-security-retirement-benef.how_to_get_it:
Eligibility requirements:
- The applicant is under 18 years
- The applicant’s marital status is unmarried
- The applicant is a US citizen or an eligible non-citizen
- The applicant is the child or spouse of a person who is receiving retirement or disability benefits

Visit the official website or call for more information.

federal-social-security-supplemental-sec.name: Social Security: Supplemental Security Income (ssi) for Children
federal-social-security-supplemental-sec.description: Monthly cash payments to meet the basic needs of children with disabilities and caretakers with limited income, savings, or other resources. You only need one application to apply for all disability benefits offered by SSA.
federal-social-security-supplemental-sec.what_they_offer: Administers Social Security, as well as disability insurance, and other benefits.
federal-social-security-supplemental-sec.how_to_get_it:
Eligibility requirements:
- The applicant is under 18 years
- The applicant is a US citizen or an eligible non-citizen
- The applicant has a disability or impairment
- The applicant is unable to work for a year or more because of a disability
- The applicant has limited income and resources

Visit the official website or call for more information.

federal-centers-for-medicare-with-disabi.name: Medicare/Medicaid: Medicare with Disabilities
federal-centers-for-medicare-with-disabi.description: A health insurance program for Americans aged 65 and older, and for people with disabilities.
federal-centers-for-medicare-with-disabi.what_they_offer: Administers Medicare, Medicaid, and the Health Insurance Exchanges.
federal-centers-for-medicare-with-disabi.how_to_get_it:
Eligibility requirements:
- The applicant is at least 65 years
- The applicant is a US citizen or an eligible non-citizen
- The applicant has a disability or impairment
- The applicant is unable to work for a year or more because of a disability

Visit the official website or call for more information.

federal-veterans-affairs-veteran-s-pensi.name: VA: Veteran's Pension with Disabilities
federal-veterans-affairs-veteran-s-pensi.description: Monthly payments to wartime veterans with specific age, disability, income, or net worth.
federal-veterans-affairs-veteran-s-pensi.what_they_offer: Provides a wide range of benefits in support of veterans, service members, and their families.
federal-veterans-affairs-veteran-s-pensi.how_to_get_it:
Eligibility requirements:
- The applicant is at least 65 years
- The applicant has a disability or impairment
- The applicant has limited income and resources
- The applicant served in the active military
- The applicant’s service status is: honorable, general or other than dishonorable discharge

Visit the official website or call for more information.

federal-veterans-affairs-veteran-readine.name: VA: Veteran Readiness And Employment (vr&e)
federal-veterans-affairs-veteran-readine.description: Employment support for service members and veterans with a disability that limits their ability to work.
federal-veterans-affairs-veteran-readine.what_they_offer: Provides a wide range of benefits in support of veterans, service members, and their families.
federal-veterans-affairs-veteran-readine.how_to_get_it:
Eligibility requirements:
- The applicant has a disability or impairment
- The applicant served in the active military
- The applicant's service status is: active-duty service member or honorable, general or other than dishonorable discharge
- The applicant’s disability was caused or made worse by their active-duty military service

Visit the official website or call for more information.

federal-department-of-combat-related-spe.name: DOD: Combat-related Special Compensation (crsc)
federal-department-of-combat-related-spe.description: Pays added benefits to retirees with at least 20 years of service and who receive VA compensation for combat-related disabilities.
federal-department-of-combat-related-spe.what_they_offer: Provides support for qualified spouses, children, and other family members of deceased service members.
federal-department-of-combat-related-spe.how_to_get_it:
Eligibility requirements:
- The applicant has a disability or impairment
- The applicant served in the active military
- The applicant’s service status is: retired from the service
- The applicant’s disability was caused or made worse by their active-duty military service

Visit the official website or call for more information.

federal-social-security-ticket-to-work-p.name: Social Security: Ticket To Work Program
federal-social-security-ticket-to-work-p.description: Career development for Social Security disability beneficiaries ages 18 to 64 years who would like to work.
federal-social-security-ticket-to-work-p.what_they_offer: Administers Social Security, as well as disability insurance, and other benefits.
federal-social-security-ticket-to-work-p.how_to_get_it:
Eligibility requirements:
- The applicant is between 18-64 years
- The applicant is a US citizen or an eligible non-citizen
- The applicant has a disability or impairment
- The applicant is unable to work for a year or more because of a disability

Visit the official website or call for more information.

federal-social-security-supplemental-sec.name: Social Security: Supplemental Security Income (ssi)
federal-social-security-supplemental-sec.description: Financial assistance to adults with disabilities, and people 65 and older without disabilities who meet specific financial limits. You only need one application to apply for all disability benefits offered by SSA.
federal-social-security-supplemental-sec.what_they_offer: Administers Social Security, as well as disability insurance, and other benefits.
federal-social-security-supplemental-sec.how_to_get_it:
Eligibility requirements:
- The applicant is a US citizen or an eligible non-citizen
- The applicant has a disability or impairment
- The applicant is unable to work for a year or more because of a disability
- The applicant has limited income and resources

Visit the official website or call for more information.

federal-internal-revenue-tax-relief-prog.how_to_get_it:
Eligibility requirements:
- The applicant has a disability or impairment

Visit the official website or call for more information.

federal-social-security-social-security-.name: Social Security: Social Security Disability Insurance for Children
federal-social-security-social-security-.description: Financial assistance to minor children whose parents receive disability benefits. You only need one application to apply for all disability benefits offered by SSA.
federal-social-security-social-security-.what_they_offer: Administers Social Security, as well as disability insurance, and other benefits.
federal-social-security-social-security-.how_to_get_it:
Eligibility requirements:
- The applicant is under 18 years
- The applicant’s marital status is unmarried
- The applicant is a US citizen or an eligible non-citizen
- The applicant is the child or spouse of a person who is receiving retirement or disability benefits

Visit the official website or call for more information.

federal-social-security-social-security-.name: Social Security: Social Security Disability Insurance for Parents
federal-social-security-social-security-.description: Financial assistance to people with disabilities and their family members. You only need one application to apply for all disability benefits offered by SSA.
federal-social-security-social-security-.what_they_offer: Administers Social Security, as well as disability insurance, and other benefits.
federal-social-security-social-security-.how_to_get_it:
Eligibility requirements:
- The applicant’s marital status is unmarried or divorced
- The applicant is a US citizen or an eligible non-citizen
- The applicant is caring for the child of someone who died, is retired, or has a disability, and the child has a disability or is under 16 years

Visit the official website or call for more information.

federal-social-security-social-security-.name: Social Security: Social Security Disability Insurance for Spouses
federal-social-security-social-security-.description: Financial assistance to people with disabilities and their family. You only need one application to apply for all disability benefits offered by SSA.
federal-social-security-social-security-.what_they_offer: Administers Social Security, as well as disability insurance, and other benefits.
federal-social-security-social-security-.how_to_get_it:
Eligibility requirements:
- The applicant is at least 62 years
- The applicant's marital status is married
- The applicant is a US citizen or an eligible non-citizen
- The applicant is the child or spouse of a person who is receiving retirement or disability benefits

Visit the official website or call for more information.

federal-social-security-retirement-benef.name: Social Security: Retirement Benefits for Spouses
federal-social-security-retirement-benef.description: A replacement income for spouses of qualified retirees. You only need one application to apply for all disability benefits offered by SSA.
federal-social-security-retirement-benef.what_they_offer: Administers Social Security, as well as disability insurance, and other benefits.
federal-social-security-retirement-benef.how_to_get_it:
Eligibility requirements:
- The applicant is at least 62 years
- The applicant’s marital status is married
- The applicant is a US citizen or an eligible non-citizen
- The applicant is the child or spouse of a person who is receiving retirement or disability benefits

Visit the official website or call for more information.

federal-social-security-retirement-benef.name: Social Security: Retirement Benefits for Children with Disabilities
federal-social-security-retirement-benef.description: A replacement income for adult children with disabilities of qualified retirees and families receiving retirement benefits. You only need one application to apply for all disability benefits offered by SSA.
federal-social-security-retirement-benef.what_they_offer: Administers Social Security, as well as disability insurance, and other benefits.
federal-social-security-retirement-benef.how_to_get_it:
Eligibility requirements:
- The applicant is under 18 years
- The applicant’s marital status is unmarried
- The applicant is a US citizen or an eligible non-citizen
- The applicant has a disability or impairment
- The applicant is unable to work for a year or more because of a disability

Visit the official website or call for more information.

federal-department-of-public-safety-offi.name: DOJ: Public Safety Officers' Disability Benefits
federal-department-of-public-safety-offi.description: A one-time benefit to public safety officers who were permanently and totally disabled as a result of an injury while in the line of duty.
federal-department-of-public-safety-offi.what_they_offer: Offers financial and educational support to help families of fallen public safety officers.
federal-department-of-public-safety-offi.how_to_get_it:
