Eligibility requirements:
- The applicant has a disability or impairment
- The applicant is unable to work for a year or more because of a disability
- You are a public safety officer who was catastrophically injured in the line of duty

Visit the official website or call for more information.

federal-centers-for-medicare-with-retire.name: Medicare/Medicaid: Medicare With Retirement
federal-centers-for-medicare-with-retire.description: A health insurance program for Americans aged 65 and older, and for people with disabilities.
federal-centers-for-medicare-with-retire.what_they_offer: Administers Medicare, Medicaid, and the Health Insurance Exchanges.
federal-centers-for-medicare-with-retire.how_to_get_it:
Eligibility requirements:
- The applicant is at least 65 years old
- The applicant is a US citizen or an eligible non-citizen

Visit the official website or call for more information.

federal-department-of-concurrent-retirem.name: DOD: Concurrent Retirement And Disability Payments (crdp)
federal-department-of-concurrent-retirem.description: Offsets military retired pay due for VA disability compensation. Eligibility is automatic. No application is needed.
federal-department-of-concurrent-retirem.what_they_offer: Provides support for qualified spouses, children, and other family members of deceased service members.
federal-department-of-concurrent-retirem.how_to_get_it:
Eligibility requirements:
- The applicant’s date of birth is 60 years or older
- The applicant has a disability or impairment
- The deceased served in the active military
- The applicant’s service status is: retired from the service or member of the National Guard or Reserves

Visit the official website or call for more information.

federal-department-of-death-gratuity.name: DOD: Death Gratuity
federal-department-of-death-gratuity.description: Tax free payment of $100,000 to eligible survivors of members of the Armed Forces who died while on active duty or while serving in certain reserve statuses.
federal-department-of-death-gratuity.what_they_offer: Provides support for qualified spouses, children, and other family members of deceased service members.
federal-department-of-death-gratuity.how_to_get_it:
Eligibility requirements:
- The deceased served in the active military
- The service status of the deceased is: active-duty service member or member of the National Guard/Reserves
- One of the following applies to the deceased: died while on active duty or Died while on inactive-duty service training
- The applicant’s relationship to the deceased is: spouse, child, parent, or other family member

Visit the official website or call for more information.

federal-veterans-affairs-disability-comp.name: VA: Disability Compensation
federal-veterans-affairs-disability-comp.description: A monthly tax-free payment to veterans who got sick or injured while serving in the military or whose service made an existing condition worse.
federal-veterans-affairs-disability-comp.what_they_offer: Provides a wide range of benefits in support of veterans, service members, and their families.
federal-veterans-affairs-disability-comp.how_to_get_it:
Eligibility requirements:
- The applicant has a disability or impairment
- The applicant served in the active military
- The applicant’s disability was caused or made worse by their active-duty military service

Visit the official website or call for more information.

federal-social-security-extra-help-with-.name: Social Security: Extra Help With Medicare Prescription Drug Plan (part D) Costs
federal-social-security-extra-help-with-.description: Helps with the cost of prescription drugs, like deductibles and copays.
federal-social-security-extra-help-with-.what_they_offer: Administers Social Security, as well as disability insurance, and other benefits.
federal-social-security-extra-help-with-.how_to_get_it:
Eligibility requirements:
- The applicant is at least 65 years old
- The applicant has a disability or impairment
- The applicant has limited income and resources

Visit the official website or call for more information.

federal-department-of-housing-improvemen.name: BIA: Housing Improvement Program
federal-department-of-housing-improvemen.description: Helps with home repair, renovation, replacement, and new housing for American Indian and Alaska Native individuals and families with no resources for standard housing.
federal-department-of-housing-improvemen.what_they_offer: The Bureau of Indian Affairs enhances the quality of life and protects and improves the trust assets of American Indians, Indian tribes, and Alaska Natives.
federal-department-of-housing-improvemen.how_to_get_it:
Eligibility requirements:
- The applicant has limited income and resources
- The applicant is a member of an American Indian Tribe or an Alaska Native

Visit the official website or call for more information.

federal-veterans-affairs-survivors-pensi.name: VA: Survivors Pension for Children
federal-veterans-affairs-survivors-pensi.description: Monthly payments to qualified unmarried dependent children of deceased wartime veterans.
federal-veterans-affairs-survivors-pensi.what_they_offer: Provides a wide range of benefits in support of veterans, service members, and their families.
federal-veterans-affairs-survivors-pensi.how_to_get_it:
Eligibility requirements:
- The deceased served in the active military
- The service status of the deceased is: honorable, general or other than dishonorable discharge
- The applicant is under 18 years
- The applicant’s marital status is unmarried
- The applicant’s relationship to the deceased is: child

Visit the official website or call for more information.

federal-social-security-survivors-benefi.name: Social Security: Survivors Benefits for Parents
federal-social-security-survivors-benefi.description: Social Security survivors benefits to parents of eligible workers.
federal-social-security-survivors-benefi.what_they_offer: Administers Social Security, as well as disability insurance, and other benefits.
federal-social-security-survivors-benefi.how_to_get_it:
Eligibility requirements:
- The deceased worked and paid Social Security taxes
- The applicant is at least 62 years
- The applicant is a US citizen or an eligible non-citizen
- The applicant’s relationship to the deceased is: parent

Visit the official website or call for more information.

federal-social-security-survivors-benefi.name: Social Security: Survivors Benefits for Spouses
federal-social-security-survivors-benefi.description: Social Security survivors benefits to surviving spouses and certain divorced spouses of eligible workers.
federal-social-security-survivors-benefi.what_they_offer: Administers Social Security, as well as disability insurance, and other benefits.
federal-social-security-survivors-benefi.how_to_get_it:
Eligibility requirements:
- The deceased worked and paid Social Security taxes
- The applicant is at least 60 years
- The applicant’s marital status is widowed or divorced
- The applicant is a US citizen or an eligible non-citizen
- The applicant’s relationship to the deceased is: spouse

Visit the official website or call for more information.

federal-library-of-braille-and-audio-mat.name: Library of Congress: Braille And Audio Materials Service
federal-library-of-braille-and-audio-mat.description: Braille and audio materials and services at no cost for people who are blind or have a visual, physical, perceptual, or reading disability.
federal-library-of-braille-and-audio-mat.what_they_offer: Provides Congress with research for the legislative process, administers the national copyright system, and manages the largest collection of books, recordings, photographs, maps and manuscripts in the world.
federal-library-of-braille-and-audio-mat.how_to_get_it:
Eligibility requirements:
- The applicant has a disability or impairment

Visit the official website or call for more information.

federal-department-of-housing-choice-vou.name: HUD: Housing Choice Voucher (section 8)
federal-department-of-housing-choice-vou.description: Learn if you are eligible for a Section 8 housing choice voucher to pay rent for private housing. Housing choice vouchers are for families with low incomes, seniors, and people with disabilities.Find your public housing agency to learn if you are eligible and apply.
federal-department-of-housing-choice-vou.what_they_offer: Administers programs that provide housing and community development assistance and ensures fair and equal housing opportunities for everyone.
federal-department-of-housing-choice-vou.how_to_get_it:
Eligibility requirements:
- The applicant has limited income and resources
- The applicant is a U.S. citizen or eligible non-citizen

Visit the official website or call for more information.

calvet-benefits-portal.name: CalVet Benefits & Services Portal
calvet-benefits-portal.description: The California Department of Veterans Affairs (CalVet) connects California veterans and their families with their earned state and federal benefits through education, advocacy, and direct services. The CalVet website helps veterans find housing, education, employment, healthcare, and financial assistance.
calvet-benefits-portal.what_they_offer:
- myCalVet profile for customized benefits and services information
- Home loans with competitive rates (CalVet Home Loans)
- College fee waivers for dependents (CalVet College Fee Waiver)
- Veterans Homes of California (8 locations statewide)
- Employment and transition services
- Help with VA claims through County Veterans Service Offices (CVSOs)
- Mental health and wellness resources
- Veteran designation on driver licenses and ID cards
calvet-benefits-portal.how_to_get_it:
1. Visit calvet.ca.gov or call CalVet toll-free
2. Create a myCalVet profile to get customized benefits information
3. Find your local County Veterans Service Office (CVSO) at 1-844-737-8838 (1-844-SERV-VET) for free in-person help with claims and applications
4. Apply for the specific programs you qualify for

calvet-dvbe.name: Disabled Veteran Business Enterprise (DVBE) Program
calvet-dvbe.description: California's Disabled Veteran Business Enterprise (DVBE) certification, administered by the Department of General Services' Office of Small Business and DVBE Services (OSDS), helps businesses owned and run by disabled veterans compete for state contracts. The state's goal is to award at least 3% of its overall annual contract dollars to certified DVBEs.
calvet-dvbe.what_they_offer:
- DVBE certification recognized by California state agencies
- Eligibility for the DVBE Participation Program (3% statewide contract goal)
- "SB/DVBE Option": state agencies can contract directly with certified DVBEs (with quotes from at least two) for goods, services, IT, and public works above $5,000, up to set limits
- Free certification workshops and outreach events
calvet-dvbe.how_to_get_it:
1. The veteran must have a service-connected disability of at least 10% and live in California
2. The business must be at least 51% owned by one or more disabled veterans (LLCs must be wholly owned) and managed day-to-day by disabled veterans
3. The home office must be located in the U.S.
4. Register your business on Cal eProcure and complete the online certification application
5. Submit requested documents, including federal tax returns for the past three years

calvet-caltap.name: California Transition Assistance Program (CalTAP)
calvet-caltap.description: CalVet's California Transition Assistance Program (CalTAP) informs and connects veterans of all eras to their earned federal and state benefits, and provides continued support as their needs change, through five pathways - Core Curriculum, Education, Employment, Entrepreneurship, and Service Providers.
calvet-caltap.what_they_offer:
- Core curriculum: Veteran 101, California benefits, and financial literacy
- Education pathway: choosing a school and using education benefits
- Employment pathway: apprenticeships, job search, and state employment
- Entrepreneurship pathway: DVBE certification and business resources
- Connections to service providers (attorneys, employers, primary care, supportive housing)
- Free virtual and in-person workshops and recorded webinars
calvet-caltap.how_to_get_it:
1. Visit the CalTAP page to find upcoming workshops or watch past webinars
2. Submit a CalTAP Request for Response to ask about benefits, County Veterans Service Offices, or pathways
3. Or email CalTAP@calvet.ca.gov
4. Community partners can request CalTAP workshops, presentations, or resource tables

calvet-vhhp.name: Veterans Housing and Homelessness Prevention (VHHP)
calvet-vhhp.description: The Veterans Housing and Homelessness Prevention program develops affordable permanent supportive housing for veterans and their families who are experiencing homelessness or have extremely low income. CalVet has awarded $580.5 million to 99 housing projects with over 5,190 units.
calvet-vhhp.what_they_offer:
- Affordable permanent housing for veterans
- Supportive services included
- Priority for homeless and at-risk veterans
- Family housing available
- Case management and support
- Connection to VA benefits
calvet-vhhp.how_to_get_it:
1. Contact your local County Veterans Service Office
2. Verify veteran status and eligibility
3. Complete housing needs assessment
4. Get referral to VHHP housing project in your area
5. Work with case manager through application process

va-vet-centers.name: VA Vet Centers
va-vet-centers.description: VA Vet Centers provide confidential community-based counseling, outreach, and referral services for eligible veterans, service members, and their families outside of traditional VA medical facilities.
va-vet-centers.what_they_offer:
- Confidential mental health counseling
- Readjustment counseling services
- PTSD and trauma support
- Employment assistance
- Family counseling
- Community outreach and referrals
va-vet-centers.how_to_get_it:
1. Locate nearest Vet Center online
2. Call or walk in during hours
3. No VA enrollment required
4. Services are confidential
5. Meet with counselor or specialist
6. Access ongoing support as needed

calvet-home-loans.name: CalVet Home Loans
calvet-home-loans.description: CalVet Home Loans provides California veterans with competitive mortgage financing to purchase homes, farms, or manufactured homes. The program often offers below-market interest rates and unique benefits not available through conventional lenders.
calvet-home-loans.what_they_offer:
- Competitive fixed interest rates
- Low or no down payment options
- Disaster protection (fire, earthquake, flood)
- Rehabilitation and home improvement loans
- Farm and manufactured home loans
- No prepayment penalties
- Sellers may assist with closing costs
calvet-home-loans.how_to_get_it:
1. Must be an eligible California veteran
2. Must purchase property in California
3. Apply online at CalVet Home Loans website
4. Get pre-qualified before house hunting
5. Complete application with CalVet-approved lender
6. Provide DD214, income verification, and credit check

calvet-property-tax-exemption.name: Disabled Veteran Property Tax Exemption
calvet-property-tax-exemption.description: California offers one of the nation's most valuable property tax exemptions for disabled veterans. The exemption can eliminate thousands in annual property taxes based on disability rating and income level.
calvet-property-tax-exemption.what_they_offer:
- Full or partial property tax exemption
- Basic exemption up to $161,083 (2024) for 100% disabled
- Low-income exemption up to $241,627 (2024) for qualifying veterans
- Applies to primary residence only
- Unmarried surviving spouses may also qualify
- Annual savings can be thousands of dollars
calvet-property-tax-exemption.how_to_get_it:
1. Must have service-connected disability from VA
2. Must be California resident
3. Property must be primary residence
4. File claim with County Assessor's Office
5. Provide VA disability rating letter and DD214
6. Renew annually with county
calvet-property-tax-exemption.timeframe: Annual (file by February 15 for full year)

ca-military-retirement-tax-exclusion.name: Military Retirement Income Tax Exclusion
ca-military-retirement-tax-exclusion.description: Starting in 2025, California veterans receiving military retirement pay can exclude up to $20,000 annually from state income taxes. Surviving spouses receiving Survivor Benefit Plan payments also qualify for this new tax break.
ca-military-retirement-tax-exclusion.what_they_offer:
- Exclude up to $20,000 military retirement pay from state taxes
- Survivor Benefit Plan payments also eligible
- Available to military retirees of all ages
- Surviving spouses qualify independently
- Reduces California state income tax liability
ca-military-retirement-tax-exclusion.how_to_get_it:
1. Must receive military retirement pay or SBP payments
2. Must file California state income tax return
3. Claim exclusion on California tax return (Form 540)
4. Follow FTB instructions for military retirement exclusion
5. Keep documentation of military retirement income

calable.name: CalABLE
calable.description: CalABLE is California's tax-advantaged savings program for people with disabilities, allowing them to save money without affecting eligibility for public benefits like SSI and Medi-Cal.
calable.what_they_offer:
- Tax-advantaged savings account (529A ABLE account)
- Save up to $18,000 per year (2024 limit)
- Account balances up to $100,000 don't affect SSI eligibility
- Funds can be used for qualified disability expenses
- Multiple investment options available
- No California state income tax on earnings
calable.how_to_get_it:
1. Must have qualifying disability that began before age 26
2. Visit calable.ca.gov to open an account
3. Complete online enrollment
4. Choose investment options
5. Start saving with as little as $25
6. Manage account online

aarp-tax-aide.name: AARP Foundation Tax-Aide
aarp-tax-aide.description: AARP Foundation Tax-Aide is the nation's largest free volunteer-run tax assistance program, providing free tax preparation with a focus on taxpayers 50 and older with low to moderate income.
aarp-tax-aide.what_they_offer:
- Free tax preparation and e-filing
- Help with federal and state returns
- Assistance with tax credits (EITC, Child Tax Credit, etc.)
- Special attention to seniors 50+
- No age requirement to use the service
- IRS-certified volunteers
aarp-tax-aide.how_to_get_it:
1. Use the AARP Tax-Aide locator to find a site near you
2. Many sites require appointments; some accept walk-ins
3. Bring all tax documents (W-2s, 1099s, ID, etc.)
4. Meet with a volunteer preparer
5. Review and sign your return
6. File electronically or by mail

alameda-county-vita.name: Alameda County Social Services Agency VITA
alameda-county-vita.description: Alameda County Social Services Agency offers free tax preparation through the IRS Volunteer Income Tax Assistance (VITA) program for low to moderate income residents.
alameda-county-vita.what_they_offer:
- Free tax preparation for low- and moderate-income residents
- Help claiming Earned Income Tax Credit (EITC)
- CalEITC (California Earned Income Tax Credit) assistance
- IRS-certified volunteer preparers
- Document drop-off/pick-up or in-person appointments
- E-filing with direct deposit (refund in as little as 7-10 business days)
alameda-county-vita.how_to_get_it:
1. Check the Alameda County Social Services website for VITA site locations and hours (North Oakland, Hayward, and East Oakland sites)
2. Book an appointment through the ACSSA VITA/EITC Appointment Portal (available January-April)
3. Gather physical copies of required documents (photo ID, Social Security cards or ITIN letters, W-2s, 1099s)
4. Attend your scheduled appointment
5. Review and sign your return

community-gatepath-vita.name: Catholic Charities of Santa Clara County Tax Ez (VITA)
community-gatepath-vita.description: Catholic Charities of Santa Clara County's Tax Ez program provides free VITA tax preparation for low-to-moderate income individuals and families, in partnership with United Way Bay Area and the IRS.
community-gatepath-vita.what_they_offer:
- Free in-person and drop-off tax preparation
- Federal and California returns e-filed for free
- Help claiming EITC, CalEITC, Child Tax Credit, and other credits
- Prior-year tax returns
- ITIN application and renewal help
- Interpreter services available
- IRS-certified volunteer preparers
community-gatepath-vita.how_to_get_it:
1. Check the Tax Ez page for current locations and hours (main site: 2625 Zanker Road, San Jose)
2. Make an appointment online or by emailing Taxez@ccscc.org
3. Gather photo ID, Social Security cards or ITIN letters, and income documents
4. Attend your appointment
community-gatepath-vita.timeframe: Seasonal; check website for current hours (limited off-season hours at the San Jose site)

csu-east-bay-vita.name: CSU East Bay VITA
csu-east-bay-vita.description: CSU East Bay's accounting students provide free virtual tax preparation through the VITA program for California taxpayers with adjusted gross income of $89,000 or less.
csu-east-bay-vita.what_they_offer:
- Free virtual tax preparation via Zoom
- Available for adjusted gross income up to $89,000
- Federal and California state tax returns
- IRS-certified student preparers supervised by faculty
- Not available for married filing separately, digital asset transactions, or other out-of-scope returns
csu-east-bay-vita.how_to_get_it:
1. Visit the CSU East Bay VITA website to check eligibility
2. Email vita@csueastbay.edu to schedule an appointment
3. Gather your tax documents (Social Security numbers/ITINs, W-2s, 1099s, 1098-T, etc.)
4. Attend your Zoom appointment
5. Review and sign your return electronically
csu-east-bay-vita.timeframe: Tax season, roughly late February to mid-April (Fridays 12-3 PM & Saturdays 9 AM-12 PM)

irs-vita-locator.name: IRS VITA Site Locator
irs-vita-locator.description: The IRS VITA (Volunteer Income Tax Assistance) program offers free tax help to people who generally make $69,000 or less, persons with disabilities, and limited English speakers.
irs-vita-locator.what_they_offer:
- Free tax preparation and e-filing
- Help with EITC, Child Tax Credit, and other credits
- Service for income generally $69,000 or less
- Assistance in multiple languages
- IRS-certified volunteers
- Available at community centers, libraries, schools
irs-vita-locator.how_to_get_it:
1. Use the IRS VITA locator tool to find a site
2. Check site requirements (appointment vs. walk-in)
3. Bring required documents (ID, Social Security cards, W-2s, 1099s)
4. Meet with a volunteer preparer
5. Review, sign, and file your return

ebaldc-vita.name: EBALDC VITA
ebaldc-vita.description: East Bay Asian Local Development Corporation (EBALDC) hosts free tax preparation each tax season through the IRS VITA program for low-income individuals and families in Oakland, paired with a savings initiative.
ebaldc-vita.what_they_offer:
- Free tax preparation
- Federal and state returns
- Help with tax credits (EITC, CalEITC)
- IRS-certified volunteer preparers
- Savings Initiative that encourages saving part of your refund
ebaldc-vita.how_to_get_it:
1. Check the EBALDC VITA page for the upcoming tax season schedule (sites are closed between seasons)
2. Email sparkpoint@ebaldc.org with questions
3. Make an appointment when sites open
4. Bring required tax documents
5. Complete your tax filing
ebaldc-vita.timeframe: Seasonal, during tax season (sites closed off-season; check website)

samaritan-house-vita.name: Samaritan House VITA
samaritan-house-vita.description: Samaritan House provides free in-person tax preparation through the IRS VITA program for San Mateo County residents at its San Mateo headquarters.
samaritan-house-vita.what_they_offer:
- Free in-person tax preparation (no virtual appointments)
- Federal and state returns
- Help with tax credits
- IRS-certified volunteers with a quality review before filing
- Copy of your filed return
samaritan-house-vita.how_to_get_it:
1. Sign up for a tax appointment online
2. Gather all required tax documents
3. Bring your documents to Samaritan House headquarters and complete an intake form
4. A preparer completes your return and a quality reviewer confirms it with you
5. Your return is filed once you approve it
samaritan-house-vita.timeframe: Tax season, early February to early April (2026 season ran February 3 – April 8)

sf-state-vita.name: SF State VITA
sf-state-vita.description: San Francisco State University's VITA program provides free in-person tax preparation for eligible low-to-moderate income taxpayers, students, older adults, people with disabilities, and limited English speakers.
sf-state-vita.what_they_offer:
- Free in-person tax preparation (AGI limit $69,000)
- DIY Facilitated Self Assistance option (AGI limit $89,000; bring your own laptop)
- Federal and California state returns
- IRS-certified student volunteers with faculty oversight
- Service for students and community members, including F-1/J-1 international students
sf-state-vita.how_to_get_it:
1. Book an appointment online at calendly.com/sfsuvita (appointments required; limited walk-ins early in the season)
2. Gather hard copies of required tax documents, photo ID, and Social Security/ITIN documents
3. Go to SFSU Creative Arts Building #134 (weekdays) or the SF VA Medical Center auditorium (select Saturdays)
4. Work with a volunteer preparer
5. Review, sign, and file your return
sf-state-vita.timeframe: Tax season, late January to April 15 (2026 season ran January 29 – April 15)

sparkpoint-fremont-vita.name: SparkPoint Fremont VITA
sparkpoint-fremont-vita.description: SparkPoint Fremont at the Fremont Family Resource Center offers free tax preparation for current year and back taxes for low to moderate income families.
sparkpoint-fremont-vita.what_they_offer:
- Free current year tax preparation (February-April)
- Free back tax preparation (year-round)
- Federal and state returns
- Help with tax credits
- IRS-certified preparers
sparkpoint-fremont-vita.how_to_get_it:
1. For current year taxes, book an in-person appointment online (call 510-298-1796 for scheduling help)
2. For back taxes, call 510-574-2026 to request an appointment
3. Gather required tax documents using the checklist on the City of Fremont website
4. Attend your appointment at the Fremont Family Resource Center
5. Review and sign your return
sparkpoint-fremont-vita.timeframe: February-April for current year; year-round for back taxes

united-way-bay-area-taxes.name: United Way Bay Area
united-way-bay-area-taxes.description: United Way Bay Area's Free Tax Help coalition partners with local organizations and the IRS to provide free, high-quality tax preparation for households earning under $89,000 across the Bay Area.
united-way-bay-area-taxes.what_they_offer:
- Free in-person tax preparation at sites across the Bay Area
- Free online self-preparation through TaxSlayer, with optional Zoom help
- Remote preparation by an online tax team through GetYourRefund
- Help with Federal EITC, CalEITC, Child Tax Credit, and Young Child Tax Credit
- Free ITIN assistance through VITA
- IRS-certified volunteers
united-way-bay-area-taxes.how_to_get_it:
1. Visit the United Way Bay Area Free Tax Help page
2. Choose in-person help, remote assistance, or free self-preparation
3. For in-person help, use the map to find a site and check its days and hours
4. Gather required documents
5. Get your taxes filed for free
united-way-bay-area-taxes.timeframe: Tax season (January-April); federal and state deadline is April 15

baec-entrepreneur-center.name: Bay Area Entrepreneur Center
baec-entrepreneur-center.description: The Bay Area Entrepreneur Center (BAEC) of Skyline College is a business accelerator and resource center in downtown San Bruno that helps students and community entrepreneurs turn skills and passions into businesses.
baec-entrepreneur-center.what_they_offer:
- Consultations and individual coaching to start or grow a business
- Workshops and easy-to-use business tools and guides
- Guidance on basic business licenses and permits
- Maker and beauty/barbering business programs
- Pop-up market opportunities (free booths for Skyline students)
- Student fellowship program supporting local businesses and nonprofits
baec-entrepreneur-center.how_to_get_it:
1. Visit the Bay Area Entrepreneur Center website
2. Choose a program that fits your business
3. Sign up for a consultation
4. Attend workshops and coaching sessions
5. Access ongoing support as your business grows

sf-score.name: SCORE San Francisco & East Bay
sf-score.description: SCORE is a nonprofit network of volunteer business mentors affiliated with the SBA. The San Francisco & East Bay chapter offers free, confidential mentoring plus webinars and workshops for small business owners in San Francisco, the East Bay, and Marin.
sf-score.what_they_offer:
- Free one-on-one business mentoring
- Mentors are experienced business leaders
- Webinars, workshops, and courses on business topics
- Online resources and templates
- Guidance on starting, growing, or scaling a business
- Meet by email, video, phone, or online chat
sf-score.how_to_get_it:
1. Visit the SCORE San Francisco & East Bay page on score.org
2. Browse local mentor profiles and areas of expertise
3. Request a free mentoring session online
4. Meet with your mentor (in-person or virtual)
5. Continue meeting as needed—mentoring is always free

san-mateo-sbdc.name: San Mateo Small Business Development Center
san-mateo-sbdc.description: The San Mateo SBDC, part of the Northern California Small Business Development Center network, provides no-cost, confidential business advising and training to help small businesses start, grow, and succeed in San Mateo County.
san-mateo-sbdc.what_they_offer:
- No-cost one-on-one business advising
- Help with business planning and strategy
- Access to capital and help with loan applications
- Guidance on human resources, compliance, marketing, and accounting
- Workshops and free on-demand webinars
san-mateo-sbdc.how_to_get_it:
1. Visit the San Mateo SBDC website or call the center
2. Sign up for SBDC advising
3. Complete intake form describing your business needs
4. Get matched with an advisor
5. Meet for ongoing support as needed

nova-workforce.name: NOVAworks Workforce Development
nova-workforce.description: NOVAworks is the workforce development board for San Mateo County and seven northwest Santa Clara County cities (Cupertino, Los Altos, Milpitas, Mountain View, Palo Alto, Santa Clara, and Sunnyvale), offering career services for job seekers and no-cost services for businesses.
nova-workforce.what_they_offer:
- Personalized career advising and coaching
- Skills training and financial aid for training
- Job search resources
- Paid internship and career exploration opportunities for young adults
- Recruitment, outplacement, HR consulting, and employee training for businesses at no cost
nova-workforce.how_to_get_it:
1. Visit the NOVAworks website or call 408-730-7232
2. Contact NOVAworks to get started with services
3. Meet with a career advisor
4. Access training and job search services
5. Get connected to employment opportunities

ibank-small-business.name: Small Business Finance Center (IBank)
ibank-small-business.description: California's IBank Small Business Finance Center offers loan guarantee programs that encourage lenders to provide capital to small businesses (1-750 employees) that face barriers to financing.
ibank-small-business.what_they_offer:
- Small Business Loan Guarantee Program (start-up costs, working capital, expansion, lines of credit, and more)
- Disaster Relief Loan Guarantee Program
- Jump Start microloans for small businesses in low-wealth communities
- Farm Loan Program
- Citizenship or immigration status not considered for loan guarantee eligibility
- Focus on job creation in low- to moderate-income communities
ibank-small-business.how_to_get_it:
1. Visit the IBank website to learn about programs
2. Determine which program fits your needs
3. Contact one of IBank's seven partner Financial Development Corporations (FDCs) or a participating lender
4. Submit your loan application through the lender (credit decisions follow lender criteria)
5. The FDC processes the IBank guarantee for qualifying businesses

calfile.name: CalFile – Free State Tax Filing
calfile.description: CalFile is California's free online tax filing service from the Franchise Tax Board, allowing eligible residents to file their state income tax returns at no cost directly with the state.
calfile.what_they_offer:
- Free California state tax return filing
- File current year plus two prior years (currently tax years 2023, 2024, and 2025)
- Direct deposit refunds
- Instant confirmation of filing
- Secure, official FTB system; FTB does the math
- Takes about 15 to 30 minutes for most filers
calfile.how_to_get_it:
1. Create a MyFTB account at ftb.ca.gov (you must have filed a California return in 1 of the last 5 years)
2. Check the CalFile qualifications for the tax year you are filing
3. Gather W-2s, 1099s, and other tax documents
4. Log in and complete your return online
5. Review and submit electronically
6. Receive refund via direct deposit or check
calfile.timeframe: Opens each January; file by April 15 (automatic extension to file until October 15; payment still due April 15)

caleitc.name: CalEITC – California Earned Income Tax Credit
caleitc.description: The California Earned Income Tax Credit (CalEITC) provides cash back to low-income working Californians. Combined with the federal EITC, families can receive thousands of dollars in tax refunds even if they owe no taxes.
caleitc.what_they_offer:
- Cash back tax credit up to $3,756 for tax year 2025 (varies by income and number of children)
- Refundable credit – get money even if you owe no taxes
- Young Child Tax Credit adds up to $1,189 for children under 6
- Foster Youth Tax Credit up to $1,189 for eligible former foster youth
- Can be combined with federal EITC for larger refund
- Available to ITIN filers
- Must be at least 18 or have a qualifying child
caleitc.how_to_get_it:
1. Earned income must be between $1 and $32,900 (tax year 2025)
2. File California state tax return (Form 540)
3. Complete form FTB 3514 (California Earned Income Tax Credit)
4. Claim Young Child Tax Credit if you have children under 6
5. Use free tax prep services (VITA) or CalFile for help filing
6. File by April 15; you can generally claim CalEITC for up to four prior years by filing or amending
caleitc.timeframe: File by April 15 annually (prior-year claims allowed for up to four years)

alameda-food-bank.name: Alameda County Community Food Bank
alameda-food-bank.description: The Alameda County Community Food Bank is one of the largest food banks in the nation, distributing millions of pounds of food annually through a network of partner agencies and direct distribution programs.
alameda-food-bank.what_they_offer:
- Free groceries and hot meals through 350+ partner food pantries, hot-meal programs, and senior centers
- Emergency Food Helpline that connects callers to food the same day, in multiple languages
- Fresh fruit, vegetables, milk, eggs, bread, and staples
- Free summer meals for children under 18
- CalFresh (food stamps) application assistance
alameda-food-bank.how_to_get_it: Call the Emergency Food Helpline at 510-635-3663 (Monday-Friday, 9 a.m.-4 p.m.) or visit FoodNow.net to find a food pantry or hot meal near you. If you leave a message, staff will call back the same day. Each partner site sets its own hours and guidelines.

alameda-meals-on-wheels.name: Alameda Meals on Wheels
alameda-meals-on-wheels.description: Alameda Meals on Wheels is a locally funded nonprofit that delivers a hot midday meal every day to homebound Alameda residents of all ages, including people recovering from surgery or hospitalization and those who can't shop or cook for themselves.
alameda-meals-on-wheels.what_they_offer:
- Hot midday meal delivered 7 days a week, including holidays
- Serves City of Alameda residents of all ages who need help
- Sliding fee scale based on ability to pay
- Daily personal contact from volunteer drivers
- Alameda Friendly Visitors program for weekly companionship visits
alameda-meals-on-wheels.how_to_get_it: Call 510-865-6131 during office hours (9 a.m.-12 noon weekdays) to ask about starting meal delivery. Service is for Alameda residents who are homebound or unable to shop or cook, such as after surgery or hospitalization.

bernal-heights-brown-bag.name: Bernal Heights Neighborhood Center - Food Pantries & Senior Food Boxes
bernal-heights-brown-bag.description: Bernal Heights Neighborhood Center runs weekly free food pantries with the SF-Marin Food Bank and a monthly senior food box program at its Cortland Avenue and Excelsior senior centers.
bernal-heights-brown-bag.what_they_offer:
- Four weekly food pantries in partnership with SF-Marin Food Bank (one visit per week, no cost)
- Fresh fruits, vegetables, grains, protein, and pantry items
- Monthly food box for qualifying seniors 60+ (federal Commodity Supplemental Food Program)
- Senior program services for adults 60+ and adults with disabilities, in English, Spanish, Mandarin, and Cantonese
bernal-heights-brown-bag.how_to_get_it: Call the senior program at (415) 289-9346 to learn about pantry days and times and whether you qualify for the monthly senior food box. Sites are at 515 Cortland Avenue and 4468 Mission Street.

calfresh-online.name: CalFresh Online
calfresh-online.description: Through the EBT Online Purchasing Pilot, CalFresh (California's SNAP/food stamps program) households and SUN Bucks families can buy groceries online from approved retailers, making food access more convenient for those with transportation or mobility challenges.
calfresh-online.what_they_offer:
- Online grocery ordering with EBT food benefits
- Available only at USDA-approved online retailers (such as Amazon and Walmart)
- Same eligible food items as in-store
- Returns with a receipt are refunded to your EBT card
- Food benefits can't pay delivery fees, and cash benefits can't be used online
calfresh-online.how_to_get_it: If you have a CalFresh EBT card, check the USDA "Stores that accept SNAP online" list (linked from the CDSS page) and choose California. Create an account with an approved retailer, add your EBT card, and shop for eligible groceries.

calfresh-rmp.name: CalFresh Restaurant Meals Program (RMP)
calfresh-rmp.description: The CalFresh Restaurant Meals Program allows eligible CalFresh recipients (older adults, people with disabilities, people experiencing homelessness, and their spouses) to use their EBT food benefits for prepared meals at approved participating restaurants.
calfresh-rmp.what_they_offer:
- Use CalFresh EBT food benefits to buy prepared meals
- Hot, ready-to-eat meals at approved participating restaurants
- Statewide program; use benefits at any participating restaurant, even outside your county
- Online map and county lists of participating restaurants
calfresh-rmp.how_to_get_it: All members of your CalFresh household must be 60 or older, have a disability, be experiencing homelessness, or be the spouse of someone who qualifies. Use the CDSS map or county list to find participating restaurants and look for the CalFresh RMP sign in the window. For questions, call the CalFresh Information Line at 1-877-847-3663 or contact your county social services office.

food-bank-contra-costa-solano.name: Food Bank of Contra Costa & Solano
food-bank-contra-costa-solano.description: The Food Bank of Contra Costa and Solano serves two counties with free food distribution, helping fight hunger through 245+ partner nonprofits and direct community programs.
food-bank-contra-costa-solano.what_they_offer:
- Free groceries at partner food pantries (each pantry sets its own eligibility and pick-up rules)
- Mobile pantry distributions with produce, proteins, dairy, and nonperishables
- Community Produce Program (up to 15 pounds of fresh produce twice a month)
- Senior food program for low-income seniors 55+ (twice a month)
- College and school pantries and weekend meals for kids
- CalFresh enrollment assistance
food-bank-contra-costa-solano.how_to_get_it: Use the online Find Food map or city list to locate a distribution site near you, or call 855-309-FOOD (3663). Bring two bags with handles. Call partner pantries to confirm hours; some require proof of address.

j-sei-meals-on-wheels.name: J-Sei Meals on Wheels
j-sei-meals-on-wheels.description: J-Sei, a Japanese American community center in Emeryville, delivers hot Japanese-style lunches to seniors in parts of Alameda and Contra Costa counties, designed with a registered dietitian to meet seniors' nutritional needs.
j-sei-meals-on-wheels.what_they_offer:
- Hot Japanese-style lunches delivered to your home
- Meals designed with a registered dietitian (low-sugar, low-sodium, heart-conscious)
- Voluntary contribution of $5/meal for seniors 60+
- Monthly pantry grocery delivery for enrolled home-delivered meal clients
- Thursday congregate lunch at J-Sei in Emeryville (reserve 2 days ahead)
j-sei-meals-on-wheels.how_to_get_it: Call Sianne Susbilla, Nutrition Services Manager, at 510-654-4000 ext. 105 or email sianne@j-sei.org. You must be 60+, have some difficulty shopping, cooking, or leaving home, live within the delivery area, and complete a home visit and assessment.

market-match.name: Market Match
market-match.description: Market Match is California's healthy food incentive program that matches CalFresh benefits dollar-for-dollar at participating farmers markets and other farm-direct sites, making fresh, locally grown fruits and vegetables more affordable.
market-match.what_they_offer:
- Dollar-for-dollar match of CalFresh EBT spending (most markets match up to $15; some match more)
- Match funds for fresh fruits, vegetables, fresh-cut herbs, and edible plant starts
- Available at 270+ sites statewide, including farmers markets, farm stands, CSAs, and mobile markets
- At farm stands and other farm-direct outlets, usually offered as a 50% discount
market-match.how_to_get_it: Use the Farmers' Market Finder to find a participating site. At a farmers market, go to the information booth, have staff swipe your CalFresh EBT card for the amount you choose, and receive tokens or vouchers plus matching Market Match to spend on produce. Check with your market for its match limit.

mow-contra-costa.name: Meals on Wheels Contra Costa
mow-contra-costa.description: Meals on Wheels Contra Costa is a Martinez-based nonprofit that funds home-delivered meals for homebound seniors across Contra Costa County and connects seniors with the three local partners that deliver the meals.
mow-contra-costa.what_they_offer:
- Help connecting to a local meal delivery provider
- Meals delivered by partners - Meals on Wheels Diablo Region (county-wide, 925-937-8607), J-Sei (Japanese cuisine; Concord, Pleasant Hill, Walnut Creek, El Cerrito, Richmond, Kensington; 510-654-4000 ext. 105), and Meals on Wheels West Contra Costa (Richmond, San Pablo, Pinole, Hercules, and nearby; 510-412-0166)
- Funding that helps shorten waitlists for homebound seniors
mow-contra-costa.how_to_get_it: You must be 60 or older and homebound, unable to buy or prepare nutritious meals, with no one else to do so for you. To sign up, call the delivery partner that serves your area, or contact Meals on Wheels Contra Costa at (866) 669-6697 or info@mowcontracosta.org for help getting connected.

mow-diablo-region.name: Meals on Wheels Diablo Region
mow-diablo-region.description: Meals on Wheels Diablo Region serves all of Contra Costa County (West, Central, and East), delivering meals with safety checks to homebound seniors and offering grocery delivery, senior lunch cafés, and friendly visitor programs.
mow-diablo-region.what_they_offer:
- Home-delivered meals with a safety check from the driver
- Grocery Bag Program - groceries and fresh produce delivered twice a month to low-income homebound seniors 55+ (with Food Bank of Contra Costa and Solano)
- Senior Cafés - free or low-cost lunches at senior centers in Bay Point, Brentwood, Concord, Pittsburg, Rodeo, and more (reservations required)
- Friendly Visitors and other supportive programs
- Voluntary contributions accepted for meals
mow-diablo-region.how_to_get_it: Home-delivered meals are for seniors 60+ who are homebound, unable to drive to get food, and don't have a caregiver who prepares their meals. Call 925-937-8311, email info@mowdr.org, or fill out the online Meals Inquiry Form. For the Grocery Bag Program, call 925-448-3694.

mow-san-francisco.name: Meals on Wheels San Francisco
mow-san-francisco.description: Meals on Wheels San Francisco delivers nutritious meals, safety checks, and social work services to seniors 60+ in San Francisco and northern San Mateo County, helping them stay independent at home.
mow-san-francisco.what_they_offer:
- One meal a day, 7 days a week (including holidays) in San Francisco; weekdays in northern San Mateo County
- Hot or frozen meal plans based on your needs
- Diabetic, low-sodium, and mechanically softened options
- Safety check with each delivery; drivers can bring meals inside
- Home-delivered groceries with the SF-Marin Food Bank for seniors who can cook
- Nutrition and social work services
mow-san-francisco.how_to_get_it: You must be 60 or older and live in San Francisco or northern San Mateo County; being homebound, unable to shop or cook, or having recent health problems also factor in. San Francisco residents apply through the Department of Disability and Aging Services intake line at 415-355-6700 (Monday-Friday, 8 a.m.-5 p.m.). Northern San Mateo County residents call MOWSF intake at 415-920-1111. Note - the waitlist has been closed due to funding; call to check current status.
mow-san-francisco.timeframe: Ongoing (waitlist currently closed due to funding)

mow-san-mateo.name: Meals on Wheels San Mateo County (Peninsula Volunteers)
mow-san-mateo.description: Peninsula Volunteers (PVI) operates Meals on Wheels in San Mateo and Santa Clara counties, delivering over 3,000 healthy meals a week to primarily homebound seniors and disabled people who are unable to cook and shop for themselves.
mow-san-mateo.what_they_offer:
- Weekday meal delivery, plus some holiday and weekend meals for eligible clients
- Subsidized meals for eligible seniors 60+ (based on circumstance, not income)
- Private-pay meal delivery for anyone, with no age or disability requirement
- Safety check with each delivery
- Nutrition counseling from a registered dietitian and in-home assessments
- Referrals to other community resources
mow-san-mateo.how_to_get_it: Call 650-323-2022 or fill out the online form to apply. Subsidized meals are for adults 60+ who are homebound, unable to reliably shop or cook due to a health condition, or recovering from a hospital stay. An in-home assessment is required at the start of service. There may be a waiting list depending on where you live.

project-open-hand.name: Project Open Hand
project-open-hand.description: Project Open Hand provides medically tailored meals and groceries to people living with serious illnesses in San Francisco and Alameda County, plus community lunches for older adults and adults with disabilities in San Francisco.
project-open-hand.what_they_offer:
- Wellness Program - medically tailored meals and groceries for pick-up, with home delivery for homebound clients
- Nutrition counseling from registered dietitians
- Community Nutrition Program - breakfast and lunch at sites across San Francisco for adults 60+ and adults 18-59 with disabilities
- Home-delivered meals for adults with disabilities in San Francisco
- CalAIM Community Supports meals for eligible Medi-Cal members (SF Health Plan, Anthem Blue Cross, Alameda Alliance for Health, Contra Costa Health Plan)
- Two grocery centers
project-open-hand.how_to_get_it: For the Wellness Program, a licensed medical provider (RN, NP, MD, DO, RD, LCSW, or PA) must complete and sign an application. Eligible diagnoses in San Francisco include HIV/AIDS, COPD, congestive heart failure, coronary artery disease, type 2 diabetes (HbA1c 7%+), end stage renal disease, and recent major surgery; in Alameda County, HIV/AIDS and recent major surgery. CalAIM referrals go through your Medi-Cal health plan. Any San Francisco resident 60+ or 18-59 with a disability can join community meal sites. Call 415-447-2300 (SF) or 510-622-0221 (Oakland).

rainbow-grocery.name: Rainbow Grocery
rainbow-grocery.description: Rainbow Grocery is a worker-owned cooperative grocery store in San Francisco's Mission District offering natural, organic, and vegetarian foods, with a 10% discount for seniors and volume discounts.
rainbow-grocery.what_they_offer:
- 10% off everything for seniors 60+ with ID
- Volume discounts (10% off $100+, 15% off $200+, 20% off $400+ per department) and case discounts
- 5 cents off for each reused container in Bulk, Bakery, or Produce
- Natural, organic, local, and vegetarian foods
- Bulk foods to save money
- Planned 10% Community Discount pilot for CalFresh/EBT, WIC, SSI, CalWORKs, and other program participants (not yet launched; ask the store)
rainbow-grocery.how_to_get_it: Tell the cashier at the start of your transaction that you plan to use a discount and show ID for the senior discount. Discounts are in-store only and not available through delivery services. Open 9 a.m. to 9 p.m. daily except holidays.

second-harvest-silicon-valley.name: Second Harvest of Silicon Valley
second-harvest-silicon-valley.description: Second Harvest of Silicon Valley is the food bank serving all of Santa Clara and San Mateo counties, where 1 in 6 people turn to it each month for nutritious food.
second-harvest-silicon-valley.what_they_offer:
- Free fresh groceries and ready-to-eat meals at sites across Santa Clara and San Mateo counties
- Online Food Locator to find sites by day and time
- Food Connection team to help you find food, in English, Spanish, Vietnamese, Chinese, and Tagalog
- CalFresh enrollment assistance
- Referrals to Meals on Wheels, senior meal programs, and WIC
second-harvest-silicon-valley.how_to_get_it: Use the online Food Locator to choose fresh groceries or ready-to-eat meals and find days and times that fit your schedule, or call the Food Connection team at 1-800-984-3663. You can also request a call back in your preferred language.

sf-marin-food-bank.name: SF-Marin Food Bank
sf-marin-food-bank.description: The San Francisco-Marin Food Bank works to end hunger in San Francisco and Marin, distributing free groceries (more than 70% fresh produce) through 205 food pantries and partnerships with 265 community organizations.
sf-marin-food-bank.what_they_offer:
- Free weekly groceries at 205 food pantries in a farmers market-style setting
- Home-delivered groceries for low-income seniors, adults with disabilities, and some pregnant people and parents of infants or children with disabilities
- Monthly USDA food box for low-income seniors 60+ (Supplemental Food Program)
- One-time emergency food
- CalFresh application and renewal help
- Serves residents regardless of immigration status
sf-marin-food-bank.how_to_get_it: Use the online Food Locator to find weekly groceries, senior food boxes, or emergency food near you. For home-delivered groceries or CalFresh help, call 415-824-3663 (hdg@sfmfoodbank.org for grocery delivery).

sos-meals-on-wheels.name: SOS Meals on Wheels
sos-meals-on-wheels.description: SOS Meals on Wheels delivers nutritious meals to about 3,000 older adults in Oakland, Hayward, San Leandro, Castro Valley, San Lorenzo, Fremont, Newark, and Union City, along with wellness checks and friendly visits. It has served Alameda County for 60 years.
sos-meals-on-wheels.what_they_offer:
- Nutritionally balanced meals delivered Monday-Friday
- Wellness checks and friendly visits from trained drivers
- Referrals to other services that help seniors stay at home
- Suggested donation of $4 per meal, but no senior is turned away
sos-meals-on-wheels.how_to_get_it: Call 510-582-1263 (ext. 118 for Oakland, San Leandro, Hayward, Castro Valley, San Lorenzo; ext. 156 for Fremont, Newark, Union City) or fill out the Client Interest Form online. You must be 60+, unable to shop for or prepare meals, and without a reliable caregiver. Intake screening is done by phone.

sourcewise-meals-on-wheels.name: Sourcewise Meals on Wheels
sourcewise-meals-on-wheels.description: Sourcewise provides Meals on Wheels throughout Santa Clara County, delivering a weekly box of frozen meals and extras to homebound seniors who can't shop or cook for themselves.
sourcewise-meals-on-wheels.what_they_offer:
- 5 frozen meals delivered once a week, plus bread, fruit, milk, juice, and breakfast items
- Meals meet 2/3 of daily nutritional needs for seniors and are low in sodium and sugar
- Microwave loaned if you don't have one
- Fixed menu (special diets can't be accommodated)
- Suggested contribution of $3/day ($90/month), but no one is denied meals
sourcewise-meals-on-wheels.how_to_get_it: Call Sourcewise at 408-350-3200, option 1 (Mon-Fri 8am-5pm) or fill out the online interest form. You must be 60+, live in Santa Clara County, and be homebound and unable to shop or cook due to illness or disability. Intake is done by phone, and meals can start in about 5-7 days.

spectrum-mow.name: Spectrum Community Services Meals on Wheels
spectrum-mow.description: Spectrum Community Services delivers Meals on Wheels to homebound seniors in the Tri-Valley (Pleasanton, Livermore, Dublin, and Sunol), helping older adults stay safe, nourished, and independent at home.
spectrum-mow.what_they_offer:
- Hot meals delivered Monday-Friday
- Frozen meals can be pre-ordered for weekends and holidays
- Heart-healthy, diabetic-friendly menus with dietitian oversight
- Friendly wellness check with each delivery
- Suggested contribution of $5 per meal, but no senior is refused
spectrum-mow.how_to_get_it: You must be 60+, homebound, and unable to prepare your own meals. For Livermore, call 510-881-0304. For Dublin, Pleasanton, and Sunol, call 510-881-0305.

st-anthonys-dining.name: St. Anthony's Dining Room
st-anthonys-dining.description: St. Anthony's Dining Room has served San Francisco's Tenderloin neighborhood since 1950, providing free hot meals daily with dignity and respect to all who are hungry, no questions asked.
st-anthonys-dining.what_they_offer:
- Free hot meals served 7 days a week
- Breakfast from 7am (dine-in or to go)
- Lunch 10am-1:30pm (dine-in)
- Afternoon hot meal to go at 2pm, Monday-Friday
- Weekly grocery "Farmers Market" for low-income Tenderloin residents and seniors
- No ID, referral, or questions asked
- Connections to other St. Anthony's services
st-anthonys-dining.how_to_get_it: Simply show up during meal service hours at 121 Golden Gate Avenue, 1st Floor. No paperwork, ID, or appointment needed. All are welcome.

universal-school-meals.name: Universal School Meals
universal-school-meals.description: California became the first state to offer universal free school meals to all public school students regardless of family income, ensuring every child has access to nutritious breakfast and lunch.
universal-school-meals.what_they_offer:
- Free breakfast for all TK-12 students
- Free lunch for all TK-12 students
- Available at all California public schools
- No income verification or application required
- Nutritious, balanced meals meeting USDA standards
- Available every school day
universal-school-meals.how_to_get_it: Your child automatically qualifies. Simply have them request meals at school. No forms or applications needed. Contact your school's food services if you have questions about meal times or menus.

wic-program.name: WIC – Women, Infants & Children
wic-program.description: WIC is California's nutrition program for pregnant and postpartum women, infants, and children under 5, providing healthy food, nutrition education, breastfeeding support, and healthcare referrals.
wic-program.what_they_offer:
- Monthly benefits for healthy foods (fruits, vegetables, whole grains, milk, eggs)
- Infant formula and baby food
- WIC card accepted at most grocery stores
- Nutrition counseling
- Breastfeeding support from trained experts
- Use your WIC Card at select farmers' markets
- Referrals to healthcare and social services
wic-program.how_to_get_it: Use the online eligibility check, then find and call your local WIC office for an appointment. You may qualify if you live in California, are pregnant, breastfeeding, or had a baby in the last 6 months, or care for a child under 5, and have income up to 185% of the poverty level (about $29,526/year for 1 person through June 2027). If you get Medi-Cal, CalFresh, or CalWORKs, you meet the income rule. Statewide help line 1-800-852-5770 (Mon-Fri 8am-5pm).

ymca-food-pantries.name: YMCA Food Pantries
ymca-food-pantries.description: The YMCA of Greater San Francisco runs weekly food pantries in San Francisco, San Mateo, and Marin counties, providing free groceries and essentials to seniors, families, and anyone struggling to make ends meet.
ymca-food-pantries.what_they_offer:
- Free groceries and essentials each week
- Serves 6,900+ people weekly across its pantry sites
- Sites include Chinatown, Mission, Richmond District, Bayview Hunters Point, Urban Services YMCA, and South San Francisco
- Food provided in partnership with SF-Marin Food Bank and Second Harvest
ymca-food-pantries.how_to_get_it: Check the website for pantry locations, days, and times. Some sites require registration first, and some are walk-in only. Contact your local YMCA branch to confirm before you go.

ecumenical-hunger-program.name: Ecumenical Hunger Program
ecumenical-hunger-program.description: The Ecumenical Hunger Program (EHP) has served East Palo Alto and surrounding communities for 50 years with food boxes, hot lunches, fresh produce, clothing, and other basic necessities.
ecumenical-hunger-program.what_they_offer:
- Nutritionally balanced emergency food boxes, Monday-Thursday
- Food bags for people without a way to cook or store food
- Fresh produce (Second Harvest delivery every Tuesday, plus EHP's garden)
- Hot lunch Monday-Thursday after 11am
- Pack the Bag snacks and light meals for children
- Back-to-school and holiday help for families
- Clothing and household items
ecumenical-hunger-program.how_to_get_it: Visit EHP at 2411 Pulgas Avenue, East Palo Alto. Food box pickup is Monday-Thursday, 9am-12pm and 2pm-5pm (closed Friday-Sunday; holiday schedule in November and December). Call 650-323-7781 with questions.

jfcs-food-pantry.name: JFCS Food Pantry
jfcs-food-pantry.description: Jewish Family and Children's Services (JFCS) runs food banks offering nutritious, high-protein food to seniors on fixed incomes, adults with disabilities, low-income young families, and others facing a temporary crisis.
jfcs-food-pantry.what_they_offer:
- Nutritious, high-protein food
- For seniors on fixed incomes and adults with disabilities
- For low-income young families and people facing a temporary crisis
- Food banks at JFCS offices in San Francisco, Marin, San Mateo, and Palo Alto
- Volunteer grocery delivery to some clients' homes
jfcs-food-pantry.how_to_get_it: Call JFCS at 415-449-3700 to ask about eligibility and how to get food from your nearest JFCS Food Bank.

pvi-got-groceries.name: Got Groceries Program
pvi-got-groceries.description: Peninsula Volunteers' Got Groceries program provides weekly bags of free groceries to individuals and families facing food insecurity, feeding about 150 families each week.
pvi-got-groceries.what_they_offer:
- Full bag of groceries weekly
- Fruits, vegetables, fresh perishables, proteins, and breads
- Available to individuals and families
- Pickup every Wednesday
pvi-got-groceries.how_to_get_it: Register first using the "Register Here" form on PVI's Nutrition Services page, then pick up your groceries on Wednesdays. Call Peninsula Volunteers at 650-326-0665 for pickup location and times.

usda-farmers-market-directory.name: USDA Farmers Market Directory
usda-farmers-market-directory.description: The USDA's national directory of thousands of farmers markets across the United States, searchable by location to find fresh, locally-grown produce and farm products near you.
usda-farmers-market-directory.what_they_offer:
- Searchable directory of farmers markets nationwide
- Market locations and open days/months
- Products sold at each market
- Accepted payment methods (including SNAP/EBT)
- Search by distance or by state
usda-farmers-market-directory.how_to_get_it: Visit the USDA Local Food Portal's Farmers Market Directory and search by location (within 10 to 250 miles) or by state. Filter by open months, days, products, and more.

cdfa-certified-farmers-markets.name: California Certified Farmers' Markets
cdfa-certified-farmers-markets.description: The official California Department of Food and Agriculture list of certified farmers' markets statewide, where California farmers sell directly to consumers.
cdfa-certified-farmers-markets.what_they_offer:
- Hundreds of certified farmers' markets in California
- Markets listed by county, with location, days, hours, season, and manager contact
- Direct-from-farm produce and products
- Certification ensures products are California-grown
- Ask your market whether it accepts CalFresh EBT and Market Match
cdfa-certified-farmers-markets.how_to_get_it: View the CDFA directory (updated regularly; current list as of July 1, 2026) to find certified farmers' markets in your county, then check the market's days and hours.

calvet-veterans-homes.name: Veterans Homes of California
calvet-veterans-homes.description: The Veterans Homes of California operate 8 residential care facilities across the state providing housing, healthcare, and supportive services to eligible veterans and their spouses.
calvet-veterans-homes.what_they_offer:
- Long-term residential care (domiciliary and skilled nursing)
- On-site medical and dental care
- Physical therapy and rehabilitation
- Memory care for Alzheimer's/dementia
- Social and recreational activities
- Three meals daily
- Transportation to VA medical appointments
calvet-veterans-homes.how_to_get_it:
1. Must be California veteran with 90+ days active duty
2. Must have honorable discharge
3. Apply online or by mail through CalVet
4. Submit DD214, medical records, and financial info
5. Complete health assessment
6. Select preferred home location

988-suicide-crisis-lifeline.name: 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline
988-suicide-crisis-lifeline.description: The 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline is a national network of local crisis centers providing free, confidential emotional support 24/7 to people in suicidal crisis or emotional distress.
988-suicide-crisis-lifeline.what_they_offer:
- 24/7 phone, text, and chat support
- Trained crisis counselors available in English and Spanish
- Specialized support for veterans (press 1)
- LGBTQ+ specific support available
- Deaf/hard of hearing support via TTY
988-suicide-crisis-lifeline.how_to_get_it: Call or text 988 from any phone, anytime. You can also chat online at 988lifeline.org. No appointment or insurance needed.

crisis-text-line.name: Crisis Text Line
crisis-text-line.description: Crisis Text Line is a free, 24/7 text-based mental health support service connecting people in crisis with trained volunteer counselors through text messages.
crisis-text-line.what_they_offer:
- Free 24/7 crisis support via text
- Trained volunteer crisis counselors
- Confidential conversations
- Support for anxiety, depression, suicidal thoughts, abuse, and more
- Available in English and Spanish
crisis-text-line.how_to_get_it: Text HOME to 741741 from anywhere in the US. A trained crisis counselor will respond within minutes. Free on all carriers.

sf-suicide-prevention.name: San Francisco Suicide Prevention
sf-suicide-prevention.description: San Francisco Suicide Prevention provides 24/7 confidential emotional support and crisis intervention through their hotline, operated by Felton Institute.
sf-suicide-prevention.what_they_offer:
- 24/7 crisis phone support
- Compassionate, judgment-free listening
- Crisis intervention and de-escalation
- Referrals to local mental health resources
- Support for anyone in emotional distress
- Other 24/7 lines: HIV Nightline 415-434-2437, Drug Info Line 415-362-3400, Relapse Line 415-834-1144
- Peer-led grief support group for people who lost someone to suicide
sf-suicide-prevention.how_to_get_it: Call 415-781-0500 or text 415-200-2920 anytime, day or night. Free and confidential. No appointment needed. TTY 415-227-0245.

sf-behavioral-health-access.name: SF Behavioral Health Access Line
sf-behavioral-health-access.description: San Francisco's 24/7 behavioral health access line gives information about mental health and substance use services and helps people access and navigate care. No referral is needed.
sf-behavioral-health-access.what_they_offer:
- Information about SF mental health and substance use services
- Help accessing and navigating care, including benefits enrollment
- Referrals to mental health and substance use treatment
- Drop-in help at the Behavioral Health Access Center (1380 Howard Street)
sf-behavioral-health-access.how_to_get_it: Call 415-255-3737 or toll-free 888-246-3333 anytime (TTY 1-888-484-7200). Or drop in at the Behavioral Health Access Center, 1380 Howard Street, 1st Floor (Mon-Fri 8am-7pm, weekends 9am-4pm). For a mental health crisis, call Comprehensive Crisis at 628-217-7000 or 988.

sf-mobile-crisis-team.name: SF Mobile Crisis Team
sf-mobile-crisis-team.description: San Francisco Department of Public Health's Comprehensive Crisis Services (including the Mobile Crisis Team and Child Crisis) responds to mental health and substance use crises, with clinicians who can do outreach visits for adults and children.
sf-mobile-crisis-team.what_they_offer:
- 24/7 crisis phone line
- Outreach visits during a mental health crisis for adults and children
- Crisis intervention and de-escalation
- Connection to appropriate services
sf-mobile-crisis-team.how_to_get_it: Call Comprehensive Crisis at 628-217-7000, available 24 hours a day, 7 days a week. For a life-threatening emergency or overdose, call 911.

alameda-crisis-support.name: Crisis Support Services of Alameda County
alameda-crisis-support.description: Crisis Support Services of Alameda County is the local 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline center, offering 24/7 crisis support by phone, text, and chat, plus therapy and support groups.
alameda-crisis-support.what_they_offer:
- 24/7 crisis and suicide prevention line (call, text, or chat 988)
- Local Alameda County crisis hotline
- Information and referrals to Alameda County Mobile Crisis Teams
- Therapy for youth, adults, older adults, and families
- Support groups in Oakland and around Alameda County
alameda-crisis-support.how_to_get_it: Call, text, or chat 988 anytime. Alameda County residents can also call the local crisis hotline at 1-800-309-2131. Free and confidential.

contra-costa-crisis-center.name: Contra Costa Crisis Center
contra-costa-crisis-center.description: The Contra Costa Crisis Center provides 24/7 crisis intervention, suicide prevention, and grief counseling services to Contra Costa County residents.
contra-costa-crisis-center.what_they_offer:
- 24/7 crisis and suicide hotline
- Crisis text line (text HOPE to 20121)
- 24-hour grief phone counseling and bereavement support groups in Walnut Creek
- 211 information and referral to local resources
- Free and confidential support
contra-costa-crisis-center.how_to_get_it: Call 988 or 800-273-8255 anytime for crisis support, or text HOPE to 20121. For grief counseling, call 211 or 800-830-5380.

santa-clara-suicide-crisis.name: Santa Clara County Crisis Line
santa-clara-suicide-crisis.description: Santa Clara County's 24/7 Crisis and Suicide Prevention Lifeline (988) provides immediate support for mental health and substance use crises and connects callers to county behavioral health services and mobile response teams.
santa-clara-suicide-crisis.what_they_offer:
- 24/7 suicide and crisis support
- Mental health and substance use crisis intervention
- Referrals to county behavioral health services
- Interpretation in more than 200 languages
- Connection to mobile crisis response teams when needed
santa-clara-suicide-crisis.how_to_get_it: Call or text 988 anytime. If your phone doesn't have a 408, 650, or 669 area code, call 1-800-704-0900 and press 1 to reach Santa Clara County's local counselors. The same 800 number is for non-emergency behavioral health questions. Free, anonymous, and confidential.

marin-suicide-hotline.name: Marin County Suicide Prevention Hotline
marin-suicide-hotline.description: Buckelew Programs (formerly Family Service Agency of Marin) runs Marin County's suicide prevention hotline as part of the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline, plus free grief support groups for people who have lost someone to suicide.
marin-suicide-hotline.what_they_offer:
- 24/7 free, confidential suicide prevention and crisis hotline (988)
- Trained counselors for people with suicidal thoughts or emotional distress
- Free suicide bereavement support groups on Zoom (adults, ages 14-24, and Spanish speakers)
- Suicide prevention education for schools, workplaces, and organizations
marin-suicide-hotline.how_to_get_it: Call or text 988 anytime. Calls from Marin are answered by Buckelew's local 988 counselors. Marin County's resource guide also lists Buckelew's local hotline at 415-499-1100.

napa-crisis-hotline.name: Napa County Mental Health Crisis Line
napa-crisis-hotline.description: Napa County's 24-hour mental health crisis hotline provides immediate support for Napa County residents of all ages experiencing a mental health crisis or emergency.
napa-crisis-hotline.what_they_offer:
- 24/7 crisis support for all ages
- Anyone in crisis is seen and assessed regardless of eligibility
- Crisis Stabilization Services (short-term care lasting less than 24 hours)
- Intake and referrals to county mental health services
- Bilingual English/Spanish services
napa-crisis-hotline.how_to_get_it: Call 707-253-4711, 24 hours a day. The Crisis Stabilization Services Program is at 2751 Napa Valley Corporate Way, Building B, Napa. For a life-threatening emergency, call 911.

solano-crisis-line.name: Solano County Crisis Line
solano-crisis-line.description: Solano County Behavioral Health's 24/7 Mobile Crisis team (operated by Pacific Clinics) helps people in an urgent mental health crisis by phone, at home, or in the community.
solano-crisis-line.what_they_offer:
- 24/7/365 mobile crisis hotline
- Phone support, de-escalation, and safety planning
- In-person response at home or in the community when needed
- Transportation to the Crisis Stabilization Unit or emergency room if necessary
- Anyone can call, regardless of insurance
solano-crisis-line.how_to_get_it: Call Mobile Crisis at 707-806-0866 anytime for an urgent mental health crisis, such as suicidal thoughts. For non-urgent mental health and substance use services, call the Behavioral Health Access Line at 800-547-0495. You can also call or text 988.

sf-women-against-rape.name: San Francisco Women Against Rape (SFWAR)
sf-women-against-rape.description: SFWAR provides a 24-hour crisis hotline and support services for survivors of rape and sexual assault in San Francisco.
sf-women-against-rape.what_they_offer:
- 24/7 crisis hotline (collect calls accepted)
- Emotional support for survivors and their family and friends
- Medical accompaniment at Zuckerberg San Francisco General Hospital
- Legal and social service advocacy
- In-person peer counseling and support groups
sf-women-against-rape.how_to_get_it: Call 415-647-7273 (647-RAPE) anytime for immediate support. For advocacy and accompaniment, call 415-861-2024 ext. 319 (ext. 304 for Spanish).

friendship-line-elderly.name: Institute on Aging Friendship Line
friendship-line-elderly.description: Institute on Aging's Friendship Line is an accredited 24/7 toll-free emotional support and crisis line for Californians 60+, adults with disabilities, and caregivers, offering crisis intervention and friendly conversation.
friendship-line-elderly.what_they_offer:
- 24/7 emotional support and crisis intervention
- Suicide prevention
- Friendly conversation, plus regular check-in calls on request
- Grief support, including virtual bereavement groups
- Caregiver support
- Help in English, Spanish, Cantonese, Mandarin, Tagalog, Vietnamese, Korean, and Russian
friendship-line-elderly.how_to_get_it: Call 888-670-1360 anytime (toll-free in California). No appointment or application. For regular outbound check-in calls, fill out the intake form online. Other languages - Spanish 888-571-0411, Cantonese/Mandarin 888-670-2504, Tagalog 888-570-0867, Vietnamese 888-670-1361, Korean 888-560-7684, Russian 888-560-7360.

denti-cal.name: Denti-Cal
denti-cal.description: Medi-Cal Dental (formerly called Denti-Cal) is California's Medicaid dental program, providing free or low-cost dental care to Medi-Cal members of all ages.
denti-cal.what_they_offer:
- Preventive care (cleanings, exams, x-rays, fluoride)
- Restorative services (fillings, crowns)
- Extractions and oral surgery
- Dentures and partials
- Emergency dental services
- Orthodontics for children under 21 (when medically necessary)
denti-cal.how_to_get_it: If you have Medi-Cal, dental benefits are included. Find a Medi-Cal dentist with the online Find-A-Dentist search or call the Medi-Cal Dental Telephone Service Center at 1-800-322-6384 (free call, Mon-Fri 8am-5pm). Starting July 1, 2027, some adult members will lose full dental benefits based on immigration status (emergency dental care stays covered); children under 19, pregnant and postpartum members, and former foster youth under 26 keep full benefits.

eyecare-america.name: EyeCare America
eyecare-america.description: EyeCare America is a public service program of the American Academy of Ophthalmology that matches uninsured and underinsured adults 18+ with volunteer ophthalmologists for a medical eye exam at no out-of-pocket cost.
eyecare-america.what_they_offer:
- Medical eye exam by a volunteer ophthalmologist
- Up to one year of follow-up visits for conditions found at the first exam
- No out-of-pocket cost for covered exam and follow-up care
- Does NOT cover glasses, contacts, eyeglass prescriptions, surgery, medications, or tests
- One-time referral program
eyecare-america.how_to_get_it: You must be 18 or older, a US citizen or legal resident, have no HMO, PPO, private insurance, or VA benefits, not have seen an ophthalmologist in 3+ years, and not have used EyeCare America before. Fill out the online referral questionnaire to get matched right away, or call 877-887-6327 (Mon-Fri 8am-2pm PT). Not for urgent eye problems.

medi-cal.name: Medi-Cal (Medicaid)
medi-cal.description: Medi-Cal is California's Medicaid program, providing free or low-cost health coverage to millions of Californians including low-income adults, families, seniors, pregnant women, and people with disabilities.
medi-cal.what_they_offer:
- Doctor and hospital visits
- Prescription medications
- Preventive care and screenings
- Mental health services
- Dental care (Medi-Cal Dental)
- Vision care
- Substance use treatment
- Long-term care services
medi-cal.how_to_get_it: Apply online at CoveredCA.com or BenefitsCal.com, through your county social services office, or by phone with Covered California at 1-800-300-1506 (Mon-Fri 8am-6pm). Adults generally qualify with income up to 138% of the poverty level (266% for children), or if they get CalFresh, SSI/SSP, or CalWORKs. You can apply any time of year and must renew once a year. Some benefits for certain adults are changing based on immigration status, so check with your county office.

needymeds.name: NeedyMeds
needymeds.description: NeedyMeds is a nonprofit providing a comprehensive database of patient assistance programs, helping people find affordable medications and healthcare services regardless of insurance status.
needymeds.what_they_offer:
- Searchable database of patient assistance programs
- Free drug discount card
- Drug price and pharmacy lookup
- Listings of free/low-cost clinics
- Coupons and rebates for medications
needymeds.how_to_get_it: Visit needymeds.org and search programs by drug name, or search for clinics and coupons. Request the free NeedyMeds Drug Discount Card online.

planned-parenthood.name: Planned Parenthood
planned-parenthood.description: Planned Parenthood offers sexual and reproductive health care at health centers across California and by telehealth, for patients with private insurance, Medi-Cal, or no insurance.
planned-parenthood.what_they_offer:
- Birth control and contraception counseling
- STI testing and treatment
- HIV testing
- Cancer screenings (breast, cervical)
- Pregnancy testing and options counseling
- Abortion services
- Gender-affirming care, including hormone therapy
- Vasectomies, menopause services, and wellness exams
- Telehealth visits
planned-parenthood.how_to_get_it: Find your nearest health center online or call 1-800-230-PLAN. Appointments recommended. Many centers accept Medi-Cal and Family PACT and offer sliding scale fees if you qualify.

ryan-white-program.name: Ryan White HIV/AIDS Program
ryan-white-program.description: The Ryan White HIV/AIDS Program provides comprehensive care and support services for people living with HIV who are uninsured or underinsured, filling gaps in care not covered by other sources.
ryan-white-program.what_they_offer:
- Primary medical care and specialist visits
- HIV medications and treatment
- Mental health services
- Substance abuse treatment
- Case management
- Transportation to appointments
- Emergency financial assistance
- Housing assistance
ryan-white-program.how_to_get_it: Contact your local Ryan White provider or AIDS service organization. You'll need proof of HIV diagnosis, residency, and income. Use the HIV care locator to find services near you.

samhsa-helpline.name: SAMHSA National Helpline
samhsa-helpline.description: SAMHSA's National Helpline is a free, confidential, 24/7 treatment referral and information service for individuals and families facing mental health and/or substance use disorders.
samhsa-helpline.what_they_offer:
- 24/7 confidential support
- Treatment referrals in your area
- Information about mental health and substance use
- Support in English and Spanish
- Referrals to local support groups
- Information about state-funded treatment programs
- Help finding sliding-scale or free treatment
samhsa-helpline.how_to_get_it: Call 1-800-662-4357 anytime, 24/7, 365 days a year. Specialists will connect you with local treatment facilities, support groups, and community organizations. TTY available at 1-800-487-4889. You can also text your ZIP code to 435748 (HELP4U) or search FindTreatment.gov. The helpline does not provide counseling.

va-health-benefits.name: VA Health Benefits
va-health-benefits.description: VA Health Benefits provide comprehensive healthcare services to eligible veterans through the Veterans Health Administration, the nation's largest integrated healthcare system.
va-health-benefits.what_they_offer:
- Primary care and specialty care
- Mental health services and counseling
- Prescription medications
- Preventive care and screenings
- Women's health services
- Urgent and emergency care
- Telehealth appointments
- Prosthetics and medical equipment
