va-health-benefits.how_to_get_it: Apply online at VA.gov, by phone at 1-877-222-8387, or in person at any VA medical center. You'll need your DD214 or other discharge documents. Most veterans who served on active duty are eligible.

wic-health.name: WIC (Women, Infants, Children)
wic-health.description: WIC is a nutrition program providing healthy food, nutrition education, breastfeeding support, and healthcare referrals to pregnant and postpartum women, infants, and children under 5 in California.
wic-health.what_they_offer:
- Monthly benefits for nutritious foods (fruits, vegetables, whole grains, milk, eggs)
- Infant formula and baby food
- Nutrition education and counseling
- Breastfeeding support and breast pumps
- Health screenings and referrals
- Farmers' market benefits
- WIC card accepted at most grocery stores
wic-health.how_to_get_it: Contact your local WIC office, call 1-888-942-9675 (24 hours), or call 1-800-852-5770 during business hours. You'll need proof of income (up to 185% of poverty level; families on Medi-Cal or CalFresh usually qualify automatically), residency, and identity. Pregnant women, new mothers, infants, and children under 5 may qualify, and dads, grandparents, and foster parents of young children can apply too.

smc-bhrs.name: Behavioral Health and Recovery Services (BHRS)
smc-bhrs.description: San Mateo County Behavioral Health and Recovery Services provides mental health and substance use treatment, prevention, and recovery services to residents of all ages in San Mateo County.
smc-bhrs.what_they_offer:
- Mental health assessment and treatment
- Substance use disorder treatment
- Crisis intervention services
- Youth and family services
- Older adult services
- Peer support programs
- Prevention and early intervention
- Housing support for clients
smc-bhrs.how_to_get_it: Call the Access Call Center at 1-800-686-0101 (TDD 1-800-943-2833) for consultation, assessment, and referral. BHRS serves Medi-Cal members and uninsured or undocumented residents (some Medicare, HPSM, and private insurance members too), and helps people of any age in a major crisis. Pregnant and parenting women get priority for substance use services.

smc-aging-adult-services.name: Aging and Disability Services
smc-aging-adult-services.description: San Mateo County Aging and Disability Services (formerly Aging and Adult Services) provides protective services, in-home care, case management, and nutrition programs to help older adults and people with disabilities live safely and independently. It is also the county's Area Agency on Aging.
smc-aging-adult-services.what_they_offer:
- Adult Protective Services (abuse prevention and 24-hour emergency response)
- In-Home Supportive Services (IHSS)
- Public Guardian/Conservator services
- Group dining sites and home-delivered meals for older adults
- Case management (Linkages, CalAIM Enhanced Care Management)
- Information and referral through the Aging and Disability Resource Connection (ADRC)
smc-aging-adult-services.how_to_get_it: Call the Aging and Disability Resource Connection at 888-762-2372 for information and referrals, or the main office at (650) 573-3900. To report abuse or get 24-hour emergency response, call the Aging and Disability Services Hotline at 1-844-868-0938 (711 for TDD). Services are for older adults and adults with disabilities.

smc-pregnancy-children-families.name: San Mateo County Pregnancy, Children and Families
smc-pregnancy-children-families.description: San Mateo County Health's Pregnancy, Children and Families services offer prenatal support, home visiting, nutrition, and child health programs to support healthy pregnancies and child development for families throughout the county.
smc-pregnancy-children-families.what_they_offer:
- Free home visiting (Nurse-Family Partnership, Healthy Families San Mateo County, Promoting First Relationships)
- Black Infant Health program
- Help getting prenatal care for Medi-Cal-eligible pregnant women
- WIC nutrition program and breastfeeding support
- California Children's Services (CCS) for children with certain medical conditions
- Oral health program for young children on Medi-Cal
- Lead poisoning prevention and parenting classes
- Services in your native language
smc-pregnancy-children-families.how_to_get_it: Call (650) 573-2501 for program information. Services are free for families on Medi-Cal and on a sliding fee scale for other San Mateo County residents.

calrx-naloxone.name: CalRx OTC Naloxone Nasal Spray
calrx-naloxone.description: CalRx is California's initiative to make naloxone, a life-saving medication that reverses opioid overdoses, affordable and accessible to all residents without a prescription.
calrx-naloxone.what_they_offer:
- 4mg naloxone nasal spray (Narcan-equivalent)
- Twin pack for $19 plus shipping and handling
- No prescription required
- Well below typical retail price
- Simple nasal spray administration
- Organizations may qualify for free naloxone through the state Naloxone Distribution Project
calrx-naloxone.how_to_get_it: Anyone living in California can order online at calrxnaloxone.com (linked from the CalRx page). Orders must ship to a California address, and the minimum order is one twin pack. Naloxone cannot be resold.

naloxone-distribution-project.name: Naloxone Distribution Project (NDP)
naloxone-distribution-project.description: California's Naloxone Distribution Project provides free naloxone and fentanyl test strips to eligible organizations working to prevent opioid overdose deaths in their communities. It does not serve individuals directly.
naloxone-distribution-project.what_they_offer:
- Free naloxone nasal spray (generic or Narcan brand)
- Free fentanyl test strips
- Shipped directly to approved organizations
- Available to eligible organizations statewide
naloxone-distribution-project.how_to_get_it: Organizations apply through the Department of Health Care Services' online NDP application. Eligible entities include community organizations (harm reduction groups, opioid coalitions), schools and universities, tribal entities, county public health and behavioral health departments, fire/EMS and first responders, and law enforcement. Fentanyl test strip requests require a business license, FEIN, or tax-exempt letter. Individuals can buy low-cost naloxone through CalRx.

adap.name: AIDS Drug Assistance Program (ADAP)
adap.description: California's AIDS Drug Assistance Program provides life-saving HIV/AIDS medications and health insurance assistance to low-income Californians living with HIV who lack adequate coverage.
adap.what_they_offer:
- Free FDA-approved HIV/AIDS medications on the ADAP formulary
- Premium payment assistance for private health insurance (OA-HIPP)
- Premium payment assistance for Medicare Part C and Part D plans
- For California residents 18+ with income up to 600% FPL (MAGI)
- For people not fully covered by Medi-Cal or other insurance
adap.how_to_get_it: Make an appointment with a certified ADAP Enrollment Worker at an ADAP enrollment site (use the state's site locator or call the ADAP call center at 844-421-7050, Monday-Friday 8am-5pm). You'll need proof of HIV diagnosis, California residency, income, and current insurance status. Re-enroll in person every year before your birthday.

kick-it-california.name: Kick It California (Quit Smoking Helpline)
kick-it-california.description: Kick It California is the state's free quit smoking and tobacco helpline, offering personalized coaching, a mobile app, and resources to help Californians quit tobacco, vaping, and marijuana.
kick-it-california.what_they_offer:
- Free one-on-one phone coaching
- Personalized quit plan
- Mobile app for tracking progress
- Text messaging program and online chat
- Help quitting cigarettes, vapes, and smokeless tobacco
- Marijuana coaching (ages 13-29)
- Available in English and Spanish (Asian-language help through the Asian Smokers' Quitline)
- Free nicotine patches for those who qualify
kick-it-california.how_to_get_it: Call 1-800-300-8086 (Spanish 1-800-600-8191), chat, or fill out the web form at kickitca.org to get started. Coaching is free and confidential. You can also use the Kick It mobile app.

black-infant-health.name: Black Infant Health Program
black-infant-health.description: The Black Infant Health Program is California's free, community-based program providing group and one-on-one support to Black women and birthing people during pregnancy and after birth.
black-infant-health.what_they_offer:
- 10 prenatal and 10 postpartum group sessions (ages 18+)
- One-on-one support and goal setting (including ages 16-17)
- Life skills and stress management
- Health education on pregnancy, labor, and newborn care
- Social support and community building
- Referrals to medical, dental, and social services
- Available through local health departments in participating counties
black-infant-health.how_to_get_it: Contact your local Black Infant Health program through the state website. Services are free and open to Black women and birthing people age 16+ who are pregnant or up to six months postpartum when they enroll, regardless of income.

california-home-visiting.name: California Home Visiting Program
california-home-visiting.description: The California Home Visiting Program provides free, voluntary home visits to pregnant and newly parenting families facing challenges, offering parenting support, health education, and connections to community resources.
california-home-visiting.what_they_offer:
- Regular home visits by a Public Health Nurse or trained home visitor
- Parenting education and support
- Child health and development support
- Maternal health and well-being support
- Connections to healthcare and social services
- Visits at home or another agreed-upon location
- Services typically last two to three years
california-home-visiting.how_to_get_it: Contact your local health department or use the state website to find programs in your area. Serves pregnant and newly parenting families with one or more risk factors, such as low income, unstable housing, domestic violence, less than 12 years of education, substance use, or depression/mental health challenges.

vaccines-for-children.name: Vaccines for Children (VFC) Program
vaccines-for-children.description: The Vaccines for Children program provides free vaccines to children 18 and under who might not otherwise be vaccinated because of inability to pay, ensuring all children have access to life-saving immunizations.
vaccines-for-children.what_they_offer:
- Federally recommended childhood vaccines at no cost (protecting against 18 diseases)
- Available for children from birth through age 18
- DTaP, Polio, MMR, Hepatitis, HPV, and more
- Flu vaccines
- Catch-up vaccines for older children
- Offered by enrolled doctors, clinics, hospitals, and some pharmacies
vaccines-for-children.how_to_get_it: Ask your child's doctor or clinic if they are a VFC provider, or search the My Turn Vaccine Locator (myturn.ca.gov). Children qualify if they have Medi-Cal, are uninsured, or are American Indian/Alaska Native. Underinsured children can get VFC vaccines at federally qualified health centers (FQHCs) and rural health clinics. Bring your child's immunization record.

prep-assistance-program.name: PrEP Assistance Program (PrEP-AP)
prep-assistance-program.description: California's PrEP Assistance Program makes HIV prevention medication accessible to residents who might not otherwise afford it, covering the cost of PrEP medication, doctor visits, and lab tests.
prep-assistance-program.what_they_offer:
- Free PrEP medication (Truvada, Descovy, or generic)
- Coverage for doctor visits and HIV testing
- Lab work costs covered
- Available to residents with income under 600% FPL
- Minors ages 12-17 and adults with confidentiality concerns can enroll
- PrEP-AP Immediate Access: One free month of PrEP for anyone
- Available regardless of immigration status (not subject to Public Charge)
- Helps uninsured and insured individuals
prep-assistance-program.how_to_get_it: Enroll at a PrEP-AP enrollment site, using the list of acceptable eligibility documents (proof of California residency and income). If uninsured, a minor, or concerned about confidentiality, see a provider in the PrEP-AP Clinical Provider Network; if insured, see a provider in your health plan. Anyone can get one free month by creating an account and enrolling in PrEP-AP Immediate Access.

every-woman-counts.name: Every Woman Counts
every-woman-counts.description: Every Woman Counts provides free breast and cervical cancer screenings to uninsured and underinsured California women, helping detect cancer early when treatment is most effective.
every-woman-counts.what_they_offer:
- Free mammograms
- Clinical breast exams
- Pap tests (cervical cancer screening)
- HPV tests
- Follow-up diagnostic testing if needed
- Connection to free treatment through the Breast and Cervical Cancer Treatment Program (BCCTP)
- Available at providers statewide (online provider locator)
- Help available in English, Spanish, and many other languages
every-woman-counts.how_to_get_it: Call 1-800-511-2300 (24/7) or use the online provider locator to find a provider and check eligibility. You must be a California resident with income at or below 200% of the federal poverty level and uninsured or underinsured for these services. Cervical screening is for ages 21+; breast screening is for ages 40+ (any age if high risk).

cpsp.name: Comprehensive Perinatal Services Program (CPSP)
cpsp.description: The Comprehensive Perinatal Services Program provides enhanced prenatal and postpartum care to Medi-Cal recipients, offering additional support services beyond standard obstetric care to improve birth outcomes.
cpsp.what_they_offer:
- Enhanced prenatal care visits
- Nutrition counseling and education
- Psychosocial assessment and support
- Health education classes
- Care coordination
- Postpartum care through 60 days after delivery
- Breastfeeding support
- Referrals to community resources
cpsp.how_to_get_it: If you're pregnant and have Medi-Cal, ask your prenatal care provider if they're a CPSP provider. CPSP services are covered at no additional cost through Medi-Cal.

childhood-lead-poisoning-prevention.name: Childhood Lead Poisoning Prevention Program
childhood-lead-poisoning-prevention.description: California's Childhood Lead Poisoning Prevention Program provides screening, case management, and environmental investigation to protect children from lead exposure, which can cause learning disabilities and developmental delays.
childhood-lead-poisoning-prevention.what_they_offer:
- Blood lead screening guidance for children (testing is covered by Medi-Cal)
- Case management for children with elevated lead levels
- Environmental investigation of lead sources
- Home assessment and lead hazard identification
- Nutritional counseling
- Connection to developmental services
- Education for parents and caregivers
childhood-lead-poisoning-prevention.how_to_get_it: Under updated state screening rules (effective July 6, 2026), almost all California children should get a blood lead test at ages 1 and 2 - ask your child's doctor. Contact your local health department's lead program if your child has been exposed to lead or you're concerned about lead in your home.

myturn.name: MyTurn
myturn.description: MyTurn is California's official vaccine scheduling and digital record system, making it easy to find vaccine appointments, access your immunization records, and stay up to date on recommended vaccines.
myturn.what_they_offer:
- COVID-19 vaccine appointments
- Flu vaccine appointments (during flu season, early fall through late spring)
- Mpox vaccine scheduling
- Routine and back-to-school vaccine appointments
- Vaccine Locator, including walk-in clinics and no-cost options for the uninsured
- Link to your Digital Vaccine Record
- Phone help in 250+ languages
myturn.how_to_get_it: Visit myturn.ca.gov to make an appointment or use the Vaccine Locator to find clinics near you. For help, call the hotline at 833-422-4255 (Monday-Friday, 8am-5pm). Get your digital vaccine record at myvaccinerecord.cdph.ca.gov.

sf-behavioral-health-directory.name: SF Mental Health & Substance Use Provider Directory
sf-behavioral-health-directory.description: San Francisco's official directory of mental health and substance use disorder treatment providers, maintained by the Department of Public Health Behavioral Health Services.
sf-behavioral-health-directory.what_they_offer:
- Mental health plan provider and clinician directories (reviewed monthly)
- Substance use services (Drug Medi-Cal) provider directories
- Shows addresses, services, languages, and whether providers accept new members
- Available in English, Spanish, Chinese, Vietnamese, Russian, and Tagalog
- Free paper copies and large print on request
sf-behavioral-health-directory.how_to_get_it: Download the directories online, or call the 24/7 Behavioral Health Access Line at 1-888-246-3333 or 415-255-3737 (TDD 711) for help finding services and scheduling assessments. Request printed copies at BHSMemberServices@sfdph.org.

smc-behavioral-health-directory.name: San Mateo County Behavioral Health Provider Directory
smc-behavioral-health-directory.description: San Mateo County's official directory of behavioral health providers, including mental health clinics, substance use treatment programs, and crisis services throughout the county.
smc-behavioral-health-directory.what_they_offer:
- County programs, contracted agencies, and private providers contracted with BHRS
- Mental health and substance use providers and programs
- Behavioral Health Programs and Services Guide (updated annually)
- Service descriptions, contact information, and how to request services
smc-behavioral-health-directory.how_to_get_it: Visit the online directory or call the Access Call Center at 1-800-686-0101 for help finding providers and getting assessed for services.

santa-clara-behavioral-health-directory.name: Santa Clara County Behavioral Health Provider Directory
santa-clara-behavioral-health-directory.description: Santa Clara County's official searchable directory of behavioral health providers, updated monthly with mental health clinics, substance use programs, and community services.
santa-clara-behavioral-health-directory.what_they_offer:
- Online searchable provider database
- Mental health outpatient clinics
- Substance use disorder treatment
- Children's mental health services
- Crisis and emergency services
santa-clara-behavioral-health-directory.how_to_get_it: Search the online directory or call 1-800-704-0900 for help accessing mental health and substance use services in Santa Clara County.

alameda-behavioral-health-directory.name: Alameda County Behavioral Health Provider Directory
alameda-behavioral-health-directory.description: Alameda County Behavioral Health's ACCESS line and online provider directory help Medi-Cal members and uninsured residents find mental health clinics, substance use treatment, and community resources throughout the county.
alameda-behavioral-health-directory.what_they_offer:
- 24/7 ACCESS line for mental health screening and referrals
- Substance Use Access & Referral Helpline (screening, assessment, referral, care coordination)
- Online provider directory (acbh.my.site.com/ProviderDirectory)
- Crisis services information
- For Medi-Cal members and uninsured Alameda County residents
alameda-behavioral-health-directory.how_to_get_it: Call the 24/7 Mental Health ACCESS line at 1-800-491-9099. For substance use services, call the Substance Use Access & Referral Helpline at 1-844-682-7215. For crisis services, call 510-891-5600.

contra-costa-behavioral-health-directory.name: Contra Costa County Mental Health Provider Directory
contra-costa-behavioral-health-directory.description: Contra Costa County's official mental health provider directory, updated weekly with licensed clinics, treatment programs, and crisis services for county residents.
contra-costa-behavioral-health-directory.what_they_offer:
- Weekly updated provider listings
- Mental health treatment facilities
- Substance use disorder services
- Children and youth services
- Crisis and emergency contacts
contra-costa-behavioral-health-directory.how_to_get_it: Search the online directory or call the 24/7 Access Line at 1-888-678-7277. For crisis support, call the A3 Miles Hall Crisis Center at 844-844-5544.

marin-behavioral-health-directory.name: Marin County Behavioral Health Provider Directory
marin-behavioral-health-directory.description: Marin County Behavioral Health and Recovery Services' official provider directory, including Medi-Cal mental health providers and Drug Medi-Cal substance use treatment facilities.
marin-behavioral-health-directory.what_they_offer:
- Medi-Cal mental health provider listings
- Drug Medi-Cal substance use providers
- Community mental health services
- Crisis intervention resources
- Recovery support services
marin-behavioral-health-directory.how_to_get_it: View the online provider directories or call the Access Line at 888-818-1115 for help finding mental health and substance use services in Marin County.

sonoma-behavioral-health-directory.name: Sonoma County Behavioral Health Provider Directory
sonoma-behavioral-health-directory.description: Sonoma County's official behavioral health provider directories, listing mental health clinics and substance use disorder treatment providers serving county residents.
sonoma-behavioral-health-directory.what_they_offer:
- Mental health provider directory (PDF, 2026, English and Spanish)
- Substance use disorder provider directory (PDF, 2026, English and Spanish)
- 24-hour Access Team for mental health screening, assessment, and referral
- Adult (18+) and youth (0-20) outpatient mental health services for Medi-Cal members
- Crisis services information
sonoma-behavioral-health-directory.how_to_get_it: Download the provider directories from the county's Medi-Cal Informing Materials page, or call the 24-hour Access Line at 707-565-6900 or toll-free 1-800-870-8786 for help finding mental health services in Sonoma County.

napa-behavioral-health-directory.name: Napa County Behavioral Health Provider Directory
napa-behavioral-health-directory.description: Napa County's official partners and providers directory for behavioral health services, including mental health treatment facilities and substance use programs.
napa-behavioral-health-directory.what_they_offer:
- Mental health provider listings
- Substance use treatment providers
- Crisis services information
- Community resources
- Recovery support programs
napa-behavioral-health-directory.how_to_get_it: View the online directory (English and Spanish) or call Mental Health Services Access at 707-259-8151 or 1-800-648-8650. For 24-hour crisis support, call 707-253-4711.

solano-behavioral-health-directory.name: Solano County Behavioral Health Provider Directory
solano-behavioral-health-directory.description: Solano County Behavioral Health Plan's official provider directory, listing specialty mental health providers serving Medi-Cal members throughout the county.
solano-behavioral-health-directory.what_they_offer:
- Mental health provider directory (PDF, English and Spanish)
- Member handbook in English, Spanish, and Tagalog
- Substance use providers are listed in Partnership HealthPlan's Medi-Cal directory for now (county directory adds them starting January 1, 2027)
- Access to services information
- Crisis resources
solano-behavioral-health-directory.how_to_get_it: View the directory online or call the Behavioral Health Access Line at 1-800-547-0495 (Monday-Friday, 8am-5pm) for mental health and co-occurring substance use services, or email BHAccess@SolanoCounty.gov.

court-fee-waivers.name: Court Fee Waivers
court-fee-waivers.description: California courts offer fee waivers for individuals who cannot afford to pay court filing fees, ensuring access to the justice system regardless of income.
court-fee-waivers.what_they_offer:
- Waiver of court filing fees
- Free copies of court papers, including certified copies
- Waiver of sheriff fees to serve your papers
- Waiver of court reporter fees to attend trial
- Other fees listed on form FW-003 (does not cover lawyer fees, private mediation, fines, or written transcripts)
court-fee-waivers.how_to_get_it:
1. Fill out Form FW-001 (Request to Waive Court Fees) and item 1 of Form FW-003; the form is confidential
2. You qualify if you receive public benefits (Medi-Cal, CalFresh, SSI, etc.)
3. Or if your gross monthly household income is below the limit on FW-001 (about 200% of the federal poverty level, e.g. $2,660/month for 1 person as of March 2026)
4. Or if you can't pay court fees and still meet your household's basic needs
5. File with the court clerk at the same time as your other papers or later in your case
6. The clerk or judge writes the decision on Form FW-003; tell the court within 5 days if your finances improve

justice-diversity-center.name: Justice & Diversity Center (JDC)
justice-diversity-center.description: The Justice & Diversity Center is the nonprofit arm of the Bar Association of San Francisco, providing free legal services to those who cannot afford attorneys.
justice-diversity-center.what_they_offer:
- Legal Advice and Referral Clinic (LARC)
- Homeless Advocacy Project (HAP) for unhoused San Franciscans
- Pro bono help in nearly every area of civil law, including eviction and domestic violence
- Special Immigrant Juvenile Status (SIJS) Project and Immigrant Legal Defense Program
- Community Organization Representation Project (CORP) for nonprofits serving low-income communities
justice-diversity-center.how_to_get_it:
1. Visit the JDC Legal Services Programs page or call 415-982-1600 (Monday–Friday, 9 AM–5 PM)
2. Unhoused residents can visit the Homeless Advocacy Project drop-in intake clinic at 125 Hyde Street, Tuesday–Friday, 1–3 PM (415-575-3130)
3. Complete intake and eligibility screening
4. If eligible, receive free legal advice or representation
5. Nonprofits can apply to CORP separately

racial-equity-project.name: Racial Equity Partnership (REP)
racial-equity-project.description: The Racial Equity Partnership, run by the Justice & Diversity Center's Community Organization Representation Project (CORP) with the East Bay Community Foundation's ASCEND:BLO Initiative and the Greenlining Institute, provides free legal support to Black-led organizations in California.
racial-equity-project.what_they_offer:
- Pro bono legal support for Black-led organizations (BLOs)
- Help with employment law, corporate governance and structure, and commercial leases
- Help with contracts, risk management, and IRS reinstatement
- Matching with experienced volunteer transactional attorneys
racial-equity-project.how_to_get_it:
1. Organization must be Black-led (led by Black staff and/or Black board members)
2. Email corp@sfbar.org to learn more and ask about eligibility
3. Describe your legal needs and your organization's mission
4. If accepted, be matched with pro bono attorneys

sf-financial-justice-project.name: SF Economic Justice Center (formerly Financial Justice Project)
sf-financial-justice-project.description: The San Francisco Treasurer's Economic Justice Center (which now houses the Financial Justice Project's work) helps low-income residents and people experiencing homelessness lower city fines and fees, and offers free financial counseling.
sf-financial-justice-project.what_they_offer:
- Online tool to find discounts on city fines, fees, and tickets
- Discounts for towing and booting, public transit, tickets, and utilities
- Help with legal and court debt, ambulance bills, and animal care fees
- Free 1-on-1 financial counseling
- Advocacy to reform fines and fees that hurt low-income communities
sf-financial-justice-project.how_to_get_it:
1. Visit the Fine & Fee Discounts page on the Economic Justice Center website
2. Filter by the type of fine or fee you need help with
3. Review the discounts you may qualify for and follow the steps to claim them
4. Many low-income San Franciscans qualify for 50% or more off
5. Questions: email economic.justice@sfgov.org or call 415-701-2311

sf-immigrant-support.name: San Francisco Immigrant Support
sf-immigrant-support.description: San Francisco provides resources and support for immigrants, including connections to free and low-cost immigration legal services regardless of immigration status.
sf-immigrant-support.what_they_offer:
- Free or low-cost immigration legal consultations
- Help with citizenship and naturalization applications
- DACA renewal assistance
- Green card and visa support
- Know Your Rights information
- Referrals to trusted legal providers
sf-immigrant-support.how_to_get_it:
1. Visit immigrants.sf.gov and answer a few questions to find the right community legal services
2. Call the provider first; listed organizations are operating at limited capacity
3. Complete intake and eligibility screening with the provider
4. Receive legal assistance based on your needs
5. If you see ICE activity in San Francisco, call the SF Rapid Response hotline at 415-200-1548

uscis-i-912-fee-waiver.name: USCIS I-912 Fee Waiver
uscis-i-912-fee-waiver.description: U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) offers fee waivers for certain immigration applications for individuals who cannot afford the filing fees.
uscis-i-912-fee-waiver.what_they_offer:
- Waiver of filing fees for certain immigration forms
- Available for naturalization (N-400), green card replacement (I-90), removal of conditions (I-751), work permits (I-765), and other listed forms
- Based on receipt of a means-tested benefit, household income, or financial hardship
- Not available for DACA requests
- Some fees created by the 2025 H.R.-1 law cannot be waived (a separate DHS fee may still be waivable)
uscis-i-912-fee-waiver.how_to_get_it:
1. Download Form I-912 from uscis.gov and check that your form is on the eligible list
2. Determine your basis for a fee waiver (means-tested benefit, income at or below 150% of the federal poverty guidelines, or financial hardship)
3. Gather supporting documents (current benefit letters, tax returns, pay stubs)
4. Submit I-912 together with your application (by mail, or online for certain forms); you cannot send it later
5. Sign the form, or USCIS will reject it
6. If the waiver is denied, USCIS rejects the application and you can refile with the fee

clsepa-legal-services.name: Community Legal Services in East Palo Alto
clsepa-legal-services.description: Community Legal Services in East Palo Alto (CLSEPA) provides free legal assistance to low-income families in San Mateo County and surrounding areas.
clsepa-legal-services.what_they_offer:
- Immigration legal services (family petitions, DACA, citizenship)
- Housing and tenant rights assistance
- Workers' rights and wage theft claims
- Criminal record clearance (expungement)
- Consumer protection
- Community education workshops
clsepa-legal-services.how_to_get_it:
1. Call CLSEPA at 650-326-6440 (phones answered until 1 PM; leave a message after hours)
2. Or walk in to 1861 Bay Road, East Palo Alto, Monday–Friday, 9 AM–1 PM
3. Complete intake and financial eligibility screening (must meet income guidelines)
4. Attend an initial consultation with staff
5. Receive ongoing representation if your case is accepted

legal-aid-smc.name: Legal Aid Society of San Mateo County
legal-aid-smc.description: The Legal Aid Society of San Mateo County provides free civil legal services to low-income residents, helping protect their rights and improve their lives.
legal-aid-smc.what_they_offer:
- Housing law (eviction, habitability, lock-outs, utility shut-offs, subsidized housing, fair housing)
- Health care access through the Health Consumer Center (Medi-Cal, insurance)
- Public benefits (CalWORKs, SSI, Social Security, CAPI, CalFresh)
- Immigration assistance and public charge information
- Special education and services for children with disabilities
- Protection from domestic violence and elder abuse
legal-aid-smc.how_to_get_it:
1. Call 650-558-0915 to find out how Legal Aid can help and schedule an appointment
2. Tenants with housing issues can call 650-517-8911
3. Complete eligibility screening (for low-income San Mateo County residents)
4. Describe your legal issue
5. Receive legal advice, brief services, or full representation (no traffic or criminal cases)

project-sentinel-fair-housing.name: Project Sentinel Fair Housing
project-sentinel-fair-housing.description: Project Sentinel is a nonprofit housing agency that fights housing discrimination and helps tenants and landlords resolve disputes. In the Bay Area, its fair housing services cover Santa Clara and San Mateo counties and the City of Fremont.
project-sentinel-fair-housing.what_they_offer:
- Free fair housing education and counseling
- Investigation of housing discrimination complaints
- Help filing complaints and referrals to fair housing attorneys
- Tenant-landlord counseling and dispute resolution (in select cities, including Redwood City and Fremont, and Santa Clara County)
- HUD-certified homeowner counseling (first-time homebuyer education, foreclosure prevention, reverse mortgage counseling)
project-sentinel-fair-housing.how_to_get_it:
1. Fair housing: call 888-324-7468 or email fairhousing@housing.org (Monday–Friday, 9 AM–4:30 PM)
2. Tenant-landlord counseling: call 800-339-6043
3. Homeowner counseling: call 408-470-3730
4. Describe your housing situation or discrimination concern and staff will explain your rights
5. Services are free

bay-area-legal-aid.name: Bay Area Legal Aid (BayLegal)
bay-area-legal-aid.description: Bay Area Legal Aid is the largest civil legal aid provider in the Bay Area, offering free legal help to low-income residents of Alameda, Contra Costa, Marin, Napa, San Francisco, San Mateo, and Santa Clara counties.
bay-area-legal-aid.what_they_offer:
- Housing law (eviction defense, habitability, Section 8)
- Public benefits (CalFresh, Medi-Cal, CalWORKs appeals)
- Health care access through the Health Consumer Center (855-693-7285)
- Consumer rights and debt issues
- Domestic violence restraining orders
- Disaster legal services
- Self-help clinics and Know Your Rights materials
bay-area-legal-aid.how_to_get_it:
1. Call the Legal Advice Line at 800-551-5554 (Mon & Thu 9:30 AM–3 PM; Tue & Wed 9:30 AM–1 PM, or until capacity is reached)
2. Call right at 9:30 AM, or request a call-back or leave a voicemail, since wait times can be long
3. Complete a short confidential intake to check eligibility
4. Have your paperwork (notices, letters) ready when you call
5. If eligible, receive legal advice, brief services, or representation (no criminal matters)

legal-aid-at-work.name: Legal Aid at Work
legal-aid-at-work.description: Legal Aid at Work provides free legal services and resources to workers facing employment problems, including discrimination, wage theft, and wrongful termination.
legal-aid-at-work.what_they_offer:
- Workers' Rights Clinic (free, confidential information in Spanish, Mandarin, Cantonese, and other languages)
- Helplines for work and family issues, language rights, racial economic justice, and survivors of domestic violence (Project SURVIVE)
- Help with discrimination and harassment claims
- Wage theft, health and safety, and paid leave issues
- Disability and pregnancy accommodation
- 100+ free fact sheets and Know Your Rights resources
legal-aid-at-work.how_to_get_it:
1. Call the general line at 415-864-8848 (toll-free 866-864-8208) if you're not sure which helpline fits
2. Or use the Clinics and Helplines page to call a specific helpline
3. Services are for low-income California workers
4. Complete intake to determine eligibility
5. Receive legal advice, referrals, or representation

centro-legal-de-la-raza.name: Centro Legal de la Raza
centro-legal-de-la-raza.description: Centro Legal de la Raza provides free bilingual legal services to low-income, immigrant, and communities of color, specializing in immigration, housing, and workers' rights.
centro-legal-de-la-raza.what_they_offer:
- Immigration legal services, including help for detained people in removal proceedings, asylum seekers, and crime victims
- Tenant rights and eviction defense for Alameda and Contra Costa County tenants
- Workers' rights help for low-wage immigrant workers (wage theft, unsafe conditions, retaliation)
- Alameda County Housing Secure legal help and emergency financial assistance for tenants and homeowners
- Free Know Your Rights clinics for immigrants, tenants, and workers
- Bilingual services (English/Spanish)
centro-legal-de-la-raza.how_to_get_it:
1. Call 510-437-1554 to request a consultation or register for a clinic
2. Remote workers' rights drop-in clinics are held monthly (third Wednesday 9 AM–12 PM; 2nd, 4th, and 5th Thursdays 6–9 PM); appointments recommended
3. Tenants can join monthly tenants' rights clinics and workshops
4. To report ICE activity or get rapid response help in Alameda County, call ACILEP at 510-241-4011
5. Complete intake and eligibility screening

asian-law-caucus.name: Asian Law Caucus
asian-law-caucus.description: Asian Law Caucus provides free legal information, assistance, and referrals for low-income Asian American and Pacific Islander communities, with consultation and representation in some cases on immigration, housing, workers' rights, and civil rights.
asian-law-caucus.what_they_offer:
- Help with immigration detention and deportation
- Workers' rights (unpaid wages, wrongful termination, discrimination, unemployment insurance, health and safety)
- Free, confidential tenant consultations, with a focus on Bay Area tenants
- Civil rights help (surveillance, profiling, police misconduct)
- Pardons and commutations
- Free interpretation in 200+ languages
asian-law-caucus.how_to_get_it:
1. Call 415-896-1701 (Monday–Friday, 10 AM–12 PM and 1–3 PM)
2. Or fill out the Get Help form on the Asian Law Caucus website
3. Complete eligibility screening (services are for low-income community members)
4. Receive legal information, a referral, or consultation and representation in some cases

la-raza-centro-legal.name: La Raza Centro Legal
la-raza-centro-legal.description: La Raza Centro Legal provides free legal services and advocacy to Latino and immigrant communities in San Francisco, specializing in immigration, workers' rights, and elder and disability law.
la-raza-centro-legal.what_they_offer:
- Affirmative immigration services (applications such as citizenship and green cards)
- Immigration removal (deportation) defense and asylum
- Workers' rights for low-wage and immigrant workers
- Elder & Disability Law Program for SF residents 60+ or adults 19–59 with a disability (SSI/SSDI appeals, simple wills and trusts, advance health care directives, powers of attorney, debt collection defense)
- Bilingual services (English/Spanish)
la-raza-centro-legal.how_to_get_it:
1. Call the front desk at 415-575-3500 or email info@lrcl.org
2. Must meet program eligibility guidelines
3. Complete intake screening
4. Receive legal advice or representation

eviction-defense-collaborative.name: Eviction Defense Collaborative
eviction-defense-collaborative.description: The Eviction Defense Collaborative is the lead organization for San Francisco's Tenant Right to Counsel program, providing free legal help, rental assistance, and shelter advocacy to keep people housed.
eviction-defense-collaborative.what_they_offer:
- Free legal help and representation for tenants facing eviction (Tenant Right to Counsel)
- Help responding to unlawful detainer lawsuits and notices to quit
- Rental assistance for tenants behind on rent (RADCo)
- Shelter Client Advocacy for people at risk of losing a City-funded shelter or transitional housing placement
- Tenant rights workshops and education
eviction-defense-collaborative.how_to_get_it:
1. If you got a Summons & Complaint or a notice to quit, call the legal assistance line at 415-659-9184 or email legal@evictiondefense.org
2. Or drop in at 976 Mission Street (Mon, Tue, Wed, Fri: 10–11:30 AM and 1–2:30 PM)
3. Bring your eviction notice and any court papers
4. For shelter issues, call Shelter Client Advocacy at 415-669-0284
5. General questions: 415-947-0797

tenants-union-sf.name: San Francisco Tenants Union
tenants-union-sf.description: The San Francisco Tenants Union provides tenant counseling, education, and advocacy to help renters understand and exercise their rights under SF rent control laws.
tenants-union-sf.what_they_offer:
- Tenant counseling and advice (free for members)
- Help understanding rent control laws
- Assistance with habitability complaints
- Guidance on eviction defense
- Tenant rights workshops
- Advocacy for tenant-friendly policies
tenants-union-sf.how_to_get_it:
1. Become a member ($50/year sliding scale)
2. Attend drop-in counseling hours
3. Call the counseling line for advice
4. Attend free tenant rights workshops
5. Get referrals to legal services if needed

court-self-help-sf.name: SF Superior Court Self-Help Center
court-self-help-sf.description: The SF Superior Court Self-Help Center provides free legal information and assistance to people representing themselves in court matters.
court-self-help-sf.what_they_offer:
- Free help with court forms and procedures
- Assistance with family law matters (divorce, custody, support)
- Help with restraining orders
- Small claims court assistance
- Eviction/unlawful detainer guidance
- Referrals to legal aid organizations
court-self-help-sf.how_to_get_it:
1. Visit the Self-Help Center at SF Civic Center Courthouse
2. Or call for information
3. No appointment needed for many services
4. Bring your court papers and case information
5. Staff cannot give legal advice but can help with forms and procedures

court-self-help-alameda.name: Alameda County Court Self-Help Center
court-self-help-alameda.description: The Alameda County Superior Court Self-Help Center and Family Law Facilitator's Office gives free legal information and forms help to people who don't have a lawyer.
court-self-help-alameda.what_they_offer:
- Free help choosing and filling out court forms
- Family law (divorce, parentage, custody, visitation, support)
- Restraining orders (domestic violence, civil harassment, elder abuse)
- Small claims and eviction defense
- Guardianship, limited conservatorship, name and gender changes
- Remote workshops and referrals to community legal clinics
- Language services available
court-self-help-alameda.how_to_get_it:
1. Contact the Self-Help Center by LiveChat (Mon-Thu, 9 AM-12 PM) on the court website
2. Or call 510-272-1393 (Mon-Thu, 2-4 PM); calls returned within 5 business days
3. Get screened for an in-person or remote appointment or workshop (walk-ins not available)
4. Staff can explain procedures and forms but cannot give legal advice
5. For legal research help, the Alameda County Law Library (125 12th St, Oakland, 510-208-4832) is also open to the public

court-self-help-santa-clara.name: Santa Clara County Self-Help Center
court-self-help-santa-clara.description: The Santa Clara County Self-Help Center provides free assistance to people representing themselves in court matters.
court-self-help-santa-clara.what_they_offer:
- Free help with court processes and review of completed forms
- Online workshops (starting a divorce, parentage, financial disclosures, guardianship, limited conservatorship, eviction answers)
- Family law help (custody, visitation, child and spousal support)
- Restraining order and emergency custody help
- Landlord/tenant (eviction) help
- Guardianship, conservatorship, name and gender changes
- Referrals to local nonprofit legal services
court-self-help-santa-clara.how_to_get_it:
1. Watch an online workshop or email the Self-Help Center from the court website
2. Call 408-882-2926 or use LiveChat (Mon, Tue, Thu, 8:30 AM-1:30 PM)
3. For emergencies (restraining orders, emergency custody or guardianship, evictions), go in person to the Restraining Order Help Center at 201 N. First Street, San Jose (Mon-Thu 8:30 AM-1:30 PM, Fri 8:30 AM-12 PM)
4. Staff cannot give legal advice and only help people without an attorney

ilrc.name: Immigrant Legal Resource Center (ILRC)
ilrc.description: The Immigrant Legal Resource Center provides legal training, resources, and advocacy to advance immigrant rights, with free resources for immigrants and legal providers.
ilrc.what_they_offer:
- Know Your Rights resources in multiple languages
- Immigration legal guides and manuals
- Training for legal service providers
- Policy advocacy for immigrant rights
- Red Cards for asserting rights
- Community education resources
ilrc.how_to_get_it:
1. Visit ilrc.org for free community resources and explainers
2. Download Know Your Rights materials and free Red Card artwork to print
3. ILRC does not provide direct legal services or individual consultations
4. To find a lawyer, use the Immigration Advocates Network national legal services directory linked from ILRC's contact page
5. Immigrant-serving organizations and public defenders can request free Red Card shipments through ILRC's order form

catholic-charities-immigration.name: Catholic Charities Immigration Services
catholic-charities-immigration.description: Catholic Charities San Francisco's Center for Immigration Legal and Support Services helps immigrants in San Francisco, San Mateo, and Marin counties with citizenship, family petitions, asylum, and deportation defense.
catholic-charities-immigration.what_they_offer:
- Citizenship and naturalization applications
- Family-based petitions
- DACA and TPS
- Asylum and deportation defense, including bond hearings
- U visas, T visas, and VAWA for survivors of crime and domestic violence
- Know Your Rights workshops
- ESL classes and vocational training
catholic-charities-immigration.how_to_get_it:
1. Call 415-972-1200 (main office) or 650-285-6451, or submit the consultation request form on the website
2. Schedule a legal consultation
3. Bring all immigration documents to your appointment
4. Receive help with applications and representation
5. Catholic Charities does not charge fees over the phone or through online ads

iiba-immigration.name: Immigration Institute of the Bay Area
iiba-immigration.description: The Immigration Institute of the Bay Area (IIBA) provides free and low-cost immigration legal services, education, and citizenship classes from seven offices in six Northern California counties.
iiba-immigration.what_they_offer:
- Immigration legal consultations with an attorney or accredited representative
- Citizenship and naturalization help (N-400, N-600, fee waivers)
- Family petitions and green cards (I-130, adjustment of status)
- DACA renewals and Advance Parole
- Humanitarian relief and deportation defense
- Immigration clinics, free citizenship classes, and Know Your Rights
iiba-immigration.how_to_get_it:
1. Call the IIBA office nearest you: San Francisco (415-538-8100), Redwood City (650-587-1558), Oakland (510-451-2846), Fremont, Brentwood (925-237-8581), Napa (707-266-1568), or Petaluma (707-932-7000)
2. Consultations are by appointment only (some offices also offer online booking)
3. Speak with an IIBA attorney or qualified legal representative about your options
4. No one is denied service due to inability to pay

eblc-immigration.name: East Bay Community Law Center - Immigration
eblc-immigration.description: East Bay Community Law Center provides free immigration legal advice and representation to income-eligible East Bay residents and certain student populations.
eblc-immigration.what_they_offer:
- Free immigration legal advice and representation
- DACA and Advance Parole
- Asylum, U visas, T visas, and VAWA
- Special Immigrant Juvenile Status (SIJS) and TPS
- Adjustment of status (green card) and naturalization
- Advice on immigration effects of arrests, convictions, and public benefits
- Consultations only for employment-based visas
eblc-immigration.how_to_get_it:
1. Call EBCLC at 510-548-4040 to reach the immigration team
2. Eligible if you live in Alameda or Contra Costa County, are a UC Berkeley student, are a California Community College student or staff member, or are referred by a La Clinica school-based health center
3. Must meet income eligibility requirements
4. Complete an intake assessment to confirm eligibility
5. Receive advice, representation, or referrals

five-keys.name: Five Keys Schools and Programs
five-keys.description: Five Keys is a nonprofit charter school and organization offering free adult education (high school diploma, GED, HiSET) to Californians ages 16 and up, with a focus on people affected by incarceration, plus workforce and reentry programs.
five-keys.what_they_offer:
- Free high school diploma programs
- GED and HiSET preparation
- College Pathways program
- Workforce development and transitional employment
- Classes at 70+ teaching sites, including county jails and community locations
- Wraparound support services
five-keys.how_to_get_it:
1. Contact Five Keys at 415-734-3310 or through the website
2. Open to anyone 16 or older living in California
3. Complete enrollment and intake
4. Attend classes at a community site or program location
5. Receive supportive services while you study

project-rebound.name: Project Rebound
project-rebound.description: Project Rebound helps formerly incarcerated individuals earn college degrees at California State University campuses, providing support services and a community of peers.
project-rebound.what_they_offer:
- CSU admission support
- Financial aid navigation
- Academic advising and tutoring
- Peer mentorship from formerly incarcerated students
- Career development
- Community and belonging
- Available at 20 CSU campuses, including San Francisco State and Cal State East Bay
project-rebound.how_to_get_it:
1. Contact Project Rebound at your desired CSU
2. Complete intake and assessment
3. Receive application support
4. Enroll at CSU campus
5. Access ongoing support services
6. Join peer community

anti-recidivism-coalition.name: Anti-Recidivism Coalition (ARC)
anti-recidivism-coalition.description: The Anti-Recidivism Coalition provides reentry support, advocacy, and community for people coming home from incarceration in California, with member offices in Los Angeles and Sacramento.
anti-recidivism-coalition.what_they_offer:
- Case management, trauma-informed counseling, and mentorship
- Housing assistance
- Workforce, career readiness, and credential programs
- Education support
- Felony expungement help
- Programs inside prisons and detention facilities
- Policy advocacy
anti-recidivism-coalition.how_to_get_it:
1. Fill out the ARC member application online
2. Attend an in-person orientation (Mon-Fri, 11 AM-12 PM; arrive 15 minutes early)
3. Orientations are held at ARC's Los Angeles office (601 N. Alvarado St) or Sacramento office (2830 G St, Suite 210)
4. Meet with staff to access services and join the member community
5. Call 213-955-5885 (Los Angeles) or 916-850-3158 (Sacramento) with questions

centerforce-reentry.name: Centerforce Reentry Services
centerforce-reentry.description: Centerforce provides reentry services and family support for incarcerated individuals and their families, helping maintain connections and prepare for successful reintegration.
centerforce-reentry.what_they_offer:
- Reentry planning and case management
- Family visiting programs
- Children's services and support
- Housing assistance
- Employment readiness
- Connection to community resources
centerforce-reentry.how_to_get_it:
1. Contact Centerforce for intake
2. Currently or formerly incarcerated individuals welcome
3. Family members also eligible
4. Complete assessment
5. Access services and support

lib-001.name: Berkeley Tool Lending Library
lib-001.description: The Berkeley Public Library operates the only tool lending library in Northern California, allowing library cardholders to borrow tools for free.
lib-001.what_they_offer:
- Power tools (drills, saws, sanders)
- Lawn and garden equipment
- Hand tools (hammers, wrenches, screwdrivers)
- Specialty tools (tile cutters, pipe wrenches)
- Automotive tools
- Free to borrow with library card
lib-001.how_to_get_it:
1. Get a Berkeley Public Library card (free for residents)
2. Visit the Tool Lending Library at the South Branch
3. Browse available tools in person
4. Check out tools with your library card
5. Return within the borrowing period (typically 3-7 days)

lib-002.name: California State Parks Library Pass
lib-002.description: California State Library's Parks Pass program allows library patrons to check out day-use passes for free entry to over 200 state parks.
lib-002.what_they_offer:
- Free vehicle day-use entry to 200+ state parks
- Covers 1 vehicle with up to 9 people or 1 motorcycle
- Valid at participating state parks statewide
- Does not cover camping or special events
- Does not cover museums within parks
lib-002.how_to_get_it:
1. Have a valid library card from a participating library
2. Check your library's website for pass availability
3. Reserve or check out a parks pass
4. Bring the pass and your library card to the park
5. Return pass by the due date

lib-003.name: Calm Meditation App
lib-003.description: San Mateo County Library provides free access to the Calm app, offering guided meditations, sleep stories, and stress management tools.
lib-003.what_they_offer:
- Full access to Calm premium features
- Guided meditations
- Sleep stories
- Relaxing music
- Breathing exercises
- Stress management courses
lib-003.how_to_get_it:
1. Have a San Mateo County Library card
2. Visit smcl.org/get-calm
3. Follow instructions to create or link Calm account
4. Access Calm via web browser or mobile app
5. Enjoy unlimited access while program continues

lib-004.name: Discover & Go Museum Passes
lib-004.description: Discover & Go connects library cardholders with free and discounted admission to California museums, zoos, aquariums, and cultural institutions.
lib-004.what_they_offer:
- Free or reduced admission to many cultural institutions
- Museums, zoos, aquariums, gardens, and more
- Passes cover varying group sizes
- Available at participating libraries statewide
- New passes released regularly
lib-004.how_to_get_it:
1. Check if your library participates at discoverandgo.org
2. Log in with your library card
3. Browse available passes
4. Reserve a pass for your preferred date
5. Print or save pass to mobile device
6. Present pass at venue for entry

lib-005.name: Hoopla Digital
lib-005.description: Hoopla is a digital media service that allows library cardholders to borrow movies, TV shows, music, ebooks, audiobooks, and comics for free.
lib-005.what_they_offer:
- Streaming movies and TV shows
- Music albums
- Ebooks and audiobooks
- Comics and graphic novels
- No waitlists—instant access
- Monthly borrowing limit varies by library
lib-005.how_to_get_it:
1. Check if your library offers Hoopla
2. Download the Hoopla app or visit hoopladigital.com
3. Create an account using your library card
4. Browse and borrow content instantly
5. Content auto-returns after lending period

lib-006.name: Kanopy
lib-006.description: Kanopy is a free video streaming service for library cardholders offering thoughtful entertainment including films, documentaries, and educational content.
lib-006.what_they_offer:
- Thousands of films and documentaries
- Criterion Collection films
- Independent and international cinema
- Great Courses educational videos
- PBS documentaries
- Monthly credit system (varies by library)
lib-006.how_to_get_it:
1. Check if your library offers Kanopy
2. Visit kanopy.com and find your library
3. Sign up with your library card
4. Stream on web, mobile, or TV apps
5. Credits refresh monthly

lib-007.name: New York Times Digital Access
lib-007.description: California State Library provides free digital access to The New York Times for Californians through participating public libraries.
lib-007.what_they_offer:
- Access to NYTimes.com news articles, video, and multimedia
- Archives back to 1851
- Spanish and Chinese editions of NYTimes.com
- 72-hour passes that you can redeem again when they expire
- Does not include NYT Games, NYT Cooking, Wirecutter, or The Athletic
lib-007.how_to_get_it:
1. Get a library card from a participating California public library
2. Go to your library's New York Times page to get an access code
3. Create a free NYT account or log in, and redeem the code
4. Enjoy 72 hours of access
5. Return to your library's page to redeem a new code when the pass expires

sfpl-elibrary.name: SFPL eLibrary
sfpl-elibrary.description: San Francisco Public Library's eLibrary provides free digital access to ebooks, audiobooks, databases, learning courses, and streaming content.
sfpl-elibrary.what_they_offer:
- Ebooks and audiobooks (Libby, OverDrive)
- Digital magazines and newspapers
- Streaming movies and music
- LinkedIn Learning courses
- Research databases
- Language learning (Mango Languages)
sfpl-elibrary.how_to_get_it:
1. Get a San Francisco Public Library card (free for residents)
2. Visit sfpl.org/elibrary
3. Browse available digital resources
4. Sign in with your library card
5. Access content on computer or mobile devices

sfpl-digital-collections.name: SF Digital Collections
sfpl-digital-collections.description: DigitalSF, San Francisco Public Library's digital collections site, provides free access to more than 80,000 digitized and born-digital historical photos, documents, manuscripts, maps, oral histories, and audiovisual materials.
sfpl-digital-collections.what_they_offer:
- Historical photographs of San Francisco
- Manuscripts, documents, and publications (including local newspapers)
- Maps and ephemera
- Oral histories and audiovisual recordings
- Born-digital collections
- Free to browse without library card
sfpl-digital-collections.how_to_get_it:
1. Visit digitalsf.org
2. Browse or search collections
3. View materials for free
4. No library card required for access

open-library.name: Open Library
open-library.description: Open Library is a project of the Internet Archive that provides free access to millions of books, with the goal of creating one web page for every book ever published.
open-library.what_they_offer:
- Free ebooks to read online or borrow
- Borrowing system for in-copyright books
- Public domain books you can download
- Multiple formats available
- Community-contributed book data
- Free Open Library account (no local library card needed)
open-library.how_to_get_it:
1. Visit openlibrary.org
2. Sign up for a free Open Library account (uses an Internet Archive login)
3. Browse or search for books
4. Read online or borrow ebooks
5. Return borrowed books to allow others to read

libby-app.name: Libby by OverDrive
libby-app.description: Libby is the free reading app from OverDrive that connects library cardholders to their library's collection of ebooks, audiobooks, and magazines.
libby-app.what_they_offer:
- Ebooks from your library's collection
- Audiobooks for on-the-go listening
- Digital magazines
- Sync across devices
- Read offline
- Works with multiple library cards
libby-app.how_to_get_it:
1. Download the free Libby app (iOS or Android)
2. Open the app and find your library
3. Sign in with your library card number
4. Browse and borrow from your library's collection
5. Books automatically return—no late fees

california-digital-newspaper-collection.name: California Digital Newspaper Collection
california-digital-newspaper-collection.description: The California Digital Newspaper Collection provides free access to digitized California newspapers from 1846 to the present for historical research.
california-digital-newspaper-collection.what_they_offer:
- Digitized California newspapers from 1846-present
- Searchable full text
- Historical newspapers from across the state
- Free to access without library card
- High-quality scans of original pages
california-digital-newspaper-collection.how_to_get_it:
1. Visit cdnc.ucr.edu
2. Search by keyword, date, or location
3. Browse available newspaper titles
4. View and download pages for free
5. No registration or library card required

career-online-high-school.name: Career Online High School
career-online-high-school.description: Career Online High School is offered free by scholarship through select California public libraries, allowing adults to earn an accredited high school diploma and career certificate.
career-online-high-school.what_they_offer:
- Accredited high school diploma
- Career certificate in your chosen field
- Career portfolio with resume and cover letter
- Academic coach, certified instructors, and library staff support
- Online classes with 24/7 access
- 10 career paths, including child care, commercial driving, home care, manufacturing, office management, and security
career-online-high-school.how_to_get_it:
1. Must be 19 years of age or older
2. Have a library card in good standing at a participating library
3. Take the short "Are You Ready?" online survey at ca.careeronlinehs.org
4. Follow your library's application steps (scholarships are limited)
5. If accepted, complete coursework online
6. Graduate with diploma and career certificate

online-archive-of-california.name: Online Archive of California
online-archive-of-california.description: The Online Archive of California provides free access to more than 60,000 collection guides (finding aids) from over 350 California libraries, archives, and museums.
online-archive-of-california.what_they_offer:
- 60,000+ collection guides to archival collections
- Primary source materials
- Collections from 350+ institutions
- Photographs and documents
- Historical records
- Free to search and browse
online-archive-of-california.how_to_get_it:
1. Visit oac.cdlib.org
2. Search or browse collections by topic or institution
3. Find detailed descriptions of archival materials
4. Identify materials of interest
5. Contact holding institution for access to originals

alameda-county-library-digital.name: Alameda County Library Digital Resources
alameda-county-library-digital.description: Alameda County Library provides free digital resources including ebooks, audiobooks, databases, and online learning for cardholders.
alameda-county-library-digital.what_they_offer:
- Ebooks and audiobooks via Libby
- Streaming video and music
- Online databases and research tools
- Learning platforms (LinkedIn Learning, etc.)
- Magazines and newspapers
- Language learning resources
alameda-county-library-digital.how_to_get_it:
1. Get an Alameda County Library card (free for residents)
2. Visit aclibrary.org/resource
3. Browse available digital resources
4. Sign in with your library card
5. Access content on any device

oakland-library-digital.name: Oakland Public Library Digital Resources
oakland-library-digital.description: Oakland Public Library provides free digital resources including ebooks, audiobooks, streaming media, and learning platforms for Oakland cardholders.
oakland-library-digital.what_they_offer:
- Ebooks and audiobooks
- Streaming movies and music
- Online learning courses
- Research databases
- Magazines and newspapers
- Language learning
oakland-library-digital.how_to_get_it:
1. Get an Oakland Public Library card (free for Oakland residents)
2. Visit oaklandlibrary.org/resource
3. Browse available digital resources
4. Sign in with your library card
5. Access content on any device

san-mateo-county-library-digital.name: San Mateo County Library Digital Resources
san-mateo-county-library-digital.description: San Mateo County Library offers free digital resources including ebooks, audiobooks, streaming content, and online learning for all cardholders.
san-mateo-county-library-digital.what_they_offer:
- Ebooks and audiobooks via Libby
- Streaming video (Kanopy)
- Calm meditation app access
- LinkedIn Learning
- Research databases
- Digital magazines
san-mateo-county-library-digital.how_to_get_it:
1. Get a San Mateo County Library card (free for residents)
2. Visit smcl.org/resource
3. Browse available digital resources
4. Sign in with your library card
5. Access content on any device

peninsula-library-digital.name: Peninsula Library System E-Services
peninsula-library-digital.description: Peninsula Library System provides e-services and digital resources for cardholders from member libraries throughout San Mateo County.
peninsula-library-digital.what_they_offer:
- Ebooks and eAudiobooks (eMedia) through your member library
- eMagazines
- Research databases with full-text articles
- Online courses, videos, and homework help
- Discover & Go free passes to local museums and cultural institutions
- California Missions ebooks for elementary students
peninsula-library-digital.how_to_get_it:
1. Have a library card from a PLS member library
2. Visit plsinfo.org/e-services
3. Choose your library to see its available resources
4. Sign in with your library card
5. Access content online

contra-costa-library-digital.name: Contra Costa County Library Digital Resources
contra-costa-library-digital.description: Contra Costa County Library provides free digital resources including ebooks, audiobooks, streaming media, and learning platforms for cardholders.
contra-costa-library-digital.what_they_offer:
- Ebooks and audiobooks via Libby
- Streaming movies and TV
- Online learning platforms
- Research databases
- Digital magazines and newspapers
- Language learning resources
contra-costa-library-digital.how_to_get_it:
1. Get a Contra Costa County Library card (free for residents)
2. Visit ccclib.org/resource
3. Browse available digital resources
4. Sign in with your library card
5. Access content on any device

sfpl-services.name: San Francisco Public Library Services
sfpl-services.description: San Francisco Public Library offers a wide range of free services and programs beyond just books, including digital resources, programs, and community offerings.
sfpl-services.what_they_offer:
- Digital resources (eBooks, streaming, databases)
- Free WiFi, public computer reservations, printing and scanning
- Free programs and events
- Homework help and an online high school diploma program
- Jobs and careers resources
- Social worker program, services for older adults, and Jail and Reentry Services (JARS)
- Discover & Go museum passes
sfpl-services.how_to_get_it:
1. Get a San Francisco Public Library card (free)
2. Visit sfpl.org/services
3. Explore available services
4. Many services available online or in-person
5. Some programs require registration

santa-clara-county-library-digital.name: Santa Clara County Library Digital Resources
santa-clara-county-library-digital.description: Santa Clara County Library District offers free digital resources including ebooks, audiobooks, streaming content, and online learning for cardholders.
santa-clara-county-library-digital.what_they_offer:
- Ebooks and audiobooks via Libby
- Streaming movies and music
- Online learning (LinkedIn Learning, The Great Courses)
- Research databases
- Digital magazines
- Language learning resources
santa-clara-county-library-digital.how_to_get_it:
1. Get a Santa Clara County Library card (free for residents)
2. Visit sccld.org/resource
3. Browse available digital resources
4. Sign in with your library card
5. Access content on any device

marin-county-library-digital.name: Marin County Free Library Digital Resources
marin-county-library-digital.description: Marin County Free Library provides free digital resources including ebooks, audiobooks, streaming media, and learning platforms for cardholders.
marin-county-library-digital.what_they_offer:
- Ebooks and audiobooks via Libby
- Streaming video and music
- Online learning platforms
- Research databases
- Digital magazines and newspapers
- Language learning
marin-county-library-digital.how_to_get_it:
1. Get a Marin County Free Library card (free for residents)
2. Visit marinlibrary.org/resource
3. Browse available digital resources
4. Sign in with your library card
5. Access content on any device

sonoma-county-library-digital.name: Sonoma County Library eLibrary
sonoma-county-library-digital.description: Sonoma County Library provides free eLibrary resources including ebooks, audiobooks, streaming content, and online learning for all cardholders.
sonoma-county-library-digital.what_they_offer:
- Ebooks and audiobooks via Libby
- Streaming movies and music
- Online learning platforms
- Research databases
- Digital magazines
- Homework help resources
sonoma-county-library-digital.how_to_get_it:
1. Get a Sonoma County Library card (free for residents)
2. Visit sonomalibrary.org/elibrary
3. Browse available digital resources
4. Sign in with your library card
5. Access content on any device

solano-county-library-digital.name: Solano County Library 24/7 Digital Library
solano-county-library-digital.description: Solano County Library provides 24/7 digital library resources including ebooks, audiobooks, streaming media, and online learning for cardholders.
solano-county-library-digital.what_they_offer:
- Ebooks and audiobooks via Libby
- Streaming video and music
- Online learning platforms
- Research databases
- Digital magazines and newspapers
- Available 24/7
solano-county-library-digital.how_to_get_it:
1. Get a Solano County Library card (free for residents)
2. Visit solanolibrary.gov/247-digital-library
3. Browse available digital resources
4. Sign in with your library card
5. Access content anytime, on any device

napa-county-library-databases.name: Napa County Library Databases
napa-county-library-databases.description: Napa County Library provides free access to research databases and digital resources for all cardholders.
napa-county-library-databases.what_they_offer:
- Research databases
- Ebooks, audiobooks, and streaming (Libby, Hoopla, Kanopy)
- Digital magazines and newspapers (New York Times, Wall Street Journal, PressReader)
- Learning resources and live homework help (Learning Express, Brainfuse HelpNow)
- Consumer and business information (Consumer Reports, Value Line, AtoZdatabases)
- Local newspaper archives (Napa Valley Register, San Francisco Chronicle)
napa-county-library-databases.how_to_get_it:
1. Get a Napa County Library card (free for residents)
2. Visit the library's A-Z Resources page
3. Browse available resources
4. Sign in with your library card
5. Access content on any device

banfield-foundation.name: Banfield Foundation - Pet Owner Resources
banfield-foundation.description: The Banfield Foundation is a nonprofit that funds nonprofit partners and shares a list of organizations that help pet owners afford vet care and pet food. It does not provide direct support to individual pet owners.
banfield-foundation.what_they_offer:
- List of national veterinary care assistance programs (such as The Pet Fund, RedRover, Brown Dog Foundation)
- National pet food assistance programs
- Local assistance programs listed by state
- List of crowdfunding sites for pet medical costs
- Information on HOPE Funds at Banfield Pet Hospital for income-qualified owners of pets with life-threatening conditions (treatment must be at a Banfield hospital)
- Safer Together resources for domestic violence survivors and their pets, and disaster preparedness tips
banfield-foundation.how_to_get_it:
1. Visit the Banfield Foundation resources page
2. Review the national programs, or pick your state under State programs
3. Contact listed organizations directly for assistance
4. For HOPE Funds, contact your local Banfield Pet Hospital
5. If you still need help, contact your local humane society or shelter

bebhs-spay-bay.name: Berkeley-East Bay Humane Society - Spay the Bay
bebhs-spay-bay.description: Berkeley Humane's Spay the Bay program provides low-cost spay/neuter surgery and vaccine clinics for Bay Area dog and cat guardians who are struggling financially. Services are currently located inside PetSmart in Pinole while the Berkeley location is closed for construction.
bebhs-spay-bay.what_they_offer:
- Low-cost spay/neuter by appointment: cat neuter $150, cat spay $175, dog neuter $300, dog spay $450
- Includes exam, surgery, post-op pain medication, and a free microchip
- Add-on rabies vaccine if needed ($25 dogs, $35 cats)
- Low-cost core vaccine clinics on select Fridays (no appointment needed; free microchip with a vaccine)
- For owned dogs and cats ages 4 months to 5 years; cats 3 lbs+, dogs 4-45 lbs; no flat-faced breeds
- Limit of 3 pets per household per year
bebhs-spay-bay.how_to_get_it:
1. Review the eligibility rules and process on the Spay the Bay page
2. Submit an online appointment request (current wait is about 1-2 months)
3. Staff will contact you to set a date and collect a non-refundable deposit ($30 per cat, $90 per dog) that goes toward the cost
4. Bring your pet to 1380 Fitzgerald Drive, Pinole (inside PetSmart) on your appointment day
5. For vaccines, check the clinic dates listed on the page, fill out the request form, and arrive during clinic hours

hssv-pet-pantry.name: HSSV Pet Pantry
hssv-pet-pantry.description: The Humane Society Silicon Valley's Pet Pantry program helps families keep their pets by providing free pet food during times of financial hardship.
hssv-pet-pantry.what_they_offer:
- Free dog and cat food (set amount based on your initial application)
- Pick up every 30 days
- Short-term safety net, not meant to be a pet's only food source
- Food depends on donations and availability
- Cat colony caretakers are not served
hssv-pet-pantry.how_to_get_it:
1. Must be a Santa Clara County resident experiencing financial hardship
2. Visit the Pet Pantry Warehouse in person to sign up (1116 Wrigley Way, Milpitas)
3. Go Thursday-Sunday, 12:00-3:30 pm
4. Bring a photo ID each time you pick up food
5. Return every 30 days as needed
6. Questions? Call ext. 110 or email petpantry@hssv.org

humane-world.name: Humane World for Animals
humane-world.description: Humane World for Animals (formerly the Humane Society of the United States) offers a guide for pet owners who are struggling to afford pet food and vet care, helping keep families and pets together.
humane-world.what_they_offer:
- List of national organizations that give financial help for pet care
- Tips for finding free pet food pantries and low-cost vet care near you
- Veterinary payment options (payment plans, CareCredit and similar services)
- Fundraising and crowdfunding ideas for vet bills
- Pet insurance and other ways to plan for future costs
humane-world.how_to_get_it:
1. Visit the Humane World for Animals affordability resources page
2. Read the sections on pet food, vet care, and financial assistance
3. Use the linked search tools to find help near you
4. Contact listed organizations directly

joybound-vet-care.name: Joybound People & Pets - Community Veterinary Care
joybound-vet-care.description: Joybound People & Pets (formerly Tony La Russa's ARF) Community Veterinary Care provides low-cost, non-urgent veterinary care at its Walnut Creek clinic for Contra Costa County residents facing serious financial crisis.
joybound-vet-care.what_they_offer:
- Low-cost, non-urgent medical treatment for pets
- Care at Joybound's clinic in Walnut Creek
- Care for dogs and cats
- Not for routine, preventive, elective, exploratory, or specialty care
joybound-vet-care.how_to_get_it:
1. Must be a Contra Costa County resident facing serious financial crisis
2. Household income must be at or below HUD very low income limits
3. Contact Joybound's Resource Center at 925-256-1273 ext. 450
4. Provide photo ID and proof of income for all household members (not including dependents)
5. If approved, schedule an appointment for your pet

joybound-pet-food.name: Joybound People & Pets - Free Pet Food
joybound-pet-food.description: Joybound's FoodShare pantry helps Contra Costa County families keep their pets by providing free pet food at pantry events.
joybound-pet-food.what_they_offer:
- Free dry dog and cat food
- Wet/canned food when available (not guaranteed)
- No special or prescription diets
- First-come, first-served while supplies last
- Helps prevent pet surrender due to cost
joybound-pet-food.how_to_get_it:
1. Must be a Contra Costa County resident, 18 or older
2. Check Joybound's website or events calendar for upcoming FoodShare pantry dates
3. Arrive early at 2890 Mitchell Drive, Walnut Creek (distribution starts at 2 pm and fills up quickly)
4. Questions? Email cs@joybound.org or call the Resource Center at ext. 450

joybound-vaccinations.name: Joybound People & Pets - Free Vaccination Clinics
joybound-vaccinations.description: Joybound holds free vaccine and microchip clinics at locations throughout Contra Costa County to help ensure all pets have access to essential preventive care.
joybound-vaccinations.what_they_offer:
- Free rabies and DAPP vaccines for dogs
- Free rabies and FVRCP vaccines for cats
- Free microchips for dogs and cats
- Pet food while supplies last
- Brief health check before vaccination (not a full exam)
- No canine influenza, leptospirosis, or Bordetella vaccines
joybound-vaccinations.how_to_get_it:
1. Check the Joybound website for upcoming clinic dates and locations
2. Must be a Contra Costa County resident (proof required) and 18 or older
3. Pets must be at least 6 weeks old; dogs on leash, cats in carriers
4. Bring prior vaccine records if you have them
5. Arrive early; service is first come, first served

joybound-pet-safety-net.name: Joybound People & Pets - Pet Safety Net
joybound-pet-safety-net.description: Joybound's Pet Safety Net helps qualifying Contra Costa County residents with critical resources to keep their pets at home and out of shelters.
joybound-pet-safety-net.what_they_offer:
- Veterinary treatment with good prognosis, spay/neuter, vaccines, and microchips
- Pet food, cat litter, and pet supplies
- Pet rental deposits and shelter impound fees
- Temporary boarding
- Behavior and training help
- Medical grooming and yard or fence repairs
joybound-pet-safety-net.how_to_get_it:
1. Must be a Contra Costa County resident who meets program qualifications
2. Contact Joybound's Resource Center at 925-256-1273 ext. 450
3. Staff will assess needs and available resources
4. Receive assistance based on availability and need

joybound-spay-neuter.name: Joybound People & Pets - Spay/Neuter Clinic
joybound-spay-neuter.description: Joybound's spay and neuter clinic in Walnut Creek, plus its mobile clinic, offers low-cost spay and neuter surgery for community dogs and cats of Contra Costa County residents.
joybound-spay-neuter.what_they_offer:
- Low-cost spay and neuter surgeries for dogs and cats
- Open to Contra Costa County residents
- Free microchip, plus age-appropriate vaccines and post-surgery pain medication
- Mobile spay/neuter clinic visits several times a month
- Pet Safety Net may help qualifying residents with the cost
joybound-spay-neuter.how_to_get_it:
1. Call the Joybound spay/neuter clinic at 925-296-3125 to schedule
2. Pay the required non-refundable deposit
3. Follow pre-surgery instructions
4. Bring pet to scheduled appointment
5. Pay the remaining fee at time of service

marin-humane-pet-care.name: Marin Humane - Pet Safety Net
marin-humane-pet-care.description: Marin Humane's Pet Safety Net helps low-income Marin County residents pay for veterinary care, vaccinations, food, and other services so they can keep their pets.
marin-humane-pet-care.what_they_offer:
- Veterinary treatment with good prognosis (through pre-approved local vets)
- Spay/neuter assistance, vaccinations, and microchips
- Free community clinics
- Pet food and supplies
- Pet rental deposits and dog license fees
- Behavior and training help, medical grooming, and humane euthanasia
marin-humane-pet-care.how_to_get_it:
