1. Must be 18+, live in Marin County with your pet, and be the pet's regular caretaker
2. Household income must be at or below HUD very low income limits
3. Submit an application with proof of income for all household members, proof of residency, and proof you are the pet's guardian
4. For vet care, call the Pet Safety Net office at 415-506-6255 for pre-authorization before making an appointment (past expenses can't be reimbursed)
5. Pets must be spayed/neutered (or have a plan to be) and dogs licensed; help is available once every two calendar years, as funds allow

muttville-cuddle-club.name: Muttville Senior Dog Rescue - Cuddle Club
muttville-cuddle-club.description: Muttville's Cuddle Club brings the joy of dogs to adults 62+ through events where they can spend time with senior dogs—no adoption required.
muttville-cuddle-club.what_they_offer:
- Cuddle time with senior dogs
- Social events for adults 62 and older
- Animal interaction and companionship
- No adoption required
- Groups can request to set up a Cuddle Club event
muttville-cuddle-club.how_to_get_it:
1. Must be 62 years or older
2. Email Muttville (seniorsforseniors@muttville.org) to find out when the next Cuddle Club is happening
3. Or email to set up a Cuddle Club event for your group
4. Attend and enjoy time with the dogs

muttville-seniors-for-seniors.name: Muttville Senior Dog Rescue - Seniors for Seniors
muttville-seniors-for-seniors.description: Muttville's Seniors for Seniors program waives the adoption fee on senior dogs for adopters 62 and older, helping both seniors and dogs find companionship.
muttville-seniors-for-seniors.what_they_offer:
- $250 adoption fee waived for adopters 62+
- Welcome kit with harness, collar, leash, and dog bowls
- Starter supply of food and medication, plus a dog bed
- Home modifications like a dog gate or stairs if needed
muttville-seniors-for-seniors.how_to_get_it:
1. Must be 62 years or older
2. Visit Muttville's website to view adoptable senior dogs
3. Fill out the Seniors for Seniors Adoption Questionnaire (or email seniorsforseniors@muttville.org)
4. Follow Muttville's standard adoption process
5. Take home your new companion with the adoption fee waived

phs-mobile-spay-neuter.name: Peninsula Humane Society & SPCA - Low-Cost Spay/Neuter Clinic
phs-mobile-spay-neuter.description: Peninsula Humane Society & SPCA's clinic at its Coyote Point shelter in San Mateo provides low-cost spay and neuter surgery for members of the public, with San Mateo County residents given priority booking.
phs-mobile-spay-neuter.what_they_offer:
- Low-cost spay/neuter surgery for dogs, cats, and rabbits
- Appointments from the 1st-15th of each month reserved for San Mateo County residents
- San Mateo County residents who need more help can ask the County of San Mateo for a Spay/Neuter Assistance Voucher
- Vaccines available at check-in for an extra cost if your pet lacks proof
- Dogs and cats must be at least 4 months old; no flat-faced (brachycephalic) breeds
phs-mobile-spay-neuter.how_to_get_it:
1. Book online (appointments open one month ahead at midnight and fill quickly)
2. Pay the $25 non-refundable deposit when booking (applied to your fees)
3. Bring proof of residency, vaccine records (DHPP/FVRCP and rabies), and any county voucher
4. Drop off at 12 Airport Blvd, San Mateo (dogs 7:00-7:30 am; cats and rabbits 7:30-8:00 am)
5. Questions? Call the spay/neuter line at 650-340-7015

phs-vaccine-clinics.name: Peninsula Humane Society SPCA Low-Cost Vaccine Clinics
phs-vaccine-clinics.description: Peninsula Humane Society & SPCA holds low-cost vaccination and microchip clinics for dogs and cats at its Coyote Point shelter in San Mateo.
phs-vaccine-clinics.what_they_offer:
- Vaccines for rabies, DHPP, FVRCP, and FeLV: $15 per vaccine
- Microchips: $30
- Dog and cat licenses available for purchase
- For cats and dogs of all ages
- Clinics on the 1st and 3rd Saturday (9:00-10:50 am) and 2nd Wednesday (6:00-7:50 pm) of each month
phs-vaccine-clinics.how_to_get_it:
1. Check the PHS vaccination clinic page for upcoming dates
2. Register online for an appointment (appointment only; sign-ups open about 2 weeks ahead and fill quickly)
3. If the clinic is full, call 650-340-7022 ext. 332 to join the waitlist
4. Bring your pet to the Coyote Point shelter at your appointment time
phs-vaccine-clinics.timeframe: 1st and 3rd Saturdays and 2nd Wednesday of each month

pet-help-finder.name: Pet Help Finder
pet-help-finder.description: Pet Help Finder is a free search tool from Open Door Veterinary Collective that helps pet owners find financially friendly veterinary care, pet food, and other pet resources near them.
pet-help-finder.what_they_offer:
- Searchable listings of free, discounted, and sliding-scale vet care
- Spay/neuter and vaccine clinics
- Vets offering payment plans or other payment options
- Pet food and supply assistance
- Available in English and Spanish
pet-help-finder.how_to_get_it:
1. Visit pethelpfinder.org
2. Choose the type of help you need (for example, Veterinary Services)
3. Enter your city, state, or zip code and search
4. Contact providers directly for services

pets-in-need.name: Pets in Need - Low-Cost Vet Services
pets-in-need.description: Pets in Need runs a Community Veterinary Clinic in Redwood City for affordable wellness care, plus a low-cost vaccine clinic and spay/neuter clinic at its Palo Alto shelter.
pets-in-need.what_they_offer:
- Community Veterinary Clinic (Redwood City): wellness consultations ($85), vaccines, flea/tick and heartworm prevention, microchipping, deworming, and basic tests
- Community Clinic is for wellness visits only (no x-rays, dental, surgery, or emergency care)
- Walk-in vaccine clinic (Palo Alto): every Wednesday 9:30-11:30 am, first come first served; most vaccines $25, microchips $30
- Low-cost spay/neuter surgeries for cats and dogs (Palo Alto), open to residents of any city; $100 deposit to book
pets-in-need.how_to_get_it:
1. Book a Community Clinic appointment online (Thursdays, by appointment only)
2. For vaccines, bring your pet to the Palo Alto shelter (3281 E. Bayshore Rd) on a Wednesday morning
3. For spay/neuter, book online and pay the deposit; pets must be at least 4 months old
4. Pay remaining fees at time of service

pets-of-homeless.name: Pets of the Homeless
pets-of-homeless.description: Pets of the Homeless (Feeding Pets of the Homeless) is a nonprofit that helps people experiencing homelessness care for their pets with free pet food and emergency veterinary care.
pets-of-homeless.what_they_offer:
- Map of pet food and supply providers, pet-friendly shelters, and other resources
- Emergency veterinary care funding for sick or injured pets, paid directly to the vet
- Limit of 3 pets per owner; does not cover routine wellness, vaccines, or spay/neuter (unless required for housing)
- Cannot pay past bills or reimburse treatment already provided
pets-of-homeless.how_to_get_it:
1. Visit petsofthehomeless.org and use the location finder for food and supplies near you (call providers first to confirm supplies)
2. For emergency vet care, submit the online application
3. Have a social worker, shelter staff, outreach worker, or similar contact verify your living situation
4. Applications are reviewed in order received, Monday-Friday 8 am-4 pm Pacific

sf-spca-community-clinic.name: San Francisco SPCA - Community Clinic
sf-spca-community-clinic.description: The SF SPCA's Community Veterinary Clinic in the Excelsior neighborhood provides affordable preventative care, including vaccines, parasite protection, and treatment for minor conditions.
sf-spca-community-clinic.what_they_offer:
- Dog and cat vaccines
- Flea, tick, and heartworm medication
- Treatment for minor skin, ear, and eye issues
- Treatment for minor illnesses such as vomiting and diarrhea
- Spay/neuter consultations and scheduling (surgery done at the Mission Campus hospital)
- Does not provide emergency care, x-rays, lab work, or health certificates
- Se habla español; Chinese spoken
sf-spca-community-clinic.how_to_get_it:
1. Book an appointment online or text 415-554-3084
2. Bring your pet to 4527 Mission Street at your scheduled time (open Wednesday-Saturday, 8 am-6 pm)
3. Pay fees at time of service

sf-spca-spay-neuter.name: San Francisco SPCA - Spay/Neuter
sf-spca-spay-neuter.description: The SF SPCA's Spay/Neuter Clinic at its Mission Campus offers affordable spay and neuter surgery for cats and dogs, with financial assistance available.
sf-spca-spay-neuter.what_they_offer:
- Affordable spay and neuter surgery for dogs and cats
- Pain medication, recovery cone, and nail trim included
- Financial assistance available for spay/neuter surgeries
- Add-on services: microchipping, vaccines, parasite treatment, heartworm and FIV/FeLV testing
sf-spca-spay-neuter.how_to_get_it:
1. Book online or text 415-554-3084 (Tuesday-Saturday, 8 am-6 pm)
2. Ask about cost and financial assistance when scheduling
3. On surgery day, cats check in 7:30-8 am and dogs 8-8:30 am; pickup is at 4:30 pm
4. Pay fees at or before check-in

sf-aid-for-animals.name: SF Aid for Animals (SFAFA)
sf-aid-for-animals.description: San Francisco Aid for Animals partners with Bay Area veterinary hospitals to fund urgent care for pets whose owners cannot afford it. Participating hospitals match SFAFA grants with their own services.
sf-aid-for-animals.what_they_offer:
- Grants for urgent veterinary care, paid to the treating hospital
- Participating hospitals match grants with discounted services
- Helps prevent economic euthanasia
- Does not give money directly to pet owners
sf-aid-for-animals.how_to_get_it:
1. Check SFAFA's list of participating veterinary hospitals
2. Take your pet to a participating hospital for treatment
3. Tell the hospital you cannot afford the full cost and ask about an SFAFA grant
4. The hospital decides whether your case qualifies and handles the paperwork with SFAFA
5. Questions: email info@sfafa.org

the-pet-fund.name: The Pet Fund
the-pet-fund.description: The Pet Fund is a national nonprofit that provides one-time grants for non-basic, non-urgent veterinary care to U.S. pet owners who cannot afford treatment.
the-pet-fund.what_they_offer:
- One-time grants for non-basic, non-urgent care (cancer treatment, heart disease, chronic conditions, endocrine and eye diseases)
- Does NOT cover basic care (spay/neuter, dental, vaccines), urgent care, or emergencies
- Usually has a waitlist, so care must be able to wait
- For already-adopted animals of U.S. residents
the-pet-fund.how_to_get_it:
1. Email The Pet Fund first with a description of your pet's medical needs and your phone number
2. Wait for staff to review; do not send an application until they tell you to
3. If invited, complete The Pet Fund application
4. Expect a waitlist before funding

vet-billing.name: Vet Billing - Payment Plans
vet-billing.description: VetBilling offers interest-free installment payment plans through participating veterinary clinics, with a searchable directory of clinics that use it.
vet-billing.what_they_offer:
- Directory of participating vets that offer VetBilling payment plans
- Interest-free installments paid by automatic withdrawal from a bank account or card
- No penalty for paying off early
- Each clinic sets its own eligibility; some may do a soft credit check or require two payment methods
vet-billing.how_to_get_it:
1. Visit vetbilling.com/find-vet and search by location
2. Contact a participating clinic directly (especially if you are not a current client)
3. Ask the clinic if you qualify for a payment plan
4. Set up the plan at the clinic (plans cannot be set up on the website)

vetco-clinics.name: VETCO Clinics
vetco-clinics.description: Vetco Vaccination Clinics inside Petco stores provide low-cost preventive care for dogs and cats, including vaccines, testing, parasite prevention, and microchipping.
vetco-clinics.what_they_offer:
- Dog and cat vaccines (rabies, distemper/parvo, leptospirosis, bordetella, feline leukemia, and more)
- Puppy, kitten, and adult vaccine packages
- Microchipping
- Heartworm and other preventive testing
- Flea, tick, and heartworm prevention and deworming
- Located inside Petco stores; prices vary by location
vetco-clinics.how_to_get_it:
1. Visit vetcoclinics.com to find a clinic at a Petco near you
2. Book an appointment online (vaccinations are by appointment only)
3. Bring your pet to the store at your appointment time
4. Pay at time of service

vip-petcare.name: VIP Petcare
vip-petcare.description: VIP Petcare runs pop-up preventive care clinics at pet stores such as Pet Food Express, Tractor Supply, and Pet Supplies Plus, offering affordable care with upfront pricing and no appointment needed.
vip-petcare.what_they_offer:
- Core and lifestyle vaccinations
- Microchipping
- Heartworm, fecal, and tick disease testing
- Flea, tick, and heartworm prevention
- No office visit fee (a small medical disposal fee applies per pet)
- Clinic dates, times, and prices vary by location
vip-petcare.how_to_get_it:
1. Visit vippetcare.com to find a clinic location and its dates and prices
2. Pre-register online to join the virtual line, or walk in and register at the clinic
3. Pets are seen in order of registration and arrival
4. Pay at time of service

imls-aircraft-carrier-hornet-foundation.name: Aircraft Carrier Hornet Foundation
imls-aircraft-carrier-hornet-foundation.description: Museum dedicated to preserving and presenting local and regional history.

ca-sp-albany-smr.name: Albany SMR
ca-sp-albany-smr.description: Albany State Marine Reserve is an urban shoreline park at the northern end of McLaughlin Eastshore State Park that protects marine habitat in the eastern San Francisco Bay.
ca-sp-albany-smr.what_they_offer:
- Shoreline hiking trails and bay vista points
- Beach area, fishing, and windsurfing
- Nature and wildlife viewing
- Parking and drinking water
- Dogs allowed
- No camping
ca-sp-albany-smr.how_to_get_it:
California State Parks does not list a day-use fee for this park.

**Getting there:** From I-80/580, take the Albany/Buchanan St exit and follow the western extension of Buchanan Street to the parking areas.

nps-alca.name: Alcatraz Island
nps-alca.description: Alcatraz Island, home to the infamous former federal penitentiary. Take a ferry to explore the cellhouse, gardens, and learn about the island's rich history from Civil War fort to Native American occupation.
nps-alca.what_they_offer:
- Free or low-cost access to trails, beaches, and historic sites
- Ranger-led walks, talks, and educational programs
- Visitor centers with exhibits and park information
- Junior Ranger programs for children
nps-alca.how_to_get_it:
Most National Park Service sites in the Bay Area offer free admission. Some sites have entrance fees:
- Standard entrance fee: $15-$35 per vehicle (where applicable)
- Alcatraz ferry tickets sold separately

**Save with park passes:**
- **America the Beautiful Pass**: $80/year for unlimited access to 2,000+ federal recreation areas
- **Every Kid Outdoors Pass**: Free for 4th graders and their families
- **Access Pass**: Free lifetime pass for visitors with permanent disabilities
- **Senior Pass**: $80 lifetime or $20/year for ages 62+

imls-alexander-f-morrison-planetarium.name: Alexander F. Morrison Planetarium
imls-alexander-f-morrison-planetarium.description: Part of California Academy of Sciences, Morrison Planetarium is the largest all-digital dome in the world featuring stunning visualizations of the cosmos.

america-the-beautiful-pass.name: America the Beautiful — NPS Pass
america-the-beautiful-pass.description: The National Park Service offers lifetime and annual passes providing access to over 2,000 federal recreation sites across the United States, including national parks, wildlife refuges, and forests.
america-the-beautiful-pass.what_they_offer:
- Senior Pass (U.S. citizens/residents 62+): $80 lifetime or $20 annual
- Military Pass: Free annual pass for current U.S. military and dependents
- Military Lifetime Pass: Free for veterans and Gold Star Family members
- Access Pass: Free lifetime pass for U.S. citizens/residents with a permanent disability
- 4th Grade Pass: Free annual pass for U.S. fourth graders
- Annual Pass: $80 for U.S. residents ($250 for non-residents)
- All passes cover entrance fees and standard amenity fees
america-the-beautiful-pass.how_to_get_it: Get a pass in person at one of 1,000+ federal recreation sites, order online from the USGS Store (allow about 3 weeks for delivery), or buy a digital pass through Recreation.gov. Access and military passes require documentation of eligibility.

imls-american-bookbinders-museum.name: American Bookbinders Museum
imls-american-bookbinders-museum.description: The only museum of its kind in North America, showcasing the artistry, history, and craft of bookbinding from the 1600s to present.

imls-anderson-art-collection.name: Anderson Art Collection
imls-anderson-art-collection.description: Private collection of 20th century American art available through tours and loans to museums worldwide.

ca-sp-angel-island-sp.name: Angel Island SP
ca-sp-angel-island-sp.description: Angel Island State Park is an island park in San Francisco Bay reached by ferry or private boat, with hiking and biking trails, bay views, camping, and history sites including the U.S. Immigration Station and Civil War-era Camp Reynolds.
ca-sp-angel-island-sp.what_they_offer:
- Hiking and biking trails with views of the bay
- Tent, group, and remote campsites (reserve up to 6 months ahead at ReserveCalifornia.com)
- Immigration Station detention barracks (limited hours; $5 adults, $3 youth 5-17, under 5 free) and free Angel Island Immigration Museum
- Seasonal café, bike rentals, and tram tours
- Park open 8 am to sunset; phone (415) 435-5390
ca-sp-angel-island-sp.how_to_get_it:
**Fees:**
- Park entry: $3 adults, $2 youth, children under 5 free
- Private boat dock: $15 per day
- Ferry fares are separate and set by ferry operators

**Save with park passes:** Angel Island accepts the Disabled Discount Pass and Distinguished Veteran Pass for dock slips and mooring, and the California Explorer, Golden Poppy, Golden Bear, and Senior Golden Bear passes for day-use boat slips.

ca-sp-ano-nuevo-sp.name: Ano Nuevo SP
ca-sp-ano-nuevo-sp.description: Año Nuevo State Park on the San Mateo coast is home to one of the world's largest mainland breeding colonies of northern elephant seals, with a Marine Education Center and coastal trails.
ca-sp-ano-nuevo-sp.what_they_offer:
- Elephant seal viewing: self-guided from April to November with a free Visitor Permit (issued 8:30 am-3:30 pm at the entrance)
- Docent-led guided seal walks required during breeding season (mid-December through March), reserved through ReserveCalifornia.com; the viewing area is closed December 1-14
- Equal Access Tours for visitors needing mobility assistance (phone reservations)
- Marine Education Center with natural history exhibits
- Day use only (no camping); no pets allowed
- Open 8:30 am to sunset; phone (650) 879-2025
ca-sp-ano-nuevo-sp.how_to_get_it:
**Fees:**
- Day use: $10 per vehicle ($9 with a senior 62+)
- Guided seal walks require a reservation during breeding season

**Save with park passes:** Año Nuevo accepts the California Explorer, Golden Poppy, Disabled Discount, Distinguished Veteran, Golden Bear, and Senior Golden Bear passes, plus the California State Library Parks Pass (free to check out at public libraries).

recgov-antioch-dunes-national-wildlife-r.name: Antioch Dunes National Wildlife Refuge
recgov-antioch-dunes-national-wildlife-r.description: Antioch Dunes National Wildlife Refuge is the only national wildlife refuge in the country established to protect endangered plants and insects – the Antioch Dunes evening primrose, the Contra Costa wallflower, and the Lange's metalmark butterfly. Created in 1980, the 55-acre refuge was once part of a larger sand dune system that stretched two miles along the southern bank of the San Joaquin River east of the City of Antioch. The sand dunes were formed by ancient deposits of glacial sands carrie
recgov-antioch-dunes-national-wildlife-r.what_they_offer: Outdoor recreation including hiking, wildlife viewing, and nature experiences. Some sites offer camping, picnicking, and water activities.
recgov-antioch-dunes-national-wildlife-r.how_to_get_it: Visit Recreation.gov to check availability, make reservations, and plan your visit. Some areas are free to visit while others may require permits or fees.

aquarium-of-bay.name: Aquarium of the Bay
aquarium-of-bay.description: Aquarium of the Bay is a nonprofit aquarium located on Pier 39 in San Francisco, dedicated to protecting, restoring, and inspiring conservation of San Francisco Bay and its watershed. The aquarium features over 20,000 local marine animals including sharks, rays, jellyfish, and river otters.
aquarium-of-bay.what_they_offer:
- Bay Area residents: $5 off general admission with local ID
- Military discount: 10% off for active duty, veterans, and families
- EBT/Museums for All: Reduced admission (check current rates)
- Children under 3: Free admission
- Annual passes available with unlimited visits
aquarium-of-bay.how_to_get_it: Purchase tickets at the door or online. Bring valid Bay Area ID for local discount, military ID for military discount, or EBT card for Museums for All pricing. Discounts cannot be combined.

ca-sp-armstrong-redwoods-snr.name: Armstrong Redwoods SNR
ca-sp-armstrong-redwoods-snr.description: Armstrong Redwoods State Natural Reserve near Guerneville protects a grove of old-growth coast redwoods, including the 310-foot Parson Jones Tree and the 1,400-year-old Colonel Armstrong Tree.
ca-sp-armstrong-redwoods-snr.what_they_offer:
- Easy walks among old-growth redwoods on self-guided nature trails
- Visitor center and picnic areas
- Group picnic area (Smokey's Den) available by reservation
- No camping in the reserve (camping at neighboring Austin Creek SRA is currently closed)
- Dogs allowed only on the paved road and in developed picnic areas, on leash
- Open 8 am to one hour after sunset; phone (707) 869-2015
ca-sp-armstrong-redwoods-snr.how_to_get_it:
**Fees:**
- Day use: $10 per vehicle ($9 with a senior 62+)

**Save with park passes:** Armstrong Redwoods accepts the California Explorer and Golden Poppy annual passes, the Free Fourth Grade Pass, and the California State Library Parks Pass (free to check out at public libraries).

imls-art-works-downtown.name: Art Works Downtown
imls-art-works-downtown.description: Nonprofit art center featuring 4 galleries, 27 art studios, and rotating exhibits by Bay Area artists.

imls-arts-benicia.name: Arts Benicia
imls-arts-benicia.description: Community-based visual arts center providing classes, exhibitions, and networking for artists.

asian-art-museum.name: Asian Art Museum
asian-art-museum.description: The Asian Art Museum of San Francisco houses one of the world's most comprehensive collections of Asian art, spanning 6,000 years of history with over 18,000 artworks from across the Asian continent.
asian-art-museum.what_they_offer:
- Free First Sundays: Free general admission for everyone on the first Sunday of each month (special exhibitions discounted)
- SF Museums for All: Free general admission for up to 4 family members with an EBT or Medi-Cal card and proof of San Francisco residency
- Active military (Blue Star Museums): Free admission for active-duty personnel and up to 5 family members
- Caregivers: One free guest pass for a caregiver accompanying a visitor with special needs (reserve at 415-581-3531)
- Discover & Go: Free passes for California public library cardholders
- Children 12 and under: Always free
- General admission: $20 adults, $17 seniors 65+, $14 ages 13-17 and college students with ID
asian-art-museum.how_to_get_it: For Museums for All and active military, bring your EBT or Medi-Cal card and proof of SF residency, or your military ID, to the admissions desk (same-day walk-up only). For Free First Sundays, reserving tickets online in advance is recommended. Discover & Go passes are reserved through your local library's website. Open Thursday 1-8 pm and Friday-Monday 10 am-5 pm; closed Tuesday and Wednesday.

ca-sp-austin-creek-sra.name: Austin Creek SRA
ca-sp-austin-creek-sra.description: Austin Creek State Recreation Area near Guerneville offers about 6,000 acres of rugged hills, meadows, and woodlands with 20 miles of trails, and preserves Pond Farm Pottery, a National Historic Landmark. It shares an entrance with Armstrong Redwoods.
ca-sp-austin-creek-sra.what_they_offer:
- Day use hiking on trails and fire roads (Gilliam Creek Trail currently closed)
- Bicycles allowed on paved roads and fire roads (not trails)
- Pond Farm Pottery historic site (occasional open houses)
- Camping is currently closed: Bullfrog Pond Campground and backcountry camps are closed until further notice
- No public drinking water; dogs not allowed on trails or dirt roads
- Open 8 am to one hour after sunset; phone (707) 869-2015
ca-sp-austin-creek-sra.how_to_get_it:
**Fees:**
- Day use: $10 per vehicle ($9 with a senior 62+), paid at the Armstrong Redwoods entrance

**Save with park passes:** Austin Creek accepts the California Explorer, Golden Poppy, Disabled Discount, Distinguished Veteran, Golden Bear, and Senior Golden Bear passes, plus the California State Library Parks Pass (free to check out at public libraries).

ca-sp-bale-grist-mill-shp.name: Bale Grist Mill SHP
ca-sp-bale-grist-mill-shp.description: Bale Grist Mill State Historic Park north of St. Helena preserves a historic water-powered grist mill, with milling demonstrations and tours on weekends. Public services are provided by the Napa County Regional Park and Open Space District.
ca-sp-bale-grist-mill-shp.what_they_offer:
- Historic mill tours and milling demonstrations on weekends
- Open weekends and some Monday holidays, 10 am-4 pm (last tour at 3 pm)
- School tours Wednesdays and Thursdays by reservation ($150 per class)
- Closed Thanksgiving, Christmas, and New Year's Day
- No camping; phone (707) 963-2236 (call before visiting)
ca-sp-bale-grist-mill-shp.how_to_get_it:
**Fees:**
- Day use: $10 per vehicle (as listed by California State Parks; fees collected by Napa County Regional Park and Open Space District)

**Save with park passes:** Bale Grist Mill accepts the Historian Passport annual pass and the California State Library Parks Pass (free to check out at public libraries).

bay-area-discovery-museum.name: Bay Area Discovery Museum
bay-area-discovery-museum.description: The Bay Area Discovery Museum is a hands-on children's museum nestled at the foot of the Golden Gate Bridge in Sausalito, featuring indoor and outdoor exhibits designed to spark creativity and curiosity in children ages 0-10.
bay-area-discovery-museum.what_they_offer:
- EBT/WIC cardholders: $5 admission per person
- Caregivers of visitors with disabilities: Free admission
- Pay-What-You-Can days: Admission at any price you choose
- Members: Unlimited free visits year-round
- Children under 1: Free admission
- Regular admission: $18 per person
bay-area-discovery-museum.how_to_get_it: For EBT/WIC discount, show your benefits card at the admissions desk. Check the museum website for scheduled Pay-What-You-Can days. Advance reservations recommended for all visits.

imls-u-s-army-corps-of-engineers-bay-mod.name: Bay Model Visitor Center
imls-u-s-army-corps-of-engineers-bay-mod.description: Free federal visitor center featuring a 1.5-acre hydraulic model of San Francisco Bay and Sacramento-San Joaquin Delta.

ca-sp-bean-hollow-sb.name: Bean Hollow SB
ca-sp-bean-hollow-sb.description: Bean Hollow State Beach covers a one-mile stretch of San Mateo Coast shoreline south of Pescadero, with two parking lots at Pebble Beach and Bean Hollow Beach connected by a coastal trail.
ca-sp-bean-hollow-sb.what_they_offer:
- Pebble Beach, known for its ocean-polished stones (collecting is not allowed)
- One-mile Arroyo de los Frijoles Trail with interpretive panels
- Tide pools and wildlife viewing
- Dogs allowed on a 6-foot leash
- No camping, beach fires, or drones; ocean is cold with rip currents and heavy surf
- Open 8 am to sunset; phone (650) 726-8819
ca-sp-bean-hollow-sb.how_to_get_it:
California State Parks does not list a day-use fee for this park.

**Getting there:** On Highway 1, about 17.5 miles south of Half Moon Bay and 3 miles south of Pescadero.

ca-sp-benicia-capitol-shp.name: Benicia Capitol SHP
ca-sp-benicia-capitol-shp.description: Benicia Capitol State Historic Park preserves the building that served as California's third seat of government (1853-1854), the only pre-Sacramento capitol still standing, along with the historic Fischer-Hanlon House next door.
ca-sp-benicia-capitol-shp.what_they_offer:
- Historic 1850s State Capitol building and museum
- Fischer-Hanlon House tours on weekends (call ahead for weekday tours)
- School field trips and group tours by reservation
- Open Friday-Sunday, 10 am-5 pm; closed Monday-Thursday and on Thanksgiving, Christmas, and New Year's Day
- Phone (707) 745-3385
ca-sp-benicia-capitol-shp.how_to_get_it:
**Fees:**
- Museum entry: $3 adults, $2 youth (6-17), children 5 and under free

**Save with park passes:** Benicia Capitol accepts the Historian Passport annual pass, the Free Fourth Grade Pass, the Disabled Discount Pass, and the California State Library Parks Pass (free to check out at public libraries).

ca-sp-benicia-sra.name: Benicia SRA
ca-sp-benicia-sra.description: Benicia State Recreation Area along the Carquinez Strait offers marshland, bay views, trails, and fishing, including the popular Dillon Point area.
ca-sp-benicia-sra.what_they_offer:
- Walking and biking trails with views of the Carquinez Strait
- Fishing, especially in the marshland at Dillon Point
- Picnicking and wildlife viewing
- Three first-come en route campsites for fully self-contained RVs/trailers only (no tents)
- Some temporary area closures possible during the Glen Cove Waterfront Enhancement Project
- Open daily 8 am to sunset; phone (707) 648-1911
ca-sp-benicia-sra.how_to_get_it:
**Fees:**
- Day use: $6 per vehicle

**Save with park passes:** Benicia SRA accepts the California Explorer, Golden Poppy, Distinguished Veteran, Golden Bear, and Senior Golden Bear passes, plus the California State Library Parks Pass (free to check out at public libraries).

ca-sp-bethany-reservoir-sra.name: Bethany Reservoir SRA
ca-sp-bethany-reservoir-sra.description: Bethany Reservoir State Recreation Area near Byron is a day-use reservoir park popular for fishing, boating, and windsurfing, with access to the California Aqueduct Bikeway.
ca-sp-bethany-reservoir-sra.what_they_offer:
- Fishing, boating, and windsurfing
- Boat launch (boats must pass a mussel inspection)
- Picnicking and trails
- No camping
- Harmful algae may be present in the reservoir; check advisories before water contact
- Open 7 am to sunset; phone (925) 447-2867
ca-sp-bethany-reservoir-sra.how_to_get_it:
**Fees:**
- Day use parking: about $10-$11 per vehicle ($1 off with a senior 62+); can be paid online through LAZ
- Boat launch: $7

**Save with park passes:** Bethany Reservoir accepts the California Explorer, Golden Poppy, Disabled Discount, Distinguished Veteran, Golden Bear, and Senior Golden Bear passes, plus the California State Library Parks Pass (free to check out at public libraries).

recgov-fac-boat-in-sites-lake-sonoma.name: BOAT-IN SITES (LAKE SONOMA)
recgov-fac-boat-in-sites-lake-sonoma.description: Overview Lake Sonoma's Boat-In Sites are scattered around beautiful Lake Sonoma, only a 45-minute drive north of Santa Rosa and a two-hour drive from San Francisco. BOAT-IN CAMPGROUNDS ARE ACCESSIBLE BY WATER OR HIKING ONLY, THERE IS NO VEHICLE ACCESS TO ANY BOAT-IN CAMPGROUND World famous vineyards and a land rich in history surround the lake, where visitors enjoy boating, fishing and exploring the area's extensive trail network. Recreation The lake provides great boating and swimming opportuni
recgov-fac-boat-in-sites-lake-sonoma.what_they_offer: Campground at Lake Sonoma. Reservations available through Recreation.gov.
recgov-fac-boat-in-sites-lake-sonoma.how_to_get_it: Make a reservation through Recreation.gov. Book early as popular sites fill up quickly.

imls-bolinas-museum.name: Bolinas Museum
imls-bolinas-museum.description: Premier fine arts museum in Marin County, dedicated to collecting, preserving and exhibiting the art and history of coastal Marin. Free admission.

ca-sp-bothe-napa-valley-sp.name: Bothe Napa Valley SP
ca-sp-bothe-napa-valley-sp.description: Bothe-Napa Valley State Park, between St. Helena and Calistoga on Highway 29, offers camping, picnicking, a seasonal swimming pool, and more than 10 miles of trails through redwood, Douglas-fir, tanoak, and madrone forests.
ca-sp-bothe-napa-valley-sp.what_they_offer:
- Tent, group, and hike-and-bike campsites, plus cabins and yurts (reserve at ReserveCalifornia.com)
- Over 10 miles of hiking trails
- Seasonal swimming pool (summer weekends, 1-5 pm)
- Large picnic grounds and a group picnic area; visitor center and Pioneer Cemetery
- Dogs allowed on leash in camp and picnic areas only (not on trails or at the pool)
- Open daily 8 am to sunset; phone (707) 942-4575
ca-sp-bothe-napa-valley-sp.how_to_get_it:
**Fees:**
- Day use: $10 per vehicle
- Pool: $5 entry (paid at the park entrance)
- Camping fees vary by site type; see ReserveCalifornia.com

**Save with park passes:** Bothe-Napa Valley accepts the California Explorer, Golden Poppy, Disabled Discount, Distinguished Veteran, Golden Bear, and Senior Golden Bear passes, plus the California State Library Parks Pass (free to check out at public libraries).

ca-sp-burleigh-h-murray-ranch-prop.name: Burleigh H Murray Ranch Prop
ca-sp-burleigh-h-murray-ranch-prop.description: Burleigh H. Murray Ranch Park Property near Half Moon Bay is a quiet canyon park along Mills Creek with a trail past the historic Mills Barn, one of only two known bank barns in California.
ca-sp-burleigh-h-murray-ranch-prop.what_they_offer:
- Hiking along a ranch service road through Mills Creek canyon
- Historic Mills Barn (late 1800s dairy bank barn)
- Guided hikes and public programs offered occasionally
- Dogs allowed on the service road only, on a 6-foot leash
- No camping, fires, or drones
- Open 8 am to sunset; phone (650) 726-8819
ca-sp-burleigh-h-murray-ranch-prop.how_to_get_it:
California State Parks does not list a day-use fee for this park. A small parking area is available.

**Getting there:** From Highway 1 just over a mile south of Highway 92, turn east onto Higgins-Purisima Road and continue about 1.5 miles to the park.

ca-sp-butano-sp.name: Butano SP
ca-sp-butano-sp.description: Butano State Park near Pescadero is a redwood park in the Santa Cruz Mountains with hiking through redwood groves and ocean views, still regrowing after the 2020 CZU Lightning Complex Fire.
ca-sp-butano-sp.what_they_offer:
- Hiking trails through redwood groves with ocean views
- Butano Trail Camp open to backpackers (reservations required)
- Main campground (Ben Ries) is closed indefinitely due to fire damage to the water system
- Dogs allowed on leash in the campground, paved areas, and fire roads
- Open 8 am to sunset; phone (650) 879-2040
ca-sp-butano-sp.how_to_get_it:
**Fees:**
- Day use: $10 per vehicle ($9 with a senior 62+)

**Save with park passes:** Butano accepts the California Explorer, Golden Poppy, Disabled Discount, Distinguished Veteran, Golden Bear, and Senior Golden Bear passes, plus the California State Library Parks Pass (free to check out at public libraries).

imls-c-e-smith-museum-of-anthropology.name: C. E. Smith Museum of Anthropology
imls-c-e-smith-museum-of-anthropology.description: Teaching museum at Cal State East Bay demonstrating human diversity and the range of human achievement throughout the world. Free admission.

cal-academy.name: California Academy of Sciences
cal-academy.description: The California Academy of Sciences in Golden Gate Park is a world-class scientific and cultural institution featuring a natural history museum, aquarium, planetarium, and rainforest all under one living roof.
cal-academy.what_they_offer:
- Museums for All: $3 per person with EBT card
- SF Resident Free Days: Free admission for SF residents (check schedule)
- Neighborhood Free Days: Free for specific SF zip codes (rotating)
- Children under 3: Always free
- Regular admission: $34-39 for adults
cal-academy.how_to_get_it: For Museums for All, present your EBT card and photo ID at the admissions desk. For SF Resident Free Days, bring proof of residence. Reservations are required for all visits - book online in advance.

ca-state-parks-adventure-pass.name: California State Parks Free Fourth Grade Pass
ca-state-parks-adventure-pass.description: California State Parks' Free Fourth Grade Pass (formerly the Adventure Pass) gives California public school fourth graders and their families free entry to 54 state parks, as part of the Outdoors for All initiative.
ca-state-parks-adventure-pass.what_they_offer:
- Unlimited free vehicle entry to 54 participating state parks
- For fourth graders attending a California public school
- Covers the student plus everyone in the same car (up to three adults)
- Valid from August of the fourth-grade year through August 31 of the following year
ca-state-parks-adventure-pass.how_to_get_it: A parent or guardian creates a free account at ReserveCalifornia.com and downloads the pass (available starting August 1 each year). Print the pass or show it on your phone to park staff at a participating park.
ca-state-parks-adventure-pass.timeframe: 2026-27 school year pass valid through August 31, 2027 (new passes each August)

ca-state-parks-disabled-discount.name: California State Parks Disabled Discount Pass
ca-state-parks-disabled-discount.description: California State Parks' Disabled Discount Pass is a $3.50 lifetime pass for people with permanent disabilities that cuts day-use, camping, and boating fees in half at over 100 state park units.
ca-state-parks-disabled-discount.what_they_offer:
- Lifetime pass for individuals with permanent disabilities ($3.50 application fee)
- 50% discount on vehicle day-use fees
- 50% discount on family camping fees
- 50% discount on boat-use fees
- Accepted at over 100 California State Parks-operated units
- Pass must be renewed every five years
ca-state-parks-disabled-discount.how_to_get_it: Apply online through ReserveCalifornia (fastest), by mail, or in person at designated pass sales locations. Include a valid photo ID, the $3.50 fee, and one form of disability certification, such as a State Regional Center letter, DMV disabled placard ID or registration, Medicare card or Social Security disability award (under 65), or a doctor's certification on the application.

ca-state-parks-distinguished-veteran.name: California State Parks Distinguished Veteran Pass
ca-state-parks-distinguished-veteran.description: California State Parks' Distinguished Veteran Pass is a free lifetime pass for eligible honorably discharged California veterans, covering day use, family camping, and boat use at over 100 state park units.
ca-state-parks-distinguished-veteran.what_they_offer:
- Free lifetime pass
- Free vehicle day use, family camping, and boat use
- Accepted at over 100 California State Parks-operated units (see the park acceptance list)
- Pass must be renewed every five years
ca-state-parks-distinguished-veteran.how_to_get_it:
Must be an honorably discharged veteran with California residency who meets one of these:
- Service-connected disability rated 50% or higher, with service during a qualifying wartime period
- Former prisoner of war
- Medal of Honor recipient

Apply online through ReserveCalifornia (fastest), by mail, or at select pass sales locations, with proof of eligibility.

ca-sp-candlestick-point-sra.name: Candlestick Point SRA
ca-sp-candlestick-point-sra.description: Candlestick Point State Recreation Area in San Francisco's Bayview/Hunters Point neighborhood was California's first urban state park, with shoreline trails, picnic areas, a public fishing pier, and free community programs.
ca-sp-candlestick-point-sra.what_they_offer:
- Accessible walking and biking trails along the bay
- Picnic areas with BBQ grills, including four group sites (first come, first served)
- Public fishing pier (no fishing license needed on the pier)
- Kayaking, windsurfing, swimming, and bird watching
- Free arts and nature programs; volunteer days the first Saturday of each month
- Sunrise Point group campground (6 sites for groups of 20-40, $35/site per night; arrange with the park manager)
- Dogs allowed on a 6-foot leash; phone (415) 798-7318
ca-sp-candlestick-point-sra.how_to_get_it:
California State Parks does not list a day-use fee for this park. Park hours are listed as 7 am-7 pm (sunrise to sunset).

**Getting there:** Main entrance at 500 Hunters Point Expressway. From Highway 101, take the Third Street exit, turn right on Gilman Avenue, and continue to the park entrance.

recgov-cedar-roughs-wilderness.name: Cedar Roughs Wilderness
recgov-cedar-roughs-wilderness.description: Overview The Cedar Roughs Wilderness now contains a total of 6,287 acres and is managed by the Bureau of Land Management. All of the Wilderness is in the state of California. In 2006 the Cedar Roughs Wilderness became part of the now over 109 million acre National Wilderness Preservation System. In wilderness, you can enjoy challenging recreational activities and extraordinary opportunities for solitude. In an age of "...increasing population, accompanied by expanding settlement and growing mech
recgov-cedar-roughs-wilderness.what_they_offer: Outdoor recreation including hiking, wildlife viewing, and nature experiences. Some sites offer camping, picnicking, and water activities.
recgov-cedar-roughs-wilderness.how_to_get_it: Visit Recreation.gov to check availability, make reservations, and plan your visit. Some areas are free to visit while others may require permits or fees.

chabot-space-center.name: Chabot Space & Science Center
chabot-space-center.description: Chabot Space & Science Center in the Oakland hills features interactive space science exhibits, planetarium shows, and three historic telescopes offering free public viewing nights. The center inspires curiosity about the universe and our place in it.
chabot-space-center.what_they_offer:
- EBT cardholders: $5 admission per person
- Free telescope viewing: Friday and Saturday evenings (weather permitting)
- Children under 2: Free admission
- Members: Unlimited visits plus guest discounts
- Regular admission: $24 for adults, $18 for children
chabot-space-center.how_to_get_it: Show your EBT card at the admissions desk for reduced admission. Telescope viewing is free and open to the public on clear Friday and Saturday nights - no reservation needed.

recgov-channel-islands-national-marine-s.name: Channel Islands National Marine Sanctuary
recgov-channel-islands-national-marine-s.description: The waters that swirl around the five islands within Channel Islands National Marine Sanctuary create a special place for several species of plants and animals. Year round, this sanctuary provides wildlife viewing opportunities of dolphins and whales, pinnipeds, and seabirds. This sanctuary also has forests of giant kelp that are home to numerous populations of fish and invertebrates. Make this visit memorable by participating in several activities such as tidepooling, kayaking, snorkeling, fish
recgov-channel-islands-national-marine-s.what_they_offer: Outdoor recreation including hiking, wildlife viewing, and nature experiences. Some sites offer camping, picnicking, and water activities.
recgov-channel-islands-national-marine-s.how_to_get_it: Visit Recreation.gov to check availability, make reservations, and plan your visit. Some areas are free to visit while others may require permits or fees.

imls-charles-m-schulz-museum-and-researc.name: Charles M Schulz Museum and Research Center
imls-charles-m-schulz-museum-and-researc.description: Museum dedicated to the life and art of Peanuts creator Charles M. Schulz.

childrens-creativity-museum.name: Children's Creativity Museum
childrens-creativity-museum.description: The Children's Creativity Museum in San Francisco's Yerba Buena Gardens is an interactive arts and technology museum for children ages 2-12, featuring hands-on exhibits that encourage creativity through music, animation, and digital media.
childrens-creativity-museum.what_they_offer:
- Museums for All: Reduced admission with EBT card (cardholder + guests)
- Must have at least one child in the group
- Children under 2: Free admission
- Regular admission: $16 per person
childrens-creativity-museum.how_to_get_it: Present your physical EBT or SNAP benefits card along with a photo ID at the admissions desk. Groups must include at least one child to qualify. Reservations recommended.

childrens-discovery-museum-sj.name: Children's Discovery Museum
childrens-discovery-museum-sj.description: Children's Discovery Museum of San Jose is one of the largest children's museums in the country, featuring interactive exhibits that inspire children to explore, question, and discover the world around them.
childrens-discovery-museum-sj.what_they_offer:
- Museums for All: $5 per person for up to 4 people
- Valid with a CalFresh EBT or SNAP EBT card plus photo ID
- Infants under 1: Free admission
- Regular admission: $22 per person ($20 seniors 60+)
childrens-discovery-museum-sj.how_to_get_it: Buy Museums for All tickets in person at the museum (no advance reservations needed; a set number are available each session). Show your photo ID and a valid, unexpired CalFresh or SNAP EBT card. EBT cards cannot be used for payment; the museum accepts cash and major credit cards. School-year hours are Tuesday-Friday 9:30 am-1 pm and Saturday-Sunday 9:30 am-4:30 pm.

childrens-fairyland.name: Children's Fairyland
childrens-fairyland.description: Children's Fairyland is a whimsical storybook theme park on the shores of Lake Merritt in Oakland, designed for children ages 0-8. As one of the first theme parks in America, it has delighted families since 1950 with its enchanting sets, live animals, and puppet shows.
childrens-fairyland.what_they_offer:
- Fairyland for All: $5 per person with an EBT, SNAP/CalFresh, BIC, or WIC card (up to 8 people per household)
- 510 Fridays: Oakland residents pay $5 for kids and $10 for adults on Fridays (walk-up, with ID showing an Oakland address)
- Military and veterans: $3 off each ticket (up to 6 tickets) with military ID
- Children under 1: Free
- Regular admission: $18 children (ages 1-17), $20 adults, $17 seniors (65+)
- Fairyland for All visitors can also get a discounted membership
childrens-fairyland.how_to_get_it: Show your EBT, SNAP/CalFresh, BIC, or WIC card at admission to get the $5 rate for up to 8 people in your household. Buy tickets online or walk up. Open Wednesday through Sunday, 10 a.m. to 4 p.m., weather permitting.

imls-children-s-museum-of-sonoma-county.name: Children's Museum of Sonoma County
imls-children-s-museum-of-sonoma-county.description: Interactive museum with hands-on STEAM exhibits for children ages 0-10. Features indoor and outdoor exhibits including Mary's Garden and Little Russian River.

ca-sp-china-camp-sp.name: China Camp SP
ca-sp-china-camp-sp.description: China Camp State Park covers 1,514 acres along the San Pablo Bay shoreline in San Rafael, with panoramic bay views, oak woodlands, more than 100 acres of protected tidal salt marsh, and a historic Chinese shrimp-fishing village.
ca-sp-china-camp-sp.what_they_offer:
- Trails for hiking, mountain biking, and horseback riding
- Tent camping and hike-and-bike sites at Back Ranch Meadows Campground (reserve at ReserveCalifornia.com)
- Picnic areas, beach, swimming, fishing, and a boat ramp
- Visitor center, museum, historic village, and ranger and Junior Ranger programs
ca-sp-china-camp-sp.how_to_get_it:
Vehicle day use is $5. The park is open 8 a.m. to sunset.

**Free and discount passes accepted here:**

recgov-contra-loma-reservoir.description: Contra Loma Dam and reservoir are part of the Central Valley Project - Delta Division and offers recreational opportunities for the East Bay area near San Francisco. recgov-cordell-bank-national-marine-sanc.name: Cordell Bank National Marine Sanctuary
recgov-cordell-bank-national-marine-sanc.description: Entirely offshore, Cordell Bank National Marine Sanctuary protects soft seafloor habitat, a rocky bank, deep-sea canyons, and diverse wildlife, while acting as a feeding ground for many marine mammals and seabirds. This protected area is home to several habitats and species that can be visited from afar through educational resources such as panels and exhibits. Visitors can enjoy this extraordinarily rich marine ecosystem by boating, fishing, and watching wildlife from the mainland.

imls-di-rosa-preserve.description: Collection of 1,600 works of Northern California art on 217 protected acres with galleries, sculpture park, 35-acre lake, and walking trails.

recgov-don-edwards-san-francisco-bay-nat.name: Don Edwards San Francisco Bay National Wildlife Refuge
recgov-don-edwards-san-francisco-bay-nat.description: Don Edwards San Francisco Bay National Wildlife Refuge is located in a vast cultural and natural landscape. As part of the San Francisco Bay National Wildlife Refuge Complex, a complex of seven refuges spanning over 125 miles and 11 counties, the protected habitats and wildlife are just as diverse as the urban communities surrounding them. imls-dutra-museum-foundation.name: Dutra Museum Foundation
imls-dutra-museum-foundation.description: Museum featuring Northern California dredging history, the California Delta, and the Dutra Family's involvement in maritime heritage.

recgov-elkhorn-slough-national-estuarine.name: Elkhorn Slough National Estuarine Research Reserve
recgov-elkhorn-slough-national-estuarine.description: Elkhorn Slough is one of the relatively few undisturbed coastal wetlands remaining in California. The main channel of the slough, which winds inland nearly seven miles, is flanked by a broad salt marsh second in size only to San Francisco Bay. More than 400 species of invertebrates, 80 species of fish and 200 species of birds have been identified in Elkhorn Slough. The channels and tidal creeks of the slough are nurseries for many species of fish. Additionally, the slough is on the Pacific flywa

recgov-ellicott-slough-national-wildlife.description: Ellicott Slough National Wildlife Refuge is located in Santa Cruz County within the Monterey Bay area. The refuge, established in 1975 to protect the endangered Santa Cruz long-toed salamander, supports two of the 24 known breeding populations of the salamander. When the California red-legged frog was listed as a threatened species in 1996 and the California tiger salamander in 2004, the purpose of the refuge expanded to include protection of these two species. imls-emeryville-center-for-the-arts.name: Emeryville Center for the Arts
imls-emeryville-center-for-the-arts.description: Art organization celebrating local art in Emeryville with annual exhibitions and community events.

ca-sp-emeryville-crescent-smr.name: Emeryville Crescent SMR
ca-sp-emeryville-crescent-smr.description: Emeryville Crescent State Marine Reserve protects tidal marsh and mudflats on the east shore of San Francisco Bay, at the south end of McLaughlin Eastshore State Park. It is a protected area for birds and other wildlife.
ca-sp-emeryville-crescent-smr.what_they_offer:
- Shoreline views of protected tidal marsh and bay wildlife
- Bird and wildlife watching from the shoreline and nearby Bay Trail
- Parking at the far west end of Powell Street in Emeryville
- No camping
ca-sp-emeryville-crescent-smr.how_to_get_it: No day-use fee is listed. Park at the west end of Powell Street in Emeryville and enjoy the reserve from the shoreline. State Parks notes this property may have limited public facilities while planning and development continue. Collecting or taking marine life is not allowed in a state marine reserve.

nps-euon.name: Eugene O'Neill National Historic Site
nps-euon.description: Eugene O'Neill National Historic Site preserves Tao House, where the Nobel Prize-winning playwright wrote his most celebrated works including Long Day's Journey Into Night and The Iceman Cometh.

exploratorium.name: Exploratorium
exploratorium.description: The Exploratorium is San Francisco's world-renowned museum of science, art, and human perception. Located on Pier 15, it features over 650 interactive exhibits that encourage hands-on exploration and discovery.
exploratorium.what_they_offer:
- California PreK-12 public school teachers: Free admission
- Museums for All: $3 admission for up to 4 people
- Valid with EBT/SNAP, Medi-Cal, WIC, or Lifeline Pass
- After Dark (18+): $3 admission with qualifying card
- Discounted memberships: $39 Family, $19 Dual After Dark
- Must purchase at ticket window (not available online)
exploratorium.how_to_get_it: California PreK-12 public school teachers can apply for free admission online and bring teacher ID. For low-income discounts, visit the ticket window with your EBT, SNAP, Medi-Cal, WIC card, or Lifeline Pass. These discounts are not available for online purchases.

imls-falkirk-cultural-center.name: Falkirk Cultural Center
imls-falkirk-cultural-center.description: Historic 1888 Queen Anne mansion on the National Register of Historical Places, serving as a cultural center since 1974.

recgov-farallon-islands-national-wildlif.name: Farallon Islands National Wildlife Refuge
recgov-farallon-islands-national-wildlif.description: The Farallon Islands National Wildlife Refuge is located on the pacific coast approximately 28 miles west of San Francisco California. Totaling 211 acres, it is composed of several islands in four groups: the North Farallon, Middle Farallon, South Farallon Islands, and Noonday Rock. The North Farallon, Middle Farallon, and Noonday Rock were designated as the Farallon Refuge by President Theodore Roosevelt in 1909 to protect seabirds and marine mammals. South Farallon Islands is the largest islan

fine-arts-museums-sf.name: Fine Arts Museums of San Francisco
fine-arts-museums-sf.description: The Fine Arts Museums of San Francisco comprise the de Young Museum in Golden Gate Park and the Legion of Honor in Lincoln Park. Together they house an encyclopedic collection spanning over 5,000 years of ancient and European art, American art, textiles, and more.
fine-arts-museums-sf.what_they_offer:
- Free Saturdays: Free general admission for residents of the nine Bay Area counties
- Free First Tuesdays: Free general admission for everyone on the first Tuesday of each month
- Museums for All: Free general admission with an EBT or Medi-Cal card, plus a discounted $48 Museums for All family membership
- Youth 17 and under: Always free
- Veterans and active military: Free general admission with military ID
- Students with ID: $10; Seniors (65+): $22; Adults: $25 (de Young general admission)
- Access Days and a discounted Access membership for visitors with disabilities
fine-arts-museums-sf.how_to_get_it: For Free Saturdays, reserve online and bring a driver's license or postmarked mail showing a Bay Area address. Show your EBT or Medi-Cal card or military ID at the ticketing desk (subject to availability). Free admission covers the permanent collection galleries; special exhibitions may cost extra.

recgov-folsom-dam.name: Folsom Dam
recgov-folsom-dam.description: Settlement of the basin began about 1844. In 1848, discovery of gold near the present site of Coloma precipitated a great influx of gold seekers from all parts of the country. At the height of the gold rush, the American River foothill area was one of the most populous in the State. Early miners quickly recognized the potential of riverflows to help in dredging, panning, and sluicing for gold. Diversion dams began appearing on the river in the 1850's. recgov-folsom-dam.what_they_offer: Outdoor recreation including hiking, wildlife viewing, and nature experiences. Some sites offer camping, picnicking, and water activities.

recgov-folsom-lake.name: Folsom Lake
recgov-folsom-lake.description: Recreation at Folsom Reservoir is managed by the California Department of Parks and Recreation under agreement with the Bureau of Reclamation, Central California Area Office. The reservoir was created by Folsom Dam across the American River. The dam is a feature of the Central Valley Project - American River Division - Folsom and Sly Park Units . ca-sp-franks-tract-sra.description: Franks Tract State Recreation Area is a flooded former Delta island near Bethel Island, surrounded by marsh and remnant levees. It is almost completely underwater and can only be reached by boat.
ca-sp-franks-tract-sra.what_they_offer:
- Fishing, including a popular striped bass fly-fishing area
- Bird watching, especially waterfowl in fall and winter
- Seasonal waterfowl hunting on part of the open water (arranged in advance through the Diablo Range District Office)
- No camping, restrooms, or land facilities
ca-sp-franks-tract-sra.how_to_get_it: Franks Tract is only accessible by water, southeast of Brannan Island between False River and Bethel Island. No entrance fee is listed. Dogs are not allowed. Call the Delta Sector at 925-447-0426 for information.

imls-gallery-route-one.name: Gallery Route One
imls-gallery-route-one.description: Non-profit arts organization presenting contemporary art exhibitions and educational programs since 1983.

imls-gardens-at-heather-farms.name: Gardens at Heather Farms
imls-gardens-at-heather-farms.description: Six-acre public garden featuring the Cowden Rose Garden, Children's Garden, Sensory Garden, and Community Garden. Free admission and open daily.

golden-gate-park-gardens.name: Gardens of Golden Gate Park
golden-gate-park-gardens.description: The Gardens of Golden Gate Park include the Conservatory of Flowers (the oldest public wood-and-glass conservatory in North America), the Japanese Tea Garden (the oldest operating public Japanese garden in North America), and the San Francisco Botanical Garden (55 acres with more than 8,000 kinds of plants).
golden-gate-park-gardens.what_they_offer:
- Free for San Francisco residents and veterans at all three gardens
- Museums for All: Free general admission with an EBT card
- Botanical Garden: Free for everyone daily 7:30-9 a.m., on the second Tuesday of each month, and on Thanksgiving, Christmas, and New Year's Day
- Japanese Tea Garden: Free hour for everyone 9-10 a.m. on Mondays, Wednesdays, and Fridays
- Conservatory of Flowers: Free for everyone on the first Tuesday of the month (closed Wednesdays)
- Special exhibitions and events may cost extra
golden-gate-park-gardens.how_to_get_it: Show proof of San Francisco residency, veteran ID, or your EBT card at the entrance. Anyone can visit free during the free hours and days listed above. Check the Admissions & Hours page for current hours, or call 415-661-1316.

golden-bear-pass.name: Golden Bear Pass
golden-bear-pass.description: California State Parks offers the Golden Bear Pass to ensure that cost is not a barrier to enjoying the state's natural treasures, providing free access to income-eligible residents and seniors.
golden-bear-pass.what_they_offer:
- Free vehicle day-use entry at more than 200 California State Parks units that accept the pass
- Valid from the date issued through December 31 of that year

- A 30-day temporary pass is issued while your pass is mailed
golden-bear-pass.how_to_get_it: Apply online through ReserveCalifornia, in person at a State Parks pass sales location, or by mail with the application and proof of eligibility. CalWORKs families can apply online through the California Department of Social Services (cdss.ca.gov/goldenbearpass). Tribal TANF recipients apply through their Tribal TANF administrator. Online applications may take longer than usual to process.

ca-sp-gray-whale-cove-sb.name: Gray Whale Cove SB
ca-sp-gray-whale-cove-sb.description: Gray Whale Cove State Beach is a secluded cove on the San Mateo coast north of Montara, reached by a long, steep trail, with turquoise water, dramatic cliffs, and views of migrating gray whales.
ca-sp-gray-whale-cove-sb.what_they_offer:
- Secluded beach with a small picnic area on the bluff
- Whale watching and wildlife viewing
- Trail access to McNee Ranch and Montara Mountain from the parking lot
- Chemical toilets in the parking lot; no drinking water and no camping
ca-sp-gray-whale-cove-sb.how_to_get_it: Park in the lot on the east side of Highway 1, cross the highway with care, and take the steep trail down to the beach. Open 8 a.m. to sunset. No day-use fee is listed, and this park does not accept the annual day-use pass. Dogs are not allowed on the beach. The nearest state park campground is at Half Moon Bay State Beach.

recgov-great-falls-basin-wsa.name: Great Falls Basin WSA
recgov-great-falls-basin-wsa.description: A perennial spring supplies the water flowing through a short distance in the Great Falls Basin Wilderness, and that reach has cut a narrow and deep slot in the bedrock forming several falls. The steep mountainous terrain includes granite outcrops which provide opportunities for cross country hiking and exploration. Elevations range from 2,000-4,500 feet. imls-jack-london-state-historic-park.description: Historic park featuring Jack London's home and ranch. National Historic Landmark with hiking trails, museums, and the House of Happy Walls.

nps-jomu.description: John Muir National Historic Site preserves the home of famed naturalist and conservationist John Muir, "Father of the National Parks." Tour his Victorian home and the orchards he tended.

recgov-knoxville-recreation-area.name: Knoxville Recreation Area
recgov-knoxville-recreation-area.description: Due to its close proximity to the Sacramento and San Francisco Bay Area regions, and because of its varied terrain, Knoxville's 17,700 acres attract many off-highway vehicle (OHV) enthusiasts each year. The landscape is characterized by steep and rolling hills with the vegetation varying from scattered hardwoods and grasses to dense chaparral brush. California gray pine and Macnab cypress are also dispersed throughout the area. Of particular note, are unusual plant communities unique to the area
recgov-knoxville-recreation-area.what_they_offer: Outdoor recreation including hiking, wildlife viewing, and nature experiences. Some sites offer camping, picnicking, and water activities.

ca-sp-kruse-rhododendron-snr.name: Kruse Rhododendron SNR
ca-sp-kruse-rhododendron-snr.description: Kruse Rhododendron State Natural Reserve, next to Salt Point State Park on the Sonoma coast, protects a quiet second-growth redwood and fir forest where pink rhododendrons bloom each spring.
ca-sp-kruse-rhododendron-snr.what_they_offer:
- More than 2 miles of forest hiking trails, including a short loop through the rhododendrons (best bloom in spring)
- Picnic area, parking, and restrooms
- No camping (campgrounds are at neighboring Salt Point State Park)
ca-sp-kruse-rhododendron-snr.how_to_get_it: No day-use fee is listed. From Jenner, drive about 21 miles north on Highway 1 to Kruse Ranch Road, then about 1 mile east to the entrance. Call 707-847-3221 for hours. Mushroom foraging is not allowed in the reserve.

recgov-lake-berryessa.name: Lake Berryessa
recgov-lake-berryessa.description: Nestled between Blue Ridge and Cedar Roughs, east of the Napa Valley, Lake Berryessa offers year-round recreation opportunities. Lake Berryessa's water reaches temperatures of up to 75 degrees in the summer, making it an ideal place for water sports. Anglers enjoy fishing for both cold and warm water species, such as rainbow trout, bass, catfish, crappie, and bluegill. The Bureau of Reclamation provides two large day use areas (Oak Shores and Smittle Creek), Capell Cove launch ramp, and many sma
recgov-lake-berryessa.what_they_offer: Outdoor recreation including hiking, wildlife viewing, and nature experiences. Some sites offer camping, picnicking, and water activities.
recgov-lake-berryessa.how_to_get_it: Visit Recreation.gov to check availability, make reservations, and plan your visit. Some areas are free to visit while others may require permits or fees.

recgov-fac-lake-berryessa-day-use.description: Lake Berryessa - Day Use is a activity pass available through Recreation.gov.

recgov-fac-lake-berryessa-day-use.how_to_get_it: Make a reservation through Recreation.gov. Book early as popular sites fill up quickly.

ca-sp-lake-del-valle-sra.name: Lake Del Valle SRA
ca-sp-lake-del-valle-sra.description: Lake Del Valle State Recreation Area, south of Livermore, is part of the State Water Project and is operated by the East Bay Regional Park District as Del Valle Regional Park. It is popular for swimming, boating, fishing, camping, and horseback riding.
ca-sp-lake-del-valle-sra.what_they_offer:
- Swimming at East and West beaches, with lifeguards on duty in summer
- Boat launch, boat rentals, and fishing
- Tent, group, and RV camping with hookups
- Hiking, biking, and horseback riding trails, plus a visitor center and naturalist programs
ca-sp-lake-del-valle-sra.how_to_get_it: Operated by the East Bay Regional Park District. Vehicle day use is $5, or $10 on weekends and holidays from April through Labor Day. State park passes are not listed as accepted here. Check ebparks.org for camping reservations and current swim conditions, including any blue-green algae advisories.

recgov-lake-natoma.name: Lake Natoma
recgov-lake-natoma.description: Recreation at Lake Natoma is managed by the California Department of Parks and Recreation under agreement with the Bureau of Reclamation. The Lake was created by Nimbus Dam across the American River. Lake Natoma is a regulating reservoir for releases from Folsom Lake. The Dam and Lake are features of the Central Valley project. Usually open 7 days per week, summer hours (April 1-October 15) are 6:00 a.m. to 9:00 p.m. Winter hours (October 16 - March 30) are 7:00 a.m. to 7:00 p.m. Facilities incl
recgov-lake-natoma.what_they_offer: Outdoor recreation including hiking, wildlife viewing, and nature experiences. Some sites offer camping, picnicking, and water activities.
recgov-lake-natoma.how_to_get_it: Visit Recreation.gov to check availability, make reservations, and plan your visit. Some areas are free to visit while others may require permits or fees.

recgov-lake-solano.name: Lake Solano
recgov-lake-solano.description: Lake Solano Park, Solano Project , is located at the base of coastal foothills at the western edge of the Sacramento Valley and offers an array of recreational opportunities. Through an agreement with the Bureau of Reclamation, Lake Solano has been administered as a recreational area by the County of Solano since 1971. More than 200,000 visitors a year enjoy a wealth of recreational activities both on and off the water. Lake Solano is formed by Putah Diversion Dam .The park caters especially to
recgov-lake-solano.what_they_offer: Outdoor recreation including hiking, wildlife viewing, and nature experiences. Some sites offer camping, picnicking, and water activities.

recgov-lake-sonoma.name: Lake Sonoma
recgov-lake-sonoma.description: Lake Sonoma is located in the wine-growing region of Sonoma County, CA. A picturesque lake with secluded vehicle and boat-in camping available for the fishing and boating enthusiast.
recgov-lake-sonoma.what_they_offer: Outdoor recreation including hiking, wildlife viewing, and nature experiences. Some sites offer camping, picnicking, and water activities.

imls-lamorinda-arts-alliance.name: Lamorinda Arts Alliance
imls-lamorinda-arts-alliance.description: Organization of local artists serving Lafayette, Moraga, Orinda and East Bay communities. Provides exhibits, education, and coordination for artists.

lawrence-hall-science.name: Lawrence Hall of Science
lawrence-hall-science.description: The Lawrence Hall of Science is UC Berkeley's public science center, perched in the hills above campus with stunning bay views. It offers hands-on exhibits, planetarium shows, and outdoor science activities for all ages.
lawrence-hall-science.what_they_offer:
- EBT cardholders: $1 admission per person
- Cal Day: Free admission (one day per year in April)
- Children under 3: Free admission
- UC Berkeley students/staff: Free with ID
- Regular admission: $16 adults, $13 children
lawrence-hall-science.how_to_get_it: Present your EBT card at the admissions desk. No limit on number of people in your party. Advance reservations recommended on weekends and during school breaks.

imls-lawson-galleries.name: Lawson Galleries
imls-lawson-galleries.description: Art museum featuring collections and exhibitions.

recgov-fac-liberty-glen-lake-sonoma.name: LIBERTY GLEN (LAKE SONOMA)
recgov-fac-liberty-glen-lake-sonoma.description: Overview Liberty Glen Campground is located at the top of Rockpile Road overlooking Lake Sonoma. A short 45-minute drive north of Santa Rosa and a two-hour drive from San Francisco. World famous vineyards and a rich history surround the lake, where visitors enjoy boating, fishing and exploring the area's extensive trail network. Recreation Lake Sonoma offers a wide variety of recreational activities such as, Archery Range, Air Rifle Range, Disc Golf, Outdoor Gym, Dog Park as well as other nearby
recgov-fac-liberty-glen-lake-sonoma.what_they_offer: Campground at Lake Sonoma. Reservations available through Recreation.gov.
recgov-fac-liberty-glen-lake-sonoma.how_to_get_it: Make a reservation through Recreation.gov. Book early as popular sites fill up quickly.

recgov-fac-little-flat-day-use.description: Little Flat Day Use is a activity pass available through Recreation.gov.

recgov-fac-little-flat-day-use.how_to_get_it: Make a reservation through Recreation.gov. Book early as popular sites fill up quickly.

imls-livermore-heritage-guild.name: Livermore Heritage Guild
imls-livermore-heritage-guild.description: Historical society and research center in the 1911 Carnegie Library with extensive archives, newspapers, photos, and oral histories.

recgov-fac-lone-rock-day-use.description: Lone Rock Day Use is a activity pass available through Recreation.gov.

ca-sp-marconi-conference-center-shp.name: Marconi Conference Center SHP
ca-sp-marconi-conference-center-shp.description: Marconi Conference Center State Historic Park is a 62-acre park above Tomales Bay near Marshall, known for its history and natural beauty. Its historic buildings are home to the Lodge at Marconi, which offers lodging and event space.
ca-sp-marconi-conference-center-shp.what_they_offer:
- Hiking trails, bird and wildlife watching, and Tomales Bay views
- Historic site open to the public from sunrise to sunset
- Overnight lodging and meeting and event space at the Lodge at Marconi (fees apply)
- No camping
ca-sp-marconi-conference-center-shp.how_to_get_it: The park is open to the public from sunrise to sunset. No day-use fee is listed. For lodging or events at the Lodge at Marconi, call 415-663-9020.

recgov-marin-islands-national-wildlife-r.what_they_offer: Outdoor recreation including hiking, wildlife viewing, and nature experiences. Some sites offer camping, picnicking, and water activities.

imls-mountain-bike-hall-of-fame.name: Marin Museum of Bicycling & Mountain Bike Hall of Fame
imls-mountain-bike-hall-of-fame.description: Premier bicycle history museum at the birthplace of mountain biking, featuring 19th century bikes and the Mountain Bike Hall of Fame.

imls-mountain-bike-hall-of-fame-and-muse.name: Marin Museum of Bicycling & Mountain Bike Hall of Fame
imls-mountain-bike-hall-of-fame-and-muse.description: Premier bicycle history museum at the birthplace of mountain biking, featuring 19th century bikes and the Mountain Bike Hall of Fame.

imls-marin-womens-hall-of-fame.name: Marin Women's Hall of Fame
imls-marin-womens-hall-of-fame.description: Since 1987, recognizes Marin women of distinction, preserves their stories, and inspires future generations. Operated by YWCA Golden Gate Silicon Valley.

imls-maritime-museum-san-francisco.name: Maritime Museum-San Francisco
imls-maritime-museum-san-francisco.description: National Park Service museum in the historic Aquatic Park Bathhouse featuring West Coast maritime history and WPA-era art.

imls-markham-arboretum.name: Markham Arboretum
imls-markham-arboretum.description: 16-acre nature park featuring International Garden, Community Garden, and native plants. Volunteer-run with emphasis on quiet discovery.

ca-sp-marsh-creek-state-park.name: Marsh Creek State Park
ca-sp-marsh-creek-state-park.description: Marsh Creek State Park (Cowell Ranch/John Marsh) near Brentwood covers 3,659 acres of natural habitat and includes the historic John Marsh Home, completed in 1856. It is one of California's newest state parks and is not currently open to the public.
ca-sp-marsh-creek-state-park.what_they_offer:
- Future state park with natural habitat, wildlife, and the historic John Marsh Home
- Not currently open to the public; State Parks and the City of Brentwood have planned future public access
- Occasional guided events (such as First Day Hikes) may be announced on the State Parks events calendar
ca-sp-marsh-creek-state-park.how_to_get_it: The park is not currently open for general public use. Check the State Parks page for any scheduled events, or call the Diablo Range District, Contra Solano Sector, at 925-673-2891.

ca-sp-martial-cottle-park-sra.name: Martial Cottle Park SRA
ca-sp-martial-cottle-park-sra.description: Martial Cottle Park is a state recreation area in south San Jose operated by Santa Clara County Parks. It celebrates the valley's farming history and highlights modern organic, sustainable, and urban farming.
ca-sp-martial-cottle-park-sra.what_they_offer:
- Paved trails for walking, biking, and horseback riding
- Leashed dogs welcome
- Picnic areas, including reservable group picnic sites
- No camping
ca-sp-martial-cottle-park-sra.how_to_get_it: Operated by Santa Clara County Parks. Vehicle day use is $6. State park passes are not listed as accepted here. Call the park office at 408-535-4060 for hours and group picnic reservations.

ca-sp-mclaughlin-eastshore-sp-ss.name: McLaughlin Eastshore SP SS
ca-sp-mclaughlin-eastshore-sp-ss.description: McLaughlin Eastshore State Park stretches along 8.5 miles of San Francisco Bay shoreline from Richmond to Oakland, including tidal marshes and mudflats such as the Emeryville Crescent, Albany Mudflat, and Hoffman Marsh. It is operated by the East Bay Regional Park District.
ca-sp-mclaughlin-eastshore-sp-ss.what_they_offer:
- Walking and biking on the San Francisco Bay Trail
- Bird watching and wildlife viewing
- Fishing, beach areas, and windsurfing
- Parking and restrooms in developed areas; no camping
ca-sp-mclaughlin-eastshore-sp-ss.how_to_get_it: No day-use fee is listed. Operated by the East Bay Regional Park District; call 510-562-7275 or visit ebparks.org for access points and parking. Some areas of the park are still being planned and developed.

imls-mexican-museum.name: Mexican Museum
imls-mexican-museum.description: First US museum devoted exclusively to Mexican, Chicano, and Latino art. Collection of 16,000+ art objects (currently relocating to Yerba Buena).

ca-sp-montara-sb.name: Montara SB
ca-sp-montara-sb.description: Montara State Beach is a sandy San Mateo coast beach surrounded by rocky outcrops, popular for beachcombing, surfing, and shore fishing. Across Highway 1, the McNee Ranch area offers trails on Montara Mountain.
ca-sp-montara-sb.what_they_offer:
- Sandy beach for strolling, surfing, and shore fishing (reached by staircase)
- Hiking and horseback riding trails at McNee Ranch on Montara Mountain, east of Highway 1
- Leashed dogs allowed
- No drinking water and no camping
ca-sp-montara-sb.how_to_get_it: Open 8 a.m. to sunset. No day-use fee is listed. Horses are allowed only on trails east of Highway 1. Overnight stays nearby are available at the Point Montara Lighthouse hostel.

recgov-monterey-bay-national-marine-sanc.name: Monterey Bay National Marine Sanctuary
recgov-monterey-bay-national-marine-sanc.description: Monterey Bay National Marine Sanctuary is one of the most spectacular marine protected areas. This sanctuary also has one of the largest underwater canyons and closest-to-shore deep ocean environments. By balancing activities and commercial uses with protection of natural resources, the vast area of waters provides some of the best wildlife viewing, as well as a variety of marine life, including several species of marine mammals, seabirds and shorebirds, invertebrates, and algae. Visitors can en

ca-sp-mount-diablo-sp.name: Mount Diablo SP
ca-sp-mount-diablo-sp.description: Mount Diablo State Park is known for summit views that can stretch more than 100 miles on clear days. Hikers, bicyclists, equestrians, and campers enjoy its varied habitats, wildlife, and wildflowers.
ca-sp-mount-diablo-sp.what_they_offer:
- Summit Visitor Center (open daily 10 a.m. to 4 p.m.) and Mitchell Canyon Visitor Center (weekends)
- Trails for hiking, biking, and horseback riding
- Tent, group, and hike-and-bike camping (reserve at ReserveCalifornia.com)
- Picnic areas and wildlife and wildflower viewing
ca-sp-mount-diablo-sp.how_to_get_it:
The vehicle entrance fee is $10 at the North Gate and South Gate entrances (a lower $6 rate may apply off-peak). Gates open at 8 a.m. and close at sunset.

ca-sp-mount-tamalpais-sp.name: Mount Tamalpais SP
ca-sp-mount-tamalpais-sp.description: Mount Tamalpais State Park rises from the heart of Marin County just north of the Golden Gate Bridge, with redwood forests, oak woodlands, and grasslands. Views from the upper mountain reach the Farallon Islands, San Francisco Bay, and Mount Diablo.
ca-sp-mount-tamalpais-sp.what_they_offer:
- Hiking and horseback riding trails with sweeping views
- First-come, first-served camping at Pantoll and Bootjack; reservable Alice Eastwood Group Camp and Steep Ravine cabins and campsites (ReserveCalifornia.com)
- East Peak Visitor Center, Gravity Car Barn, and programs at the Mountain Theater
- Picnic areas
ca-sp-mount-tamalpais-sp.how_to_get_it:
There is no park entrance fee, but parking fees apply at the East Peak, Pantoll, and Bootjack lots (credit cards at Pantoll during business hours; cash or check self-registration otherwise). Open daily 7 a.m. to sunset.

nps-muwo.description: Muir Woods National Monument protects old-growth coast redwood trees, some over 1,000 years old. Walk among these ancient giants in one of the last remaining old-growth redwood forests.
