imls-musee-mecanique.name: Musée Mécanique
imls-musee-mecanique.description: World's largest privately owned collection of coin-operated antique arcade machines with 300+ games. Free admission.

imls-museo-italo-americano.name: Museo Italo Americano
imls-museo-italo-americano.description: First US museum devoted to Italian and Italian-American art and culture, with galleries, library, and Italian language classes.

museum-craft-design.name: Museum of Craft and Design
museum-craft-design.description: The Museum of Craft and Design (MCD) in San Francisco's Dogpatch neighborhood explores the creative process through contemporary craft and design. It's the only museum in San Francisco devoted exclusively to craft and design.
museum-craft-design.what_they_offer:
- Free First Thursdays: Free admission for everyone on the first Thursday of the month
- EBT cardholders: Free admission
- SF Museums for All: Medi-Cal or CalFresh recipients get 4 free admission passes per visit
- Active-duty military, veterans, first responders, and their families: Free
- Children through age 12: Free
- Students with ID and seniors (65+): $8
- General admission: $10
museum-craft-design.how_to_get_it: Show your EBT, Medi-Cal, or CalFresh card, military or first responder ID, student ID, or proof of age at the front desk. Tickets are sold at the museum or online up to 60 days ahead; reserving is encouraged but not required. Open Thursday through Sunday, 12 to 5 p.m.

imls-museum-of-performance-design.name: Museum of Performance & Design
imls-museum-of-performance-design.description: Founded 1947, preserves Bay Area performing arts history with 3.5 million items including photos, costumes, and archives from SF Ballet, Opera, and more.

imls-museum-of-russian-culture.name: Museum of Russian Culture
imls-museum-of-russian-culture.description: Established 1948, features folk costumes, art, photographs from pre-revolutionary Russia, and WWII memorabilia. Free admission, open Wed & Sat 10:30am-2:30pm.

moad-museum.name: Museum of the African Diaspora (MoAD)
moad-museum.description: The Museum of the African Diaspora (MoAD) in San Francisco celebrates the history, art, and cultural contributions of people of African descent. Located in the Yerba Buena arts district, it features rotating contemporary art exhibitions and cultural programs.
moad-museum.what_they_offer:
- Museums for All: $3 admission with EBT card
- Active Military: Free admission with valid ID
- Students with ID: $8 admission
- Seniors (65+): $8 admission
- Children under 5: Free admission
- Community/Free days: Check website for schedule
- Regular admission: $12 adults
moad-museum.how_to_get_it: Present your EBT card, military ID, student ID, or proof of age at the admissions desk. Check website for community free day schedules.

imls-museum-of-the-san-ramon-valley.name: Museum of the San Ramon Valley
imls-museum-of-the-san-ramon-valley.description: Local history museum in the restored 1891 Southern Pacific Depot and 1888 schoolhouse, both on the National Register of Historic Places.

museums-for-all.name: Museums for All
museums-for-all.description: Museums for All is a national program that helps people receiving SNAP food assistance visit museums for free or at reduced cost. It is an initiative of the Institute of Museum and Library Services, administered by the Association of Children's Museums.
museums-for-all.what_they_offer:
- Free or reduced admission (typically $3 or less per person) for SNAP/CalFresh recipients
- More than 1,600 participating museums nationwide
- Includes science centers, children's museums, art museums, zoos, gardens, and more
- Many museums extend the discount to family members (group size varies by museum)
museums-for-all.how_to_get_it: Find a participating museum on the Museums for All map, then show your EBT (SNAP/CalFresh) card and a photo ID at admissions. Some museums may require advance booking, so check the museum's website first.

imls-napa-auto-museum.name: Napa Auto Museum
imls-napa-auto-museum.description: Museum with diverse collections and exhibits.

imls-napa-valley-museum.name: Napa Valley Museum
imls-napa-valley-museum.description: Nonprofit museum offering exhibitions and programs on art, nature, and history since 1972. Free for Yountville Veterans Home residents and active military.

recgov-naras-pacific-region-san-francisc.name: NARA's Pacific Region - San Francisco
recgov-naras-pacific-region-san-francisc.description: NARA's Pacific Region (San Francisco) has more than 48,000 cubic feet of archival holdings dating from 1850 to the 1980s, including textual documents, photographs, maps, and architectural drawings. These archival holdings were created or received by the Federal courts and more than 100 Federal agencies in northern California, Guam, Hawaii, Nevada (except Clark County), American Samoa, and the Trust Territory of the Pacific Islands. imls-natalie-and-james-thompson-art-gall.name: Natalie and James Thompson Art Gallery
imls-natalie-and-james-thompson-art-gall.description: San Jose State University art gallery featuring student exhibitions, Tuesday Night Lectures, and internationally renowned artists. Part of SJSU School of Art and Design.

imls-national-liberty-ship-memorial.name: National Liberty Ship Memorial (SS Jeremiah O'Brien)
imls-national-liberty-ship-memorial.description: Rare survivor of the 6,939-ship D-Day armada, one of only two operational Liberty ships remaining. National Historic Landmark.

imls-naturebridge.name: NatureBridge
imls-naturebridge.description: Environmental education nonprofit since 1971. Programs for students at Yosemite and Golden Gate National Recreation Area (Marin Headlands).

recgov-nimbus-fish-hatchery.name: Nimbus Fish Hatchery
recgov-nimbus-fish-hatchery.description: Nimbus Dam , on the American River 7 miles below Folsom Dam formed Lake Natoma to reregulate the releases for power made through Folsom Powerplant. The Nimbus Fish Hatchery was built on the left bank below the dam to compensate for the spawning areas of salmon and steelhead that were inundated by construction of Nimbus Dam. Nimbus Dam is a feature of the Central Valley Project - American River Division - Folsom and Sly Park Units . Open year-round for fish rearing and educational actvities. Fish
recgov-nimbus-fish-hatchery.what_they_offer: Outdoor recreation including hiking, wildlife viewing, and nature experiences. Some sites offer camping, picnicking, and water activities.
recgov-nimbus-fish-hatchery.how_to_get_it: Visit Recreation.gov to check availability, make reservations, and plan your visit. Some areas are free to visit while others may require permits or fees.

recgov-fac-no-name-flat-day-use.name: No Name Flat Day Use
recgov-fac-no-name-flat-day-use.description: No Name Flat Day Use is a activity pass available through Recreation.gov.
recgov-fac-no-name-flat-day-use.what_they_offer: Activity Pass at Lake Sonoma. Reservations available through Recreation.gov.
recgov-fac-no-name-flat-day-use.how_to_get_it: Make a reservation through Recreation.gov. Book early as popular sites fill up quickly.

recgov-oneill-forebay.name: O'Neill Forebay
recgov-oneill-forebay.description: O'Neill Dam and Forebay are joint Federal-State facilities located on San Luis Creek 2.5 miles downstream from San Luis Dam. O'Neill Forebay Dam is a feature of the Central Valley Project - San Joaquin Division - San Luis Unit . The reservoir has a surface area of 2,250 acres and 14 miles of shoreline. The Park includes boating, camping, picnic facilities, fishing, hiking, and serves as a major family destination for many in the west central valley. Currently an expansion of the Maderos boat ram
recgov-oneill-forebay.what_they_offer: Outdoor recreation including hiking, wildlife viewing, and nature experiences. Some sites offer camping, picnicking, and water activities.
recgov-oneill-forebay.how_to_get_it: Visit Recreation.gov to check availability, make reservations, and plan your visit. Some areas are free to visit while others may require permits or fees.

recgov-fac-oak-shores-day-use-area-ca.name: OAK SHORES DAY USE AREA (CA)
recgov-fac-oak-shores-day-use-area-ca.description: Overview Nestled between Blue Ridge and Cedar Roughs east of Napa Valley, Lake Berryessa provides ample public recreation opportunities. Popular activities on and around the large, yet uncrowded lake include fishing, boating, water skiing, wake boarding, jet skiing, sailing, swimming, kayaking, canoeing, wildlife viewing, hiking, biking and picnicking. The Dufer Point Visitor Center offers year-round interpretive events and exhibits highlighting natural and cultural resources. Lake Berryessa is
recgov-fac-oak-shores-day-use-area-ca.what_they_offer: Campground at Lake Berryessa. Reservations available through Recreation.gov.
recgov-fac-oak-shores-day-use-area-ca.how_to_get_it: Make a reservation through Recreation.gov. Book early as popular sites fill up quickly.

oakland-museum.name: Oakland Museum of California
oakland-museum.description: The Oakland Museum of California (OMCA) is a multidisciplinary museum celebrating California's art, history, and natural sciences. Located near Lake Merritt, it features gardens, exhibitions, and the popular Friday Nights @ OMCA events.
oakland-museum.what_they_offer:
- EBT cardholders: $1 admission per person
- Free First Sundays: Free admission for everyone
- Children under 9: Free admission
- Friday Nights @ OMCA: Half-price admission with food trucks and live music
- Regular admission: $16 adults
oakland-museum.how_to_get_it: Present your EBT card at the admissions desk for $1 admission any day. Visit on the first Sunday of each month for free entry. No reservations required for most visits.

imls-oakland-zoo.name: Oakland Zoo
imls-oakland-zoo.description: Wildlife facility dedicated to animal conservation and education.

oakland-zoo.name: Oakland Zoo – Bay to Zoo
oakland-zoo.description: Oakland Zoo is home to over 850 native and exotic animals on 100 acres in the Oakland hills. The zoo is committed to conservation and education, featuring the California Trail exhibit showcasing native wildlife.
oakland-zoo.what_they_offer:
- Bay to Zoo tickets for low-income Bay Area residents with a Golden State Advantage EBT card or California WIC card
- Up to 2 adult tickets (ages 15-64) at $5 each
- Up to 2 senior tickets (65+) and up to 4 child tickets (ages 2-14) at $3 each
- One free parking pass
- Good for regular daytime hours (not special events like Glowfari)
- Regular ticket prices vary by day; booking early costs less
oakland-zoo.how_to_get_it: Reserve Bay to Zoo tickets online in advance, since weekends and holidays sell out. On weekdays, tickets may be available at entry if not sold out; call 510-632-9525 x100 to check first. Bring your EBT or WIC card.

ca-sp-olompali-shp.name: Olompali SHP
ca-sp-olompali-shp.description: Olompali State Historic Park in Novato overlooks the Petaluma River and San Pablo Bay from the slopes of Mount Burdell. The Coast Miwok lived here from as early as 6,000 BC, and the name Olompali may mean southern village or southern people.
ca-sp-olompali-shp.what_they_offer:
- Hiking and horseback riding trails on Mount Burdell
- Coast Miwok cultural sites and historic ranch features
- Picnic areas
- No camping
ca-sp-olompali-shp.how_to_get_it:
Parking is $8 per vehicle (cash, check, or smartphone QR code with a $0.55 fee). Open daily 9 a.m. to 5 p.m.; the gate closes promptly at 5 p.m. You can also borrow a free State Park pass from Novato or other public libraries.

**Free and discount passes accepted here:**
- **Golden Bear Pass** (free): Free vehicle day use for CalWORKs, SSI, and Tribal TANF recipients, and income-eligible adults 62+
- **Senior Golden Bear Pass** ($20/year): Free entry for adults 62+ and a spouse or partner during non-peak season
- **Distinguished Veteran Pass** (free): Free day use, camping, and boating for eligible California veterans
- **Disabled Discount Pass** ($3.50, lifetime): 50% off vehicle day use and camping
- **California State Library Parks Pass**: Borrow a free vehicle day-use pass from your public library
- **Historian Passport** ($50/year): Admission for up to four people at state historic parks

imls-pacific-bus-museum.name: Pacific Bus Museum
imls-pacific-bus-museum.description: Collection of 20+ fully-restored running buses from the 1920s-1990s. Open 1st and 3rd Saturday, 10am-2pm. $5 donation for adults.

ca-sp-pacifica-sb.name: Pacifica SB
ca-sp-pacifica-sb.description: Pacifica State Beach (Linda Mar) is a wide, crescent-shaped beach off Highway 1 in Pacifica, popular for surfing. It is operated by the City of Pacifica.
ca-sp-pacifica-sb.what_they_offer:
- Sandy beach for surfing, swimming, and fishing
- Walking and biking trails
- Drinking water and wheelchair-accessible facilities
- Day use only (no camping)
ca-sp-pacifica-sb.how_to_get_it: Operated by the City of Pacifica. Vehicle day use is $9. The beach is day use only and closes at sundown. State Parks annual day-use passes are not accepted here. The parking lot is just south of Crespi Drive on Highway 1.

imls-peninsula-museum-of-art.name: Peninsula Museum of Art
imls-peninsula-museum-of-art.description: Nonprofit art museum (physical locations closed; virtual exhibitions available online).

ca-sp-pescadero-sb.name: Pescadero SB
ca-sp-pescadero-sb.description: Pescadero State Beach has a long sandy beach, rocky tide pools, and dramatic coastal views. Across Highway 1, Pescadero Marsh Natural Preserve is one of the region's richest wetland habitats for birds and wildlife.
ca-sp-pescadero-sb.what_they_offer:
- Mile-long shoreline with sandy coves, rocky cliffs, and tide pools
- Bird watching at Pescadero Marsh Natural Preserve
- Fishing and picnic areas
- No camping; limited facilities (pit toilet, no running water at the north lot)
ca-sp-pescadero-sb.how_to_get_it:
Parking is $8 per vehicle, paid on entry (U.S. cash or check; use the self-registration envelope when no attendant is present). Open 8 a.m. to sunset.

**Free and discount passes accepted here:**
- **Golden Bear Pass** (free): Free vehicle day use for CalWORKs, SSI, and Tribal TANF recipients, and income-eligible adults 62+
- **Senior Golden Bear Pass** ($20/year): Free entry for adults 62+ and a spouse or partner during non-peak season
- **Distinguished Veteran Pass** (free): Free day use, camping, and boating for eligible California veterans
- **Disabled Discount Pass** ($3.50, lifetime): 50% off vehicle day use and camping
- **California State Library Parks Pass**: Borrow a free vehicle day-use pass from your public library

ca-sp-petaluma-adobe-shp.name: Petaluma Adobe SHP
ca-sp-petaluma-adobe-shp.description: Petaluma Adobe State Historic Park preserves the huge adobe building at the center of one of California's most prosperous private ranchos during the Mexican period (1834-1846).
ca-sp-petaluma-adobe-shp.what_they_offer:
- Historic adobe building with exhibits
- Guided tours and family programs
- Picnic areas
- No camping
ca-sp-petaluma-adobe-shp.how_to_get_it:
Museum entry is $3 for adults, $2 for youth, and free for children 5 and under. Open daily 10 a.m. to 5 p.m. (the adobe closes at 4:30 p.m.); closed Thanksgiving, Christmas, and New Year's Day.

**Passes accepted here:**
- **Historian Passport** ($50/year): Admission for up to four people at state historic parks
- **Free Fourth Grade Pass**: Free entry for fourth graders and their families

imls-philippine-folklife-museum-foundati.name: Philippine Folklife Museum Foundation
imls-philippine-folklife-museum-foundati.description: Museum with diverse collections and exhibits.

ca-sp-pigeon-point-light-station-shp.name: Pigeon Point Light Station SHP
ca-sp-pigeon-point-light-station-shp.description: Pigeon Point Light Station State Historic Park sits on a cliff about 50 miles south of San Francisco. Its 115-foot lighthouse, one of the tallest on the West Coast, has guided mariners since 1872.
ca-sp-pigeon-point-light-station-shp.what_they_offer:
- Grounds with lighthouse views, picnic areas, and whale and seal watching
- The original 1872 Fresnel lens on display in the fog signal building
- Visitor center and park store (Thursday through Tuesday, 10 a.m. to 4 p.m., as staffing permits)
- Overnight lodging at HI Pigeon Point Lighthouse Hostel (fees apply); no camping
ca-sp-pigeon-point-light-station-shp.how_to_get_it: Admission and parking are free. The day-use area is open 8 a.m. to sunset. The lighthouse tower is closed for restoration but can be viewed from the grounds. For hostel reservations, call 650-879-0633.

imls-planetarium.name: Planetarium
imls-planetarium.description: Science and technology museum with interactive exhibits and educational programs.

imls-playland-not-at-the-beach.name: Playland-Not-At-The-Beach
imls-playland-not-at-the-beach.description: Nonprofit museum celebrating bygone amusements, featuring artifacts from San Francisco's historic Playland at the Beach and Sutro Baths.

ca-sp-point-montara-light-station.name: Point Montara Light Station
ca-sp-point-montara-light-station.description: Point Montara Light Station is a historic lighthouse on a bluff above the Pacific in Montara, about 25 miles south of San Francisco. It is home to HI Point Montara Lighthouse Hostel, which offers affordable dorm beds and private rooms.
ca-sp-point-montara-light-station.what_they_offer:
- Dorm beds, private rooms, and family and group accommodations (fees apply)
- Shared kitchen, native plant garden, and outdoor picnic area
- Access to tide pools and a small cove beach
- Close to Montara State Beach and McNee Ranch trails
ca-sp-point-montara-light-station.how_to_get_it: Book online through Hostelling International USA or call 650-728-7177.

nps-pore.name: Point Reyes National Seashore
nps-pore.description: Point Reyes National Seashore features dramatic coastal cliffs, pristine beaches, and diverse wildlife including tule elk. Explore the historic lighthouse and Point Reyes Station.
nps-pore.what_they_offer:
- Free or low-cost access to trails, beaches, and historic sites
- Ranger-led walks, talks, and educational programs
- Visitor centers with exhibits and park information
- Junior Ranger programs for children
nps-pore.how_to_get_it:
Most National Park Service sites in the Bay Area offer free admission. Some sites have entrance fees:
- Standard entrance fee: $15-$35 per vehicle (where applicable)
- Alcatraz ferry tickets sold separately

**Save with park passes:**

- **Senior Pass**: $80 lifetime or $20/year for ages 62+

ca-sp-pomponio-sb.name: Pomponio SB
ca-sp-pomponio-sb.description: Pomponio State Beach is a rugged San Mateo coast beach about 12 miles south of Half Moon Bay, where bluffs, broad sandy flats, and Pomponio Creek meet.
ca-sp-pomponio-sb.what_they_offer:
- Beach, creek mouth, and vista point
- Picnic areas and restrooms
- Fishing and wildlife viewing
- No camping
ca-sp-pomponio-sb.how_to_get_it:
Vehicle day use is $8. Open 8 a.m. to sunset.

**Free and discount passes accepted here:**
- **Golden Bear Pass** (free): Free vehicle day use for CalWORKs, SSI, and Tribal TANF recipients, and income-eligible adults 62+
- **Senior Golden Bear Pass** ($20/year): Free entry for adults 62+ and a spouse or partner during non-peak season

nps-poch.description: Port Chicago Naval Magazine National Memorial commemorates the 1944 explosion that killed 320 men and the subsequent mutiny trial of African American sailors who refused unsafe working conditions.

ca-sp-portola-redwoods-sp.name: Portola Redwoods SP
ca-sp-portola-redwoods-sp.description: Portola Redwoods State Park offers a quiet getaway in the Santa Cruz Mountains, with trails along creeks where coast redwoods stand among ferns and redwood sorrel.
ca-sp-portola-redwoods-sp.what_they_offer:
- Redwood forest hiking trails along creeks
- Tent, group, hike-and-bike, and backcountry camping (reserve at ReserveCalifornia.com)
- Visitor center (open daily 9 a.m. to 5 p.m.)
ca-sp-portola-redwoods-sp.how_to_get_it:
Vehicle day use is $10. Day-use hours are 6 a.m. to sunset. The park is reached by steep, winding mountain roads, and there is no gas or store in or near the park.

imls-portuguese-heritage-society-of-cali.name: Portuguese Heritage Society of California
imls-portuguese-heritage-society-of-cali.description: Operates the Portuguese Historical Museum at History Park and hosts the annual Dia de Portugal Festival on the second Saturday of June.

nps-prsf.name: Presidio of San Francisco
nps-prsf.description: Presidio of San Francisco, a former military post turned national park, offers trails, historic architecture, art installations, and stunning views of the Golden Gate Bridge and bay.
nps-prsf.what_they_offer:
- Free or low-cost access to trails, beaches, and historic sites
- Ranger-led walks, talks, and educational programs
- Visitor centers with exhibits and park information
- Junior Ranger programs for children

recgov-fac-public-boat-ramp-lake-sonoma.name: Public Boat Ramp (Lake Sonoma)
recgov-fac-public-boat-ramp-lake-sonoma.description: Public Boat Ramp (Lake Sonoma) is a activity pass available through Recreation.gov.

recgov-fac-public-boat-ramp-lake-sonoma.how_to_get_it: Make a reservation through Recreation.gov. Book early as popular sites fill up quickly.

recgov-fac-putah-canyon-campground-napa-.name: Putah Canyon Campground- Napa, CA (BOR)
recgov-fac-putah-canyon-campground-napa-.description: Overview Located in beautiful Napa County, Putah Canyon Campground is approximately 1/2 mile north of Pope Canyon Road, on Berryessa Knoxville Road, Napa, CA. It takes about 45 minutes from both Winters and Napa. Perfect for a quick getaway. Recreation Boating Fishing Swimming Stand-up Paddleboarding (SUPs) Kayaking Natural Features Putah Canyon Campground is located on the Northwestern shore of Lake Berryessa in Napa County, a resorvior created by the United States Bureau of Reclamation in 1957
recgov-fac-putah-canyon-campground-napa-.what_they_offer: Campground at Lake Berryessa. Reservations available through Recreation.gov.
recgov-fac-putah-canyon-campground-napa-.how_to_get_it: Make a reservation through Recreation.gov. Book early as popular sites fill up quickly.

recgov-fac-putah-canyon-day-use-and-boat.name: Putah Canyon Day Use and Boat Launch
recgov-fac-putah-canyon-day-use-and-boat.description: Putah Canyon Day Use and Boat Launch is a activity pass available through Recreation.gov.

recgov-fac-putah-canyon-day-use-and-boat.how_to_get_it: Make a reservation through Recreation.gov. Book early as popular sites fill up quickly.

imls-redwood-empire-live-steamers.name: Redwood Empire Live Steamers
imls-redwood-empire-live-steamers.description: Volunteer-run miniature railroad offering free train rides May-October, first weekend of the month, noon-4pm. Features steam and diesel locomotives on 2,000-foot track.

ca-sp-robert-louis-stevenson-sp.name: Robert Louis Stevenson SP
ca-sp-robert-louis-stevenson-sp.description: Robert Louis Stevenson State Park is a 5,272-acre undeveloped park north of Calistoga with trails to the summit of Mount St. Helena and views of Napa, Sonoma, and Lake counties. It is operated by the Napa County Regional Park and Open Space District.
ca-sp-robert-louis-stevenson-sp.what_they_offer:
- Hiking trails, including the climb to the summit of Mount St. Helena
- Vista points and geocaching
- No camping and no dogs allowed
- Open sunrise to sunset
ca-sp-robert-louis-stevenson-sp.how_to_get_it:
No day use fee. Parking is a small lot on Highway 29, about 7 miles north of Calistoga, and fills early on busy days.

Call the park at (707) 942-4575 or see the Napa County Regional Park and Open Space District website for trail conditions.

ca-sp-robert-w-crown-memorial-sb.name: Robert W Crown Memorial SB
ca-sp-robert-w-crown-memorial-sb.description: Robert W. Crown Memorial State Beach in Alameda has 2.5 miles of bay beach bordered by lawns, picnic areas, and a bike trail, plus the Crab Cove Visitor Center. It is operated by the East Bay Regional Park District.
ca-sp-robert-w-crown-memorial-sb.what_they_offer:
- Sandy bay beach for swimming, windsurfing, kiteboarding, and kayaking
- Picnic areas, lawns, and a paved bike trail
- Crab Cove Visitor Center with free naturalist programs
- Open 5am to 10pm; dogs allowed on lawns and paved paths only, not on the beach
ca-sp-robert-w-crown-memorial-sb.how_to_get_it:
Parking: $5 per vehicle (card only at the pay station). Walking or biking in is free.

Contact the East Bay Regional Park District at 510-562-PARK (7275) for programs and current conditions.

imls-rosicrucian-egyptian-museum.name: Rosicrucian Egyptian Museum
imls-rosicrucian-egyptian-museum.description: Largest collection of Egyptian artifacts on exhibit in western North America.

imls-rosicrucian-planetarium.name: Rosicrucian Planetarium
imls-rosicrucian-planetarium.description: Part of the Rosicrucian Egyptian Museum, featuring astronomy shows and one of the largest Egyptian artifact collections in the western United States.

nps-rori.name: Rosie the Riveter WWII Home Front National Historical Park
nps-rori.description: Rosie the Riveter/WWII Home Front National Historical Park commemorates the contributions of American civilians on the World War II home front, especially women who worked in wartime industries.
nps-rori.what_they_offer:
- Free or low-cost access to trails, beaches, and historic sites
- Ranger-led walks, talks, and educational programs
- Visitor centers with exhibits and park information
- Junior Ranger programs for children
nps-rori.how_to_get_it:
Most National Park Service sites in the Bay Area offer free admission. Some sites have entrance fees:
- Standard entrance fee: $15-$35 per vehicle (where applicable)
- Alcatraz ferry tickets sold separately

**Save with park passes:**

- **Every Kid Outdoors Pass**: Free for 4th graders and their families
- **Access Pass**: Free lifetime pass for visitors with permanent disabilities
- **Senior Pass**: $80 lifetime or $20/year for ages 62+

recgov-s-f-bay-model-regional-visitor-ce.name: S F Bay Model Regional Visitor Center
recgov-s-f-bay-model-regional-visitor-ce.description: The Bay Model was built in 1957 as a research tool to test the impact of proposed changes to San Francisco Bay and its related waterways. The model has been used to study the effects of chemical/oil spills, altering of shipping channels, levee failures, and bay in-filling. The hydraulic model was used to simulate currents, tidal action, sediment movement and the mixing of fresh and salt water. In 1980 the visitor center portion was added, and the Model adopted the function of an Educational Cent
recgov-s-f-bay-model-regional-visitor-ce.what_they_offer: Outdoor recreation including hiking, wildlife viewing, and nature experiences. Some sites offer camping, picnicking, and water activities.
recgov-s-f-bay-model-regional-visitor-ce.how_to_get_it: Visit Recreation.gov to check availability, make reservations, and plan your visit. Some areas are free to visit while others may require permits or fees.

ca-sp-salt-point-sp.name: Salt Point SP
ca-sp-salt-point-sp.description: Salt Point State Park includes six miles of rugged Sonoma coastline with coves, sandstone cliffs, forested hills, prairies, a pygmy forest, and an underwater park.
ca-sp-salt-point-sp.what_they_offer:
- 20+ miles of hiking trails
- Tide pools, fishing, and scuba diving in the underwater park
- Tent, RV, group, hike-and-bike, and environmental campsites (reserve at ReserveCalifornia.com)
- Picnic areas and interpretive programs
ca-sp-salt-point-sp.how_to_get_it:
- Vehicle day use: $10
- Camping: reserve at ReserveCalifornia.com
- Park phone: (707) 847-3221

**Passes accepted at this park:**
- **California State Library Parks Pass**: Free vehicle day use; check one out from your public library
- **Golden Bear Pass**: Free vehicle day use for income-eligible Californians
- **Senior Golden Bear Pass**: $20/year for ages 62+ (not valid in peak season)
- **Disabled Discount Pass**: 50% off vehicle day use and camping
- **Distinguished Veteran Pass**: Free vehicle day use and camping for eligible veterans

ca-sp-samuel-p-taylor-sp.name: Samuel P Taylor SP
ca-sp-samuel-p-taylor-sp.description: Samuel P. Taylor State Park in west Marin has 2,882 acres of redwood groves along Lagunitas Creek, oak grasslands, and hikes to Barnabe Peak.
ca-sp-samuel-p-taylor-sp.what_they_offer:
- Hiking, biking, and horseback riding trails, including the Cross Marin Trail
- Tent, RV, group, equestrian, and hike-and-bike campsites, plus cabins (reserve at ReserveCalifornia.com)
- Picnic areas and interpretive programs
- Creek access closed December 1 to June 15 each year to protect salmon
ca-sp-samuel-p-taylor-sp.how_to_get_it:
- Vehicle day use: $8
- Camping: reserve at ReserveCalifornia.com
- Park phone: (415) 488-9897

**Passes accepted at this park:**
- **California State Library Parks Pass**: Free vehicle day use; check one out from your public library
- **Golden Bear Pass**: Free vehicle day use for income-eligible Californians
- **Senior Golden Bear Pass**: $20/year for ages 62+ (not valid in peak season)
- **Disabled Discount Pass**: 50% off vehicle day use and camping
- **Distinguished Veteran Pass**: Free vehicle day use and camping for eligible veterans
- **Free Fourth Grade Pass**: Free vehicle day use for California 4th graders and their families

ca-sp-san-bruno-mountain-sp.name: San Bruno Mountain SP
ca-sp-san-bruno-mountain-sp.description: San Bruno Mountain State Park near Daly City and Brisbane offers hiking trails, habitat for rare plants and endangered butterflies, and views of San Francisco and the bay. It is operated by San Mateo County Parks.
ca-sp-san-bruno-mountain-sp.what_they_offer:
- Hiking, biking, and horseback riding trails
- Picnic areas and guided tours
- Group campsites
- Open 8am to before sunset; no dogs allowed
ca-sp-san-bruno-mountain-sp.how_to_get_it:
- Vehicle day use: $6
- Park is operated by San Mateo County Parks; call (650) 363-4020 to confirm hours and group camp reservations.

State park passes are not listed as accepted at this park.

recgov-san-francisco-bay-national-estuar.name: San Francisco Bay National Estuarine Research Reserve
recgov-san-francisco-bay-national-estuar.description: The San Francisco Bay National Estuarine Research Reserve comprises two components located along the salinity gradient of the San Francisco Bay. The reserve's 3,710 acres are located at China Camp State Park in San Rafael and Rush Ranch in Suisun City, 30 miles north and 50 miles northeast of San Francisco, respectively. A primary focus of the reserve is to support tidal marsh restoration through research, monitoring and education. These sites serve as valuable reference sites in the San Francis
recgov-san-francisco-bay-national-estuar.what_they_offer: Outdoor recreation including hiking, wildlife viewing, and nature experiences. Some sites offer camping, picnicking, and water activities.
recgov-san-francisco-bay-national-estuar.how_to_get_it: Visit Recreation.gov to check availability, make reservations, and plan your visit. Some areas are free to visit while others may require permits or fees.

imls-san-francisco-jewelry-museum.name: San Francisco Jewelry Museum
imls-san-francisco-jewelry-museum.description: Museum with diverse collections and exhibits.

nps-safr.name: San Francisco Maritime National Historical Park
nps-safr.description: San Francisco Maritime National Historical Park preserves a fleet of historic vessels and the maritime heritage of the Pacific Coast. Visit Hyde Street Pier to board historic ships.
nps-safr.what_they_offer:
- Free or low-cost access to trails, beaches, and historic sites
- Ranger-led walks, talks, and educational programs
- Visitor centers with exhibits and park information
- Junior Ranger programs for children
nps-safr.how_to_get_it:
Most National Park Service sites in the Bay Area offer free admission. Some sites have entrance fees:
- Standard entrance fee: $15-$35 per vehicle (where applicable)
- Alcatraz ferry tickets sold separately

**Save with park passes:**
- **America the Beautiful Pass**: $80/year for unlimited access to 2,000+ federal recreation areas
- **Every Kid Outdoors Pass**: Free for 4th graders and their families
- **Access Pass**: Free lifetime pass for visitors with permanent disabilities
- **Senior Pass**: $80 lifetime or $20/year for ages 62+

sfmoma.name: San Francisco Museum of Modern Art (SFMOMA)
sfmoma.description: SFMOMA is one of the largest museums of modern and contemporary art in the United States, featuring an expansive collection of painting, sculpture, photography, architecture, design, and media arts in its distinctive building in downtown San Francisco.
sfmoma.what_they_offer:
- Ages 18 and under: Always free
- Museums for All: Free for San Francisco residents with Medi-Cal, CalFresh, SNAP, or EBT (up to 4 adult tickets, including special exhibitions)
- Military: Free general admission with active military or veteran ID, plus one guest; free for up to five guests during Blue Star Museums (Armed Forces Day through Labor Day)
- Free Community Days and Free Family Days throughout the year
- Discover & Go: Free passes through participating Bay Area libraries
- Regular admission: $30 adults, $25 seniors 65+, $23 full-time students
sfmoma.how_to_get_it: Youth 18 and under get free admission. For Museums for All, bring your benefits card and proof of San Francisco residency on the day of your visit. Military tickets are same-day, walk-up only at the ticketing desk. Check your library for Discover & Go passes. Free Day tickets are released online in advance. The museum is closed Wednesdays.

imls-san-francisco-zoological-gardens.name: San Francisco Zoo & Gardens
imls-san-francisco-zoological-gardens.description: AZA-accredited 100-acre zoo with 2,000+ animals including grizzlies, gorillas, and the largest outdoor lemur habitat in the US.

ca-sp-san-gregorio-sb.name: San Gregorio SB
ca-sp-san-gregorio-sb.description: San Gregorio State Beach, south of Half Moon Bay, is a wide sandy beach with coastal bluffs and a driftwood-strewn estuary that is home to many birds.
ca-sp-san-gregorio-sb.what_they_offer:
- Beach access for walking, fishing, and surfing
- Estuary wildlife viewing and picnic areas
- Day use only (no camping); no dogs or beach fires allowed
- Open 8am to sunset
ca-sp-san-gregorio-sb.how_to_get_it:
- Vehicle day use: $8
- Park phone: (650) 726-8819

**Passes accepted at this park:**
- **California State Library Parks Pass**: Free vehicle day use; check one out from your public library
- **Golden Bear Pass**: Free vehicle day use for income-eligible Californians
- **Senior Golden Bear Pass**: $20/year for ages 62+ (not valid in peak season)
- **Disabled Discount Pass**: 50% off vehicle day use and camping
- **Distinguished Veteran Pass**: Free vehicle day use and camping for eligible veterans

recgov-san-joaquin-river-national-wildli.name: San Joaquin River National Wildlife Refuge
recgov-san-joaquin-river-national-wildli.description: The San Joaquin River National Wildlife Refuge located in Stanislaus County encompasses more than 7,300 acres of riparian woodlands, wetlands, and grasslands that host a diversity of wildlife native to California’s Great Central Valley. The refuge is situated where three major Valley rivers – San Joaquin, Tuolumne, and Stanislaus – join creating a mosaic of habitats that provide ideal conditions for great wildlife and plant diversity. The refuge was established in 1987 under the Endangered Speci
recgov-san-joaquin-river-national-wildli.what_they_offer: Outdoor recreation including hiking, wildlife viewing, and nature experiences. Some sites offer camping, picnicking, and water activities.
recgov-san-joaquin-river-national-wildli.how_to_get_it: Visit Recreation.gov to check availability, make reservations, and plan your visit. Some areas are free to visit while others may require permits or fees.

sj-museum-art.name: San Jose Museum of Art
sj-museum-art.description: The San Jose Museum of Art is the leading museum of modern and contemporary art in Silicon Valley, located in a beautiful historic building in downtown San Jose. It features rotating exhibitions and a growing permanent collection.
sj-museum-art.what_they_offer:
- EBT cardholders: Free admission for up to four people (Museums for All)
- Youth 17 and under, college students, and teachers: Free admission
- First Fridays: Free admission for everyone after 6pm
- Discover & Go: Free passes for up to four people through participating libraries
- Active-duty military and family: Free from Memorial Day weekend through Labor Day (Blue Star Museums)
- Regular admission: $20 adults, $15 seniors 65+
sj-museum-art.how_to_get_it: Show your EBT card when you arrive for free admission for up to four people. Youth, college students, and teachers can order free tickets online. Visit after 6pm on the first Friday of the month for free admission. The museum is open Tuesday through Sunday.

recgov-san-justo-reservoir.name: San Justo Reservoir
recgov-san-justo-reservoir.description: San Justo Dam and Reservoir are features of the San Felipe Project. The reservoir is approximately 3 miles southwest of Hollister, California . Facilities open for use Wednesday through Sunday. Operation hours: sunrise to sunset. Good access roads. The park offers recreation to anglers, boaters, windsurfers, picnickers, and mountain bikers. Boat size restricted to 16 feet. Gas engines prohibited. Ideal for small sailboats and windsurfers in the beginning to intermediate range. Experienced surfer
recgov-san-justo-reservoir.what_they_offer: Outdoor recreation including hiking, wildlife viewing, and nature experiences. Some sites offer camping, picnicking, and water activities.
recgov-san-justo-reservoir.how_to_get_it: Visit Recreation.gov to check availability, make reservations, and plan your visit. Some areas are free to visit while others may require permits or fees.

recgov-san-luis-reservoir.name: San Luis Reservoir
recgov-san-luis-reservoir.description: Recreation area lakes include O'Neill Forebay, San Luis Reservoir, and Los Banos Creek Reservoir. All are part of the California Water Project and operated jointly by the California Department of Parks and Recreation, the California Department of Water Resources, and the Bureau of Reclamation. Office hours; 8:00a.m. - 4:30p.m., Monday through Friday. Closed holidays. Facilities open 7 days a week. Good access roads. Camping, boating, picnicking, and swimming. Regular strong winds make O'Neill Fo
recgov-san-luis-reservoir.what_they_offer: Outdoor recreation including hiking, wildlife viewing, and nature experiences. Some sites offer camping, picnicking, and water activities.
recgov-san-luis-reservoir.how_to_get_it: Visit Recreation.gov to check availability, make reservations, and plan your visit. Some areas are free to visit while others may require permits or fees.

recgov-san-pablo-bay-national-wildlife-r.name: San Pablo Bay National Wildlife Refuge
recgov-san-pablo-bay-national-wildlife-r.description: In response to rapidly disappearing wetlands and its prime location within the Pacific Flyway, the refuge was created in 1974 to protect migratory birds, wetland habitat, and endangered species. The refuge and San Pablo Bay supports the largest wintering population of canvasbacks on the west coast of the United States and protects the endangered salt marsh harvest mouse and California Ridgway's rail. The San Pablo Bay National Wildlife Refuge lies along the north shore of San Pablo Bay in Sonoma
recgov-san-pablo-bay-national-wildlife-r.what_they_offer: Outdoor recreation including hiking, wildlife viewing, and nature experiences. Some sites offer camping, picnicking, and water activities.
recgov-san-pablo-bay-national-wildlife-r.how_to_get_it: Visit Recreation.gov to check availability, make reservations, and plan your visit. Some areas are free to visit while others may require permits or fees.

imls-sanchez-art-center.name: Sanchez Art Center
imls-sanchez-art-center.description: Nonprofit arts center with three exhibition galleries and annual juried shows. Free admission. Home to the Art Guild of Pacifica.

imls-secession-gallery.name: Secession Gallery
imls-secession-gallery.description: Art museum featuring collections and exhibitions.

senior-golden-bear-pass.name: Senior Golden Bear Pass
senior-golden-bear-pass.description: California State Parks offers a $20 Senior Golden Bear Pass for people age 62 and over, giving free vehicle day-use entry to over 200 state park units outside the peak summer season.
senior-golden-bear-pass.what_they_offer:
- $20 pass for people 62+ that also covers a spouse or registered domestic partner
- Free vehicle day-use entry at over 200 parks operated by California State Parks
- Not valid during peak season (the Friday before Memorial Day through Labor Day at most parks)
- Valid from the date issued until December 31 of that year
senior-golden-bear-pass.how_to_get_it: Apply in person at a designated State Parks pass sales location (fastest), online through ReserveCalifornia, or by mail with the application form. You'll need proof of age (62 or older) and the $20 payment. After approval you get a 30-day temporary pass to use while your card is mailed.
senior-golden-bear-pass.timeframe: Annual (valid through December 31 of the year issued)

ca-sp-sonoma-coast-sp.name: Sonoma Coast SP
ca-sp-sonoma-coast-sp.description: Sonoma Coast State Park is a series of beaches from Bodega Bay to the Russian River with coves, headlands, natural arches, tide pools, and some of the best winter whale watching in California.
ca-sp-sonoma-coast-sp.what_they_offer:
- Beaches, tide pools, fishing, and whale watching
- Hiking and horseback riding trails
- Tent, RV, hike-and-bike, and environmental campsites (reserve at ReserveCalifornia.com)
- Dogs allowed on specific beaches only
ca-sp-sonoma-coast-sp.how_to_get_it:
- Vehicle day use: $10
- Camping: reserve at ReserveCalifornia.com
- Park phone: (707) 875-3483

**Passes accepted at this park:**
- **California State Library Parks Pass**: Free vehicle day use; check one out from your public library
- **Golden Bear Pass**: Free vehicle day use for income-eligible Californians
- **Senior Golden Bear Pass**: $20/year for ages 62+ (not valid in peak season)
- **Disabled Discount Pass**: 50% off vehicle day use and camping
- **Distinguished Veteran Pass**: Free vehicle day use and camping for eligible veterans

imls-sonoma-museum-of-visual-art.name: Sonoma Museum of Visual Art
imls-sonoma-museum-of-visual-art.description: Art museum featuring collections and exhibitions.

ca-sp-sonoma-shp.name: Sonoma SHP
ca-sp-sonoma-shp.description: Sonoma State Historic Park preserves historic sites around Sonoma Plaza, including Mission San Francisco Solano, the Sonoma Barracks, and General Vallejo's home, in the birthplace of the California Bear Flag.
ca-sp-sonoma-shp.what_they_offer:
- Museums and historic buildings, including Mission San Francisco Solano and the Sonoma Barracks
- Guided tours, family programs, and special events
- Free public parking behind the Sonoma Barracks
- Open daily 10am to 5pm (closed Thanksgiving, Christmas, and New Year's Day)
ca-sp-sonoma-shp.how_to_get_it:
Museum entry fees:
- Adults: $3
- Youth: $2
- Children 5 and under: Free

Park phone: (707) 938-9560

**Passes accepted at this park:**
- **Historian Passport**: Annual day use admission pass for state historic parks
- **Free Fourth Grade Pass**: Free entry for California 4th graders and their families

imls-sonoma-valley-museum-of-art.name: Sonoma Valley Museum of Art
imls-sonoma-valley-museum-of-art.description: Contemporary and modern art museum one block from Sonoma's historic Town Plaza. Free admission on Wednesdays.

recgov-fac-south-lake-trailhead.name: South Lake Trailhead
recgov-fac-south-lake-trailhead.description: South Lake Trailhead is a activity pass available through Recreation.gov.
recgov-fac-south-lake-trailhead.what_they_offer: Activity Pass at Lake Sonoma. Reservations available through Recreation.gov.
recgov-fac-south-lake-trailhead.how_to_get_it: Make a reservation through Recreation.gov. Book early as popular sites fill up quickly.

imls-starab-planetarium.name: Starab Planetarium
imls-starab-planetarium.description: Science and technology museum with interactive exhibits and educational programs.

recgov-stone-lakes-national-wildlife-ref.name: Stone Lakes National Wildlife Refuge
recgov-stone-lakes-national-wildlife-ref.description: Established in 1992, Stone Lakes National Wildlife Refuge is an urban refuge located 10 miles from downtown Sacramento sandwiched between the city of Elk Grove and agricultural lands. Conserving and enhancing Central Valley habitat and wildlife, the refuge hosts a variety of Central Valley habitats including grassland savannah, riparian forest, wetlands, and native freshwater lakes. Year-round and seasonal public use activities include the free environmental education site Blue Heron Trails , do
recgov-stone-lakes-national-wildlife-ref.what_they_offer: Outdoor recreation including hiking, wildlife viewing, and nature experiences. Some sites offer camping, picnicking, and water activities.
recgov-stone-lakes-national-wildlife-ref.how_to_get_it: Visit Recreation.gov to check availability, make reservations, and plan your visit. Some areas are free to visit while others may require permits or fees.

ca-sp-sugarloaf-ridge-sp.name: Sugarloaf Ridge SP
ca-sp-sugarloaf-ridge-sp.description: Sugarloaf Ridge State Park near Kenwood contains the headwaters of Sonoma Creek and trails to the summit of Bald Mountain. It is operated by the nonprofit Sonoma Ecology Center and is home to the Robert Ferguson Observatory.
ca-sp-sugarloaf-ridge-sp.what_they_offer:
- Hiking, biking, and horseback riding trails
- Tent, RV, and group campsites (reserve at ReserveCalifornia.com)
- Robert Ferguson Observatory astronomy programs
- Day use hours 6am to 10pm
ca-sp-sugarloaf-ridge-sp.how_to_get_it:
- Vehicle day use: $8
- Camping: reserve at ReserveCalifornia.com
- Park phone: (707) 833-6084

**Passes accepted at this park:**
- **California State Library Parks Pass**: Free vehicle day use; check one out from your public library
- **Golden Bear Pass**: Free vehicle day use for income-eligible Californians
- **Senior Golden Bear Pass**: $20/year for ages 62+ (not valid in peak season)
- **Disabled Discount Pass**: 50% off vehicle day use and camping
- **Distinguished Veteran Pass**: Free vehicle day use and camping for eligible veterans

imls-sunnyvale-heritage-park-museum.name: Sunnyvale Heritage Park Museum
imls-sunnyvale-heritage-park-museum.description: Historical museum in a replica of the 1850 Martin Murphy House, with heritage orchard and agricultural history exhibits. Free admission.

recgov-the-geysers.name: The Geysers
recgov-the-geysers.description: The Geysers encompasses about 7,100 acres of public lands and straddles the Lake County/Sonoma County line. The Geysers is administered by BLM's Ukiah Field Office.
recgov-the-geysers.what_they_offer: Outdoor recreation including hiking, wildlife viewing, and nature experiences. Some sites offer camping, picnicking, and water activities.
recgov-the-geysers.how_to_get_it: Visit Recreation.gov to check availability, make reservations, and plan your visit. Some areas are free to visit while others may require permits or fees.

the-tech-interactive.name: The Tech Interactive
the-tech-interactive.description: The Tech Interactive (formerly The Tech Museum) is a hands-on science and technology center in downtown San Jose. Featuring innovative exhibits on robotics, virtual reality, renewable energy, and more, it inspires the next generation of innovators.
the-tech-interactive.what_they_offer:
- Museums for All: $5 per person general admission for up to six people with a SNAP/EBT, BIC, or WIC card
- Add an educational IMAX film for $5 more per person with Museums for All
- Military and veterans: Free general admission (galleries only) year-round; up to five family members also free May through September (Blue Star Museums)
- Regular admission: $38 adults; $28 children 3-17, students, and seniors 65+ (includes one educational IMAX film)
the-tech-interactive.how_to_get_it: Show a valid SNAP/EBT, BIC, or WIC card with ID at the box office; this discount is redeemed in person, not online. The Tech is closed most Mondays, so check hours before you go.

ca-sp-thornton-sb.name: Thornton SB
ca-sp-thornton-sb.description: Thornton State Beach in Daly City is currently closed to the public. There is no beach access, but a viewing platform just west of the parking lot overlooks the coast.
ca-sp-thornton-sb.what_they_offer:
- The beach is currently not open to the public
- Viewing platform west of the parking lot
- The Bay Area Ridge Trail starts nearby on Mayfair Drive
ca-sp-thornton-sb.how_to_get_it: The beach is closed and there is no beach access. Check the California State Parks page for reopening updates before visiting.

ca-sp-tomales-bay-sp.name: Tomales Bay SP
ca-sp-tomales-bay-sp.description: Tomales Bay State Park sits on the eastern edge of the Point Reyes Peninsula, with sheltered coves, swimming beaches such as Heart's Desire Beach, tidal marshes, and a bishop pine forest.
ca-sp-tomales-bay-sp.what_they_offer:
- Sheltered beaches for swimming, kayaking, and picnicking
- Hiking trails through bishop pine forest
- Boat ramp and fishing
- Day use only (8am to sunset); dogs allowed only at Vista Point Picnic Area
ca-sp-tomales-bay-sp.how_to_get_it:
- Vehicle day use: $8
- Park phone: (415) 669-1140

**Passes accepted at this park:**
- **California State Library Parks Pass**: Free vehicle day use; check one out from your public library
- **Golden Bear Pass**: Free vehicle day use for income-eligible Californians
- **Senior Golden Bear Pass**: $20/year for ages 62+ (not valid in peak season)
- **Disabled Discount Pass**: 50% off vehicle day use and camping
- **Distinguished Veteran Pass**: Free vehicle day use and camping for eligible veterans

imls-treasure-island-museum-association.name: Treasure Island Museum
imls-treasure-island-museum-association.description: Free museum covering the 1939 Golden Gate International Exposition, Navy history, and island development. Open daily.

ca-sp-trione-annadel-sp.name: Trione Annadel SP
ca-sp-trione-annadel-sp.description: Trione-Annadel State Park on the eastern edge of Santa Rosa is a favorite for hikers, mountain bikers, and horseback riders, with miles of trails and spring wildflowers around Lake Ilsanjo.
ca-sp-trione-annadel-sp.what_they_offer:
- Miles of trails for hiking, mountain biking, and horseback riding
- Fishing at Lake Ilsanjo
- Picnic areas
- Day use only (8am to sunset); dogs allowed only in developed areas, not on trails
ca-sp-trione-annadel-sp.how_to_get_it:
- Vehicle day use: $7
- Park phone: (707) 539-3911

**Passes accepted at this park:** California Explorer and Golden Poppy annual vehicle day use passes. Golden Bear, Disabled Discount, and Distinguished Veteran passes are not listed as accepted here.

imls-uc-berkeley-art-museum.name: UC Berkeley Art Museum (BAMPFA)
imls-uc-berkeley-art-museum.description: Berkeley Art Museum and Pacific Film Archive with 25,000+ artworks and 18,000 films. Free for UC Berkeley students and first Thursdays.

imls-valle-del-sur.name: Valle Del Sur
imls-valle-del-sur.description: Art museum featuring collections and exhibitions.

imls-valley-children-s-museum.name: Valley Children's Museum
imls-valley-children-s-museum.description: Interactive museum designed for children and families with hands-on exhibits.

walt-disney-family-museum.name: Walt Disney Family Museum
walt-disney-family-museum.description: The Walt Disney Family Museum in San Francisco's Presidio tells the story of Walt Disney's life through interactive galleries featuring original artwork, early drawings, films, music, and a stunning model of Disneyland.
walt-disney-family-museum.what_they_offer:
- US military (active, retired, and veteran) and dependents: Free general admission year-round with valid ID
- San Francisco Museums for All: Free general admission for the cardholder plus three guests with SF residency and a CalFresh, EBT, or Medi-Cal card
- Primary caregiver of a person with a disability: Free general admission
- Students with ID: $20 admission
- Seniors (65+): $20 admission
- Youth 6-17: $15 admission
- Children 5 and under: Free
- Regular admission: $30 adults
walt-disney-family-museum.how_to_get_it: For military free admission, show valid military or dependent ID. For Museums for All, present your benefits card and proof of San Francisco residency in person at the Ticket Desk. The museum is open Thursday through Sunday, 10am-5:30pm; timed tickets are recommended.

recgov-fac-warm-springs-rec-area.name: WARM SPRINGS REC AREA
recgov-fac-warm-springs-rec-area.description: Overview Warm Springs Recreation Area is a day-use park located at Lake Sonoma, which is just a 45 minute drive north of Santa Rosa and a 2 hour trip from San Francisco. There is no overnight camping available at this facility World famous vineyards and a land rich in history surround the lake, where visitors enjoy boating, fishing and exploring the area's extensive trail network. Recreation The Woodland Ridge Nature Trail begins at the park and winds up the ridge, rewarding hikers with great vi
recgov-fac-warm-springs-rec-area.what_they_offer: Campground at Lake Sonoma. Reservations available through Recreation.gov.
recgov-fac-warm-springs-rec-area.how_to_get_it: Make a reservation through Recreation.gov. Book early as popular sites fill up quickly.

recgov-fac-yorty-creek-recreation-area-d.name: Yorty Creek Recreation Area Day Use
recgov-fac-yorty-creek-recreation-area-d.description: Yorty Creek Recreation Area Day Use is a activity pass available through Recreation.gov.
recgov-fac-yorty-creek-recreation-area-d.what_they_offer: Activity Pass at Lake Sonoma. Reservations available through Recreation.gov.
recgov-fac-yorty-creek-recreation-area-d.how_to_get_it: Make a reservation through Recreation.gov. Book early as popular sites fill up quickly.

7-eleven-gold-pass.name: 7-Eleven Gold Pass
7-eleven-gold-pass.description: 7-Eleven is one of the world's largest convenience store chains. Their Gold Pass membership offers free drinks, fuel savings, $0 delivery fees, and member-only deals, with up to 40% off for students, EBT card holders, and other verified community members.
7-eleven-gold-pass.what_they_offer:
- Gold Pass regularly $9.95/month or $95/year
- Up to 40% off ($5.95/month or $55/year) for students, EBT card holders, and other ID.me-verified community members (such as military and veterans)
- 7 free drinks per month (coffee, Big Gulp, or Slurpee; 1 per day)
- Extra 5¢/gallon off fuel at participating locations
- $0 delivery fee on 7NOW orders and 10% back in 7-Eleven Cash
- 30-day free trial
7-eleven-gold-pass.how_to_get_it:
1. Download the 7-Eleven or 7NOW app on your smartphone
2. Create an account or sign in
3. Open the Gold Pass hub or 'Community Discounts' in your profile
4. Verify your eligibility with ID.me (students, EBT card holders, military, and other communities)
5. Start your discounted membership

amazon-prime-access.name: Amazon Prime Access
amazon-prime-access.description: Amazon is the world's largest online retailer. Prime Access offers a discounted Prime membership for those receiving government assistance, providing free shipping, streaming, and more.
amazon-prime-access.what_they_offer:
- Discounted Prime membership at $6.99/month (regularly $14.99/month)
- Free two-day shipping on millions of items
- Prime Video streaming (movies, TV shows)
- Amazon Music, Prime Reading, Grubhub+, and more
- 30-day free trial for new customers
amazon-prime-access.how_to_get_it:
1. Visit amazon.com/primeaccess
2. Verify eligibility with an EBT card or proof of a qualifying program (SNAP, Medicaid, SSI, TANF, National School Lunch Program, and others)
3. Or verify household income
4. Complete enrollment and start your membership
5. Re-verify eligibility when Amazon asks

att-access.name: AT&T Access
att-access.description: AT&T is one of the largest telecommunications companies in the United States. Access from AT&T provides low-cost home internet service to eligible low-income households.
att-access.what_they_offer:
- Low-cost home internet on AT&T Fiber or AT&T Internet Air
- Monthly price and speed depend on what's available at your address
- Eligible customers with AT&T Fiber or Internet Air may get $10/month off an eligible unlimited AT&T wireless plan
- Existing AT&T internet customers can switch to the lower price once approved
att-access.how_to_get_it:
1. Enter your address at att.com/internet/access to see options and pricing
2. Qualify through a government program (such as SNAP, SSI, TANF, LIHEAP, federal public housing, or school lunch programs) or household income at or below 200% of the federal poverty guideline
3. Apply online and upload proof of eligibility
4. Once approved, order service or call 855-220-5211 to apply the price to existing service

california-lifeline.name: California LifeLine Program
california-lifeline.description: California LifeLine is a state program that provides discounted home phone and cell phone services to eligible low-income households, ensuring everyone has access to basic communication services.
california-lifeline.what_they_offer:
- Discounts on home phone service
- Discounts on cell phone service
- Choice of approved participating phone companies
- One discount per household (exceptions for teletypewriter users and Deaf and Disabled Telecommunications Program participants)
california-lifeline.how_to_get_it:
1. Check eligibility (participate in a qualifying program such as Medi-Cal, CalFresh, or SSI, or meet income guidelines)
2. Use 'Provider Search' at californialifeline.com to find an approved phone company
3. Call the phone company and ask for the California LifeLine discount to start your application
4. Complete the application and renewal forms sent by the California LifeLine Administrator
5. For general program questions, call 866-272-0349 (Mon-Fri 7am-7pm)

good360.name: Good360
good360.description: Good360 is a nonprofit organization that partners with major retailers and manufacturers to distribute donated goods, such as excess inventory and returns, to approved nonprofits and schools.
good360.what_they_offer:
- Donated products from top brands (excess inventory and returns, often in excellent condition)
- Items like hygiene kits, school supplies, apparel, furniture, and toys
- Online marketplace for approved members
- Small shipping or administrative fee per order; no hidden costs
- Availability varies based on donor shipments
good360.how_to_get_it:
1. Complete the online nonprofit membership application at good360.org
2. Eligible: 501(c)(3) public charities, faith-based organizations, and schools with an NCES ID (private foundations, government agencies, and for-profit schools are not eligible)
3. Get approved, usually within a few business days
4. Browse donated products in the online marketplace
5. Place orders and pay the admin/shipping fee

goodstack-nonprofit-discounts.name: Goodstack Nonprofit Discounts
goodstack-nonprofit-discounts.description: Goodstack (formerly Percent) is a free platform that verifies nonprofits and helps them access discounted software from major companies like Zoom, Docusign, Adobe, Asana, and OpenAI.
goodstack-nonprofit-discounts.what_they_offer:
- Up to 50% off select Zoom products
- 30-50% off select Docusign products
- 50% off Asana Starter and Advanced plans
- Discounts on ChatGPT plans through OpenAI for Nonprofits
- Adobe Acrobat Pro for Nonprofits
- Nonprofit profile to receive funding from Goodstack corporate partners
goodstack-nonprofit-discounts.how_to_get_it:
1. Visit goodstack.org and sign up (free)
2. Verify your nonprofit status (501c3 or equivalent)
3. Create an organizational account
4. Browse available software discounts
5. Claim discounts directly through the platform

instacart-ebt.name: Instacart for EBT/SNAP
instacart-ebt.description: Instacart is a grocery delivery and pickup service. They offer special discounts for EBT/SNAP recipients, making grocery delivery more accessible and affordable.
instacart-ebt.what_they_offer:
- 50% off Instacart+ membership for one year
- Skip delivery and pickup fees at participating stores
- New customers get $0 delivery on first 3 orders
- Use EBT/SNAP benefits for eligible food items
instacart-ebt.how_to_get_it:
1. Download the Instacart app or visit instacart.com
2. Create an account
3. Add your EBT card to your payment methods
4. Apply for the discounted Instacart+ membership
5. Start shopping with reduced fees

internet-essentials.name: Internet Essentials by Xfinity
internet-essentials.description: Internet Essentials is Comcast/Xfinity's low-cost internet program designed to help connect low-income families to affordable high-speed internet at home.
internet-essentials.what_they_offer:
- Affordable high-speed internet (up to 50 Mbps)
- WiFi modem included at no extra cost
- No credit check or term contract
- Option to purchase low-cost computer
- Free internet training resources
internet-essentials.how_to_get_it:
1. Check if Xfinity service is available in your area
2. Verify eligibility through SNAP, Medicaid, SSI, public housing, or other programs
3. Apply online at internetessentials.com or by phone
4. Receive equipment and self-install or schedule technician

kanopy-students.name: Kanopy for Students
kanopy-students.description: Kanopy is a video streaming service that partners with libraries and universities to provide free access to thousands of films, documentaries, and educational videos.
kanopy-students.what_they_offer:
- Free streaming of thousands of films and documentaries
- Criterion Collection, indie films, and world cinema
- Educational and documentary content
- Access through participating campus libraries
kanopy-students.how_to_get_it:
1. Check if your college or university participates
2. Visit kanopy.com/signup/find/university
3. Search for your school
4. Sign in with your campus credentials
5. Start streaming immediately

tech-exchange.name: Tech Exchange
tech-exchange.description: Tech Exchange is a Bay Area nonprofit that provides affordable refurbished computers to individuals, schools, nonprofits, and community organizations, along with free digital literacy classes and tech support.
tech-exchange.what_they_offer:
- Low-cost refurbished MacBooks, PC laptops, and desktops at the Oakland TecHub store
- Extra discount for households receiving qualifying public benefits (bring proof)
- 1 year of free tech support on computers purchased
- Free computer after completing an 8-hour digital literacy class
- Online store with 15-50% off devices, delivered to your door
- Bulk device orders (10-500) for organizations and businesses
- Device donation drop-off and e-waste solutions
tech-exchange.how_to_get_it:
1. Visit the TecHub at 1716 Telegraph Ave, Oakland (Mon-Fri 10am-5pm)
2. Bring proof of qualifying benefits for the low-income discount
3. Or shop the online store at techexchange.org
4. Sign up for a free digital literacy class to earn a free computer
5. Organizations: email Tech Exchange for bulk orders

techsoup-discount-marketplace.name: TechSoup Discount Marketplace
techsoup-discount-marketplace.description: TechSoup is a nonprofit technology assistance organization that helps nonprofits, charities, and libraries access donated and discounted software, hardware, and cloud services from major tech companies.
techsoup-discount-marketplace.what_they_offer:
- Discounted Microsoft 365 and other Microsoft for Nonprofits products
- Adobe Creative Cloud for nonprofits
- Hardware from Dell, Lenovo, and others
- Cloud services from AWS, Google, and Microsoft
- Training and learning resources
techsoup-discount-marketplace.how_to_get_it:
1. Register your nonprofit at techsoup.org (basic membership is free)
2. Complete the validation process to confirm nonprofit status
3. Some partners validate separately (for Microsoft, register at nonprofit.microsoft.com)
4. Browse the catalog and request products
5. Pay the administrative fee listed for each product

t-mobile-project-10million.name: T-Mobile Project 10Million
t-mobile-project-10million.description: T-Mobile Project 10Million is an initiative to provide free internet connectivity to underserved K-12 student households across the U.S., helping close the homework gap.
t-mobile-project-10million.what_they_offer:
- Free mobile hotspot device (one per household)
- 200GB high-speed data per year for 5 years
- No fees, costs, or annual re-certifications
- Free Web Guard content filtering for safety
- Optional $10 data pass for additional 10GB when needed
t-mobile-project-10million.how_to_get_it:
1. Household must have a K-12 student
2. Student must be eligible for the National School Lunch Program, SNAP/EBT, Community Eligibility Provision, Medicaid, or FDPIR
3. Parents apply online at T-Mobile's Project 10Million page (or get help at a T-Mobile store)
4. Upload proof of enrollment in a qualifying program dated within the past year
5. Sign the service agreement; the hotspot ships free in about 3-5 business days
t-mobile-project-10million.timeframe: Ongoing; limited-time offer subject to change

walmart-plus-assist.name: Walmart+ Assist
walmart-plus-assist.description: Walmart+ is Walmart's membership program offering free delivery, fuel discounts, and more. Walmart+ Assist provides the full membership at half price for people enrolled in qualifying government assistance programs.
walmart-plus-assist.what_they_offer:
- 50% off Walmart+ membership ($6.47/month or $49/year)
- Free delivery from your local store
- Member prices on fuel
- Choice of Paramount+ or Peacock streaming
- Same benefits as a regular Walmart+ membership
walmart-plus-assist.how_to_get_it:
1. Visit walmart.com/plus/assist
2. Confirm you are enrolled in a qualifying program such as SNAP, WIC, Medicaid, SSI, TANF, Tribal TANF, the National School Lunch Program, or LIHEAP
3. Complete eligibility verification through Walmart's partner, SheerID
4. Start your discounted membership

world-computer-exchange.name: World Computer Exchange
world-computer-exchange.description: World Computer Exchange is a nonprofit that collects donated computers, refurbishes them, and provides them at low cost to schools, NGOs, nonprofits, and underserved youth, mostly in developing countries.
world-computer-exchange.what_they_offer:
- Refurbished laptops for schools, NGOs, and nonprofits (roughly $95-$180 per laptop, plus shipping and import costs)
- Equipment for educational and community use
- A Palo Alto chapter that accepts computer donations; mail-in donations also accepted
- Computers refurbished and distributed to those in need
world-computer-exchange.how_to_get_it:
1. Visit worldcomputerexchange.org/get-computers
2. Submit an application describing your project and needs
3. If approved, review the quote, confirm your order, and pay the invoice
4. Devices are prepared (typically 2-4 weeks), then shipped or picked up
5. Check that your country allows imports of used computers before applying

spectrum-internet-assist.name: Spectrum Internet Assist
spectrum-internet-assist.description: Spectrum Internet Assist is Charter Communications' affordable internet program for qualifying low-income households, including seniors receiving SSI and families with students in free lunch programs.
spectrum-internet-assist.what_they_offer:
- 50 Mbps internet for $25/month for qualifying households
- $15/month for households in the National School Lunch Program (NSLP), its Community Eligibility Provision (CEP), or receiving SSI
- No data caps or contracts
- Modem included
- One Unlimited Mobile line included for 1 year
- Advanced WiFi available for $10/month; upgrade to 100 Mbps (Internet Advantage) for $5 more
spectrum-internet-assist.how_to_get_it:
1. Check if Spectrum service is available in your area
2. Check qualifications on Spectrum's site (participation in a government program may qualify you)
3. For the $15/month rate, have a household member in NSLP or CEP, or be 65+ and receiving Supplemental Security Income (SSI)
4. Gather your documentation and apply using the online form

menlo-park-library-hotspots.name: Menlo Park Library Wi-Fi Hotspots
menlo-park-library-hotspots.description: The Menlo Park Library offers portable WiFi hotspot devices that library cardholders can borrow, providing free internet access at home or on the go.
menlo-park-library-hotspots.what_they_offer:
- Free 7-day checkout of a portable WiFi hotspot
- Internet access at home or on the go
- Hotspots are equipment loans and cannot be renewed
menlo-park-library-hotspots.how_to_get_it:
1. Get a Menlo Park Library card
2. Contact or visit the library to check hotspot availability
3. Check out a hotspot at the library
4. Return it within 7 days (hotspots cannot be renewed)

calvet-troops-to-trucks.name: Troops to Trucks (CDL Waiver Program)
calvet-troops-to-trucks.description: The California Troops to Trucks program allows qualifying service members and veterans with military driving experience to obtain a commercial driver's license (CDL) without taking the driving skills test. This fast-tracks veterans into high-demand trucking careers.
calvet-troops-to-trucks.what_they_offer:
- CDL driving (skills) test waiver for qualified service members and recent veterans
- Exempt from Entry-Level Driver Training (ELDT) requirements
- Faster path to a Class A or B commercial license
- Does not apply to passenger or school bus endorsements
- Leverages existing military driving experience
calvet-troops-to-trucks.how_to_get_it:
1. Be active duty, reserve, or National Guard, or within 12 months of discharge
2. Have operated a military vehicle equivalent to a commercial motor vehicle, including at least 2 years immediately before discharge (or currently in that role)
3. Have a qualifying driving record (no disqualifying offenses in the past 2 years)
4. Complete the Commercial Military Waiver form (DL 965)
5. Bring the DL 965, identity document, Social Security or Armed Forces ID, and DD 214 (veterans) to a DMV office
6. Meet all other CA CDL requirements; the driving test is waived
calvet-troops-to-trucks.timeframe: Ongoing; veterans must apply within 12 months of discharge

ac-transit-stpp.name: AC Transit
ac-transit-stpp.description: AC Transit (Alameda-Contra Costa Transit District) is the third-largest public bus system in California, serving the East Bay including Oakland, Berkeley, and surrounding cities with local and transbay service.
ac-transit-stpp.what_they_offer:
- Student Transit Pass Program (STPP), run by Alameda CTC: free unlimited rides on AC Transit, Union City Transit, or Wheels (local routes serving your school) for eligible middle and high school students
- Transbay and BART trips are not free; students under 19 get the pass on a Youth Clipper card with 50% off BART and youth discounts elsewhere
- Valid year-round, including summer, until the student leaves high school
ac-transit-stpp.how_to_get_it:
1. Check eligibility and apply online at alamedactc.org/programs-projects/studentpass
2. Once approved, a Youth Clipper card with the pass is mailed to your school (4-6 weeks or more); pick it up from your school's site administrator
3. If you already have a Youth Clipper card, the pass is loaded onto it within 2-4 weeks
4. Register the card in an online Clipper account so it can be replaced if lost
5. Questions: ask your school's site administrator or contact Alameda CTC (510-208-7400)

bart-discount.name: BART
bart-discount.description: BART (Bay Area Rapid Transit) is a heavy rail rapid transit system serving the San Francisco Bay Area, connecting San Francisco, Oakland, Berkeley, and surrounding suburbs with 50 stations across 131 miles of track.
bart-discount.what_they_offer:
- High-Value Discount (HVD): 6.25% savings for adult Clipper cards ($48 of BART value for $45, or $64 for $60)
- Available only by setting up Autoload on a registered Clipper card or through a transit benefit program
- Works on all BART stations and routes
bart-discount.how_to_get_it:
1. Get an adult Clipper card and register it in an online Clipper account
2. In your Clipper account, select Add Value, then Transit Pass, then BART
3. Choose the HVD amount and set it up as Autoload
4. The bonus value is added each time the Autoload reloads

bart-muni-a-pass.name: BART + Muni
bart-muni-a-pass.description: A joint program between BART and SFMTA offering unlimited transit within San Francisco on both systems with a single monthly pass.
bart-muni-a-pass.what_they_offer:
- "A" Fast Pass ($104/month): Unlimited Muni rides plus unlimited BART rides within San Francisco
- Valid on all Muni buses, light rail, cable cars, and historic streetcars
- Valid on BART between Embarcadero and Balboa Park stations only
bart-muni-a-pass.how_to_get_it:
1. Purchase through your Clipper account, the Clipper app, or retail locations
2. Load the monthly "A" pass onto your Clipper card
3. Pass is valid for one calendar month
4. Tap Clipper card when boarding Muni or entering BART

bike-share-for-all.name: Bike Share for All (Bay Wheels)
bike-share-for-all.description: Bay Wheels (operated by Lyft) is the Bay Area's bike share system with thousands of bikes available at stations throughout San Francisco, Oakland, Berkeley, and San Jose. Bike Share for All makes it affordable for low-income residents.
bike-share-for-all.what_they_offer:
- Reduced-rate membership: $5 for the first year, then $5/month (no annual commitment)
- Unlimited free 60-minute rides on classic bikes ($0.13/min after that)
- Free unlocks and e-bike rides at $0.05/min (max $1 per ride)
- Pay with a prepaid, debit, or credit card; bikes can also be unlocked with a Clipper card
bike-share-for-all.how_to_get_it:
1. Must be 18 or older
2. Household must qualify for CalFresh, SFMTA Lifeline Pass, or PG&E CARE
3. Start an application online and submit proof of eligibility
4. For in-person help, visit Oakland Public Library (Main, 125 14th St) or Berkeley Public Library (Main, 2090 Kittredge St)
5. Once approved, start riding with the Lyft app or a Clipper card

caltrain-youth-fares.name: Caltrain Dollar Fares for Youth
caltrain-youth-fares.description: Caltrain is a commuter rail line running 77 miles along the San Francisco Peninsula, connecting San Francisco to San Jose and Gilroy. The Dollar Fares program makes train travel extremely affordable for young riders.
caltrain-youth-fares.what_they_offer:
- $1 One-Way fare for youth 18 and under (all zones)
- $2 Day Pass for unlimited rides in one day
- $24 Monthly Pass (all zones)
- No income requirements—available to all youth
caltrain-youth-fares.how_to_get_it:
1. Get a free Youth Clipper card (apply online at clippercard.com)
2. The $1 one-way fare works with all payment methods; buy Day Passes on Caltrain Mobile or at ticket machines
3. Tap Clipper card or show your ticket when boarding
4. One child age 4 and under rides free with each paying adult
caltrain-youth-fares.timeframe: Ongoing; current youth fares set through July 2027

city-coach-solano.name: City Coach
city-coach-solano.description: City Coach is the local public transit service for the City of Vacaville in Solano County, providing fixed-route bus service throughout the city.
city-coach-solano.what_they_offer:
- Free rides for Solano Community College students
- Valid on Vacaville City Coach fixed routes and on SolanoExpress within Solano County
- Does not apply to City Coach Direct or paratransit (Special Services)
- No additional fees or passes required
city-coach-solano.how_to_get_it:
1. Must be currently enrolled at Solano Community College
2. Show your current student ID to the bus driver when boarding
3. No separate application or pass needed

clipper-baypass.name: Clipper BayPass
clipper-baypass.description: Clipper BayPass is the Bay Area's first prepaid, all-system transit pass, offering unlimited rides on Bay Area buses, trains, and ferries. It is provided through participating colleges, employers, and affordable housing organizations.
clipper-baypass.what_they_offer:
- Unlimited rides on participating Bay Area transit agencies
- Includes BART, Muni, AC Transit, Caltrain, VTA, and more
- Single pass covers buses, rail, and ferries
- Significant savings compared to paying per ride
clipper-baypass.how_to_get_it:
1. Check if your college, employer, or housing provider participates
2. Get your BayPass on a Clipper card through that institution
3. Organizations can submit an interest form at clipperbaypass.com for a custom price quote
4. Program eligibility and fees vary by institution

clipper-start.name: Clipper START
clipper-start.description: Clipper START is a regional program that provides discounted transit fares for low-income adults on participating Bay Area transit systems, helping make public transportation more accessible.
clipper-start.what_they_offer:
- 50% off single-ride bus, BART, rail, and ferry fares on Bay Area transit agencies that accept Clipper
- Valid on AC Transit, BART, Caltrain, Golden Gate Transit/Ferry, Muni, SamTrans, and more
- Discounts automatically applied when using your Clipper START card (can also be added to a mobile wallet)
- Now a permanent program (no longer a pilot)
clipper-start.how_to_get_it:
1. Must be a Bay Area resident age 19-64 with household income at or below 200% of the Federal Poverty Level
2. Apply online at clipperstartcard.com or by mail
3. Provide proof of income or participation in qualifying benefit programs
4. Receive your Clipper START card by mail (processing may take up to 30 days)
5. Load cash value and ride with automatic discounts

dmv-reduced-fee-id.name: DMV Reduced-Fee ID Card
dmv-reduced-fee-id.description: The California Department of Motor Vehicles offers reduced-fee identification cards for income-eligible residents, providing an affordable way to obtain government-issued photo ID.
dmv-reduced-fee-id.what_they_offer:
- Reduced-fee state ID card ($11 instead of the regular $40)
- Reduced fee applies to original, renewal, replacement, and information-change ID applications
- Valid government-issued photo identification
- No-fee ID cards are also available for people experiencing homelessness and seniors 62+
dmv-reduced-fee-id.how_to_get_it:
1. Contact your local public assistance agency or the governmental or nonprofit program you receive services from
2. Ask them to verify your eligibility and complete the Verification for Reduced Fee Identification Card form (DL 937)
3. Take the completed DL 937 form to a DMV office
4. Complete the ID card application and pay the reduced fee

emergency-ride-home-marin.name: Emergency Ride Home
emergency-ride-home-marin.description: The Transportation Authority of Marin (through Marin Commutes) reimburses emergency rides home for people who walk, bike, carpool, vanpool, or take transit to work or college in Marin County.
emergency-ride-home-marin.what_they_offer:
- Reimbursement for emergency rides home by taxi, Uber, Lyft, or similar service
- Up to $125 per ride (tips not included)
- Up to 4 trips and $500 per fiscal year (July 1-June 30)
- Covers illness or crisis, unexpected late work, carpool/vanpool falling through, or bike problems
emergency-ride-home-marin.how_to_get_it:
1. Must be 18+ and work in Marin County or attend a college in Marin County
2. Use an alternative commute mode (transit, vanpool, carpool, bike, or walk) on the day of the emergency
