3. When an eligible emergency occurs, take a taxi or rideshare home and keep your receipt
4. Submit the reimbursement request form with receipts within 30 days of the trip
5. Reimbursement is mailed as a check, usually within 30 days of approval
emergency-ride-home-marin.timeframe: Ongoing; available until program funds are exhausted

emery-go-round.name: Emery Go-Round
emery-go-round.description: Emery Go-Round is a free shuttle bus service operated by the Emeryville Transportation Management Association, connecting Emeryville destinations with the MacArthur BART station.
emery-go-round.what_they_offer:
- Fare-free shuttle service open to the public
- Multiple routes throughout Emeryville
- Connection to MacArthur BART station
- Weekday and weekend service (closed on some holidays)
- Bike racks and wheelchair accessible shuttles
emery-go-round.how_to_get_it:
1. No registration or pass needed
2. Check the route map and schedule online
3. Go to any Emery Go-Round stop
4. Board when shuttle arrives—no fare required

511-emergency-rides-contra-costa.name: 511 Emergency Rides
511-emergency-rides-contra-costa.description: 511 CCTA (a program of the Contra Costa Transportation Authority) offers free Guaranteed Ride Home "commuter insurance" that reimburses emergency rides home for people who walk, bike, carpool, vanpool, or take transit to work or college.
511-emergency-rides-contra-costa.what_they_offer:
- Reimbursement for up to 6 emergency rides home per year
- Rides by Uber, Lyft, taxi, bike rental, or transit
- Qualifying emergencies include illness or injury (you or immediate family), supervisor-requested late work, carpool/vanpool falling through, bike theft or breakdown, a home emergency, or transit shut down for the day
- Free to register
511-emergency-rides-contra-costa.how_to_get_it:
1. Must work or attend college in Contra Costa County and commute by walking, biking, transit, or sharing a ride
2. Register online with 511 CCTA's Guaranteed Ride Home program before you need it
3. When an emergency occurs, arrange your own ride home and save the receipt
4. Log in and submit the reimbursement form within 30 days

511-transit-incentives-contra-costa.name: 511 Transit Incentives
511-transit-incentives-contra-costa.description: 511 CCTA's Try Transit program encourages commuters and college students in Contra Costa County to try public transit instead of driving alone, providing a Clipper card preloaded with $25.
511-transit-incentives-contra-costa.what_they_offer:
- Free Clipper card preloaded with $25 when you pledge to try transit
- Separate offers for commuters and college students
- Some West Contra Costa commuters with a 19-digit Clipper account can get $25 added to their existing account
- Can be used on any transit agency that accepts Clipper
511-transit-incentives-contra-costa.how_to_get_it:
1. Commuters: live or work in Contra Costa County, be 18+, and otherwise drive alone to work
2. Students: attend an eligible Contra Costa college or adult school (such as DVC, Contra Costa College, Los Medanos, Saint Mary's, or CSU East Bay Concord) with at least 9 units, and otherwise drive alone
3. Apply online and agree to complete a brief survey
4. Receive your $25 Clipper card by mail
5. Limit one 511 CCTA incentive per household per July-June funding year
511-transit-incentives-contra-costa.timeframe: Ongoing; one incentive per household each July-June funding year

lime-access.name: Lime Access
lime-access.description: Lime is a micromobility company offering electric scooters and bikes for short trips. Lime Access makes these transportation options affordable for low-income riders.
lime-access.what_they_offer:
- Discounted or free Lime scooter and bike rides
- Up to 30 minutes free per ride (varies by market)
- 50% off all rides after free minutes
- Available in Bay Area cities where Lime operates
lime-access.how_to_get_it:
1. Download the Lime app on your smartphone
2. Create an account
3. Apply for Lime Access in the app settings
4. Provide proof of income eligibility (SNAP, Medicaid, LIHEAP, or similar)
5. Approval usually within a few days

low-cost-auto-insurance.name: Low Cost Auto Insurance
low-cost-auto-insurance.description: California's Low Cost Automobile Insurance Program (CLCA) is a state-sponsored program providing affordable liability insurance for income-eligible drivers who might otherwise go uninsured.
low-cost-auto-insurance.what_they_offer:
- State-sponsored low-cost liability insurance
- Helps meet California's financial responsibility (insurance) laws
- Premiums vary by county
- Covers bodily injury and property damage liability
low-cost-auto-insurance.how_to_get_it:
1. Check income eligibility (250% of Federal Poverty Level or less)
2. Must have valid California driver's license
3. Must own a vehicle valued at $25,000 or less
4. Good driving record required (limited violations allowed)
5. Check eligibility at mylowcostauto.com or call 1-866-602-8861
6. Enroll through a certified CLCA agent in your area

marin-transit-students.name: Marin Transit
marin-transit-students.description: Marin Transit provides local bus service throughout Marin County, connecting communities with schools, shopping, and employment centers. The agency partners with College of Marin to offer free rides for students.
marin-transit-students.what_they_offer:
- Free rides for College of Marin students with a COM pass (funded by a student transportation fee)
- Valid on Marin Transit buses within Marin County
- Not valid on Golden Gate Transit buses or ferries, or the Muir Woods Shuttle
- Pass is loaded on a free Clipper card and renewed each semester
marin-transit-students.how_to_get_it:
1. Must be currently enrolled at College of Marin (one or more units)
2. Pick up a free Clipper card with a COM pass at the Cashier's Office, Kentfield campus (415-883-2211 ext. 7806)
3. Tap your Clipper card each time you board a Marin Transit bus
4. A new COM pass is added to the same card at the start of each fall and spring semester
marin-transit-students.timeframe: Renewed each semester: Fall pass valid August–January, Spring pass valid January–August

muni-free.name: Muni
muni-free.description: San Francisco Municipal Transportation Agency (SFMTA) operates Muni, the city's public transit system including buses, light rail (Metro), cable cars, and historic streetcars. Multiple free and discounted fare programs are available.
muni-free.what_they_offer:
- Free Muni for All Youth (18 and under): Free on all Muni except cable cars, regardless of income or residency
- Free Muni for Seniors (65+) and People with Disabilities: For San Francisco residents with income at or below 100% of Bay Area Median Income (includes cable cars)
- Access Pass: Free Muni for people experiencing homelessness
- Lifeline Pass: $43 monthly pass for low-income adults (moving to Clipper START on January 1, 2027)
- Clipper START: 50% off single rides ($1.40) for income-eligible adults 19-64
- Free Muni (except cable cars) on the day of a Chase Center event with your event ticket
muni-free.how_to_get_it:
1. Youth: No application or Clipper card needed; just board (youth 16+ should carry ID)
2. Seniors/People with Disabilities: Apply online (preferred) or by mail with proof of age or disability and income; requires a Clipper card
3. Lifeline Pass: Apply for a Clipper START card now; Lifeline passes will be sold through Clipper START starting January 2027
4. Chase Center: Show your event ticket on the day of the event

petaluma-transit-free.name: Petaluma Transit
petaluma-transit-free.description: Petaluma Transit is the local public bus service for the City of Petaluma in Sonoma County, providing fixed-route service throughout the city and connections to regional transit.
petaluma-transit-free.what_they_offer:
- All fixed-route buses are fare-free (since July 1, 2024)
- Paratransit service is also fare-free
- No fare required for any rider
- Service throughout Petaluma, with connections to regional transit
petaluma-transit-free.how_to_get_it:
1. No registration, pass, or payment needed
2. Check route map and schedule online
3. Go to any Petaluma Transit stop
4. Board when bus arrives—completely free

clipper-access.name: Clipper Access (RTC)
clipper-access.description: Clipper Access (formerly RTC Clipper Card) provides discounted fares for people with disabilities on participating Bay Area transit systems. The Regional Transit Connection program offers reduced fares across the entire Bay Area transit network.
clipper-access.what_they_offer:
- Reduced fares on most Bay Area transit agencies
- Typically 50% or more off regular adult fares
- Valid on BART, Muni, AC Transit, Caltrain, VTA, SamTrans, and more
- Discounts automatically applied when using Clipper Access card
- Works on all Clipper-accepting transit agencies
clipper-access.how_to_get_it:
1. Complete the RTC/Clipper Access application at clippercard.com
2. Provide proof of disability (Medicare card, SSI/SSDI documentation, or medical certification)
3. Submit application online or by mail
4. Once approved, receive Clipper Access card by mail
5. Load cash value and ride with automatic discounts

samtrans.name: SamTrans Way2Go Pass
samtrans.description: SamTrans is San Mateo County's public transit bus service. In partnership with SamTrans, the San Mateo County Community College District provides free Way2Go unlimited bus passes to its students.
samtrans.what_they_offer:
- FREE unlimited SamTrans bus pass
- Can be linked to your existing Clipper card
- Distributed first-come, first-served
- Current passes valid through February 2027
samtrans.how_to_get_it:
1. Must be enrolled in at least 1 unit at Cañada College, College of San Mateo, or Skyline College
2. Complete the Way2Go application online
3. Watch for a follow-up email with instructions to finish the process
4. Receive the Way2Go pass on your Clipper card
samtrans.timeframe: Current pass valid through February 2027; limited supply

samtrans-youth.name: SamTrans
samtrans-youth.description: SamTrans offers a special Summer Youth Pass for young riders, making it easy and affordable for youth to travel throughout San Mateo County during summer months.
samtrans-youth.what_they_offer:
- Summer Youth Pass: $40 for unlimited rides from June 1 to August 31
- Year-round youth options: $27 Local/Express Youth monthly pass, $2 Youth Day Pass
- Youth Unlimited: free fares for socioeconomically disadvantaged students through the San Mateo County Office of Education
- Great for summer activities, jobs, and recreation
samtrans-youth.how_to_get_it:
1. Must be 18 years old or younger
2. Apply for a Youth Clipper card (required for youth riders)
3. Purchase the Summer Youth Pass before or during summer
4. Pass is valid June 1 through August 31
5. Bus operators may ask for proof of age
samtrans-youth.timeframe: Seasonal (June 1–August 31 each summer); youth monthly and day passes available year-round

santa-rosa-citybus.name: Santa Rosa CityBus
santa-rosa-citybus.description: Santa Rosa CityBus provides local public transit service throughout the City of Santa Rosa in Sonoma County, with multiple routes connecting neighborhoods, schools, shopping, and employment centers.
santa-rosa-citybus.what_they_offer:
- Free rides for youth ages 5-18 and children 4 and under
- Free rides for veterans with qualifying ID
- Free rides for Santa Rosa Junior College students with valid student ID
- Free rides for paratransit users with a valid paratransit ID
- Free rides for City of Santa Rosa and County of Sonoma employees
- Half fare ($0.75) for seniors 65+, people with disabilities, and Medicare card holders
santa-rosa-citybus.how_to_get_it:
1. Youth: Show a school ID or DMV-issued ID (high school age); schools without IDs can provide a special pass
2. Veterans: Show a VA ID card, Sonoma County Veterans ID card, or California driver's license with veteran designation
3. SRJC Students: Show current student ID
4. City/County Employees: Show proof of employment
5. No separate application needed—just show ID when boarding

senior-clipper-card.name: Senior Clipper Card
senior-clipper-card.description: The Senior Clipper Card provides discounted fares for riders 65 and older on participating Bay Area transit systems.
senior-clipper-card.what_they_offer:
- Reduced fares and discounted passes on Bay Area transit agencies
- Discounts vary by agency (for example, 62.5% off BART; reduced single rides and monthly passes on Muni)
- Valid on BART, Muni, AC Transit, Caltrain, and more
- Discounts automatically applied; card can also be added to your phone's mobile wallet
senior-clipper-card.how_to_get_it:
1. Apply online at clippercard.com, or by mail, email, or fax
2. Provide an accepted proof-of-age document showing you are 65 or older
3. Or get a card in person at a Clipper Customer Service Center
4. Receive your Senior Clipper card
5. Load cash value or passes and ride with automatic senior discounts

bay-area-park-ride.name: Bay Area Park & Ride Lots
bay-area-park-ride.description: Free parking lots located near major transit hubs and freeway on-ramps throughout the Bay Area, allowing commuters to park and continue their trip via transit, carpool, or vanpool.
bay-area-park-ride.what_they_offer:
- Over 150 free Park & Ride lots across the Bay Area and nearby counties
- Many lots are close to transit connections; some have bike lockers or racks
- Convenient for carpool and vanpool meetups
- Reduces single-occupancy vehicle trips
- Open to all commuters
bay-area-park-ride.how_to_get_it:
1. Visit 511.org to search Park & Ride lots by county or view them on the interactive map
2. Check lot details (spaces, bike parking, lighting, transit access)
3. Drive to lot and park in designated spaces
4. Continue commute via transit, carpool, or vanpool
5. Some lots may have time limits or overnight restrictions

express-lanes-start.name: I-880/I-80 Express Lanes START Program
express-lanes-start.description: Express Lanes START is an MTC/Bay Area Infrastructure Financing Authority trial program that gives income-eligible Bay Area drivers at least 50% off tolls on the I-880 and I-80 Express Lanes.
express-lanes-start.what_they_offer:
- At least 50% off all tolled trips
- Available on I-880 Express Lanes
- Available on I-80 Express Lanes (not valid on other Bay Area express lanes)
- Helps lower-income commuters access faster travel times
- Works with FasTrak Flex toll tag
express-lanes-start.how_to_get_it:
1. Must live in the nine-county Bay Area with gross household income at or below 200% of federal poverty level
2. Apply online at expresslanesstart.org (mail or fax applications also accepted)
3. Provide proof of income and residency
4. Use a FasTrak Flex toll tag if approved
5. Discount automatically applied when using the covered express lanes

smc-101-express-lanes-go-card.name: San Mateo 101 Express Lanes Go Card
smc-101-express-lanes-go-card.description: The San Mateo 101 Express Lanes Go Card Program helps cover transportation costs for income-eligible San Mateo County residents with a $200 prepaid card each year.
smc-101-express-lanes-go-card.what_they_offer:
- $200 prepaid card, available once a year, for transportation purchases
- Use it for public transit, express lanes, toll bridges, paratransit, and bike or scooter rentals
- Accepted by providers such as Clipper, FasTrak, BART, Caltrain, SamTrans, Amtrak, Bay Wheels, and SF Bay Ferry
- Can be used to add funds to Clipper START, Youth, Senior, or RTC cards, or an Express Lanes START FasTrak account
smc-101-express-lanes-go-card.how_to_get_it:
1. Must be a San Mateo County resident, age 18 or older
2. Individual annual income at or below $88,260 (60% of Area Median Income); household size is considered if household income is higher
3. Visit or call one of the program's community partners to sign up (see the How to Enroll page)
4. Each eligible household member applies separately
5. Recipients may reapply one year after their initial application

bay-area-casual-carpool.name: Bay Area Casual Carpool
bay-area-casual-carpool.description: Casual carpooling (also called "slugging") is an informal ridesharing system for commuting to San Francisco. Drivers and passengers meet at designated pickup spots in the East Bay and form carpools of three to use HOV lanes and the discounted Bay Bridge carpool toll.
bay-area-casual-carpool.what_they_offer:
- Free rides for passengers to San Francisco
- Discounted Bay Bridge carpool toll for drivers (FasTrak required)
- HOV lane access for drivers
- No formal registration required
- About two dozen pickup locations in the East Bay, Vallejo, and Fairfield
bay-area-casual-carpool.how_to_get_it:
1. Find a casual carpool pickup location near you on 511.org
2. Line up at designated spots during commute hours
3. Drivers pull up and passengers get in (carpools of three)
4. Ride is free for passengers
5. Drivers benefit from carpool toll rates and HOV access

bay-area-vanpool.name: Bay Area Vanpool Program
bay-area-vanpool.description: The Bay Area Vanpool Program (through 511.org) helps commuters form and join vanpools, where groups of 7-15 people share a van for their daily commute, splitting costs and reducing traffic.
bay-area-vanpool.what_they_offer:
- $600 monthly discount on Commute with Enterprise vanpool rentals
- Help finding or starting a vanpool
- "Empty seat" subsidies for owner-operated vanpools
- Free bridge tolls for larger vanpools (11-15 passengers)
- Help signing up for discounted parking in San Francisco and Oakland
- HOV lane access; extra benefits may be available from your county
bay-area-vanpool.how_to_get_it:
1. Visit 511.org's Vanpool page
2. If you don't own a van, contact Commute with Enterprise to join or start a vanpool
3. If you own a 7-15 passenger van, learn about starting an owner-operated vanpool
4. Split monthly costs with vanpool members (usually month-to-month)
5. Ask your employer about vanpool subsidies or pre-tax commuter benefits

bay-area-biking-maps.name: Bay Area Biking Maps & Trails
bay-area-biking-maps.description: 511.org gathers bike trail maps and city and county bikeway maps from across the Bay Area, along with tips on bike safety, bike parking, and taking bikes on transit and bridges.
bay-area-biking-maps.what_they_offer:
- Links to regional trail maps (Bay Trail, Ridge Trail, Bay Bridge Trail, Transit to Trails)
- City and county bike maps for about 30 Bay Area communities
- Bike safety and riding-in-traffic tips
- Info on bike parking and bikes on transit, bridges, and tunnels
- Links to local bicycle coalitions
bay-area-biking-maps.how_to_get_it:
1. Visit 511.org's Biking Maps & Trails page
2. Pick a regional trail map or search for your city or county map
3. Open the map from the local agency or trail organization

guaranteed-ride-home.name: Guaranteed Ride Home
guaranteed-ride-home.description: County-based programs that provide free or reimbursed emergency rides home for commuters who use alternative transportation (transit, carpool, vanpool, biking, or walking) to get to work.
guaranteed-ride-home.what_they_offer:
- Free or reimbursed rides home during emergencies
- Covers illness, family emergencies, unscheduled overtime
- Available via taxi, Uber/Lyft, rental car, or transit (varies by county)
- Number of rides and reimbursement limits vary by county
- Separate programs in each Bay Area county (based on where you work or attend college)
guaranteed-ride-home.how_to_get_it:
1. Must commute using alternative transportation (not driving alone) on the day of the emergency
2. Find the program for the county where you work on 511.org
3. Register if your county requires it (free; Alameda, Santa Clara, Solano, and Napa require an account)
4. When an emergency arises, take a taxi or rideshare home
5. Submit your receipt for reimbursement through your county program

commute-rewards.name: Bay Area Commute Rewards
commute-rewards.description: County-level incentive programs that reward Bay Area commuters for using alternatives to driving alone, including transit, carpooling, biking, and walking.
commute-rewards.what_they_offer:
- Links to county carpool and commute incentive programs
- Incentives such as rewards or prizes for logging green commutes (varies by county)
- Carpool savings calculator to compare costs and CO2 with driving alone
- Different programs by county; rules and rewards vary
commute-rewards.how_to_get_it:
1. Visit 511.org's Carpool Savings & Commute Programs page
2. Choose the county where you live or work
3. Register through your county's program website
4. Log your alternative commute trips if the program requires it
5. Earn incentives based on program rules

safe-routes-to-school.name: Bay Area Safe Routes to School
safe-routes-to-school.description: Regional initiative helping students travel safely to and from school through walking, biking, and transit, with programs in all nine Bay Area counties.
safe-routes-to-school.what_they_offer:
- Engineering improvements to school routes
- Crossing guard programs
- Free or subsidized transit passes (varies by county)
- Walking and biking safety education
- Incentive programs and contests
- Community education campaigns
safe-routes-to-school.how_to_get_it:
1. Contact your county's Safe Routes to School program
2. Programs available through participating schools
3. Some counties offer free transit passes for youth
4. Schools can request safety assessments
5. Visit sparetheairyouth.org for county contacts

bay-area-cycling-organizations.name: Bay Area Bicycle Coalitions
bay-area-cycling-organizations.description: Regional bicycle advocacy organizations providing resources, community support, and advocacy for cyclists throughout the Bay Area.
bay-area-cycling-organizations.what_they_offer:
- Bicycle route information and maps
- Riding clubs and group rides
- Bike repair resources and workshops
- Safety education and classes
- Advocacy for bike infrastructure
- Community events and programs
bay-area-cycling-organizations.how_to_get_it:
1. Visit 511.org's Bicycle Coalitions page
2. Find your local coalition (East Bay, Marin, Napa, San Francisco, Silicon Valley, or Sonoma)
3. Join as a member or sign up for updates
4. Access resources, maps, and community
5. Participate in group rides and events

bikelink-bike-lockers.name: BikeLink Bike Lockers
bikelink-bike-lockers.description: BikeLink operates secure electronic bike lockers at BART stations and transit hubs throughout the Bay Area. These on-demand lockers are available 24/7 and rent for just 5 cents per hour.
bikelink-bike-lockers.what_they_offer:
- Secure electronic bike lockers at BART, Caltrain, and other transit hubs
- Available 24/7, first-come, first-served
- Low cost: typically 5¢/hour
- Works with the BikeLink app ($5 to start), a BikeLink card ($20 with $20 of credit), or a linked Clipper card at some locations
- Weather-protected storage
bikelink-bike-lockers.how_to_get_it:
1. Download the BikeLink app and load value (or buy a BikeLink card online or from a vendor)
2. Check the BikeLink map to see which access methods each location accepts
3. Find an available locker
4. Use the app or card to open the locker and start your rental
5. Use the same app or card to unlock when returning; unused value is refunded

bikeep-smart-racks.name: Bikeep Free Bike Parking at BART
bikeep-smart-racks.description: Bikeep high-security smart bike racks at seven BART stations provide free secure bike parking. The racks use electronic locking arms with alarms and security monitoring for much better theft protection than a U-lock alone.
bikeep-smart-racks.what_they_offer:
- Free secure bike parking at 16th St Mission, 24th St Mission, 12th St Oakland, MacArthur, Concord, Pleasant Hill, and Union City BART
- Smart locking arm secures frame and one wheel
- 24-hour maximum continuous parking
- Industrial-grade security with alarm system
- Works with a registered physical Clipper card (not the Clipper mobile app)
bikeep-smart-racks.how_to_get_it:
1. Register online with BikeHub (takes about 30 seconds)
2. Link your physical Clipper card to your account
3. Find an available Bikeep rack at the station
4. Tap your Clipper card to lock your bike; use a personal lock for your other wheel
5. Tap again to unlock when returning

caltrain.name: Caltrain
caltrain.description: Caltrain is a commuter rail line serving the San Francisco Peninsula and Santa Clara Valley, running from San Francisco to Gilroy. Stations offer bike parking, car parking, and transit connections.
caltrain.what_they_offer:
- Commuter rail service from SF to Gilroy
- BikeLink e-lockers at 24 of 31 stations (5¢/hour; 2¢/hour nights and weekends)
- Parking at most stations ($5.50/day; $82.50/month permit for Monthly Pass or GoPass holders)
- Free parking at stations south of San Jose Diridon; fee waived for disabled placards/plates
- Accessible stations with elevators at select locations
- Restrooms at SF and San Jose Diridon, plus pilot restrooms at Redwood City, Palo Alto, and Sunnyvale
caltrain.how_to_get_it:
1. Plan your trip at caltrain.com
2. Buy tickets at station vending machines or use Clipper card
3. BikeLink e-lockers: Download the BikeLink app; first-time users get 100 free hours at Caltrain eLockers
4. Parking: Pay at ticket machine or via ParkMobile app
5. Bikes are allowed on board; check Caltrain's Bikes on the Train rules

bay-area-ada-paratransit.name: Bay Area ADA Paratransit
bay-area-ada-paratransit.description: ADA Paratransit is a shared-ride, door-to-door transportation service for people who cannot use regular public transit due to a disability. Bay Area transit agencies provide coordinated paratransit service with regional certification—eligibility with one operator grants access to all Bay Area paratransit programs.
bay-area-ada-paratransit.what_they_offer:
- Door-to-door or curb-to-curb pickup and drop-off service
- Shared rides via small buses, vans, taxis, or sedans (usually reserved at least one day ahead)
- Service available in the same areas and during the same hours as regular fixed-route transit
- Regional certification accepted by all Bay Area operators
- Personal care attendants ride free
bay-area-ada-paratransit.how_to_get_it:
1. Contact your local transit agency to request an application (dial 511 for a free transfer)
2. Complete the ADA paratransit eligibility application
3. You may need a phone interview or in-person assessment; decisions are due within 21 days
4. Once certified, you can use paratransit across the Bay Area
5. Call 511 and say "paratransit" then your city name for local info

ac-transit-paratransit.name: AC Transit: East Bay Paratransit
ac-transit-paratransit.description: East Bay Paratransit, run jointly by AC Transit and BART, is a shared-ride, door-to-door service for people who are unable to use AC Transit or BART due to a disability. It serves areas within 3/4 mile of an operating AC Transit bus route or BART station, mainly in Alameda and western Contra Costa counties.
ac-transit-paratransit.what_they_offer:
- Door-to-door shared ride service
- Service area covers AC Transit and BART service areas, during their operating hours
- Reservations taken 1-7 days in advance (no same-day trips)
- Fares from $4 to $7 within the East Bay; $6 to $10 to or from San Francisco
- Free rides for personal care attendants
- Wheelchair accessible vehicles
ac-transit-paratransit.how_to_get_it:
1. Call 510-287-5000 or visit actransit.org/paratransit for an application
2. Complete the written application
3. An in-person interview is part of the eligibility process
4. Once certified, call 510-287-5000 (8 am-5 pm daily) by 5 pm the day before to book rides

samtrans-paratransit.name: SamTrans: Redi-Wheels Paratransit
samtrans-paratransit.description: SamTrans provides ADA paratransit through Redi-Wheels (bayside) and RediCoast (coastside) for people in San Mateo County who cannot use regular bus service due to a disability.
samtrans-paratransit.what_they_offer:
- Door-to-door shared ride service
- Redi-Wheels on the bayside and RediCoast on the coastside of San Mateo County
- Trips must be booked at least one day in advance
- Same-day trips offered based on availability (weekdays 9:30 am-6 pm)
- Reduced Lifeline fare for San Mateo County residents on SSI, General Assistance, or Medi-Cal
- Wheelchair accessible vehicles
- Personal care attendants ride free
samtrans-paratransit.how_to_get_it:
1. Call 650-366-4856 or visit samtrans.com to get the paratransit application
2. Complete and submit the ADA paratransit application
3. An eligibility assessment may be required
4. Once certified, book rides using the reservation number on your paratransit ID card

sfmta-paratransit.name: SFMTA: SF Paratransit
sfmta-paratransit.description: SF Paratransit is SFMTA's van and taxi program for people who are unable to independently use Muni because of a disability or disabling health condition. Services include SF Access van rides, the Paratransit Taxi program, and Group Van service.
sfmta-paratransit.what_they_offer:
- SF Access van service (shared-ride, door-to-door) anywhere in San Francisco, including Treasure Island
- Paratransit Taxi and Ramp Taxi program with a taxi debit card
- Group Van service to community-based programs
- Shop-a-Round shuttle for grocery shopping
- Personal care attendants ride free
sfmta-paratransit.how_to_get_it:
1. Complete the SF Paratransit eligibility application (call 415-351-7000, weekdays 9 am-4:45 pm)
2. Applications available online or by phone
3. Functional assessment may be required
4. Choose service options based on your needs
5. Book SF Access rides by calling 415-285-6945, option 2

vta-paratransit.name: VTA: ACCESS Paratransit
vta-paratransit.description: VTA ACCESS is an ADA paratransit service providing shared-ride transportation in Santa Clara County for people who cannot use regular VTA buses or light rail due to a disability.
vta-paratransit.what_they_offer:
- Shared ride service within VTA's bus and light rail service area and hours
- Reservations accepted 1-3 days in advance
- Standard trips $4; premium trips (same-day, extended area, open return) $16
- Wheelchair accessible vehicles
- Personal care attendants ride free
vta-paratransit.how_to_get_it:
1. Complete the VTA ACCESS Eligibility Data Card (online, PDF, or by mail)
2. Call Eligibility at 408-321-2381 to request a Data Card by mail
3. Complete a phone interview about your functional abilities
4. Once certified, book rides by calling 408-321-2380 (8 am-5 pm)

golden-gate-paratransit.name: Golden Gate Transit: Paratransit
golden-gate-paratransit.description: Golden Gate Transit's regional ADA paratransit service is operated by Marin Access for eligible riders who cannot use Golden Gate Transit's regional bus service due to a disability. It runs between Marin, Contra Costa, and San Francisco counties within 3/4 mile of Golden Gate Transit's regional bus routes.
golden-gate-paratransit.what_they_offer:
- Regional paratransit service complementing Golden Gate Transit's regional, non-commute bus routes
- Covers trips between Marin, San Francisco, and Contra Costa counties
- Reservations required; fares are charged
- Wheelchair accessible vehicles
golden-gate-paratransit.how_to_get_it:
1. Contact Marin Access Travel Navigators at 415-454-0902
2. Complete the ADA paratransit application
3. Assessment may be required
4. Once certified, call to schedule rides

marin-transit-paratransit.name: Marin Transit: Paratransit
marin-transit-paratransit.description: Marin Transit provides ADA paratransit service (Marin Access) for people in Marin County who cannot use regular local bus service due to a disability. You don't need to be a Marin resident if you're certified anywhere in the Bay Area.
marin-transit-paratransit.what_they_offer:
- Door-to-door shared ride service
- Local service within Marin County ($4 one-way) and regional trips (200% of Golden Gate fare)
- Reservations 1-7 days in advance
- Same-day service pilot for local trips on an as-available basis (premium fare)
- Wheelchair accessible vehicles
- Personal care attendants ride free
marin-transit-paratransit.how_to_get_it:
1. Call Travel Navigators at 415-454-0902 to start the application
2. Complete the application and provide a licensed professional's statement
3. An assessment may be required; decisions within 21 days
4. Once certified, schedule rides by phone

county-connection-paratransit.name: County Connection: LINK Paratransit
county-connection-paratransit.description: LINK is County Connection's ADA paratransit service for Central Contra Costa County residents who cannot use regular bus service due to a disability.
county-connection-paratransit.what_they_offer:
- Door-to-door shared ride service
- Serves locations within 1.5 miles of a County Connection bus route (or 3/4 mile of BART when buses aren't running)
- Reservations 1-7 days in advance
- $5 per person each way
- Wheelchair accessible vehicles
- Personal care attendants ride free
county-connection-paratransit.how_to_get_it:
1. Complete the LINK eligibility and registration form
2. Application at countyconnection.com/paratransit
3. An assessment may be required
4. Once registered, book rides by calling 925-938-RIDE (7433)

fast-paratransit.name: FAST: FAST Connect ADA Paratransit
fast-paratransit.description: FAST Connect ADA (formerly DART) is Fairfield and Suisun Transit's ADA paratransit service for people who cannot use FAST local buses due to a disability. It runs within 3/4 mile of FAST local routes in the Fairfield area, during the same days and hours as the buses.
fast-paratransit.what_they_offer:
- Origin-to-destination shared ride service (door-to-door on request)
- Service within the City of Fairfield ADA zone, within 3/4 mile of FAST local routes
- Trips booked 1-7 days in advance; same-day only if space is available
- 10-Ride pass for $40; single rides also sold through the Token Transit app
- Wheelchair accessible vehicles
- One personal care attendant rides free
fast-paratransit.how_to_get_it:
1. Call the Solano County Paratransit Eligibility Center at 707-541-7184 for an assessment
2. Complete the ADA eligibility assessment
3. Once certified, call FAST Connect ADA to book (8 am-5 pm, Monday-Saturday); dispatch is 707-422-2877 and FAST's office is 707-434-3800

tri-delta-paratransit.name: Tri Delta Transit: Paratransit
tri-delta-paratransit.description: Tri Delta Transit provides ADA paratransit service for eastern Contra Costa County residents who cannot use regular bus service due to a disability.
tri-delta-paratransit.what_they_offer:
- Door-to-door shared ride service
- Service in eastern Contra Costa (Antioch, Brentwood, Pittsburg, Oakley)
- Advance reservations required
- Wheelchair accessible vehicles
tri-delta-paratransit.how_to_get_it:
1. Complete the paratransit eligibility application (questions: Accessible Services, 925-706-4398)
2. Application at trideltatransit.com
3. Assessment may be required
4. Once certified, book rides by calling 925-754-3060

westcat-paratransit.name: WestCAT: Paratransit
westcat-paratransit.description: WestCAT provides ADA paratransit service for western Contra Costa County residents who cannot use regular bus service due to a disability.
westcat-paratransit.what_they_offer:
- Curb-to-curb shared ride service
- Service in Pinole, Hercules, Montalvin Manor, Tara Hills, Bayview, Rodeo, Crockett, and Port Costa
- Advance reservations required
- One-seat regional rides (no transfers) to County Connection, Tri Delta, and Wheels areas through a pilot program
- Wheelchair accessible vehicles
westcat-paratransit.how_to_get_it:
1. Complete the ADA paratransit application
2. Application and rider guide at westcat.org
3. Assessment may be required
4. Once certified, schedule rides by phone

union-city-paratransit.name: Union City Transit: Paratransit
union-city-paratransit.description: Union City Transit provides ADA paratransit service for Union City residents who cannot use regular bus service due to a disability.
union-city-paratransit.what_they_offer:
- Door-to-door shared ride service
- ADA service within Union City city limits
- Paratransit Plus (non-ADA) with limited service to southern Hayward and northern Fremont and Newark
- Reservations up to 3 days in advance
- Same fares as Union City Transit; 10-ride ticket book $27.50
- Wheelchair accessible vehicles
union-city-paratransit.how_to_get_it:
1. Complete the ADA Paratransit Application (fill out online, then print, sign, and mail)
2. Request a printed copy by calling 510-675-5373
3. Assessment may be required
4. Once certified, book rides by calling 510-476-1500, option 1 (8 am-5 pm daily)

soltrans-paratransit.name: SolTrans: Paratransit
soltrans-paratransit.description: SolTrans provides ADA paratransit service for Vallejo and Benicia residents who cannot use regular bus service due to a disability.
soltrans-paratransit.what_they_offer:
- Origin-to-destination shared ride service
- Service in Vallejo and Benicia, during the same days and hours as SolTrans buses
- Rides prescheduled 1-7 days in advance
- Wheelchair accessible vehicles
soltrans-paratransit.how_to_get_it:
1. Call the Solano County eligibility center at 707-541-7184 to schedule an eligibility appointment
2. Complete the eligibility assessment
3. Once certified, you'll receive an ID card
4. Schedule rides by phone (SolTrans: 707-648-4666)

napa-vine-paratransit.name: Vine Transit: Vine Go Paratransit
napa-vine-paratransit.description: VineGo is Napa County's ADA paratransit service for people who cannot use regular Vine bus service due to a disability.
napa-vine-paratransit.what_they_offer:
- Curb-to-curb shared ride service
- Service within 3/4 mile of Vine fixed-route bus service in Napa County
- Book up to 7 days in advance; same-day requests welcome if space allows
- Fares from $4 to $8 based on distance; discount passes ($20 for $24 value)
- Wheelchair accessible vehicles
napa-vine-paratransit.how_to_get_it:
1. Complete the VineGo paratransit application (available online in several languages)
2. Complete a phone eligibility interview (Eligibility Desk: 707-253-4649)
3. For help with the application, call NVTA at 707-259-8635
4. Once certified, call 707-252-2600 to schedule rides

vacaville-city-coach-paratransit.name: City Coach: Paratransit
vacaville-city-coach-paratransit.description: Vacaville City Coach provides Origin to Destination ADA paratransit for people who cannot use regular City Coach bus service due to a disability.
vacaville-city-coach-paratransit.what_they_offer:
- Origin-to-destination shared ride service
- Service within Vacaville city limits, during the same days and hours as City Coach buses
- Advance reservations required
- One-way ADA fare $2; 20-ride punch pass $39
- Wheelchair accessible vehicles
vacaville-city-coach-paratransit.how_to_get_it:
1. Call 707-541-7184 (weekdays) to schedule an in-person eligibility assessment
2. Complete the in-person assessment
3. You'll get a determination letter within 21 days
4. Once certified, schedule rides by phone

santa-rosa-paratransit.name: Santa Rosa CityBus: Paratransit
santa-rosa-paratransit.description: Santa Rosa CityBus provides ADA paratransit service for Santa Rosa residents who cannot use regular bus service due to a disability.
santa-rosa-paratransit.what_they_offer:
- Curb-to-curb shared ride service, seven days a week
- Service within 3/4 mile of Santa Rosa CityBus routes
- Unlimited trips can be booked 1-7 days in advance; same-day requests not guaranteed
- $3 one-way fare
- Wheelchair accessible vehicles
santa-rosa-paratransit.how_to_get_it:
1. Complete the paratransit eligibility application
2. Get the application from Santa Rosa CityBus (srcitybus.org)
3. Assessment may be required
4. Once certified, call 707-546-1999 to book (or use the online portal after registering by phone)

sonoma-county-paratransit.name: Sonoma County Transit: Paratransit
sonoma-county-paratransit.description: Sonoma County Transit provides ADA paratransit service for Sonoma County residents who cannot use regular bus service due to a disability.
sonoma-county-paratransit.what_they_offer:
- Shared ride service operated by Volunteer Wheels
- Service within 3/4 mile of Sonoma County Transit fixed routes
- Reservations from the next day up to 14 days in advance
- Zone-based fares; local paratransit along several local routes is fare-free
- Fare-free rides for veterans and college students with ID
- Wheelchair accessible vehicles
sonoma-county-paratransit.how_to_get_it:
1. Complete the ADA Paratransit Service Eligibility Application (download at sctransit.com or call 707-565-7433)
2. Mail it or email it to sct-paratransit@sonomacounty.gov
3. Eligibility is decided within 21 days of a complete application
4. Once certified, book rides with Volunteer Wheels at 707-573-3377 or 800-992-1006

petaluma-paratransit.name: Petaluma Transit: Paratransit
petaluma-paratransit.description: Petaluma Transit provides ADA paratransit service for Petaluma residents who cannot use regular bus service due to a disability.
petaluma-paratransit.what_they_offer:
- Shared ride service within Petaluma
- Fare-free (Petaluma Transit has not charged fares since July 2024)
- Reservations 1-7 days in advance
- Service runs Monday through Friday only (no weekend service as of August 10, 2026)
- Book and track rides with the Access by LumaGo app, or by phone
- Wheelchair accessible vehicles
petaluma-paratransit.how_to_get_it:
1. Complete a Basic or Medical eligibility application
2. Get the application from Petaluma Transit (707-778-4460)
3. Assessment may be required
4. Once certified, book rides by calling 707-778-4460 or using the LumaGo app

rio-vista-paratransit.name: Rio Vista Delta Breeze: Paratransit
rio-vista-paratransit.description: Rio Vista Delta Breeze gives ADA-certified paratransit riders priority on its Dial-A-Ride service in Rio Vista. Delta Breeze runs weekdays only, with no service on weekends or holidays.
rio-vista-paratransit.what_they_offer:
- Priority Dial-A-Ride service for ADA-certified riders
- Service within Rio Vista (Delta Breeze buses also connect to Isleton, Fairfield, and Suisun City)
- Advance reservations required
- Weekdays only, about 5 am-7:30 pm
- Wheelchair lift-equipped vehicles
rio-vista-paratransit.how_to_get_it:
1. Get ADA paratransit certification (riders certified anywhere in the Bay Area qualify)
2. Contact Delta Breeze at 707-374-2878 to ask how to apply
3. Assessment may be required
4. Once certified, call 707-374-2878 to reserve or cancel a trip

cid-borrow-battery.name: CID Borrow a Backup Battery
cid-borrow-battery.description: The Center for Independence of Individuals with Disabilities (CID) provides portable backup batteries to individuals who depend on electricity for medical equipment during Public Safety Power Shutoffs (PSPS).
cid-borrow-battery.what_they_offer:
- Loaner portable backup batteries for people who need power for medical reasons
- Highest priority for people who use life-sustaining electrical equipment
- Help signing up for PG&E's Medical Baseline program to lower your energy bill
- Tools to help you make a personal disaster plan
- Support during a PSPS or other disaster, in partnership with CFILC and Peninsula Clean Energy
cid-borrow-battery.how_to_get_it:
1. Call CID at 650-645-1780 or email info@cidsanmateo.org
2. Tell them about the medical equipment you need to keep powered
3. Ask for help enrolling in Medical Baseline and making a disaster plan
4. Contact CID when a PSPS is announced to arrange a loaner battery

cleanpowersf.name: CleanPowerSF
cleanpowersf.description: CleanPowerSF is San Francisco's community choice energy program, run by the SF Public Utilities Commission, providing renewable electricity to residents and businesses, with bill discounts and payment help for qualifying customers.
cleanpowersf.what_they_offer:
- Green service (at least 70% California-certified renewable) with automatic enrollment
- SuperGreen option for 100% California-certified renewable energy
- CARE/FERA monthly discounts (up to 35% off) apply to both the PG&E and CleanPowerSF parts of your bill
- SuperGreen Saver: 100% renewable energy plus a 20% discount for CARE/FERA customers in disadvantaged communities (currently full; waitlist open)
- Help with overdue bills: Arrearage Management Plan (forgives up to $8,000) and REACH (up to $800; funds subject to availability)
- Medical Baseline, LIHEAP, budget billing, and payment plans
cleanpowersf.how_to_get_it:
1. CleanPowerSF enrollment is automatic for SF residents
2. For a monthly discount, enroll in CARE or FERA at pge.com/carefera or call PG&E at 866-743-2273
3. If you have CARE/FERA and live in a qualifying area, apply for SuperGreen Saver to join the waitlist
4. For overdue bills, ask PG&E about AMP (800-743-5000) or Dollar Energy Fund about REACH (800-933-9677)
5. For LIHEAP, call Peninsula Energy Services at 415-416-6660

ebmud-assistance.name: EBMUD Customer Assistance Program
ebmud-assistance.description: The East Bay Municipal Utility District (EBMUD) Customer Assistance Program (CAP) provides discounts on water and wastewater bills for income-eligible residential customers and eligible homeless shelters in Alameda and Contra Costa counties.
ebmud-assistance.what_they_offer:
- 50% off the standard bimonthly water service charge
- 50% off home water use, up to 1,050 gallons per person per month
- 35% off EBMUD wastewater service and flow charges
- Discounts for eligible homeless shelters
- Payment extensions and payment arrangements
ebmud-assistance.how_to_get_it:
1. Check income limits: $67,900 or less for 1-2 people, $76,400 for 3, $84,850 for 4, $91,650 for 5, $98,450 for 6 (add $6,800 per additional person)
2. Home must be your primary residence with its own individual water meter
3. Apply online, or download an application, call 510-287-0468, or pick one up at 375 11th St., Oakland
4. Submit the application and proof of income by email (cap@ebmud.com), mail, or fax
5. Reapply every two years to keep the discount (not retroactive)

liheap.name: LIHEAP
liheap.description: The Low Income Home Energy Assistance Program (LIHEAP) is a federally funded program that helps low-income households pay their energy bills and make energy-efficient home improvements.
liheap.what_they_offer:
- One-time payment toward your heating or cooling bill
- Emergency help if your utility is about to be shut off
- Energy efficiency improvements (weatherization)
- Energy-related home repairs
- Assistance with heating and cooling costs
liheap.how_to_get_it:
1. Find your local LIHEAP provider with the search tool on the CSD website
2. Check income eligibility (2026 limit is about $3,332/month for 1 person, higher for larger households)
3. Gather documents: ID, utility bills, income verification
4. Apply through your local LIHEAP agency
5. If approved, payment goes directly to your utility company

medical-baseline.name: Medical Baseline Allowance
medical-baseline.description: The Medical Baseline Allowance program provides additional low-cost energy to customers with qualifying medical conditions that require extra electricity or gas, and includes priority notification before power shutoffs.
medical-baseline.what_they_offer:
- Additional baseline energy at lowest tier rates
- PG&E customers get about 500 extra kWh of electricity and/or 25 extra therms of gas per month (some electric rate plans get a 12% discount instead)
- Extra advance alerts before Public Safety Power Shutoffs (PSPS)
- Free to enroll
- Eligibility for PG&E's free portable battery program
medical-baseline.how_to_get_it:
1. Have a medical practitioner certify your condition or equipment on the utility's application
2. Qualifying conditions include: life-support equipment, heating/cooling needs for medical conditions, CPAP/BiPAP, oxygen concentrator, motorized wheelchair, multiple sclerosis, and more
3. Submit the application to your utility provider (PG&E, SCE, SDG&E, etc.)
4. Recertify as required (PG&E: every 2 years, or self-certify every 4 years for permanent conditions)
5. Contact your utility immediately if medical equipment is affected by an outage

pce-ebike-rebate.name: E-Bike Rebate
pce-ebike-rebate.description: WestLight Energy (formerly Peninsula Clean Energy) offers e-bike rebates to help income-qualified San Mateo County and Los Banos residents transition to clean transportation, reducing both costs and carbon emissions.
pce-ebike-rebate.what_they_offer:
- Up to $1,000 (or the price of the e-bike, whichever is less) toward a new e-bike
- Available to CARE or FERA program participants
- Can combine with other e-bike rebates (apply the other rebate first)
- One rebate per address
- Free application help from Senior Coastsiders (650-726-9056) or El Concilio (650-703-3604)
pce-ebike-rebate.how_to_get_it:
1. Must be a WestLight Energy customer living in San Mateo County or Los Banos
2. CARE or FERA must already show on page 1 of your PG&E bill when you apply
3. The program is temporarily paused while it moves to a new system; fill out the interest form to be emailed when it relaunches
4. Once approved, buy your e-bike within 60 days
5. Have a government-issued photo ID (and proof of address if different)
pce-ebike-rebate.timeframe: Temporarily paused; relaunch expected later in 2026 (sign up for notification)

pce-heat-pump-rebate.name: Heat Pump Heating & Cooling Rebate
pce-heat-pump-rebate.description: WestLight Energy (formerly Peninsula Clean Energy) offers rebates for San Mateo County and Los Banos homeowners to replace gas furnaces with efficient electric heat pumps that provide both heating and cooling.
pce-heat-pump-rebate.what_they_offer:
- $1,500 rebate for a heat pump replacing a gas heater/furnace
- Additional $1,000 for CARE/FERA customers ($2,500 total)
- Additional $1,000 for an electrical panel upgrade
- Extra $1,500 for City of Menlo Park residents while funding lasts
- Provides both heating and air conditioning
- Can combine with other federal, state, and local incentives and the 0% loan
pce-heat-pump-rebate.how_to_get_it:
1. Must be a WestLight Energy customer and the legal owner of the property
2. Hire any contractor (self-installs also qualify) and get the required city permit
3. Take photos of your old equipment before it is replaced
4. Complete installation
5. Submit rebate application with itemized invoice, photos, and permit within 90 days
6. Receive rebate check after approval

pce-home-upgrade-services.name: Home Upgrade Services
pce-home-upgrade-services.description: WestLight Energy's (formerly Peninsula Clean Energy) Full-Service Home Upgrade program offers fixed-price electrification for homeowners, and no-cost upgrades for income-eligible homeowners, converting gas appliances to electric from assessment to installation.
pce-home-upgrade-services.what_they_offer:
- Free in-home assessment
- No-cost installation for income-qualified homeowners; fixed, pre-negotiated pricing for everyone else
- Heat pump water heaters and HVAC systems (project must include one)
- Induction cooktops, electric washers/dryers, EV charging, insulation and air sealing
- Electrical upgrades if needed
- Permits and rebate applications handled for you
- Pre-vetted contractors
pce-home-upgrade-services.how_to_get_it:
1. Complete the online application
2. Must be a WestLight Energy customer who owns and lives in a single-family home (up to a fourplex) with gas appliances
3. For no-cost upgrades: home under 2,000 sq ft, income at or below 80% AMI (San Mateo County: $117,700 for 1 person, $168,100 for 4), investable assets under $500,000, and no other properties owned; CalFresh, CalWORKs, ESA and similar programs can prove eligibility
4. Schedule free in-home assessment
5. Review and approve your Home Upgrade Proposal
6. WestLight Energy's contractor handles permits and installation

pce-used-ev-rebate.name: Used Electric Vehicle Rebate
pce-used-ev-rebate.description: WestLight Energy (formerly Peninsula Clean Energy) helps income-qualified San Mateo County and Los Banos residents afford electric vehicles with a $2,000 instant rebate toward used plug-in hybrids or fully-electric vehicles.
pce-used-ev-rebate.what_they_offer:
- $2,000 instant rebate at time of purchase
- Covers used plug-in hybrid and fully-electric vehicles at least 2 model years old
- Must buy from a WestLight Energy participating dealership (no private-party or online sales)
- No maximum vehicle price
- Can combine with PG&E Pre-Owned EV Rebate and Clean Cars for All
pce-used-ev-rebate.how_to_get_it:
1. Must live in San Mateo County or Los Banos and not have received this rebate before
2. Qualify by income (e.g., household of 4 at $66,000 or less) or by enrollment in CARE, FERA, CalFresh, WIC, SSI, LIHEAP, Section 8, Clipper START, or similar programs
3. Buy an eligible used EV at a participating dealership
4. The dealer applies the rebate and submits paperwork for you
5. Keep proof of income in case you are selected for an audit

pce-water-heater-rebate.name: Water Heater Rebate
pce-water-heater-rebate.description: WestLight Energy (formerly Peninsula Clean Energy) offers substantial rebates for San Mateo County and Los Banos homeowners to replace gas or electric water heaters with efficient heat pump water heaters.
pce-water-heater-rebate.what_they_offer:
- Up to $4,000 for a heat pump water heater replacing a gas water heater (limited-time offer for installs Sept. 1 to Oct. 31, 2026)
- $500 rebate for replacing electric resistance water heater
- Additional $1,000 for CARE/FERA customers
- Additional $1,000 for electrical panel upgrade
- Up to $500 each for smart load management devices
- Can combine with zero-interest loan program and other incentives
pce-water-heater-rebate.how_to_get_it:
1. Must be a WestLight Energy customer and the legal owner of the property
2. Hire any contractor (self-installs also qualify) and get the required city permit
3. Take photos of your old water heater before it is replaced
4. Complete installation
5. Submit rebate application with itemized invoice, photos, and permit within 90 days
6. Optional: Apply for zero-interest loan (before installation, with an approved contractor)
pce-water-heater-rebate.timeframe: Ongoing; boosted gas-replacement rebate through October 31, 2026

pce-zero-interest-loan.name: Zero Interest Loan for Upgrades
pce-zero-interest-loan.description: WestLight Energy (formerly Peninsula Clean Energy) offers zero-interest financing to help its customers electrify their homes without upfront costs, with convenient repayment through monthly utility bills.
pce-zero-interest-loan.what_they_offer:
- Up to $10,000 zero-interest loan
- No money down, no fees, no credit check
- Choose a 2 to 5 year repayment term
- Covers heat pump water heaters
- Covers heat pump HVAC systems
- Covers electrical panel upgrades (when part of a heat pump project)
- Repayment on monthly electric bill
pce-zero-interest-loan.how_to_get_it:
1. Must be a WestLight Energy residential customer, own the home, and have the PG&E bill in your name
2. Have no past-due balance on your last three PG&E bills
3. Get a quote from a WestLight Energy loan-approved contractor
4. Apply online with the quote (reviewed within five business days) and sign the loan agreement before installation
5. Complete installation; WestLight Energy pays the contractor
6. Loan payments added to monthly electric bill

pge-amp.name: Arrearage Management Plan (AMP)
pge-amp.description: PG&E's Arrearage Management Plan helps CARE-enrolled customers reduce their past-due utility debt by forgiving up to $8,000 over 12 months when they make consistent on-time payments.
pge-amp.what_they_offer:
- Up to $8,000 in debt forgiveness
- Part of your past-due balance forgiven each month you pay on time
- Full forgiveness after 12 on-time monthly payments
- You can miss up to two non-consecutive payments and stay enrolled
- Amounts already forgiven stay forgiven even if you are removed
- Works alongside CARE or FERA discount
pge-amp.how_to_get_it:
1. Must be enrolled in PG&E CARE or FERA program
2. Must owe at least $500 (or $250 for gas-only accounts)
3. Balance must be more than 90 days past due
4. Must be a PG&E customer for at least 6 months with at least one on-time payment
5. Contact PG&E or apply online to enroll
6. Make on-time monthly payments for 12 months; if you leave the program, wait 12 months to reapply

pge-automated-response.name: Automated Response Technology Program
pge-automated-response.description: PG&E's Automated Response Technology Program rewards customers for enrolling smart home devices that can automatically adjust energy use during peak demand periods, helping stabilize the grid.
pge-automated-response.what_they_offer:
- Rewards paid by your enrollment provider (amounts vary by provider)
- Eligible devices: smart thermostats, EV chargers, heat pump water heaters, battery storage
- Automatic adjustments during peak times
- Helps reduce energy costs
- Supports grid reliability
pge-automated-response.how_to_get_it:
1. Must be a PG&E customer
2. Own a compatible internet-connected smart device
3. Enroll through a participating provider listed on PG&E's program page (such as SmartFlex Rewards by Uplight or Deco Energy; PG&E enrolls some batteries directly)
4. Allow device to auto-adjust during demand events
5. Receive rewards from your provider

pge-care.name: PG&E CARE & FERA
pge-care.description: PG&E's CARE (California Alternate Rates for Energy) and FERA (Family Electric Rate Assistance) programs provide significant utility bill discounts for income-qualified households.
pge-care.what_they_offer:
- CARE: 35% or more off electricity, 20% or more off natural gas
- FERA: 18% discount on electricity for larger households
- Gateway to many other programs and rebates
- Can be combined with Medical Baseline if medically necessary
- Recertify every 2 years (every 4 years on fixed income); PG&E mails a renewal notice
pge-care.how_to_get_it:
1. Check income eligibility (guidelines change each June; current limits valid through May 31, 2027)
2. CARE: Income at or below 200% federal poverty level
3. FERA: 3+ person household, slightly higher income limits
4. Apply online at pge.com/care (English, Spanish, Chinese)
5. Or mail or email (CAREandFERA@pge.com) a printed application
6. No documents needed to apply; provide income verification if requested

cpuc-esa.name: CPUC Energy Savings Assistance (ESA) Program
cpuc-esa.description: The Energy Savings Assistance Program provides free home energy upgrades and weatherization services to income-qualified households, helping reduce energy bills and improve comfort.
cpuc-esa.what_they_offer:
- Free energy assessment of your home
- LED lighting upgrades
- New energy-efficient refrigerator
- Weatherization (insulation, caulking, weather stripping)
- HVAC repairs or replacement
- Heat pump water heater installation
- Smart power strips
- All services and equipment at no cost
cpuc-esa.how_to_get_it:
1. Check income eligibility (PG&E guidelines valid through May 31, 2027)
2. Complete PG&E's short online application or call 1-800-933-9555
3. An energy specialist visits your home to assess needs and verify income
4. Receive free installation of qualifying upgrades
5. Renters and homeowners both eligible; home must be at least 5 years old
6. Proof of income can be waived if you are enrolled in programs like CalFresh, Medi-Cal, or TANF

pge-generator-battery-rebate.name: Generator & Battery Rebate
pge-generator-battery-rebate.description: PG&E provides rebates for portable generators and batteries to help customers in high fire-risk areas prepare for power outages during Public Safety Power Shutoffs and other wildfire safety outages.
pge-generator-battery-rebate.what_they_offer:
- Up to $300 rebate on a qualifying portable generator or portable battery
- Up to $200 extra for CARE or FERA customers
- For customers in Tier 2 or 3 High Fire-Threat Districts, High Fire Risk Areas, or on EPSS circuits
- Open to residential and business accounts
- Generators must be CARB-compliant and on PG&E's qualified product list; batteries must be 290-1,000 Wh
pge-generator-battery-rebate.how_to_get_it:
1. Check if your address qualifies on PG&E's Wildfire Safety Progress Map
2. Purchase a qualifying new generator or battery (no used, refurbished, rented, or leased items)
3. Wait until the product is delivered
4. Apply online within 12 months of purchase, and no later than December 31, 2026
5. Submit proof of purchase and delivery

sgip-home-battery-sgip.name: Home Battery Rebate (SGIP)
sgip-home-battery-sgip.description: The Self-Generation Incentive Program (SGIP) provides incentives for home battery storage; the Equity Resiliency rebate can cover 80-100% of battery costs for vulnerable households in wildfire and outage-prone areas, and the income-qualified Equity rebate is currently waitlisted.
sgip-home-battery-sgip.what_they_offer:
- Equity Resiliency rebate: covers 80% to 100% of battery installation cost
- Residential Solar and Storage Equity rebate (income-qualified, up to 100% with federal credits): currently closed; join the waitlist through your contractor
- Backup power during outages
- Can pair with solar
sgip-home-battery-sgip.how_to_get_it:
1. Equity Resiliency: live in a Tier 2/3 High Fire-Threat District, or have had more than two PSPS outages or 5+ EPSS outages since 2023
2. And be on Medical Baseline, meet income standards, or rely on an electric well pump (or be enrolled in ESA or have SASH/DAC-SASH incentives reserved)
3. Work with an SGIP-approved contractor, who submits the application for you
4. Enroll in a demand response program (Automated Response Technology or SmartRate)
5. Solar customers on older net metering may need to switch to the Solar Billing Plan
sgip-home-battery-sgip.timeframe: Equity Resiliency open; Equity rebate waitlisted pending new funding

pge-induction-test-drive.name: Induction Cooktop Test Drive
pge-induction-test-drive.description: PG&E's Induction Cooktop Test Drive lets customers try induction cooking at home before making a purchase decision, with a free two-week loaner including everything needed to get started.
pge-induction-test-drive.what_they_offer:
- Free two-week induction cooktop loan
- Portable single-burner induction unit
- Induction-compatible pan included
- Instructions and cooking tips
- Pre-paid return shipping label
- No cost or obligation to buy
pge-induction-test-drive.how_to_get_it:
1. Must be a PG&E customer
2. Visit the Induction Loaner Library website
3. Reserve an available induction cooktop
4. Receive unit by mail
5. Try it for two weeks
6. Return using included shipping label

pge-match-payment.name: PG&E Match My Payment Program
pge-match-payment.description: PG&E's Match My Payment Program helps customers reduce past-due balances by matching every dollar they pay, up to $1,000. The program is on hold for 2026 and not accepting new applications.
pge-match-payment.what_they_offer:
- PG&E matches your payments dollar-for-dollar toward past-due bills
- Up to $1,000 in matching funds
- Helps clear past-due balances faster
- Subject to funding availability
- On hold for 2026; REACH and payment arrangements are available in the meantime
pge-match-payment.how_to_get_it:
1. Check PG&E's program page for when applications reopen
2. Household income must be below 400% of the federal poverty level
3. Applications are processed by Dollar Energy Fund
4. Make payments toward your balance
5. PG&E matches each payment up to $1,000 total
pge-match-payment.timeframe: On hold for 2026; not accepting new applications

pge-permanent-battery-rebate.name: Permanent Battery Storage Rebate
pge-permanent-battery-rebate.description: PG&E offers a substantial rebate for permanent home battery storage to customers who have experienced frequent Wildfire Safety (EPSS) outages, helping them maintain power reliability.
pge-permanent-battery-rebate.what_they_offer:
- $7,500 rebate for permanent battery storage
- For customers with 5+ Wildfire Safety outages since January 1, 2024
- First-come, first-served with limited rebates remaining
- Battery must be on PG&E's Qualified Product List and bought on or after January 1, 2025
- Must be on a time-of-use rate plan
- Must enroll in the Emergency Load Reduction Program through your battery provider
pge-permanent-battery-rebate.how_to_get_it:
1. Enter your address on PG&E's Wildfire Safety Progress Map and check the "Backup Power Solutions" tab
2. Must be a residential PG&E electric customer getting a battery for the first time
3. Install a qualifying battery and get Permission to Operate
4. Switch to time-of-use rate plan and enroll in the Emergency Load Reduction Program
5. Apply within 12 months of Permission to Operate, and no later than December 31, 2026
pge-permanent-battery-rebate.timeframe: Open while funds last (about 200 rebates remaining as of September 2026); apply by December 31, 2026

pge-portable-battery.name: Portable Battery Program
pge-portable-battery.description: PG&E provides free portable backup batteries to customers who depend on electricity for medical equipment and have experienced power shutoffs, ensuring they can maintain critical care during outages.
pge-portable-battery.what_they_offer:
- Free portable backup battery sized to your equipment
- For Medical Baseline customers
- For Self-Identified Vulnerable customers
- Powers medical devices and assistive technology during outages
- For those who experienced a PSPS outage or 3+ EPSS outages since 2024
- Referral to the Disability Disaster Access & Resources Program if your needs exceed a portable battery
pge-portable-battery.how_to_get_it:
1. Must be enrolled in Medical Baseline program
2. Or registered as Self-Identified Vulnerable customer
3. Must rely on a medical device, assistive technology, or durable medical equipment
4. Must have experienced a PSPS outage or 3+ EPSS outages since 2024
5. No application needed; PG&E's program partners contact eligible customers directly for an assessment
6. Battery delivered at no cost

pge-reach.name: Relief for Energy Assistance through Community Help (REACH)
pge-reach.description: The REACH program provides emergency bill assistance for PG&E customers facing disconnection, offering up to $800 to help income-eligible households avoid losing power or gas service.
pge-reach.what_they_offer:
- Up to $800 energy bill credit toward past-due charges
- Helps prevent service disconnection
- For customers who received a shutoff notice
- Available once per calendar year
- Credit goes directly to your PG&E bill
- First-come, first-served while funding lasts
pge-reach.how_to_get_it:
1. Must be income-eligible (up to 200% federal poverty level)
2. Must be the customer of record and have received a 15-day or 48-hour disconnection notice
3. Apply online through Dollar Energy Fund (myappconnect.com/pge) or call for help with the form
4. Customers enrolled in the Arrearage Management Plan (AMP) are not eligible
5. Credit applied directly to your PG&E account

pge-residential-charging.name: Residential Charging Solutions Rebate
pge-residential-charging.description: PG&E's Residential Charging Solutions Rebate helps customers pay for PG&E-approved home EV charging equipment, with larger Rebate Plus amounts for income-qualified customers covering installation and panel upgrades.
pge-residential-charging.what_they_offer:
- Standard rebate: up to 50% of the purchase price of approved charging equipment
- Rebate Plus (income-qualified): up to $2,000 for charger installation
- Rebate Plus: up to $5,000 for a panel upgrade plus charger installation
- Covers approved chargers, energy management systems, and smart splitters
- One rebate per household, first-come, first-served
pge-residential-charging.how_to_get_it:
1. Must be an active PG&E residential customer who owns or leases a BEV or PHEV registered in California
2. For Rebate Plus: household income under 80% of area median income, enrollment in programs like CalFresh, Medi-Cal, or SSI, or a recent PG&E Pre-Owned EV Rebate
3. Choose PG&E-approved charging equipment
4. Have it installed by a licensed electrician (Rebate Plus uses PG&E's Trade Ally Network)
5. Apply within 180 days of equipment purchase

pge-used-ev-rebate.name: Used Electric Vehicle Rebate
pge-used-ev-rebate.description: PG&E offers a $4,000 Rebate Plus for income-qualified customers purchasing or leasing pre-owned electric vehicles. The $1,000 Standard Rebate for all customers ends September 30, 2026.
pge-used-ev-rebate.what_they_offer:
- Rebate Plus: $4,000 for income-qualified customers
- Standard Rebate: $1,000 for any residential customer (applications through September 30, 2026 only)
- Covers pre-owned Battery Electric Vehicles (BEV) and Plug-in Hybrids (PHEV) with at least an 8 kWh battery
- Purchase or lease qualifies
- Can combine with other state/local rebates (not the same vehicle's rebate from another utility)
pge-used-ev-rebate.how_to_get_it:
1. Must be an active PG&E residential electric customer
2. Check income limits for your county with the ZIP code lookup on the program site
3. Purchase or lease a qualifying pre-owned EV
4. Apply within 90 days of purchase or lease
5. Keep the vehicle registered at your PG&E address for at least 20 months
pge-used-ev-rebate.timeframe: Ongoing; Standard Rebate ends September 30, 2026 (income-qualified only starting October 1, 2026)

pge-v2x-pilot.name: Vehicle-to-Everything (V2X) Pilot Program
pge-v2x-pilot.description: PG&E's V2X program provides incentives to help offset the extra cost of bidirectional EV chargers that can power your home using your electric vehicle's battery during outages or send power back to the grid.
pge-v2x-pilot.what_they_offer:
- Upfront incentive toward a bidirectional charger (about $2,500 for homes, $3,000 in disadvantaged communities)
- Early adopter bonus and additional state grant funding may be available for eligible customers
- Powers home from EV battery during outages
- Additional earnings through performance-based incentives and the Emergency Load Reduction Program
- Growing list of eligible vehicles and chargers (Ford, GM, Tesla, Kia, Volvo, Nissan and more added in 2026)
pge-v2x-pilot.how_to_get_it:
1. Must be a PG&E residential or commercial customer (some CCA customers also qualify)
2. Own an EV and bidirectional charger combination on PG&E's Eligible Product Lists
3. Hire an EVITP-certified electrician for installation
4. Get a Rule 21 interconnection agreement for grid-connected systems; be on a time-of-use rate for Hourly Flex Pricing
5. Enroll through PG&E's V2X program page before June 30, 2027

pge-wattersaver.name: WatterSaver
pge-wattersaver.description: WatterSaver is a demand response program that pays customers to enroll their smart electric water heaters, automatically shifting water heating to off-peak times to save money and support the grid.
pge-wattersaver.what_they_offer:
- $50 enrollment bonus
- $5 per month for participation
- Automatic water heating optimization
- Shifts heating to lower-cost times
- Hot water still available when you need it; you can pause participation anytime
- Time-of-use rate no longer required (as of March 2026)
pge-wattersaver.how_to_get_it:
1. Must be an electric customer of PG&E or a participating Community Choice Aggregator
2. Must have a qualifying smart heat pump or electric resistance water heater
3. Sign up on the WatterSaver website or call 888-707-9930
4. Connect water heater to Wi-Fi
5. Receive $50 enrollment bonus
6. Earn $5/month ongoing

baaqmd-clean-cars-ev.name: Clean Cars for All - EV
baaqmd-clean-cars-ev.description: The Bay Area Air Quality Management District's Clean Cars for All program provides substantial incentives for income-qualified residents to replace older polluting vehicles with new or used electric vehicles.
baaqmd-clean-cars-ev.what_they_offer:
- $10,000-$12,000 grant for a battery electric vehicle (higher amount for disadvantaged community residents)
- $9,500-$11,500 for a plug-in hybrid
- Up to $2,000 for EV charging
- Up to $5,000 more for adaptive equipment
- Trade in a 2007 or older gas or diesel vehicle
baaqmd-clean-cars-ev.how_to_get_it:
1. Must live in the Air District's Bay Area jurisdiction (9-county region)
2. Household income at or below 300% federal poverty level (e.g., $47,880 for 1 person, $99,000 for 4)
3. Own an operational 2007 or older gas/diesel vehicle continuously registered in California for the past 2 years
4. Register and apply online; GRID Alternatives (855-256-3656) helps with applications
5. Wait for your Award Letter BEFORE buying; cars bought earlier or from non-authorized dealers are ineligible
6. Trade in old vehicle and buy/lease qualifying EV at a participating dealer

baaqmd-clean-cars-fuel-cell.name: Clean Cars for All - Fuel Cell Vehicle
baaqmd-clean-cars-fuel-cell.description: The Clean Cars for All program also offers rebates for hydrogen fuel cell vehicles, providing another zero-emission option for Bay Area residents replacing older polluting vehicles.
baaqmd-clean-cars-fuel-cell.what_they_offer:
- $10,000-$12,000 grant for a hydrogen fuel cell vehicle (higher amount for disadvantaged community residents)
- Trade in a 2007 or older gas or diesel vehicle
- Covers purchase or lease
- Zero emissions, hydrogen-powered
baaqmd-clean-cars-fuel-cell.how_to_get_it:
1. Must live in the Air District's Bay Area jurisdiction (9-county region)
2. Household income at or below 300% federal poverty level (e.g., $47,880 for 1 person, $99,000 for 4)
3. Own an operational 2007 or older gas/diesel vehicle continuously registered in California for the past 2 years
4. Register and apply online; GRID Alternatives (855-256-3656) helps with applications
5. Wait for your Award Letter BEFORE buying; cars bought earlier or from non-authorized dealers are ineligible
6. Trade in old vehicle and buy/lease fuel cell vehicle

baaqmd-clean-cars-ebike-transit.name: Clean Cars for All - E-Bike & Transit Credit
baaqmd-clean-cars-ebike-transit.description: For those who don't need a car, Clean Cars for All offers a mobility option with a pre-paid card for public transit and e-bike purchases, providing sustainable transportation alternatives when trading in an older vehicle.
baaqmd-clean-cars-ebike-transit.what_they_offer:
- $7,500 mobility option
- Pre-paid card to use for public transit and to buy an e-bike
- Trade in a 2007 or older gas or diesel vehicle
- Supports car-free lifestyle
baaqmd-clean-cars-ebike-transit.how_to_get_it:
1. Must live in the Air District's Bay Area jurisdiction (9-county region)
2. Household income at or below 300% federal poverty level (e.g., $47,880 for 1 person, $99,000 for 4)
3. Own an operational 2007 or older gas/diesel vehicle continuously registered in California for the past 2 years
4. Register and apply online; GRID Alternatives (855-256-3656) helps with applications
5. Get approved before retiring your vehicle
6. Trade in old vehicle and receive the pre-paid mobility card

baaqmd-vehicle-buyback.name: Vehicle Buy Back Program
baaqmd-vehicle-buyback.description: BAAQMD's Vehicle Buy Back program pays $2,000 for older vehicles to be scrapped, reducing air pollution from high-emitting cars while providing owners compensation for retiring their vehicles.
baaqmd-vehicle-buyback.what_they_offer:
- $2,000 payment for your old vehicle
- Vehicle must be model year 2000 or older
- Cars and small trucks eligible
- Vehicle must be in operating condition
- No income requirements
- Open to Bay Area vehicle owners
baaqmd-vehicle-buyback.how_to_get_it:
1. Vehicle must be currently registered as operable in the Bay Area, and for the past 2 years
2. Vehicle must be model year 2000 or older and in operating condition
3. If a Smog Check is due within 60 days, the vehicle must pass it
4. Contact an Air District-approved dismantler (Environmental Engineering Studies or Pick-n-Pull)
5. The dismantler inspects and scraps the vehicle and pays you $2,000

baaqmd-wood-stove.name: Wood Stove Replacement Program
baaqmd-wood-stove.description: BAAQMD's Clean HEET Program helps Bay Area homeowners replace wood-burning stoves, inserts, and fireplaces with clean electric heat pumps, improving air quality and reducing home heating costs. The 2026 application period has closed.
baaqmd-wood-stove.what_they_offer:
- Up to $6,500 for a heat pump replacing a 2014 or older wood stove/insert ($6,000 for an open-hearth fireplace; less for newer or pellet devices)
- Additional $4,000 for income-qualified participants
- $3,000 more for a second device
- $1,000 for removal only (no replacement)
- No reimbursement for work already done before approval
baaqmd-wood-stove.how_to_get_it:
1. Sign up for Clean HEET updates and future woodsmoke funding opportunities on the BAAQMD website
2. Must be a Bay Area homeowner with a wood-burning stove, insert, or fireplace
3. Apply when a new application period opens
4. Submit income documentation if claiming additional incentive
5. Get approved (or waitlisted) before starting work
6. Receive incentive after project completion
baaqmd-wood-stove.timeframe: 2026 application period closed July 14, 2026; sign up for future rounds

ca-old-vehicle-retirement.name: Old Vehicle Retirement
ca-old-vehicle-retirement.description: California's Consumer Assistance Program (CAP) pays drivers to retire operational gas or diesel vehicles, with higher payments for low-income households, helping get polluting vehicles off the road.
ca-old-vehicle-retirement.what_they_offer:
- $2,000 if income-eligible and the vehicle failed its most recent Smog Check
- $1,500 if income-eligible and the vehicle had a Smog Check (pass or fail) within 180 days before applying
- $1,350 with no income requirement if the vehicle failed its most recent Smog Check
- Vehicle must be retired (scrapped) at a BAR-contracted dismantler
- No repair required before retiring
- Payment issued after vehicle retirement
ca-old-vehicle-retirement.how_to_get_it:
1. Income-eligible means household income at or below 225% of the federal poverty level
2. Must be the registered owner with title in your name, and the vehicle must be continuously registered for the past 2 years (no lapse over 120 days)
3. Vehicle must be drivable with all major parts (doors, hood, windshield, lights, seat, exhaust, etc.)
4. Apply online or by mail and upload income documents if needed
5. Wait for your eligibility letter before retiring the vehicle
6. Take the vehicle to a BAR-contracted dismantler and receive payment

dcap-clean-cars.name: Driving Clean Assistance Program: Clean Cars 4 All
dcap-clean-cars.description: The Driving Clean Assistance Program (DCAP) helps income-qualified Californians trade in old gas vehicles for clean alternatives. Bay Area residents are served by the Air District's own Clean Cars for All program for scrap-and-replace, and DCAP's financing assistance pathway is currently closed.
dcap-clean-cars.what_they_offer:
- Clean Cars 4 All scrap-and-replace: up to $10,000 toward a clean vehicle ($12,000 in disadvantaged communities)
- $2,000 for a home Level 2 charger or a prepaid public charging card
- Alternative: $7,500 mobility option
- Scrap-and-replace is only for areas without their own air district Clean Cars 4 All program (Bay Area residents should apply through BAAQMD Clean Cars for All)
- Financing assistance pathway (down payment help, credit counseling, lower-rate loans) closed to new applications as of August 2026
dcap-clean-cars.how_to_get_it:
1. Check income eligibility (household income under 300% federal poverty level)
2. MUST apply BEFORE trading in or buying a car
3. Trade-in vehicle must be 2010 or older, under 10,000 lbs, with 2+ years of operation history
