4. Replacement vehicle must be $45,000 or less; used vehicles 75,000 miles or less
5. One incentive per household; not available if you already received a CARB light-duty vehicle incentive
dcap-clean-cars.timeframe: Scrap-and-replace open outside local CC4A air districts; financing pathway closed

weatherization-assistance.name: Weatherization Assistance Program
weatherization-assistance.description: California's Weatherization Assistance Program provides free energy efficiency upgrades to help low-income households reduce energy costs and improve home comfort and safety.
weatherization-assistance.what_they_offer:
- Free home energy audit
- Insulation (attic, wall, floor)
- Air sealing and weatherstripping
- Heating system repairs or replacement
- Water heater repairs or replacement
- Minor home repairs for energy efficiency
- All services at no cost
weatherization-assistance.how_to_get_it:
1. Find your local weatherization provider
2. Contact the provider to check income eligibility (limits vary by program)
3. Submit application with income documentation
4. Technician conducts home energy audit
5. Eligible improvements installed at no cost
6. Both homeowners and renters can apply

bayren-ease.name: Efficiency and Sustainable Energy (EASE) Home Program
bayren-ease.description: BayREN's EASE Home Program covers 80% of the cost of weatherization and efficiency upgrades for income-qualified Bay Area PG&E customers, with a co-pay capped at 20% and vetted contractors.
bayren-ease.what_they_offer:
- BayREN covers 80% of the cost of program upgrades
- Your share capped at 20% of the project cost
- Insulation, duct sealing or replacement, and air sealing
- Induction stove or cooktop (must replace a gas appliance)
- Smart thermostats and weatherstripping
- Help applying for additional rebates
- Fixed pricing with vetted contractors and a 1-year installation warranty
- Limited-time offer of up to $2,000 to fix knob-and-tube wiring
bayren-ease.how_to_get_it:
1. Must be a PG&E customer in a 1-4 unit home built before 2010
2. Household income at or below 120% of area median income
3. Check eligibility and apply on the BayREN website
4. Schedule your free in-home site visit
5. Review your proposal; plan must include insulation, duct work, or induction cooking
6. Renters need property owner permission

bayren-home-assessment.name: Home Energy Assessment
bayren-home-assessment.description: BayREN offers rebates for professional home energy assessments, providing homeowners with a comprehensive score and report identifying upgrades that can reduce energy costs.
bayren-home-assessment.what_they_offer:
- $200 rebate for energy assessment
- Professional in-home evaluation
- Home Energy Score (1-10 rating)
- Detailed report of improvement opportunities
- Cost and savings estimates
- Prioritized upgrade recommendations
- Helps plan home electrification
bayren-home-assessment.how_to_get_it:
1. Find a BayREN-qualified assessor on website
2. Schedule in-home energy assessment
3. Assessor evaluates home and provides score
4. Receive detailed report with recommendations
5. Ask your assessor about the $200 BayREN rebate before you commit
6. Receive $200 rebate

calwater-rebates.name: Water Conservation Rebates
calwater-rebates.description: Cal Water offers rebates for water-saving products and lawn-to-garden conversions, plus free conservation kits and landscape tune-ups to help customers reduce water usage and lower bills.
calwater-rebates.what_they_offer:
- High-efficiency toilet rebates (MaP Premium models)
- High-efficiency clothes washer rebates
- Smart irrigation controller and sprinkler nozzle rebates
- Lawn-to-garden rebate (per square foot; artificial turf does not qualify)
- Free conservation kit with showerheads, faucet aerators, and hose nozzle
- Free Smart Landscape Tune-Up in select service areas
calwater-rebates.how_to_get_it:
1. Must be a current Cal Water customer
2. Create an account on the Cal Water Conservation Portal
3. Check which programs are available in your district
4. Get pre-approval before starting a lawn-to-garden project
5. Submit rebate application with proof of purchase
6. Request your free conservation kit through the portal (one per address every 3 years)

energy-smart-homes-electrification.name: Whole Building Electrification
energy-smart-homes-electrification.description: The California Energy-Smart Homes program provides incentives for fully electrifying existing homes by removing all gas appliances and switching to efficient electric alternatives. 2026 funding is fully subscribed; a waitlist is open.
energy-smart-homes-electrification.what_they_offer:
- $4,250 for single-family whole-home electrification
- $2,200 per unit for multifamily low-rise buildings and ADUs
- $250 bonus for a heat pump clothes dryer
- Electrical infrastructure upgrade bonus (up to $1,000 single-family, $600 per multifamily unit)
- Must include heat pump heating, heat pump water heating, induction cooking, and an electric dryer
- Homes with existing electric cooking do not need to add induction
energy-smart-homes-electrification.how_to_get_it:
1. Must be in PG&E, SCE, or SDG&E electric territory
2. Plan to replace ALL gas appliances with electric and cap gas lines
3. Apply to the waitlist on the Energy-Smart Homes website
4. Use a licensed contractor to complete the work
5. Submit documentation for the incentive
6. Propane-to-electric conversions do not qualify
energy-smart-homes-electrification.timeframe: 2026 funding fully subscribed (as of April 20, 2026); waitlist open for future funding

quitcarbon-rebate.name: QuitCarbon Rebate
quitcarbon-rebate.description: QuitCarbon offers additional rebates when you use their free home electrification planning service and their network of contractors for qualifying projects over $4,000.
quitcarbon-rebate.what_they_offer:
- $100 rebate for first qualifying upgrade
- $200 rebate for second qualifying upgrade
- Up to $300 total
- Covers heat pump HVAC
- Covers heat pump water heater
- Covers solar/battery installations
- Covers battery-equipped induction ranges
quitcarbon-rebate.how_to_get_it:
1. Use QuitCarbon's free electrification planning
2. Get referral to their contractor network
3. Complete project over $4,000
4. Contractor and sales must be QuitCarbon referrals
5. Receive $100 for first upgrade
6. Receive $200 for second upgrade

recology-discount.name: Recology 25% Low-Income Discount Program
recology-discount.description: Recology San Francisco offers a 25% discount on garbage collection bills for income-qualified San Francisco households, helping reduce the cost of essential waste services.
recology-discount.what_they_offer:
- 25% discount on garbage collection bills
- Qualify by showing enrollment in a public benefit program
- Accepted programs include PG&E CARE, CalFresh, Medi-Cal, WIC, LIHEAP, SSI, CalWORKs, and the National School Lunch Program
- Households with premium service are not eligible
- Accounts with more than one unit are not eligible
recology-discount.how_to_get_it:
1. Must be a Recology customer in San Francisco
2. Gather your voucher or award letter from a qualifying benefit program
3. Contact your Recology service provider to apply (listed on your bill)
4. Once approved, discount applied to future bills

redwood-city-electrification.name: Building Electrification Rebate Program
redwood-city-electrification.description: The City of Redwood City offers rebates to help homeowners electrify their homes with heat pump water heaters, heat pump HVAC systems, and electrical panel upgrades.
redwood-city-electrification.what_they_offer:
- $500 rebate for heat pump water heater (replacing gas)
- $500 rebate for high-efficiency heat pump (replacing gas furnace and AC)
- Up to $500 for electrical panel upgrade if needed for new heat pump equipment
- Additional $500 for CARE, FERA, or WSRAP customers to help cover permit costs
- Up to three rebates on one application per home
- Rebates paid by check, first-come, first-served
redwood-city-electrification.how_to_get_it:
1. Must be a Redwood City homeowner
2. Call Public Works to confirm eligibility before buying equipment
3. Buy equipment between July 1, 2026 and June 30, 2027
4. Installation must be permitted by the City
5. Submit application with receipts, photos, and permit number within 90 days of installation
6. Receive rebate check (may take up to 8 weeks)
redwood-city-electrification.timeframe: Through June 30, 2027 or until funds run out

redwood-city-ev-charger.name: Electric Vehicle (EV) Charger Rebate Program
redwood-city-ev-charger.description: The City of Redwood City offers rebates for residents installing Level 2 EV chargers at home, making electric vehicle ownership more convenient.
redwood-city-ev-charger.what_they_offer:
- $500 rebate for a new Level 2 EV charger
- One rebate per residential unit
- For Redwood City residents only
- Faster charging than standard outlet
- Rebates paid by check, first-come, first-served
redwood-city-ev-charger.how_to_get_it:
1. Must be a Redwood City resident
2. Call Public Works to confirm eligibility before buying
3. Buy and install a new Level 2 charger between July 1, 2026 and June 30, 2027
4. Fill out the application from the City website
5. Submit application with receipts and documentation within 90 days
6. Receive rebate check
redwood-city-ev-charger.timeframe: Through June 30, 2027 or until funds run out

redwood-city-lawn-equipment.name: Electric Lawn Care Equipment Rebate
redwood-city-lawn-equipment.description: The City of Redwood City offers rebates for switching from gas-powered lawn equipment to electric, reducing noise and air pollution in the community.
redwood-city-lawn-equipment.what_they_offer:
- Residents: up to $150 for electric lawn equipment (string trimmer, hedge trimmer, edger, tiller/cultivator, or spare batteries)
- Residents: up to $150 more for an electric leaf blower
- Businesses: up to $300 for an electric leaf blower
- Optional drop-off of old gas equipment at Public Works
- Rebates paid by check, first-come, first-served
redwood-city-lawn-equipment.how_to_get_it:
1. Must be a Redwood City resident or business with a city business license
2. Confirm eligibility with Public Works before buying
3. Buy new electric equipment between July 1, 2026 and June 30, 2027
4. Fill out the application from the City website
5. Submit application with receipts and proof of residency or business license
6. Receive rebate check (may take up to 8 weeks)
redwood-city-lawn-equipment.timeframe: Through June 30, 2027 or until funds run out

redwood-city-solar.name: Solar Rebate Program
redwood-city-solar.description: The City of Redwood City offers rebates for residents installing solar panels, helping reduce electricity costs and promote renewable energy.
redwood-city-solar.what_they_offer:
- $500 rebate for a new residential solar system
- For Redwood City homeowners only
- One rebate per residential unit
- Rebates paid by check, first-come, first-served
redwood-city-solar.how_to_get_it:
1. Must be a Redwood City homeowner
2. Call Public Works to confirm eligibility before buying
3. Buy and install solar between July 1, 2026 and June 30, 2027
4. Installation must be permitted by the City
5. Submit application with receipts and signed building permit within 90 days
6. Receive rebate check
redwood-city-solar.timeframe: Through June 30, 2027 or until funds run out

rising-sun-green-house.name: Green House Call
rising-sun-green-house.description: Rising Sun Center for Opportunity's Green House Calls provide free energy and water-saving upgrades to Bay Area PG&E customers, through in-person summer visits or free kits by mail.
rising-sun-green-house.what_they_offer:
- In-person visit with on-the-spot upgrades (summer, select counties)
- Or a free energy-saving kit by mail after a short survey
- LED lightbulbs, high-efficiency showerheads, and faucet aerators
- Smart power strips or smart plugs, depending on location
- Services delivered by local youth in Rising Sun's Climate Careers program
- No cost to you
rising-sun-green-house.how_to_get_it:
1. Must be a PG&E residential customer not served in the past 5 years
2. In-person visits: Alameda, Contra Costa, Napa, Santa Clara, San Francisco, and Sonoma counties
3. Marin, San Mateo, and Solano counties: mailed kits only
4. Not available in the cities of Alameda, Santa Clara, Palo Alto, or Healdsburg (not on the PG&E grid)
5. Fill out the online sign-up form or call (510) 665-1501 ext. 300
rising-sun-green-house.timeframe: While supplies last; in-person visits offered in summer

sfpuc-cap.name: SFPUC Customer Assistance Program (CAP)
sfpuc-cap.description: The San Francisco Public Utilities Commission Customer Assistance Program provides 25% or 40% discounts on water and sewer bills plus protection from water shutoffs and liens for income-qualified San Francisco residents.
sfpuc-cap.what_they_offer:
- 40% discount on water and sewer bills (income at or below 30% of SF area median income)
- 25% discount (income at or below 50% of SF area median income)
- Example 2026 limits for 1 person - $34,050 (40%) or $56,750 (25%)
- Exempt from water service shutoffs and liens
- Discount lasts 36 months, then reapply
- Payment plans available if you are behind
sfpuc-cap.how_to_get_it:
1. Must be a full-time resident at the address
2. Must have an individually metered residential single-family SFPUC account
3. Apply online (income verified through TransUnion), by mail, or in person at 525 Golden Gate Ave
4. CalFresh, CalWORKs, or Medi-Cal recipients can verify income through SF Human Services Agency with a paper application
5. Discount starts the first full billing cycle after approval (allow 3-4 weeks)
6. Call to request a paper application

thermostat-care-mercury.name: Mercury Thermostat Recycling Rebate
thermostat-care-mercury.description: Thermostat Care, California's mercury thermostat disposal program, pays California residents and service technicians $30 per mercury thermostat dropped off at a participating collection location.
thermostat-care-mercury.what_they_offer:
- $30 mail-in rebate per mercury thermostat
- Up to 5 thermostats per bag and form
- Safe disposal of hazardous mercury (illegal to throw in the trash in California)
- Drop-off locations searchable by ZIP code
- For California residents and service technicians
thermostat-care-mercury.how_to_get_it:
1. Wearing gloves, remove the intact thermostat and seal it in a clear plastic bag
2. Find your nearest drop-off location on the Thermostat Care website
3. Download and fill out the $30 rebate form (or get one at the location)
4. Drop off the thermostat with the form sealed in the bag; keep a copy or photo of the form
5. Check is mailed after the thermostat is verified (can take up to a year)

svp-ebike-rebate.name: Electric Bicycle Rebate
svp-ebike-rebate.description: Silicon Valley Power offers rebates for Santa Clara residents purchasing new electric bicycles, with additional incentives for income-qualified customers.
svp-ebike-rebate.what_they_offer:
- 10% rebate on new e-bike, up to $300
- Additional $200 for income-qualified customers
- Up to $500 total for income-qualified
- Must have an electric motor, battery, and working pedals
- New purchases only; one rebate per customer
- For City of Santa Clara residents only (landlords not eligible)
svp-ebike-rebate.how_to_get_it:
1. Must be a Silicon Valley Power customer
2. Purchase new qualifying electric bicycle
3. Submit application within 60 days of purchase
4. Include paid invoice, photo of serial number, and manufacturer spec sheet
5. Income-qualified bonus requires Financial Rate Assistance Program (FRAP) enrollment
6. Rebate applied as a bill credit

svp-ev-charger-rebate.name: EV Charging Station Rebate
svp-ev-charger-rebate.description: Silicon Valley Power provides rebates for Santa Clara residential customers who install Level 2 EV charging stations at home.
svp-ev-charger-rebate.what_they_offer:
- Up to $350 per Level 2 charging station
- Limit 2 charging stations per residential account
- Hardwired or plug-in (NEMA 14-50) chargers qualify
- Plug-in chargers must be Wi-Fi enabled
- Charging cords, mobile connectors, and splitters not eligible
- Must be new and UL or ETL listed
svp-ev-charger-rebate.how_to_get_it:
1. Must be a Silicon Valley Power customer
2. Purchase and install qualifying EV charger
3. Get a City of Santa Clara permit if required
4. Apply online through SVP rebate platform
5. Apply within 60 days of permit issuance or purchase
6. Receive rebate after approval

svp-used-ev-rebate.name: Income-Qualified Pre-Owned Electric Vehicle Rebate
svp-used-ev-rebate.description: Silicon Valley Power offers substantial rebates for income-qualified Santa Clara residents purchasing pre-owned electric vehicles, with bonuses for efficiency and LIHEAP eligibility.
svp-used-ev-rebate.what_they_offer:
- $1,500 rebate for fully electric vehicles
- $1,000 rebate for plug-in hybrids
- Additional $1,000 bonus for LIHEAP-eligible
- Additional $1,000 for vehicles with MPGe 117+
- Up to $3,500 total possible
- Vehicle must cost $25,000 or less from a licensed dealer
svp-used-ev-rebate.how_to_get_it:
1. Must be a Silicon Valley Power customer
2. Enroll in SVP's Financial Rate Assistance Program before purchase
3. Purchase qualifying pre-owned EV
4. Apply online after purchase
5. Submit proof of purchase and income
6. LIHEAP customers submit additional documentation

svp-induction-cooktop-rebate.name: Induction Cooktop, Range & Oven Rebate
svp-induction-cooktop-rebate.description: Silicon Valley Power offers rebates for Santa Clara residents switching from gas to induction cooking, with enhanced rebates for income-qualified customers.
svp-induction-cooktop-rebate.what_they_offer:
- Up to $750 rebate for electric range with induction cooktop
- Up to $250 for induction cooktop alone
- Up to $200 for electric wall oven
- Income-qualified customers get up to $200 bonus
- Must be ENERGY STAR certified
- Must replace gas cooking equipment
svp-induction-cooktop-rebate.how_to_get_it:

3. Purchase qualifying induction cooktop/range/oven
4. Apply online through SVP rebate platform
5. Apply within 60 days with receipt and before/after photos
6. Income-qualified submit additional documentation

svp-heat-pump-dryer-rebate.name: Heat Pump Clothes Dryer Rebate
svp-heat-pump-dryer-rebate.description: Silicon Valley Power provides rebates for Santa Clara residents switching from gas to high-efficiency heat pump dryers, which use less energy than standard electric dryers.
svp-heat-pump-dryer-rebate.what_they_offer:
- Up to $250 rebate for heat pump dryer
- Up to $350 for income-qualified customers
- Must replace gas dryer
- Heat pump dryers use 50% less energy
- More efficient than standard electric dryers
- Gentler on clothes
svp-heat-pump-dryer-rebate.how_to_get_it:
1. Must be a Silicon Valley Power customer
2. Replace gas dryer with heat pump dryer
3. Purchase qualifying heat pump clothes dryer
4. Apply online through SVP rebate platform
5. Apply within 60 days of purchase or permit issuance
6. Income-qualified submit additional documentation

svp-electric-dryer-rebate.name: Electric Clothes Dryer Rebate
svp-electric-dryer-rebate.description: Silicon Valley Power offers rebates for Santa Clara residents switching from gas to standard electric dryers, with enhanced rebates for income-qualified customers.
svp-electric-dryer-rebate.what_they_offer:
- Up to $150 rebate for electric dryer
- Up to $350 for income-qualified customers
- Must replace gas dryer
- Standard electric dryer option
- More affordable than heat pump option
- Eliminates gas combustion indoors
svp-electric-dryer-rebate.how_to_get_it:

2. Replace gas dryer with electric dryer
3. Purchase qualifying electric clothes dryer
4. Apply online through SVP rebate platform
5. Apply within 60 days of purchase or permit issuance
6. Income-qualified submit additional documentation

svp-hpwh-gas-rebate.name: Heat Pump Water Heater Rebate (Gas Replacement)
svp-hpwh-gas-rebate.description: Silicon Valley Power offers one of the highest heat pump water heater rebates in California for Santa Clara residents replacing gas water heaters.
svp-hpwh-gas-rebate.what_they_offer:
- Up to $5,500 rebate for heat pump water heater
- Up to $6,500 for income-qualified customers
- Must replace gas water heater
- ENERGY STAR certified models required
- Significant energy savings
- Can combine with federal tax credits
svp-hpwh-gas-rebate.how_to_get_it:

2. Replace existing gas water heater
3. Purchase ENERGY STAR heat pump water heater
4. Apply online through SVP rebate platform
5. Apply within 60 days with receipt and building permit
6. Income-qualified submit additional documentation

svp-hpwh-electric-rebate.name: Heat Pump Water Heater Rebate (Electric Replacement)
svp-hpwh-electric-rebate.description: Silicon Valley Power offers rebates for Santa Clara residents upgrading from inefficient electric resistance water heaters to efficient heat pump models.
svp-hpwh-electric-rebate.what_they_offer:
- $500 rebate for heat pump water heater
- Additional $500 for income-qualified customers
- Must replace electric resistance water heater
- ENERGY STAR certified models required
- Significant energy savings (50-70%)
- Lower operating costs
svp-hpwh-electric-rebate.how_to_get_it:
1. Must be a Silicon Valley Power customer
2. Obtain permit from City of Santa Clara
3. Replace electric resistance water heater
4. Purchase ENERGY STAR heat pump water heater
5. Apply online through SVP rebate platform
6. Submit permit and proof of purchase

svp-heat-pump-hvac-rebate.name: Heat Pump HVAC Rebate
svp-heat-pump-hvac-rebate.description: Silicon Valley Power offers one of the most generous heat pump HVAC rebates in California for Santa Clara residents replacing gas furnaces.
svp-heat-pump-hvac-rebate.what_they_offer:
- Up to $10,000 rebate ($3,000 per ton) when replacing a gas furnace
- $1,000 per system when replacing electric resistance heating
- Income-qualified bonus up to $1,000 per system
- Add-on rebates for insulation (up to $5,000) and blower door test improvements
- Minimum 16 SEER2 and 8.0 HSPF2; dual-fuel systems do not qualify
- Existing air conditioning not required
svp-heat-pump-hvac-rebate.how_to_get_it:
1. Must be a Silicon Valley Power customer
2. Replace gas, propane, oil, or wood furnace/heater with heat pump
3. Use licensed HVAC contractor
4. Apply online through SVP rebate platform
5. Apply within 60 days of final permit with before/after photos
6. Income-qualified submit additional documentation

svp-hvac-tuneup-rebate.name: HVAC Tune-Up Rebate
svp-hvac-tuneup-rebate.description: Silicon Valley Power provides rebates for Santa Clara residents to have their HVAC systems professionally tuned up, improving efficiency and extending equipment life.
svp-hvac-tuneup-rebate.what_they_offer:
- Up to $75 rebate for HVAC tune-up
- Must use CA licensed contractor
- Improves system efficiency
- Extends equipment lifespan
- Reduces energy costs
- Ensures proper operation
svp-hvac-tuneup-rebate.how_to_get_it:
1. Must be a Silicon Valley Power customer
2. Schedule HVAC tune-up with licensed contractor
3. Have contractor perform full system check
4. Get receipt with contractor license number
5. Apply online through SVP rebate platform
6. Submit proof of service

svp-circuit-pauser-rebate.name: Circuit Pauser or Splitter Rebate
svp-circuit-pauser-rebate.description: Silicon Valley Power offers rebates for circuit pausers/splitters that allow Santa Clara residents to add electric appliances without expensive panel upgrades.
svp-circuit-pauser-rebate.what_they_offer:
- Up to $50 rebate for circuit pauser/splitter
- Up to $150 for income-qualified customers
- Enables electrification without panel upgrade
- Smart load management device
- Works with multiple appliances
- Cost-effective alternative to panel upgrade
svp-circuit-pauser-rebate.how_to_get_it:
1. Must be a Silicon Valley Power customer
2. Must apply as add-on to other SVP electrification rebate
3. Purchase qualifying circuit pauser/splitter
4. Have device installed by licensed electrician
5. Apply within 60 days through SVP rebate platform
6. Submit with main rebate application

svp-smart-panel-rebate.name: Smart Electric Panel Rebate
svp-smart-panel-rebate.description: Silicon Valley Power offers significant rebates for smart electric panels that enable home electrification without costly main service upgrades.
svp-smart-panel-rebate.what_they_offer:
- $4,000 rebate for smart electric panel
- Additional $1,000-$2,000 for income-qualified
- Supports KOBEN, Lumin, SPAN panels
- Avoids expensive main service upgrade
- Smart load management and monitoring
- Enables full home electrification
svp-smart-panel-rebate.how_to_get_it:
1. Must be a Silicon Valley Power customer
2. For projects starting July 1, 2025 or later
3. Purchase qualifying smart panel (KOBEN, Lumin, SPAN)
4. Have installed by licensed electrician
5. Apply online through SVP rebate platform
6. Submit within 60 days of final permit approval

svp-panel-upgrade-rebate.name: Main Service Panel Upgrade Rebate
svp-panel-upgrade-rebate.description: Silicon Valley Power provides rebates for Santa Clara residents upgrading electrical panels to support EV chargers and electric appliances.
svp-panel-upgrade-rebate.what_they_offer:
- Up to $1,500 rebate for panel upgrade
- Up to $2,500 for income-qualified customers
- Increases panel capacity for electrification
- Supports EV charger installation
- Supports electric appliance installation
- Must be add-on to other SVP rebate
svp-panel-upgrade-rebate.how_to_get_it:
1. Must be a Silicon Valley Power customer
2. Must apply as add-on to other SVP electrification rebate
3. Upgrade main panel to higher amperage
4. Use licensed electrician for installation
5. Apply online through SVP rebate platform
6. Submit with main rebate application

svp-prewire-rebate.name: New Circuits for Future Electric Appliances Rebate
svp-prewire-rebate.description: Silicon Valley Power offers rebates for Santa Clara residents to prewire circuits for future electric appliances, making electrification easier down the road.
svp-prewire-rebate.what_they_offer:
- Up to $500 per circuit (max 4 circuits)
- Up to $2,000 total for standard customers
- Income-qualified customers (FRAP or LIHEAP-eligible) may get a bonus of up to $500 more per circuit
- Eligible future appliances: dryer, cooktop/range, EV charger, and water heater
- Prepares home for future electrification
- Add-on to another SVP home electrification rebate
svp-prewire-rebate.how_to_get_it:
1. Must be a Silicon Valley Power residential customer in Santa Clara
2. Must have another SVP home electrification rebate in progress
3. Have circuits wired to the panel (wire and breaker) for future appliances
4. Contractor invoice must itemize the cost of each circuit
5. Get a building permit
6. Apply online through the SVP rebate platform

svp-battery-storage-rebate.name: Battery Storage Rebate
svp-battery-storage-rebate.description: Silicon Valley Power provides rebates for battery storage systems paired with solar PV, with enhanced incentives for income-qualified customers.
svp-battery-storage-rebate.what_they_offer:
- $0.15 per Wh up to $2,700 base rebate
- Additional $2,000 for FRAP customers
- Additional $2,000 for LIHEAP-eligible
- Up to $6,700 total for income-qualified
- Must pair with solar PV system
- Backup power during outages
svp-battery-storage-rebate.how_to_get_it:
1. Must be a Silicon Valley Power customer
2. Valid for batteries purchased/installed after July 1, 2024
3. Must install with or have existing solar PV
4. Meet City permit requirements
5. Apply online within 60 days of purchase or final permit, with final permit and paid invoice
6. One rebate per service address; FRAP/LIHEAP customers submit additional documentation

svp-hoa-energy-grant.name: Energy Efficiency Grant for HOAs
svp-hoa-energy-grant.description: Silicon Valley Power offers substantial grants to HOAs in Santa Clara for energy efficiency upgrades to common areas, reducing shared utility costs for residents.
svp-hoa-energy-grant.what_they_offer:
- Up to $25,000 grant for energy efficiency
- For HOAs with 25+ individually metered units on D-1 rate
- Funds common area upgrades
- Typical projects include hardwired lighting (exterior lights, bollards, parking lot and clubhouse lighting)
- 20% matching funds required from HOA
- Reduces shared utility costs
svp-hoa-energy-grant.how_to_get_it:
1. HOA must be in Santa Clara with 25+ individually metered units
2. Must be on D-1 electric rate
3. Plan energy efficiency upgrades for common areas
4. Submit application by June 30 (summer period) or December 31 (winter period)
5. Get pre-approval before buying or installing anything
6. HOA provides 20% matching funds
svp-hoa-energy-grant.timeframe: Applications due twice a year (June 30 and December 31); next deadline December 31, 2026

svp-income-qualified-solar.name: Income-Qualified Solar Grant
svp-income-qualified-solar.description: Silicon Valley Power provides substantial solar grants to income-qualified Santa Clara homeowners who have been on the FRAP assistance program, helping low-income residents access renewable energy.
svp-income-qualified-solar.what_they_offer:
- Free solar PV system grant
- $3.50 per watt incentive
- Up to 3 kW system covered
- Significant reduction in electricity bills
- Access to clean renewable energy
- First come, first served basis
svp-income-qualified-solar.how_to_get_it:
1. Must be a Silicon Valley Power residential customer
2. Must be currently enrolled in FRAP, with FRAP approval in at least two consecutive years
3. Must own and live in the home in Santa Clara
4. Must own the solar system (leases and power purchase agreements not eligible)
5. Submit the Income-Qualified Solar Grant Reservation Application for pre-approval
6. SVP does a solar assessment and helps you review installer bids

svp-pool-pump-rebate.name: Variable Speed Pool Pump Rebate
svp-pool-pump-rebate.description: Silicon Valley Power offers rebates for Santa Clara residents who upgrade to energy-efficient variable speed pool pumps, reducing electricity consumption for pool maintenance.
svp-pool-pump-rebate.what_they_offer:
- $100 rebate for pool pump upgrade
- Income-qualified customers may get up to $100 more
- Must be ENERGY STAR certified (WEF 8.0 or higher)
- Variable speed pump with qualifying controller required
- Significant energy savings over single-speed pumps
- One rebate per address every 7 years
svp-pool-pump-rebate.how_to_get_it:
1. Must be a Silicon Valley Power customer
2. Purchase ENERGY STAR variable speed pool pump (3 horsepower or less)
3. Ensure pump has qualifying controller
4. Install on an existing in-ground pool (new construction not eligible)
5. Apply online through SVP rebate platform
6. Submit proof of purchase and installation

svp-solar-tuneup-rebate.name: Solar Tune-Up Rebate
svp-solar-tuneup-rebate.description: Silicon Valley Power offers rebates for Santa Clara residents to have their existing solar PV systems professionally inspected and tuned up, ensuring optimal performance and energy generation.
svp-solar-tuneup-rebate.what_they_offer:
- Up to $1,500 rebate for solar tune-up
- Professional system inspection
- Performance optimization
- Identification of issues or degradation
- Cleaning and maintenance
- Ensures maximum energy production
svp-solar-tuneup-rebate.how_to_get_it:
1. Must be a Silicon Valley Power customer
2. Must have an existing, operating solar PV system (new construction not eligible)
3. Hire a California licensed solar contractor
4. Contractor completes and signs the Solar Tune-Up Contractor Checklist
5. Apply online within 60 days of the maintenance
6. One rebate per address every 12 months; rebate can't exceed the cost

sjce-sj-cares.name: SJ Cares Discount
sjce-sj-cares.description: San Jose Clean Energy provides an additional 10% discount on its electricity generation charges for income-qualified customers already enrolled in PG&E's CARE or FERA programs, helping reduce energy costs.
sjce-sj-cares.what_they_offer:
- 10% discount on SJCE electric generation charges
- Automatic enrollment for CARE/FERA customers
- Stacks with existing CARE/FERA discounts
- Can be combined with SJCE's Solar Access program
- No separate application needed
- Ongoing savings while enrolled in CARE or FERA
sjce-sj-cares.how_to_get_it:
1. Must be a San Jose Clean Energy customer
2. Enroll in CARE or FERA through PG&E
3. Once enrolled, SJ Cares discount is automatic
4. No additional application required
5. Allow up to one month; discount appears on the SJCE page of your PG&E bill
6. Maintain CARE/FERA eligibility to keep discount

sjce-solar-access.name: Solar Access Program
sjce-solar-access.description: San Jose Clean Energy's Solar Access Program gives CARE and FERA customers in qualifying disadvantaged neighborhoods 100% solar energy at a 20% bill discount, stackable with CARE/FERA for up to 55% savings.
sjce-solar-access.what_they_offer:
- 20% off electricity bill
- Stacks with CARE/FERA discounts
- Up to 55% total savings possible
- 100% solar energy sourced for you
- No solar installation or equipment required
- Program is currently full; waitlist usually about one month
sjce-solar-access.how_to_get_it:
1. Must be a San Jose Clean Energy residential customer
2. Must be enrolled in CARE or FERA
3. Must live in a qualifying neighborhood (check the online map)
4. Apply online or call 833-432-2454
5. Eligible applicants go on a waitlist and are enrolled as spots open
6. Discount shows on the SJCE page of your PG&E bill
sjce-solar-access.timeframe: Ongoing; currently full with a waitlist

sjce-ecohome-hpwh.name: EcoHome Heat Pump Water Heater Rebate
sjce-ecohome-hpwh.description: San Jose Clean Energy offers substantial rebates for replacing gas water heaters with energy-efficient heat pump water heaters, with enhanced rebates for income-qualified residents and Environmental Justice Communities.
sjce-ecohome-hpwh.what_they_offer:
- $2,500 rebate for heat pump water heater
- $3,500 for Environmental Justice Community qualified residents (including CARE, FERA, or SJ Cares customers)
- Extra $500 bonus through October 31, 2026 ($3,000 standard / $4,000 EJ)
- Must replace a gas water heater; 40 gallons or larger
- Self-installed projects allowed
- Interest-free EcoHome Payment Plan available
sjce-ecohome-hpwh.how_to_get_it:
1. Must be the primary account holder with San Jose Clean Energy service
2. Submit a Rebate Application with photos of existing equipment and get approval before installation
3. Funds are reserved for 120 days after approval
4. Install new equipment and pass final permit inspection
5. Submit Rebate Claim with itemized invoice, proof of final permit, and photos
6. Choose payment by PayPal, Venmo, or check

sjce-ecohome-hvac.name: EcoHome Heat Pump HVAC Rebate
sjce-ecohome-hvac.description: San Jose Clean Energy offers rebates for replacing gas furnaces with efficient heat pump HVAC systems that provide both heating and cooling, with enhanced rebates for qualifying residents.
sjce-ecohome-hvac.what_they_offer:
- $1,500 rebate for heat pump HVAC
- $2,500 for Environmental Justice Community qualified residents (including CARE, FERA, or SJ Cares customers)
- Must replace a gas furnace; no existing AC required
- Ducted central and ductless mini-split systems qualify (SEER2 16 or higher; dual fuel not eligible)
- Self-installed projects allowed
- Interest-free EcoHome Payment Plan available
sjce-ecohome-hvac.how_to_get_it:
1. Must be the primary account holder with San Jose Clean Energy service
2. Submit a Rebate Application with photos of existing equipment and get approval before installation
3. Funds are reserved for 120 days after approval
4. Install new system and pass final permit inspection (HERS test required)
5. Submit Rebate Claim with itemized invoice, proof of final permit, and photos
6. Choose payment by PayPal, Venmo, or check

sjce-ecohome-panel.name: EcoHome Panel Upgrade Rebate
sjce-ecohome-panel.description: San Jose Clean Energy offers rebates for electrical panel upgrades when done alongside an EcoHome heat pump water heater or heat pump HVAC project, helping homes support additional electric appliances.
sjce-ecohome-panel.what_they_offer:
- $1,000 rebate for panel upgrade
- $2,000 for Environmental Justice Community qualified residents
- Existing panel must be under 200 amps; upgrade to at least 200 amps
- Must be paired with a heat pump water heater or heat pump HVAC rebate
- Supports home electrification
- Enables additional electric appliances
sjce-ecohome-panel.how_to_get_it:
1. Must be a San Jose Clean Energy customer
2. Must be installing a heat pump water heater or heat pump HVAC through EcoHome
3. Include panel upgrade in your Rebate Application with a photo of the existing panel
4. Get approval before work begins; funds reserved for 120 days
5. Complete installation and pass final permit inspection
6. Submit Rebate Claim with itemized invoice, permit, and photos

sjce-ecohome-insulation.name: EcoHome Attic Insulation Rebate
sjce-ecohome-insulation.description: San Jose Clean Energy offers rebates for attic insulation when done alongside an EcoHome heat pump HVAC project, improving home energy efficiency and comfort.
sjce-ecohome-insulation.what_they_offer:
- $0.75 per sq. ft. for attic insulation, up to $700
- Up to $1,000 for Environmental Justice Community qualified residents
- Must be paired with a heat pump HVAC rebate
- Improves home energy efficiency
- Reduces heating and cooling costs
- Enhances comfort year-round
sjce-ecohome-insulation.how_to_get_it:
1. Must be a San Jose Clean Energy customer
2. Must be installing a heat pump HVAC system through EcoHome
3. Include attic insulation in your Rebate Application
4. Get approval before work begins; funds reserved for 120 days
5. Take before and after photos with a ruler showing insulation depth
6. Submit Rebate Claim with itemized invoice, permit, and photos

sjce-ecohome-prewire.name: EcoHome Circuit Prewiring Rebate
sjce-ecohome-prewire.description: San Jose Clean Energy offers rebates for prewiring EV charger, dryer, and cooking circuits when done alongside an EcoHome heat pump water heater or heat pump HVAC project, preparing homes for future electric appliances.
sjce-ecohome-prewire.what_they_offer:
- $500 each for EV, dryer, or cooking circuit prewiring
- $750 each for Environmental Justice Community qualified residents
- $250 for a circuit pauser/splitter device
- One rebate per circuit type per home
- No EV charger needed to get the EV circuit rebate
- Must be paired with a heat pump water heater or heat pump HVAC rebate
sjce-ecohome-prewire.how_to_get_it:
1. Must be a San Jose Clean Energy customer
2. Must be installing a heat pump water heater or heat pump HVAC through EcoHome
3. Include circuit prewiring in your Rebate Application
4. Get approval before work begins; funds reserved for 120 days
5. Complete work and pass final permit inspection
6. Submit Rebate Claim with itemized invoice listing circuits and photos

sjce-ev-new.name: New EV Instant Rebate
sjce-ev-new.description: San Jose Clean Energy offers instant rebates on new electric vehicles for income-qualified residents, making EV ownership more accessible for lower-income households.
sjce-ev-new.what_they_offer:
- $3,000 instant rebate on a new EV (starting September 15, 2026; was $4,000)
- Maximum vehicle price $50,000 (starting September 15, 2026)
- Works for buying or leasing
- For battery electric vehicles only (no plug-in hybrids)
- Applied at point of sale at participating dealerships
- One rebate per service address per year; can combine with other incentives
sjce-ev-new.how_to_get_it:
1. Must be a San Jose Clean Energy customer; vehicle registered at your SJCE home address
2. Qualify by being on CARE or FERA, or with household income at or below 100% Area Median Income
3. Apply online (CARE/FERA customers get a rebate code instantly; income applicants in 1-3 business days)
4. Or, if approved for Clean Cars for All or DCAP, bring your award letter and ID to the dealer
5. Share your rebate code with a participating dealership
6. Codes valid through June 30, 2027 unless funds run out
sjce-ev-new.timeframe: Program year through June 30, 2027 or until funds run out

sjce-ev-used.name: Used EV Instant Rebate
sjce-ev-used.description: San Jose Clean Energy provides instant rebates on used electric vehicles for income-qualified residents, offering an affordable pathway to EV ownership.
sjce-ev-used.what_they_offer:
- $1,750 instant rebate on a used EV (starting September 15, 2026; was $2,000)
- Maximum vehicle price $50,000 (starting September 15, 2026)
- Works for buying or leasing
- For battery electric vehicles only (no plug-in hybrids)
- Applied at point of sale at participating dealerships
- One rebate per service address per year; can combine with other incentives
sjce-ev-used.how_to_get_it:
1. Must be a San Jose Clean Energy customer; vehicle registered at your SJCE home address
2. Qualify by being on CARE or FERA, or with household income at or below 100% Area Median Income
3. Apply online (CARE/FERA customers get a rebate code instantly; income applicants in 1-3 business days)
4. Or, if approved for Clean Cars for All or DCAP, bring your award letter and ID to the dealer
5. Share your rebate code with a participating dealership
6. Codes valid through June 30, 2027 unless funds run out
sjce-ev-used.timeframe: Program year through June 30, 2027 or until funds run out

sjce-peak-rewards.name: Peak Rewards Program
sjce-peak-rewards.description: San Jose Clean Energy's Peak Rewards for All program pays residential customers bill credits to reduce electricity usage during peak demand periods, with no penalty for non-participation.
sjce-peak-rewards.what_they_offer:
- $1.00 per kWh reduced in summer (May-October)
- $0.50 per kWh reduced in winter (November-April)
- Up to 6 earning opportunities per month, usually 4-10 p.m.
- Alerts typically 24 hours in advance by email or text
- No penalty for non-participation
- Credits applied to your PG&E bill quarterly
sjce-peak-rewards.how_to_get_it:
1. Must be an SJCE residential customer in San Jose with a PG&E smart meter
2. Create a FlexSaver account online
3. Enroll in Peak Rewards for All
4. Can't be enrolled in another demand response program (like OhmConnect or a PG&E program)
5. Reduce usage during Peak Rewards Alerts
6. Earn bill credits based on your reduction

sjce-peak-rewards-thermostat.name: Peak Rewards for Smart Thermostats
sjce-peak-rewards-thermostat.description: San Jose Clean Energy pays customers an enrollment bonus and quarterly credits for enrolling eligible smart thermostats in its Peak Rewards for Smart Homes program, with automatic adjustments during peak events.
sjce-peak-rewards-thermostat.what_they_offer:
- $30 enrollment bonus (prepaid card)
- $9 per summer quarter and $3.50 per winter quarter in bill credits
- Compatible with Google Nest and Sensi thermostats
- Thermostat adjusts 2-4 degrees for 2-4 hours, about 3-4 times a month
- Option to override any adjustment; SJCE never locks thermostats
- Must take part in at least half of events each quarter to earn quarterly payment
sjce-peak-rewards-thermostat.how_to_get_it:
1. Must be an SJCE residential customer with a PG&E smart meter
2. Must have a supported Google Nest or Sensi smart thermostat
3. Select your thermostat brand on the Peak Rewards for Smart Homes page to enroll
4. Device can't be enrolled in another demand response program
5. Thermostat auto-adjusts during Peak Rewards Events
6. Override option always available

sjce-peak-rewards-ev-charger.name: Peak Rewards for EV Chargers
sjce-peak-rewards-ev-charger.description: San Jose Clean Energy pays EV owners for enrolling an eligible charger or EV in its managed charging program, pausing charging during peak events with an override option, plus a bonus for midday charging.
sjce-peak-rewards-ev-charger.what_they_offer:
- $25 enrollment bonus for managed charging
- $3 per month (paid quarterly) for shifting charging during events
- Midday Charging Bonus of up to $40 per quarter ($160 per year) for charging 9 a.m.-2 p.m.
- Enroll a supported charger (such as Emporia) or your EV through the free Optiwatt app
- Charging paused or reduced 2-4 hours during events, about 3-4 times a month
- Option to override any pause
sjce-peak-rewards-ev-charger.how_to_get_it:
1. Must be an SJCE residential customer with a PG&E smart meter
2. Have a home charger and a supported charger or EV (check Optiwatt's supported vehicle list)
3. Enroll through the Peak Rewards for Smart Homes page
4. Complete a home charging session within 7 days of enrolling
5. Device can't be enrolled in another demand response or managed charging program
6. Charging adjusts during events; override option always available

sjce-peak-rewards-battery.name: Peak Rewards for Battery Storage
sjce-peak-rewards-battery.description: San Jose Clean Energy rewards battery storage owners for enrolling in its Peak Rewards for Smart Homes program, providing both an upfront bonus and ongoing quarterly payments.
sjce-peak-rewards-battery.what_they_offer:
- $8 per kWh enrollment bonus, up to $240
- $0.13 per kWh quarterly bill credit (about $143 per quarter for a 15 kWh battery)
- Battery used automatically each evening when energy demand is highest
- Battery never drops below 20% charge, so backup power stays available
- Available even if you got an SJCE EcoHome battery rebate
- Helps support the grid and prevent outages
sjce-peak-rewards-battery.how_to_get_it:
1. Must be an SJCE residential customer with a PG&E smart meter
2. Must have a supported battery storage brand
3. Enroll through the Peak Rewards for Smart Homes page
4. Battery can't be enrolled in another demand response or virtual power plant program
5. Battery is managed automatically; no action needed
6. Receive quarterly credits on your electricity bill

cpau-rap.name: Rate Assistance Program (RAP)
cpau-rap.description: The City of Palo Alto Utilities Rate Assistance Program provides significant discounts on utility bills for residents with financial need or medical conditions requiring higher utility use.
cpau-rap.what_they_offer:
- 25% off gas charges
- 35% off electricity charges
- For households at or below 80% of area median income (as of July 1, 2026)
- Income limits: $113,700/year for 1 person, $162,400 for 4, $214,400 for 8
- For medical conditions requiring higher utility use (physician certification)
- Applied to monthly utility bills
cpau-rap.how_to_get_it:
1. Must be a City of Palo Alto Utilities customer
2. Qualify by financial need, based on your household's most recent monthly income
3. Or by medical need, with a physician's certification
4. Download the RAP application (English, Spanish, Traditional Chinese, or Russian)
5. Submit application with supporting documentation
6. Discount applied once approved

cpau-reap.name: Residential Energy Assistance Program (REAP)
cpau-reap.description: The City of Palo Alto's REAP program provides free home efficiency upgrades, and free electric appliance upgrades for homeowners, to residents enrolled in the Rate Assistance Program, helping reduce utility costs.
cpau-reap.what_they_offer:
- Free LED lighting
- Free insulation and weatherization (attics, roofs, walls, doors, windows)
- Free portable induction cooktops
- Homeowners may also get free heat pump HVAC and heat pump water heater upgrades
- Homeowners may also get free induction cooktops/ranges and electric dryers
- Renters are eligible for efficiency upgrades only
cpau-reap.how_to_get_it:
1. Must be a City of Palo Alto Utilities customer
2. Must be enrolled in the Rate Assistance Program (RAP) for financial need
3. Home must be under 2,500 square feet and not a short-term rental
4. Homeowners must live in the home, own no other property, and have investable assets under $500,000
5. Renters need the property owner's authorization
6. Enroll in Electrify My Home and select interest in the income-qualified program

cpau-project-pledge.name: ProjectPLEDGE
cpau-project-pledge.description: ProjectPLEDGE provides one-time utility bill assistance for Palo Alto residents facing sudden hardship such as job loss, loss of a spouse, or unexpected medical expenses, helping cover past-due utility balances.
cpau-project-pledge.what_they_offer:
- One-time utility bill assistance
- Up to $750 in assistance
- Covers past-due amounts
- Credit cannot exceed outstanding balance
- First come, first served until funds run out
- Funded through community donations
cpau-project-pledge.how_to_get_it:
1. Must be a City of Palo Alto Utilities residential customer
2. Must be the customer-of-record on account
3. Must have past-due utility balance
4. Show hardship: reduced hours or job loss, recent loss of spouse, or unexpected medical bills
5. Download the application and send it to Utilities Customer Service
6. Credit applied to account if approved

cpau-hpwh-rebate.name: Heat Pump Water Heater Rebate
cpau-hpwh-rebate.description: City of Palo Alto Utilities offers one of the most generous heat pump water heater rebates in the region, plus a full-service Electrify My Home option with fixed pricing and fast emergency replacement.
cpau-hpwh-rebate.what_they_offer:
- $3,500 rebate for replacing a gas water heater
- $500 rebate for replacing an electric resistance water heater
- Extra $500 discount for projects signed or reserved July 1 to October 31, 2026
- Full-service Electrify My Home install (65-gallon) for a fixed $3,350 after rebate
- Emergency/fast replacement within 48 hours starting at $2,100 (with the $500 discount)
- Permit fee rebate up to $638 for stand-alone permits
cpau-hpwh-rebate.how_to_get_it:
1. Must be a City of Palo Alto Utilities customer
2. For full service, call (650) 713-3411 or sign up for Electrify My Home
3. To use your own contractor, reserve your rebate in the Rebate Hub before installing
4. Funds are reserved for up to 120 days
5. Install and pass final inspection
6. Submit the final rebate application within 90 days of final inspection

cpau-hp-hvac-rebate.name: Heat Pump HVAC Rebate
cpau-hp-hvac-rebate.description: City of Palo Alto Utilities offers rebates for replacing gas furnaces with efficient heat pump HVAC systems that provide both heating and cooling from a single unit, with higher rebates for income-eligible residents.
cpau-hp-hvac-rebate.what_they_offer:
- $2,500 rebate for heat pump HVAC
- $5,000 for income-eligible residents
- Must replace a gas or other fossil fuel heater
- Add-on rebates for panel upgrades, attic insulation, and new circuits
- Permit fee rebate up to $638
- Full-service option through Electrify My Home with fixed pricing
cpau-hp-hvac-rebate.how_to_get_it:
1. Must be a City of Palo Alto Utilities customer
2. Reserve your rebate in the Rebate Hub before installing (or use a CPAU Instant Rebate Partner contractor)
3. Funds are reserved for up to 120 days
4. Install and pass final inspection
5. Submit the final rebate application within 90 days of final inspection
6. Rebate check arrives in about five weeks

cpau-gas-meter-removal.name: Gas Meter Removal Incentive
cpau-gas-meter-removal.description: City of Palo Alto Utilities rewards residents who fully electrify their homes and disconnect from natural gas service, supporting the city's sustainability goals.
cpau-gas-meter-removal.what_they_offer:
- $2,500 incentive for gas meter removal
- Rewards full home electrification
- Stacks with other electrification rebates
- Eliminates monthly gas service charges
- Incentive is taxable income (W-9 required)
- Supports city climate goals
cpau-gas-meter-removal.how_to_get_it:
1. Must be a City of Palo Alto Utilities customer
2. Replace all gas appliances with electric
3. Submit the online Gas Removal for Electrification form to CPAU
4. Gas meter is removed within about 2-10 business days
5. Apply for the incentive through the Rebate Hub with proof of meter removal and a W-9
6. Receive incentive after verification

cpau-ev-charger-mf-rebate.name: EV Charger Rebate for Multi-Family Properties
cpau-ev-charger-mf-rebate.description: City of Palo Alto Utilities provides substantial rebates for installing shared or assigned EV chargers at multi-family properties.
cpau-ev-charger-mf-rebate.what_they_offer:
- Up to $80,000 in rebates
- For shared or assigned EV chargers at multi-family properties
- Program manager guides you through the whole project
- Separate incentive available if a transformer upgrade is needed
- Supports EV adoption in shared spaces
- Funding is limited
cpau-ev-charger-mf-rebate.how_to_get_it:
1. Contact Utilities Program Services to discuss eligibility
2. Fill out EV Charger Rebate Application (Part 1) to reserve a rebate
3. Work with a contractor to design the project
4. Get a permit from Development Services
5. Install chargers and pass final inspection
6. Submit EV Charger Rebate Application (Part 2)

cpau-transformer-upgrade-rebate.name: Transformer Upgrade Rebate Program
cpau-transformer-upgrade-rebate.description: City of Palo Alto Utilities helps offset the cost of electric service and transformer upgrades needed for EV charger installations, making charging infrastructure more affordable.
cpau-transformer-upgrade-rebate.what_they_offer:
- Up to $10,000 per single-family home
- Multi-family properties: up to $10,000 per port, max $100,000 (10 ports)
- Credits utility service fees for transformer upgrades beyond standard connection fees
- Outside contractor costs needed to install the transformer also qualify
- Customer still pays the base fee
- Funding is limited
cpau-transformer-upgrade-rebate.how_to_get_it:
1. Must be a City of Palo Alto Utilities customer
2. Apply for an EV charger permit
3. CPAU Engineering tells you if a service or transformer upgrade is needed
4. Submit the Electric Service Connection Fee Incentive Application
5. Pay the Advance Engineering Fee and transformer invoice before construction
6. Finish EV charger installation within 18 months of approval

cpau-landscape-conversion.name: Landscape Conversion Rebate
cpau-landscape-conversion.description: City of Palo Alto offers rebates for converting water-intensive lawns and pools to sustainable, drought-tolerant landscaping through a partnership with Valley Water.
cpau-landscape-conversion.what_they_offer:
- $4 per square foot for the first 1,000 sq. ft. and $2 per sq. ft. after that (single-family and small multi-family)
- For converting lawns or swimming pools to low-water-use landscape
- Palo Alto adds cost sharing on top of Valley Water's base rate
- Lifetime cap of $6,000 per single-family or small multi-family site (landscape, irrigation, and stormwater rebates combined)
- Larger rates and caps for commercial and 5+ unit multi-family sites
- Significant water savings
cpau-landscape-conversion.how_to_get_it:
1. Must be a City of Palo Alto water customer (well customers don't get cost sharing)
2. Apply through Valley Water's online application portal before starting
3. Complete a pre-inspection and submit your project plan and plant list
4. Wait for a written Notice to Proceed, then finish within 90 days
5. Request a post-inspection and send photos or receipts
6. Rebate check arrives 4-6 weeks after approval
cpau-landscape-conversion.timeframe: Current funding through June 30, 2027 or until funds run out

cpau-graywater-rebate.name: Graywater Laundry-to-Landscape Rebate
cpau-graywater-rebate.description: City of Palo Alto offers rebates for installing graywater systems that reuse washing machine water for landscape irrigation, reducing water consumption.
cpau-graywater-rebate.what_they_offer:
- $400 rebate for City of Palo Alto Utilities customers ($200 base rate elsewhere)
- For laundry-to-landscape graywater systems
- Sends washer rinse water straight to your landscape, no tanks or pumps
- Good for trees, shrubs, and drought-tolerant plants
- Reduces potable water use
- Sustainable water management
cpau-graywater-rebate.how_to_get_it:
1. Must be a homeowner and City of Palo Alto Utilities customer
2. Washer should be near an exterior wall, with landscape within about 50 feet and at the same level or downhill
3. Apply to Valley Water online or by mail
4. Get application approved before starting any work
5. Install the system following the California Plumbing Code
6. Submit final documentation for rebate
cpau-graywater-rebate.timeframe: Current funding through June 30, 2027 or until funds run out

cpau-stormwater-rebates.name: Stormwater Rebates Program
cpau-stormwater-rebates.description: City of Palo Alto, in partnership with Valley Water, offers rebates for stormwater features that capture and filter rainwater, reducing runoff and protecting local creeks and the Bay.
cpau-stormwater-rebates.what_they_offer:
- Rain barrels: $70 per barrel (40-199 gallons; can be self-installed)
- Cisterns: $1.00 per gallon (200 gallons or larger; licensed contractor)
- Pervious pavement: $1.50 per sq. ft. (100 sq. ft. minimum; lifetime cap $1,000 for homes)
- Rain gardens: $2 per sq. ft. of roof diverted, up to $600 (licensed contractor)
- Renters can apply with written consent from the property owner
- Reduces stormwater runoff and protects water quality
cpau-stormwater-rebates.how_to_get_it:
1. Must own the property in Palo Alto, or rent with the owner's written consent
2. Apply before buying equipment or starting work
3. Apply for rain barrels, cisterns, and rain gardens through Valley Water's Landscape Rebate Program
4. Apply for pervious pavement through Palo Alto's Pervious Pavement Rebate Program
5. Get a building permit if required
6. Install the feature and submit documentation for rebate
